2605.q: Which other bird can you roughly compare the size of a common buzzard with?
2605.e: A common buzzard is about the size of a large crow but has much broader wings. This makes it look much bulkier in flight.
2605.m: About the size of a crow with broad wings.

2607.q: What do kingfisher parents feed their young in the nest?
2607.e: All day long the parents bring small fish to the young in the nest chamber. This way the chicks grow quickly.
2607.m: Parents feed the young small fish.

2608.q: What does a dog do when it is very hot?
a: It pants with its mouth open
It lies down in the sun
2608.e: Dogs can hardly sweat, so they pant with their mouths open to cool down. They breathe in and out quickly as they do so.

2609.q: What does the tawny owl grab its prey with?
2609.e: Like all owls, the tawny owl grabs its prey with strong, sharp claws called talons. The beak is used more for tearing the prey apart.
2609.m: The tawny owl catches prey with sharp talons.

2610.q: What kind of water does a seahorse need in an aquarium?
2610.e: Seahorses live in the sea. That is why they need clean salt water at the right temperature in an aquarium.

2611.q: Which group of fish does the brown trout belong to?
2611.e: Predatory fish eat other animals. The brown trout hunts insect larvae, crayfish and small fish.
2611.m: The brown trout is a predatory fish.

2612.q: The German name for the least weasel is “Mauswiesel”, meaning “mouse weasel”. Where does the name probably come from?
a: Because it squeaks like a mouse
Because it is born in mouse holes
2612.e: The name points directly to its favourite prey. The least weasel is one of the most effective mouse hunters of all.
2612.m: The least weasel, the mouse hunter.

2613.q: Why is the earthworm a popular bait for fishing?
a: Because it moves and attracts fish
2613.e: The worm’s movements on the hook catch the fish’s attention. That is why anglers often use it as bait.

2614.q: Which sense helps aphids find suitable plants?
a: Smell and touch with their antennae
2614.e: With their antennae aphids sense scents and touch. This is how they recognise suitable plants.

2615.q: What is a large group of jellyfish in the sea called?
2615.e: When very many jellyfish swim together in the sea, it is called a swarm of jellyfish. This can happen on some coasts.

2616.q: At what altitude in the mountains does the Alpine ibex most like to live?
a: In steep rocky areas above the tree line
Deep in the forest in the valley
Only on flat meadows in the Central Plateau
2616.e: Ibex prefer steep, rocky ground above the tree line, often between 2000 and 3200 metres. There they are well protected from enemies.
2616.m: Ibex love steep rocks high up.

2617.q: Which bird often hunts young penguins or their eggs on land?
2617.e: Skuas are skilful raiders that can steal unguarded penguin eggs or small chicks. That is why penguin parents guard their young closely.
2617.m: Skuas threaten penguin eggs and chicks.

2618.q: What does the koala’s nose look like?
2618.e: The koala has a big, black, leathery nose. It looks almost like a leather button on its face.
2618.m: Koalas have a big, leathery nose.

2619.q: After how many weeks do young common buzzards first leave the nest?
2619.e: Young buzzards stay in the nest for around six to seven weeks before they fly for the first time. After that the parents still look after them for a while.
2619.m: The young fly after seven weeks.

2620.q: What does the ibex do when there is deep snow in winter?
a: It moves to lower, sunny slopes with less snow
It digs deep caves in the rock
It travels to warm countries like a migratory bird
2620.e: When there is a lot of snow, ibex move to lower, sunlit slopes where there is less snow and food can still be found. They do not hibernate.
2620.m: In winter they look for sunny slopes with little snow.

2621.q: What colours is a giant panda’s fur?
2621.e: Pandas have striking black and white fur. That is how you recognise them straight away.
2621.m: Panda fur is black and white.

2622.q: In a group of meerkats, who usually has the young?
a: A dominant female and a dominant male
All the animals at the same time
2622.e: Usually only the dominant pair has young. The other animals help to raise them.
2622.m: Usually only the leading pair has young.

2623.q: Which animal is the largest land mammal still living in the wild in Europe?
2623.e: The European bison, also called the wisent, was almost extinct and was saved by special breeding programmes. Today it lives in selected protected areas.
2623.m: The European bison is Europe's largest land mammal.

2624.q: Which danger especially threatens the Alpine salamander today?
a: The loss of its natural habitat
Too much rain in the desert
2624.e: Because of building projects, roads and changes in how land is used, the Alpine salamander is losing parts of its habitat. Climate change also harms it.
2624.m: Habitat loss threatens the Alpine salamander.

2625.q: About how many lynx live in the whole of Switzerland?
2625.e: Swiss lynx numbers are small but have grown since they were reintroduced. Today a few hundred lynx live in the Jura and the Alps.
2625.m: A few hundred lynx live in Switzerland.

2626.q: What does a sparrow do straight away when there is danger?
2626.e: Sparrows are very alert and all fly up together at the slightest danger. This way the whole group protects itself.
2626.m: Sparrows flee at once when in danger.

2627.q: What is the Great Red Spot on Jupiter?
a: A huge storm that is centuries old
2627.e: The Great Red Spot is an enormous storm in Jupiter’s atmosphere that is bigger than the Earth. It has been observed for centuries.
2627.m: The Great Red Spot is a gigantic storm on Jupiter.

2628.q: What does a bumblebee’s fur feel like?
2628.e: Bumblebees have a thick, soft coat of lots of tiny hairs. This coat keeps them warm even in cool weather.
2628.m: Bumblebee fur is soft and thick.

2629.q: What sound does a duck typically make?
2629.e: Quacking is the typical sound of a duck. Females especially quack very loudly.

2630.q: Where does the robin most like to hide its nest?
a: In thick undergrowth close to the ground
At the very top of tall trees
In the middle of a meadow
2630.e: The nest is well hidden in thick undergrowth close to the ground, often under bushes or ivy. This way enemies do not find it so easily.
2630.m: The nest is hidden in the undergrowth.

2631.q: What shape are a leopard's pupils?
2631.e: Big cats like the leopard have round pupils. Small cats like the house cat often have slit-shaped pupils.

a: So that fish can get past obstacles in a river
So that anglers can reach the bank more easily
So that the water gets warmer
2632.e: A fish ladder is made of several small pools arranged like steps. The fish jump or swim upwards from pool to pool.
2632.m: Fish ladders help fish past obstacles.

2633.q: What is a big danger for wild chimpanzees?
2633.e: When forests are cut down, chimpanzees lose their home. That makes it very hard for them to survive.

2634.q: What do researchers look at to tell individual wild dogs apart?
2634.e: Because each animal has its own pattern of patches, individual wild dogs can be recognised in photos. This lets researchers observe packs.
2634.m: The coat pattern gives away each individual animal.

2635.q: What colour is the skin of an edible frog usually?
2635.e: Edible frogs are usually green with dark, irregular spots. Often there is a lighter stripe down the back.
2635.m: The edible frog is green with dark spots.

2636.q: Can some starfish have more than five arms?
a: Yes, some species have more arms
2636.e: Not all starfish have five arms. Some species have ten, twenty or even more arms.
2636.m: Some species have more than five arms.

2637.q: What colour is a yellow eel’s back usually?
2637.e: The back is dark and the belly yellowish. This camouflages the eel well on the bottom of rivers and lakes.
2637.m: Yellow eels are dark with a yellow belly.

2638.q: What is the function of an independent constitutional court?
a: It checks whether laws and government actions comply with the constitution.
It organises election campaigns for the government.
2638.e: A constitutional court can declare laws invalid if they violate the constitution. In doing so it limits the power of government and parliament and protects fundamental rights.

2639.q: Why is washing your hands important?
a: It removes germs and protects against illness
2639.e: Washing your hands with soap rinses away lots of bacteria and viruses. That way you get ill less often.

2640.q: What else is the cross spider called?
2640.e: Because it is found so often in gardens, the cross spider is also called the European garden spider. It likes living among plants.
2640.m: It is also called the European garden spider.

2641.q: Why are an alpaca’s padded feet better for pastures than hooves?
a: They are gentle on the soil and the turf
They fertilise the ground with salt
2641.e: The soft soles press the ground together less than hooves do. This keeps the meadow in better condition.
2641.m: Soft soles are gentle on the pasture.

2642.q: Which sense organ does the rattlesnake use to find warm-blooded prey in the dark?
2642.e: Rattlesnakes have small pits between the eye and the nose that sense heat. This lets them find their prey even in complete darkness.
2642.m: Pit organs sense heat in the dark.

2643.q: Do goats really eat tin cans?
a: No, they only nibble them out of curiosity
2643.e: Goats explore almost everything with their mouths because they are very curious. But they do not eat tin cans.

2644.q: How does a camel move when it lies down?
a: It bends its front legs first
It tips over onto its side
2644.e: Camels kneel down first and then lie down. For this they have calluses on their chest and knees.

2646.q: What danger can fish that have been released into a pond pose to edible frog spawn and tadpoles?
a: They bring the frogs extra food
They clean algae out of the water for the frogs
2646.e: Fish put into ponds often eat frogspawn and tadpoles. This can make it very hard for edible frogs to breed in that pond.
2646.m: Fish can eat spawn and tadpoles.

2647.q: Who proved with a kite experiment that lightning is electric?
2647.e: In 1752 the American Benjamin Franklin flew a kite during a thunderstorm and showed that lightning is an electrical discharge. This finding led to the invention of the lightning conductor.
2647.m: Franklin proved that lightning is electric.

2648.q: Which animal is one of the snow leopard’s important prey?
2648.e: The snow leopard mainly hunts hoofed animals of the mountains, for example blue sheep and Siberian ibex. It also eats marmots and hares.
2648.m: It hunts wild sheep and ibex.

2649.q: How do dolphins find their prey in dark water?
a: With clicking sounds that bounce back
With their eyes in the dark
2649.e: Dolphins send out clicking sounds. When these hit a fish, an echo comes back and the dolphin knows where its prey is.
2649.m: Dolphins locate things with clicks and echoes.

2650.q: In a famous old fable, a grasshopper sings all summer instead of working. Who busily gathers food instead?
2650.e: In the fable the grasshopper prefers to sing instead of preparing for winter. The ant, on the other hand, busily gathers food.
2650.m: The ant gathers, the grasshopper sings.

2651.q: About how long is the body of an adult least weasel?
2651.e: Least weasels are very small and slim. Males grow a little bigger than females.
2651.m: Least weasels are only about the length of a hand.

2652.q: Why don’t you see barn swallows in Switzerland in winter?
a: They fly to Africa because there are no flying insects here
They turn white and invisible in winter
2652.e: In winter there are hardly any flying insects here. That is why barn swallows migrate to Africa south of the Sahara and come back in spring.
2652.m: With no insects in winter, the swallow goes to Africa.

2653.q: About how old can a koala get in the wild?
2653.e: Koalas can live to about 13 to 18 years in the wild. Females often live a little longer than males.
2653.m: Koalas often live for over ten years.

2654.q: What is the name of the famous medieval story character, a cunning fox with his own name?
2654.e: Reynard the Fox is a famous character from old European animal stories. He stands for an especially clever and cunning fox.
2654.m: Reynard the Fox is a cunning hero.

2655.q: Which family of animals does the chamois belong to?
2655.e: The chamois belongs to the bovid family and, within it, to the goat-like animals. Its scientific name is Rupicapra rupicapra.

2656.q: Is the hippo dangerous to people in Africa?
a: Yes, it can be very dangerous
No, it always runs away at once
2656.e: Although it eats only plants, the hippo is one of the most dangerous animals in Africa. It defends its territory fiercely and can attack quickly.
2656.m: Hippos are dangerous even though they eat plants.

2657.q: On which continent do most dromedaries live today?
2657.e: Most dromedaries are kept in north-east Africa. There are also many in Arabia.

2658.q: What colour is a red squirrel’s fur often?
2658.e: Most squirrels in Switzerland have reddish-brown fur. Some, however, are a little darker or lighter.

2659.q: About how big does an adult badger get?
a: About as big as a medium-sized dog
2659.e: An adult badger measures about 70 to 90 centimetres including the tail. That is roughly the size of a medium-sized dog.
2659.m: Badgers are about the size of a dog.

2660.q: What are a cow’s hooves called, because they are split into two parts?
2660.e: The split hooves of a cow are called cloven hooves. That is why the cow belongs to the cloven-hoofed animals.

2661.q: What does a goldfish absolutely need to be well?
a: A big enough aquarium or a pond
2661.e: Goldfish need lots of space to swim, otherwise they stay small and get ill. A small bowl is not enough.

2662.q: Who rules an ant colony and lays almost all the eggs?
2662.e: An ant colony usually has one queen, who lays eggs all day long. The workers look after food, the nest and the young.
2662.m: The queen lays almost all the eggs in the colony.

2663.q: How many pups does a female wolf usually have in a litter?
2663.e: A female wolf usually has between 4 and 6 pups in a litter. However, not all of them survive their first year.
2663.m: Female wolves usually have 4 to 6 pups.

2664.q: How does the great spotted woodpecker move up a tree trunk?
a: hopping upwards, using its tail as a prop
not at all, it just sits still
2664.e: The great spotted woodpecker skilfully hops upwards with both feet at the same time. It supports itself with its stiff tail.

2665.q: On 6 December many children celebrate the day of a holy man. What is his name?
2665.e: Saint Nicholas was a bishop who was especially kind to poor people. On his day he often brings children small presents.
2665.m: Saint Nicholas brings presents on 6 December.

2666.q: What do people in Switzerland do to help kestrels breed?
a: They put up special nest boxes on barns and buildings
They build swimming pools for them
They put out sugar water for them
2666.e: Because kestrels do not build nests themselves, special nest boxes are often fixed to barns, towers or masts. This makes it easier for them to find a suitable place to breed.

2667.q: What do young foxes like doing to practise hunting?
a: Playing and play-fighting with each other
2667.e: Fox cubs love to tussle and play with each other outside the den. Along the way they practise important movements for hunting later.
2667.m: Play is practice for hunting later.

2668.q: What does the squirrel do with nuts and seeds in autumn?
a: It hides them as a winter store
It eats them all straight away
It sells them to other animals
It builds its nest out of them
2668.e: The squirrel buries nuts in many places and finds some of them again in winter. Some forgotten nuts grow into new trees.
2668.m: Squirrels store food for the winter.

2669.q: What does it mean when lions eat together and growl?
a: They show who owns which part of the prey
They are just playing for fun
2669.e: When eating together, lions sometimes growl to defend their place at the prey. This settles who gets how much.
2669.m: Growling settles the ranking while eating.

2670.q: What are a penguin’s young called?
2670.e: Young penguins are called chicks, just like the young of many other birds. At first they have fluffy grey feathers.

2671.q: How many eggs does a female cuckoo usually lay in another bird’s nest?
2671.e: The female cuckoo usually lays only one egg in each other bird’s nest. She spreads her other eggs over many different nests.
2671.m: One cuckoo egg per strange nest.

2672.q: Which animals are among the natural predators of the carrion crow?
a: larger birds of prey such as the goshawk
2672.e: Larger birds of prey such as the goshawk can be dangerous to adult carrion crows. Young birds and eggs are also at risk from other nest raiders.

2673.q: In which habitat does the stag beetle feel especially at home?
2673.e: It needs broadleaf woods with old oaks and lots of dead wood. There it finds food and places for its larvae.
2673.m: Stag beetles love old oak woods with lots of dead wood.

2674.q: Why is the green sea turtle called “green”?
a: Because of its greenish body fat
2674.e: The name comes from the greenish fat in the turtle’s body, not from the colour of its shell. In the past it was even made into soup, which gave it its German name “Suppenschildkröte”, meaning soup turtle.

2675.q: Where does the earwig most like to hide during the day?
a: In dark cracks under stones or bark
Out in the open on a sunny meadow
2675.e: Its flat body fits well into narrow cracks. There it is protected from enemies and from drying out.
2675.m: During the day it hides in narrow cracks.

2676.q: When did the okapi become known in Europe?
a: Already in the time of the ancient Romans
2676.e: The shy okapi lives hidden in the rainforest of the Congo. Only around 1900 did skins reach Europe and the animal was scientifically described.
2676.m: The okapi only became known in Europe around 1900.

2677.q: How can researchers often tell individual pandas apart?
a: By the pattern of their black patches
By the smell of their bamboo
By the size of their ears alone
By the sound of their footsteps
2677.e: Every panda has a slightly different pattern of black patches. This lets researchers recognise individual animals.
2677.m: Patch patterns help tell pandas apart.

2678.q: What happens when a cow is milked?
a: Milk is taken from its udder
2678.e: When milking, the milk is taken from the cow’s udder, either by hand or with a milking machine. This milk is then sold.
2678.m: Milking takes the milk from the udder.

2679.q: What is the pale grey patch behind an orca’s dorsal fin?
2679.e: Every orca has a pale saddle patch behind its dorsal fin. It looks a little different on each animal.
2679.m: The saddle patch is behind the fin.

2681.q: Which animals are among the blackbird’s enemies?
2681.e: Cats and birds of prey such as the sparrowhawk are dangerous enemies of the blackbird. Young birds are especially at risk.

2682.q: What does the anthill use the warmth of the sun for?
a: To keep the inside of the nest warm
2682.e: The dark surface of the mound absorbs the sun’s warmth. This warmth helps keep the inside of the nest warm.
2682.m: The mound stores the sun’s warmth.

2683.q: What does it usually mean when a budgie dozes calmly on one leg?
2683.e: A relaxed budgie often stands calmly on one leg and dozes. This shows that it feels safe and comfortable.

2684.q: How can you often tell Asian elephants from African elephants straight away?
2684.e: The ears of the Asian elephant are much smaller than those of the African elephant. This is an easy way to tell them apart.

2685.q: What is a mistaken belief about spotted hyenas?
2685.e: Spotted hyenas often hunt for themselves and catch a large part of their food actively. They only eat carrion on top of that.
2685.m: Spotted hyenas are also successful hunters.

2686.q: What is a proposal in a vote?
2686.e: A proposal is the issue that voters can say Yes or No to, for example a new law.
2686.m: A proposal is the subject of a vote.

2687.q: How are whitefish often prepared in the kitchen?
a: Only raw with the scales on
2687.e: Whitefish fillets, called Felchen in Switzerland, are often fried in a pan. Smoked whitefish is also popular.
2687.m: Whitefish fillets are fried or smoked.

2688.q: What are the African buffalo’s horns for?
2688.e: Buffalo use their horns to defend themselves against enemies. Bulls also use them to test their strength.
2688.m: Horns are for defence and testing strength.

2689.q: What is known about donkeys’ memory?
a: Donkeys have a very good memory
2689.e: Donkeys remember routes and familiar people for many years. They also recognise other animals they were friends with.

2690.q: When is the mating season of brown bears usually?
2690.e: Brown bears usually mate in May or June. Because of a delay in the process, the young only really start to develop in autumn.
2690.m: The bears’ mating season is in early summer.

2691.q: Which animals like to eat butterfly caterpillars?
2691.e: Many birds such as tits search for caterpillars in the garden. Caterpillars are an important, protein-rich food for them.

2692.q: Why is it important that there are several parties?
a: So that people can choose between different ideas.
So that there are more election posters.
So that everyone has the same opinion.
2692.e: Several parties offer different solutions to problems. That way the people can freely decide which idea they like best.
2692.m: Several parties give a real choice.

2693.q: What do armoured catfish from South America have on their bodies?
2693.e: Armoured catfish are covered with hard bony plates that protect them like armour. Their German name “Harnischwels” also comes from “Harnisch”, a knight’s armour.
2693.m: Armoured catfish wear armour of bony plates.

2694.q: What is the red, jagged thing on top of a chicken’s head called?
2694.e: The red comb sits on top of the head. In cockerels it is usually bigger and more striking than in hens.
2694.m: The comb sits on a chicken’s head.

2695.q: What do many people wrongly believe about the mole?
2695.e: Many gardeners think the mole destroys plants because it makes molehills. In fact it mainly eats worms and insects, not roots.

2696.q: How does the garden spider usually survive the winter as a species?
a: As eggs in a protected cocoon
As an adult in the middle of the snow
2696.e: Adult garden spiders usually die in winter. The cold season is survived as eggs in a cocoon spun to keep them warm.

2697.q: How many eggs does a female eagle owl usually lay in a clutch?
2697.e: A female eagle owl usually lays two to three eggs, sometimes more or fewer depending on how much food there is. The eggs are laid a few days apart.
2697.m: Eagle owls usually lay two to three eggs.

2698.e: Kangaroos really can swim well. When they are in danger they sometimes even escape into the water.

2699.q: Where does a stone marten most like to hide during the day?
2699.e: Stone martens rest in sheltered, dry places during the day. Lofts and barns protect them from enemies and bad weather.
2699.m: Lofts are popular marten hiding places.

2700.q: Which prey is especially often on the golden eagle’s menu in the Alps?
2700.e: In the Alps the golden eagle mainly hunts marmots, hares and other medium-sized mammals. Birds are sometimes also among its prey.
2700.m: Marmots are among its favourite prey.

2701.q: How long does a young koala usually stay with its mother?
2701.e: A young koala stays with its mother for about a year. After that it looks for its own home in the trees.
2701.m: Young koalas stay with their mother for around a year.

2702.q: What do newborn seahorses look like?
a: Like tiny mini versions of the adults
2702.e: Even at birth, baby seahorses look just like their parents, only much smaller. They have to look after themselves straight away.

2703.q: What body shape does the stone marten have that helps it slip through narrow gaps?
a: A body as round as a ball
2703.e: Its slim, long build lets the stone marten slip through very narrow openings and gaps. This way it easily gets into lofts and barns.
2703.m: A slim build helps it slip through.

2704.q: Which animal is the okapi most closely related to?
2704.e: Despite the zebra stripes on its legs, the okapi is the closest relative of the giraffe. Both have, for example, a long, dark tongue.
2704.m: The okapi is a relative of the giraffe.

2705.q: What are the GPS collars that scientists put on some wolves for?
a: To study their routes and territories
2705.e: With GPS transmitters researchers can track how far wolves travel and where they spend their time. This data helps plan how to protect the animals better.

2706.q: Which family do hyenas belong to?
a: Hyenas form their own family within the carnivores
They belong to the dog family
They belong to the cat family
They belong to the mustelid family
2706.e: Hyenas form the family Hyaenidae within the carnivores. They are more closely related to the cat-like carnivores than to dogs.
2706.m: Hyenas are a carnivore family of their own.

2707.q: What do dung beetles mainly feed on?
2707.e: Dung beetles look for the dung of animals such as cows, horses or sheep. In it they find food for themselves and their young.
2707.m: Dung beetles live on the dung of plant eaters.

2708.q: What tiny sacs make up the lungs, where gas exchange takes place?
2708.e: In the millions of air sacs, oxygen is taken into the blood. At the same time, carbon dioxide is released.
2708.m: Alveoli swap oxygen for carbon dioxide.

2709.q: What is the difference between the executive and the legislature?
a: The executive governs, the legislature makes laws
The executive makes laws, the legislature governs
Only the legislature exists in Switzerland
2709.e: The executive is the government, for example the Federal Council. The legislature is the parliament, which passes laws.
2709.m: The executive governs, the legislature makes laws.

2710.q: What do many millipedes do when they feel threatened?
a: They roll up into a spiral
2710.e: Many millipedes curl up. This protects their sensitive underside, and only the hard back is on the outside.

a: Money you get regularly from your parents to manage yourself
Money that may only be used for school
Money the bank gives you as a present
2711.e: Pocket money is money children get regularly and are allowed to manage themselves. This helps you learn early how to handle money.
2711.m: Learn to manage your pocket money yourself.

2712.q: Is the common frog protected in Switzerland?
a: Yes, it is protected by law
No, it can be caught anywhere
No, there is no law about it
2712.e: The common frog is protected in Switzerland because its habitat is getting smaller and smaller. You must not simply catch it or harm its spawn.
2712.m: The common frog is protected in Switzerland.

2713.q: What is special about an Alpine marmot’s front teeth?
a: They keep growing all its life
They fall out after a year and never grow back
It has no front teeth at all
They are as soft as rubber
2713.e: As in many rodents, marmots’ incisors keep growing throughout their lives. At the same time they are constantly worn down by gnawing on plants.

2714.q: What does a rhino’s skin feel like?
2714.e: A rhino’s skin is several centimetres thick and very tough. It protects the animal well from injuries.

2715.e: Wild boar are surprisingly good swimmers. They can even cross rivers or lakes.

2716.q: What is special about the dromedary’s body temperature?
a: It changes a lot during the day
It always stays exactly the same
2716.e: The animal lets its body get warmer during the day before it starts to sweat. This saves precious water.
2716.m: Body temperature changes to save water.

2717.q: At about what age is a red kite old enough to breed?
2717.e: Young red kites need a few years before they can breed themselves. Only at about 2 to 3 years old are they ready.
2717.m: Red kites can breed at 2 to 3 years.

2718.q: About how heavy can an adult male brown bear in Europe get?
2718.e: European male brown bears often weigh between 150 and 300 kilograms. But some subspecies in North America get much heavier.
2718.m: Male brown bears often weigh up to 300 kilograms.

2719.q: What do many millipedes of the double-legged kind do when they are threatened?
a: They roll up into a spiral
2719.e: Many of these millipedes, which have two pairs of legs on each body segment, curl up into a spiral. This protects their soft underside and their legs.

2720.q: What is special about a kangaroo’s front legs compared with its back legs?
a: They are much smaller and shorter
2720.e: Kangaroos’ front legs are short and small. The back legs, on the other hand, are very strong for hopping.

2721.q: How is the President of the Swiss Confederation chosen?
a: The Federal Assembly elects a member of the Federal Council for it every year
The people elect the president directly
The Federal Council is appointed by the UN
The president is chosen by the cantons
2721.e: Every year the Federal Assembly decides which member of the Federal Council will chair it for one year. That person still remains a member of the Federal Council with equal rights.
2721.m: The chair of the Federal Council changes every year.

2722.q: How often does the mother roe deer come to her hidden fawn to feed it?
a: Only a few times a day
All the time without a break
Never, the fawn looks for her itself
2722.e: The mother does not stay with the fawn all the time, because that could attract attention. She only comes by a few times a day to feed it with milk.
2722.m: The mother roe deer visits her fawn briefly.

2723.q: Why do you dress warmly in winter?
a: So that your body does not lose too much heat
So that your eyes see better
2723.e: Warm clothes keep your body heat in. That way you do not get cold so quickly.
2723.m: Warm clothes keep the heat in.

2724.q: Which mountain region do alpacas originally come from?
2724.e: Alpacas were bred in the Andes in countries such as Peru, Bolivia and Chile. There they live at high altitude.

2725.q: What does the Swiss foundation PanEco work for on Sumatra?
2725.e: PanEco, based in Switzerland, runs a programme on Sumatra to protect orangutans. Orphaned animals are cared for and released back into the wild.

2726.q: What does a sow build before her piglets are born?
a: A deep cave in the rock
2726.e: Before the birth the sow makes a soft nest of straw or other material. There her piglets are born safe and protected.
2726.m: Piglets are born in a soft nest.

2727.q: What does a cross next to ‘Yes’ on the ballot paper mean?
2727.e: If you tick Yes, you agree with the proposal. If you tick No, you reject it.

2728.q: How long does the female swan sit on her eggs?
2728.e: The female sits on the eggs for about five weeks. That is how long it takes until the cygnets hatch.
2728.m: Sitting on the eggs takes around five weeks.

2729.q: Why do geese usually live together in a group?
a: In a group they are safer from enemies
Because otherwise they are not allowed to eat
Because a single goose cannot honk
2729.e: In a larger group the animals notice more quickly when danger is near. This way they protect each other.
2729.m: Geese are safer in a group.

2730.q: How do bonobos often settle quarrels in the group?
a: With physical contact, comfort and affection
With loud fights until someone wins
2730.e: Bonobos often calm tensions with touching, hugs and affection. As a result, serious fights happen less often.

2731.q: About how many different kinds of bumblebee are there in Switzerland?
2731.e: Well over 40 different kinds of bumblebee live in Switzerland. They differ, for example, in size and fur pattern.
2731.m: There are many kinds of bumblebee in Switzerland.

2732.q: What is the unit of electric current called?
2732.e: Current tells you how much electric charge flows through a wire per second. The unit is named after the physicist André-Marie Ampère.

2733.q: How long does a mother giraffe carry her baby before it is born?
2733.e: Giraffes have a very long pregnancy of around fifteen months. That is much longer than in most other animals.
2733.m: Giraffe babies grow for about 15 months.

2734.q: On which continent do meerkats live in the wild?
2734.e: Meerkats live in southern Africa. They mainly live in dry, open landscapes.

2735.q: How does the wood mouse react to light?
a: It avoids bright light and hides
It is attracted to light like a moth
2735.e: As a night animal, the wood mouse avoids bright light and retreats to its burrow in daylight.
2735.m: It prefers to avoid bright light.

2736.q: What do some chimpanzees use to crack hard nuts?
2736.e: Some chimpanzees put a nut on a stone and hit it with another stone. This way they get to the tasty kernel.

2737.q: How old does a worker bumblebee usually get?
2737.e: Workers often live only a few weeks because their work is very tiring. The queen, on the other hand, lives much longer than the workers.
2737.m: Workers live only a few weeks.

2738.q: What kind of teeth does a horse have, because it chews so much?
a: Large grinding teeth that keep growing
Sharp tearing teeth like a cat’s
2738.e: Horses have large grinding teeth that they use to grind tough grass and hay well. These teeth wear down over time and keep growing.
2738.m: Horse teeth are made for grinding grass.

2739.q: What are a hedgehog’s ears like?
a: Hedgehogs have no ears at all
2739.e: The hedgehog’s ears are small and round and almost hidden in its fur and spines. Even so, it hears very well with them.

a: A canton uses it to ask the Confederation for a new law or a change to the constitution
A popular vote in a canton
An initiative only by young people
2740.e: With a cantonal initiative, a canton can make a proposal to the Confederation. Parliament then decides whether to take it up.
2740.m: A canton can make proposals with a cantonal initiative.

2741.q: Which group of animals do seahorses belong to?
2741.e: Seahorses live in water and breathe with gills, so they count as fish. They may look funny, but they are real fish.

2742.q: When is the adder’s mating season?
2742.e: After their winter rest the animals mate in spring. The males often fight each other with their bodies twisted together.
2742.m: Mating in spring after the winter rest.

2744.q: Does Parliament have to reply to the content of a petition that has been submitted?
a: No, there is no obligation, but it is often examined
2744.e: The right of petition only guarantees that a submission is received. A reply on the content or putting it into practice is not required by law.
2744.m: Petitions must be received but not answered.

2745.q: How do people in some countries protect fields from elephants?
2745.e: Elephants often eat plants in fields. Fences and ditches help reduce the damage.

2746.q: Where does the female woodlouse carry her eggs?
a: In a brood pouch on her belly
In a hole in the ground
In a cocoon on her back
2746.e: Under her body the female has a brood pouch filled with liquid. The eggs and the young develop there.
2746.m: Female woodlice carry their eggs on their belly.

2747.q: What colour are the barn owl’s eyes?
2747.e: Unlike many other owls, the barn owl has dark eyes. With them it can still see well when there is little light.

2748.q: Where does the name “earwig” probably come from?
a: People used to believe it crawled into ears at night
It makes noises like an ear
It has big ears on its head
2748.e: According to an old folk belief, the animals would crawl into the ears of sleeping people. But this is hardly ever true. The German name “Ohrwurm”, meaning “ear worm”, comes from the same belief.
2748.m: The name comes from an old folk belief.

2749.q: How are the snow leopard’s paws adapted to snow?
a: They are big and wide like snowshoes
2749.e: The wide, furry paws spread the weight across the snow. This way the animal sinks in less deeply and stays warm.
2749.m: Wide paws carry it like snowshoes.

2750.q: How do brown bears usually move about when they are not running?
2750.e: In everyday life brown bears usually move about at a leisurely, slow trot. Only when necessary, for example in danger or when hunting, do they briefly go much faster.
2750.m: Bears mostly trot about at a leisurely pace.

2751.q: What does the example of the carrion crow show about life in towns and cities?
a: it has adapted well to living near people
it disappears at once when people appear
it turns into a completely different bird in towns
2751.e: The carrion crow shows how well some birds can adapt to living near people. In parks and towns it finds plenty of food and suitable places to nest.
2751.m: Carrion crows live well in towns.

2752.q: What colour is an earthworm’s blood?
2752.e: An earthworm’s blood is red, just like in many other animals. You can sometimes see it shimmering through the skin.

2753.q: Which group of animals does the red fox belong to?
2753.e: Like the wolf and the pet dog, the red fox belongs to the dog family. Even so, it hunts more like a cat, quietly and secretly.
2753.m: The fox belongs to the dog family.

2754.q: What colour is the slow worm usually?
a: Brownish to grey, often with a metallic shine
2754.e: Its upper side is usually brown, grey or bronze-coloured and shiny. The underside is darker.
2754.m: Slow worms shine brownish like bronze.

2755.q: What do sand lizards often do in the morning before they become properly active?
a: They bask in the sun to warm up their bodies
They go straight to a pond
They dig a completely new hole
2755.e: Only after warming up in the sun for a while are they nimble enough to hunt or escape. That is why they often lie on warm stones in the morning.
2755.m: Sunbathing warms them up in the morning.

2756.q: What often happens when two strange cockerels meet?
a: They fall asleep side by side
2756.e: Strange cockerels often defend their territory and may quarrel or fight. Sometimes they use their spurs.

2757.q: What is a municipal office building?
a: The building where the municipality's administration works
2757.e: In the municipal office building, people work who look after things in the village or town. You can apply for a passport there, for example.
2757.m: The municipal administration works in the municipal office building.

2758.q: Which habitats does the edible frog need during its life?
2758.e: The edible frog is an amphibian and needs both water for breeding and swimming and land for finding food and sometimes for spending the winter. That is why amphibians are called amphibious.
2758.m: The edible frog needs water and land.

2759.q: About how old can wild eagle owls get?
2759.e: In the wild eagle owls can reach an age of around 20 years. In human care some animals live even much longer.
2759.m: Wild eagle owls live up to about 20 years.

2760.q: How many young does a female gibbon usually have at a time?
2760.e: As with great apes, usually a single baby is born. It is carried and cared for by its mother for a long time.
2760.m: Gibbons usually have only one baby.

2761.q: What are the snow leopard’s back legs like compared with its front legs?
2761.e: The strong back legs allow long leaps. This way it easily gets up steep slopes too.
2761.m: Strong back legs for long leaps.

2763.q: Why do seahorses have only a few natural enemies?
a: Their hard bony plates are hard to eat
2763.e: The hard bony rings in their bodies make it difficult for other animals to eat a seahorse. This protects them from many predators.

2764.q: What importance do adders have for nature?
a: They keep mouse numbers in check
They loosen the soil like earthworms
2764.e: As hunters they keep the number of small rodents in balance. At the same time they are food for other animals.

2765.q: How can advertising influence the way you spend money?
a: It can create wants that lead to spontaneous, unplanned purchases
Advertising has no effect on purchases
Advertising only informs about legal rules
2765.e: Advertising is designed to create wants and encourage you to buy, even if you do not really need the product. Thinking critically helps you stick to your budget.

2766.q: How does the white stork differ from the black stork?
a: the white stork has white feathers, the black stork black ones
the black stork is much smaller
2766.e: The white stork is mainly white, while the black stork has dark feathers. But both belong to the same bird family.
2766.m: White or black, two kinds of stork.

2767.q: Which fish family does the goldfish belong to?
2767.e: The goldfish belongs to the carp family, just like the carp. It is related to many other freshwater fish.
2767.m: Goldfish belong to the carp family.

2768.q: How does a carp cope when there is little oxygen in the water?
a: Much worse than all other fish
It swims to another lake at once
2768.e: The carp is a very hardy fish. It copes with little oxygen in the water better than many other kinds of fish.
2768.m: Carp cope well with little oxygen.

2769.q: What can the colours of an adult slow worm sometimes tell you about whether it is male or female?
a: Males are often more plain, females have dark sides and a back stripe
2769.e: Females often have a dark stripe along the back and dark sides. Males are usually more plain, and some have blue spots.
2769.m: Females often show a dark back stripe.

2770.q: How many humps does a Bactrian camel have?
2770.e: The Bactrian camel has two humps, the dromedary only one. It stores fat in its humps as an energy reserve.
2770.m: The Bactrian camel has two humps, the dromedary only one.

2772.q: How do common buzzards defend their territory against other buzzards?
a: With loud calls and threatening flights
By barking loudly like a dog
By hiding in a hole in the ground
2772.e: If a strange buzzard enters a territory that is taken, the owners react with loud calls and impressive flying moves. This usually drives the intruder away.
2772.m: Calls and flights defend the territory.

2773.q: What does the great tit have on its head?
2773.e: The great tit’s head is glossy black, almost like a cap. It has large white patches on its cheeks.
2773.m: The great tit wears a black cap.

2774.q: What do dolphins sometimes do with air in the water to play?
a: They blow rings of air and play with them
They make balloons out of seaweed
2774.e: Some dolphins blow small rings of air under water through their blowhole. Then they play with them and swim through them.
2774.m: Dolphins play with air rings in the water.

2775.q: When does the grass snake become active again in spring?
a: When it gets warmer, usually in March or April
Already in the middle of January in frost
2775.e: As soon as the sun warms the ground, it leaves its winter quarters. Then the mating season also begins.
2775.m: In spring it wakes up with the warmth.

a: An object with such strong gravity that not even light can escape
A hole in the Earth’s atmosphere
2776.e: A black hole often forms when a very massive star collapses in on itself at the end of its life. Its pull is so strong that not even light can escape it.
2776.m: Black holes let no light escape.

2777.q: What important role does the carrion crow play in the ecosystem?
a: it eats carrion and so helps clean up nature
it pollinates flowers like a bee
it builds dams like a beaver
it cleans rivers and lakes like a fish
2777.e: As an omnivore, the carrion crow also eats carrion and so helps get rid of dead animals naturally. This makes it a kind of natural health patrol.

2778.q: What is the group of animals that alpacas belong to called?
2778.e: Alpacas belong to the camel family, the camelids. This family also includes llamas, vicuñas and guanacos.

2779.q: What does it mean to buy something on credit or in instalments?
a: You pay for the product in several parts over time, often with extra costs
You pay the full price in cash straight away
You get the product as a present
You swap it for another product
2779.e: When paying in instalments, you do not pay everything at once but in parts. There are often extra costs or interest, which makes the product more expensive in the end.
2779.m: Paying in instalments can cost more.

2780.q: Which well-known Swiss breed of chicken has a striking crest of feathers?
2780.e: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben is an old Swiss breed of chicken with a striking crest of feathers on its head. Both the cockerels and the hens of this breed have this crest.
2780.m: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben is a Swiss breed.

2781.q: What is important for a horse to feel comfortable in its stable?
a: Lots of peace and quiet all alone
As little time outside as possible
2781.e: Horses need both exercise and contact with other horses to feel comfortable. So a stable should offer space and company.

2782.q: How endangered is the African wild dog according to the IUCN Red List?
a: It is only known in zoos
2782.e: The IUCN classes it as “endangered”. There are only a few thousand animals left.
2782.m: The African wild dog is endangered.

2783.q: Which part of its body does the cuckoo chick use to push the other eggs out of the nest?
2783.e: The cuckoo chick has a small hollow on its back. It loads eggs or small chicks into it and tips them over the edge of the nest.
2783.m: The cuckoo throws eggs out with its back.

2784.q: What is the dark patch behind the common frog’s eye?
2784.e: Behind its eye the common frog has a dark patch, called the temple patch. This makes it easy to recognise.
2784.m: The temple patch is a feature you can recognise it by.

2785.q: Apart from mussels, what else does a starfish eat?
2785.e: As well as mussels, starfish also eat snails, worms and other small animals on the sea floor.
2785.m: Starfish eat small animals on the sea floor.

2786.q: How long does a young brown bear normally stay with its mother?
2786.e: Young brown bears usually stay with their mother for two to three years. During this time they learn where to find food and how to protect themselves from danger.
2786.m: Bear cubs stay with their mother for up to three years.

2787.q: Roughly how often a year can Swiss people go to the polls?
2787.e: In Switzerland there are usually four voting dates a year. People can then decide on various questions.
2787.m: There are usually four voting dates a year.

2788.q: In which parts of Europe is the stone marten widespread?
a: Only in the far north of Scandinavia
Only on a few Mediterranean islands
2788.e: The stone marten is common mainly in central and southern Europe. In northern Europe, on the other hand, it is rarer or missing completely.
2788.m: Central and southern Europe are stone marten areas.

2789.q: Where do some horses in Switzerland spend the summer?
a: On an alp in the mountains
In a stable in the city
In a cave in the forest
2789.e: Some horses spend the summer on an alp, a mountain pasture. This is called summering. In autumn they come back down to the valley.
2789.m: In summer some horses are up on the alp.

2790.q: Which two main routes do European storks use for their flight to Africa?
a: a western route over Spain and an eastern route over the Bosporus
a route over the North Pole
2790.e: Many storks fly to Africa either over Spain and Gibraltar or over Turkey and the Middle East. Both routes avoid long flights over open sea.
2790.m: Two main routes lead to Africa.

2791.q: What does the wasp do once it has collected enough wood to build its nest?
a: It chews it with saliva into a paper pulp
It hides it in the ground
2791.e: The wasp mixes scraped-off wood with its saliva. From this it forms thin layers of paper for the nest.
2791.m: Wood is turned into nest paper.

2792.q: How is the wild Bactrian camel listed on the Red List?
2792.e: Only a few thousand wild Bactrian camels are still alive. That is why the species is considered critically endangered.
2792.m: Wild Bactrian camels are critically endangered.

2793.q: In which country is there a famous ancient forest with European bison, the Białowieża Forest?
2793.e: The ancient Białowieża Forest lies on the border between Poland and Belarus. European bison live wild here.
2793.m: Białowieża in Poland is home to European bison.

2794.q: What is the area called in which a pair of great tits breeds and looks for food?
2794.e: The area a pair of great tits defends and looks for food in is called its territory. Other great tits are kept out of it.
2794.m: The breeding area is called a territory.

2795.q: What do chimpanzees like doing to show friendship?
2795.e: Chimpanzees clean each other’s fur. This is called grooming and it strengthens friendships in the group.

2796.q: How heavy can a koala get?
2796.e: Depending on where a koala lives, it can weigh between about 4 and 15 kilograms. Koalas in southern Australia are usually heavier.

2797.q: How many wings does a wasp have?
2797.e: A wasp has two pairs of wings, so four wings altogether. With them it can fly fast and nimbly.

2798.q: What do newborn moles look like?
a: Just like little mice with tails
2798.e: Young moles are born without fur and with their eyes closed. Only after a few weeks do they grow fur and get stronger.

2799.q: About what percentage of a jellyfish’s body is water?
2799.e: A jellyfish’s body is about 95 per cent water. That is why it is so see-through and light.
2799.m: A jellyfish is made almost entirely of water.

2800.q: How can you often tell a male great tit from a female?
a: The black belly stripe is wider
Females have no tail at all
2800.e: Male great tits usually have a wider black stripe that runs all the way down the belly. In females it is often narrower and sometimes broken.
2800.m: Males have a wider belly stripe.

2801.q: Which well-known animal does the edible dormouse look like with its bushy tail?
2801.e: With its bushy tail the edible dormouse looks a lot like a squirrel. However, it is smaller and active at night.
2801.m: Its bushy tail is like a squirrel’s.

2802.q: What is one advantage when whitefish swim in shoals?
a: They are better protected from enemies
2802.e: In a shoal it is harder for predatory fish to catch a single fish. And many eyes notice danger more quickly.

2803.q: How does the pike move when it sets off to hunt?
a: It speeds up in a flash with its tail fin
It always swims slowly and calmly
It hops to the bank like a frog
2803.e: The pike’s powerful tail fin allows a lightning-fast start. This way it surprises its prey before it can escape.
2803.m: Its tail fin drives the pike at lightning speed.

2804.q: About how many hours does a koala sleep each day?
2804.e: Koalas sleep a great deal, often up to 20 hours a day. This is because their food provides little energy.

2805.q: What sound do alpacas often make when they are content?
2805.e: Alpacas often hum, for example when they are relaxed or curious. Humming is their typical sound.

2806.q: What happens if a wool sheep is never sheared?
a: The wool keeps growing and gets too thick
The wool becomes as hard as bristles
2806.e: If a wool sheep is not sheared, the wool keeps growing and becomes very thick and heavy. This can make the sheep too hot, especially in summer.

a: The larva of beetles such as the cockchafer
2807.e: White grubs are fat, pale larvae with three pairs of legs. They live in the soil and eat roots.
2807.m: White grubs are beetle larvae in the soil.

2808.q: Which animal family does the badger belong to?
2808.e: The badger belongs to the mustelids, just like the stoat or the otter. It is even the largest mustelid in Switzerland.
2808.m: The badger is a large mustelid.

2809.q: What are the little bits that sparrows in towns like to peck up called?
2809.e: In towns sparrows like to peck up breadcrumbs that people drop. But natural food such as grain is better for them.

2810.q: Why had ibex almost died out in the Alps?
a: Because they were heavily hunted for their meat and supposed healing powers
Because they ran out of food
Because they suffered from a disease that killed all the animals
Because they moved to warmer countries
2810.e: In the 19th century ibex were hunted so heavily that they almost completely disappeared from the Alps. People believed that various parts of their bodies had healing effects.
2810.m: Hunting almost wiped out the ibex.

2811.q: About how big is a common swift’s wingspan?
2811.e: Despite its small body, the swift has relatively long wings. This wingspan allows it to fly fast for a long time.

2812.q: What especially attracts mosquitoes to our bodies?
2812.e: Sweat contains scents that mosquitoes can smell especially well. That is why some people get bitten more often than others.
2812.m: The smell of sweat attracts mosquitoes.

2813.q: What is the area in which a single brown bear lives and hunts called?
2813.e: The area a brown bear uses for its daily search for food is called its home range. Male bears usually have a bigger home range than females.
2813.m: Every bear has its own home range.

2814.q: What role do buffalo play in the ecosystem?
a: They keep the grass short and are prey for predators
2814.e: By grazing they change the plant life. They are also important food for lions and other hunters.

2815.q: How do young tawny owls move about before they can fly properly?
a: They climb from branch to branch with beak and claws
They jump over the ground like kangaroos
They sit motionless in the nest
2815.e: Even before they can fly, young tawny owls often leave the nest hole and climb about skilfully with their beak and claws. This way they already explore their surroundings.
2815.m: Young tawny owls are skilful climbers.

2816.q: Which nutrients does salmon especially provide for people?
2816.e: Salmon is an oily fish with omega-3 fatty acids. These are considered good for the heart and brain.

2817.q: According to many stories, what do dolphins often do to help people in trouble?
a: They sometimes guide swimmers to the surface
They carry post to other islands
2817.e: There are many stories in which dolphins are said to have helped swimmers. Dolphins are curious and friendly animals that often seek contact with people.
2817.m: Dolphins are thought to be friendly to people.

2818.q: From when can young hedgehogs look after themselves?
a: They stay with their mother all their lives
2818.e: After about six to eight weeks young hedgehogs are independent enough to look for food on their own. Then they leave their mother and live alone.
2818.m: After a few weeks young hedgehogs are independent.

a: An organisation that connects the police forces of different countries
2819.e: Interpol helps police forces from different countries work together, for example when searching for criminals across borders. Its headquarters are in France.
2819.m: Interpol connects police forces around the world.

2821.q: Why do giraffes have to spread their legs wide when drinking?
a: Because otherwise their neck doesn’t reach the water
2821.e: Although the giraffe’s neck is very long, on its own it does not reach the ground. That is why the giraffe has to spread its front legs wide apart when drinking.
2821.m: Giraffes spread their legs to drink.

2822.q: Do male and female carrion crows look very different?
a: yes, only the male is black
yes, only the female has a beak
yes, the female is brightly coloured
2822.e: In carrion crows, males and females look very alike, with little difference on the outside. Often, however, the male is a little bigger than the female.
2822.m: Males and females look very alike.

2823.q: What is one use of the Alpine marmot’s bushy tail?
2823.e: The thick tail helps the marmot keep its balance and protects it a little from the cold. When sitting, it sometimes wraps it around its body for protection.
2823.m: The bushy tail keeps it a little warm.

2824.q: What does the green woodpecker love to eat?
2824.e: The green woodpecker pokes into anthills with its long tongue. Ants are one of its favourite foods.
2824.m: The green woodpecker loves eating ants.

2825.q: What does a penguin use to move through the water?
a: Its wings, which work like flippers
2825.e: A penguin’s wings are stiff and flat like paddles. This lets it move very quickly and skilfully under water.
2825.m: Penguin wings are flippers for swimming.

a: An office of a country abroad
2826.e: A consulate is an office of a country abroad. It helps, for example, if someone has lost their passport.

2827.q: What is the sound a stork makes with its beak called?
2827.e: Storks clatter their beaks because they cannot sing. They also greet each other at the nest this way.

2828.q: How do researchers often study snow leopards, because they are so shy?
2828.e: Camera traps automatically take pictures when an animal passes by. This way animals can be counted without disturbing them.

2829.q: What does a gorilla have on its hand, like a human?
2829.e: The opposable thumb helps the gorilla grip things well. With it, it can pick fruit, for example.
2829.m: Gorillas have a thumb for gripping.

2831.q: What colour is an elk’s fur usually?
2831.e: The fur is usually dark. The legs are often lighter.

2832.q: What sound does a cheetah make?
a: It roars loudly like a lion
2832.e: Cheetahs cannot roar. Instead they make chirping sounds that sound almost like bird calls.

2833.q: How big can an adult male polar bear get?
2833.e: Male polar bears can grow over two metres long. This makes them one of the largest predators on land.
2833.m: Male polar bears grow very big.

2834.q: What is one of the main dangers for the jaguar?
a: Too many enemies in the forest
Too few trees in the zoo
2834.e: The rainforest is being cleared to make pastures and fields. As a result the jaguar loses hunting grounds.

2835.q: What do wild boar sometimes eat even though it isn’t plant food?
2835.e: Wild boar are omnivores and also like worms, insects or small animals. This way they always find enough to eat.
2835.m: Wild boar also eat small animals.

2836.q: How do chimpanzees often communicate over long distances in the forest?
2836.e: Chimpanzees give loud calls so that other group members can hear them even far away. This way they stay in contact.

2837.q: Where do common buzzards usually build their nest?
a: High in a tree at the edge of a wood
On the ground in the middle of a meadow
On the bottom of a lake
2837.e: Common buzzards usually build their nest high up in an old tree, often at the edge of a wood. From there they have a good view over their hunting ground.
2837.m: The nest is high up in a tree.

2838.q: Do some kinds of shark have to keep swimming all the time to get enough oxygen?
a: Yes, otherwise they get too little oxygen
No, they can always lie still
No, they breathe through their skin
2838.e: In some sharks fresh water always has to flow over the gills. That is why they swim practically without stopping.
2838.m: Some sharks must always keep moving.

2839.q: How long does a harbour seal pup drink milk from its mother?
2839.e: The mother seal’s milk is very rich in fat, so the pup grows very quickly. After just three to four weeks it has to catch fish itself.
2839.m: Harbour seal pups drink milk only for a short time.

2840.q: What does a carrion crow usually build its nest from?
2840.e: The carrion crow’s nest is a rough frame of branches and twigs, lined inside with softer material such as grass or moss. It is usually built high up in a tree.
2840.m: Crows’ nests are made of twigs and branches.

2841.q: In which habitats can a leopard be found?
2841.e: Leopards are very adaptable. They live in savannahs, forests, mountains and sometimes even close to cities.

2842.q: What does a starfish use to move?
2842.e: Under its body the starfish has hundreds of tiny tube feet. With them it crawls very slowly over the sea floor.

2843.q: When is the lynx’s mating season?
a: In late winter, about February to March
In the middle of high summer
Equally often at any time of year
2843.e: During the mating season in late winter, lynx actively look for partners. They call to each other loudly, which otherwise rarely happens.
2843.m: In late winter lynx look for partners.

2844.q: How many horns does the male minotaur beetle typically have on the front of its body?
2844.e: Two side horns and a middle horn look like a bull’s head. That is where its German name “Stierkäfer”, meaning bull beetle, comes from.
2844.m: The male minotaur beetle has three horns.

2845.e: Kangaroos usually live together in groups. This makes them safer from enemies, because many eyes see more.

2846.q: What does a sheep like to eat most?
2846.e: Sheep like eating grass and herbs in the meadow best. They spend a lot of time grazing in the pasture.

2847.q: What is a female elk called?
2847.e: The females are called cows. They do not have antlers.

2848.q: Which kind of plant makes up most of the panda’s habitat?
2848.e: Pandas live in forests where a lot of bamboo grows. Without enough bamboo they cannot survive.
2848.m: Bamboo forests are the pandas’ home.

2849.q: What are whitefish mainly caught for in Switzerland?
2849.e: Whitefish are among the important food fish in Swiss lakes. Their flesh is pale and mild in taste.
2849.m: Whitefish are a popular food fish.

2850.q: About how long can a female European eel grow?
2850.e: Females grow much bigger than males and can be over a metre long. Males usually stay under 60 centimetres.
2850.m: Female eels are bigger than males.

2851.q: About how heavy can an adult African elephant get?
2851.e: The African elephant is the heaviest land animal on Earth. An adult male can weigh as much as several cars put together.
2851.m: Elephants are huge and very heavy.

2852.q: What sound does a bee make when it flies?
2852.e: The buzzing happens because the bee moves its wings up and down very fast. You can hear bees buzzing from far away.

2853.q: Is the roe deer a common wild animal in Switzerland?
a: Yes, it is one of the most common wild animals
No, there are hardly any roe deer left
It only appears once a year
2853.e: The roe deer is one of the most common wild hoofed animals in Switzerland. You can see it in many woods and fields.
2853.m: Roe deer are very common in Switzerland.

2854.q: What is the group of animals the elephant belongs to called?
2854.e: Elephants give birth to live young and feed them with milk. That is typical of mammals.

2855.q: Why is the praying mantis called that?
a: Because its folded front legs look like praying hands
Because it only hunts on Sundays
2855.e: The praying mantis holds its grasping legs bent in front of its body. It looks as if it were folding its hands in prayer.
2855.m: Folded front legs look like someone praying.

2856.q: What do you call an animal that mainly lives alone?
2856.e: The puma is a typical loner. It usually meets other pumas only to mate.

2857.q: How does a lynx typically hunt its prey?
a: It creeps up and surprises it with a short leap
It always hunts in a pack
It lies in wait at watering holes for days
2857.e: Lynx are stalking hunters. They creep up silently and surprise their prey with a short, powerful leap.

2858.q: How does the Alpine salamander usually move?
2858.e: The Alpine salamander is not a fast hunter but moves along the ground at a leisurely pace. It relies more on hiding and its poison than on running away.

2860.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker’s call often sound like?
2860.e: As well as drumming, the great spotted woodpecker also gives a short, sharp call. This is how it communicates with other woodpeckers.

2861.q: In which season do most flowers in Switzerland bloom for the first time?
2861.e: In spring it gets warmer and lighter. Many plants wake up from their winter rest and start to bloom.
2861.m: In spring the plants wake up.

2862.q: How far does a blue shark swim on its travels?
a: Thousands of kilometres through the sea
Not at all, it always stays in the same place
2862.e: The blue shark often roams far across the open sea and even crosses whole oceans. Its name comes from its blue colour.
2862.m: The blue shark travels far across the open sea.

2863.q: About how much milk does a blue whale calf drink a day?
2863.e: A blue whale calf drinks huge amounts of rich, fatty milk from its mother. This makes it grow very quickly.
2863.m: Whale calves drink huge amounts of milk.

2864.q: About how many eggs does a hen lay in a year?
2864.e: Laying hens often lay an egg almost every day. Over the whole year that adds up to over 200 eggs.
2864.m: Hens lay lots of eggs a year.

2865.q: Why do meerkats have several entrances to their burrow?
a: So that they can escape quickly when in danger
So that more rain flows in
So that enemies can get in more easily
2865.e: Several entrances give quick escape routes. They also let air move through the burrow.
2865.m: More entrances mean more escape routes.

2866.q: Apart from its pincers, how else can the earwig defend itself?
a: With a sting on its head
2866.e: It can release a liquid from glands on its back end. It smells unpleasant and scares off some enemies.
2866.m: Glands on its body release a defensive liquid.

2867.q: What does the carrion crow’s typical call sound most like?
2867.e: Carrion crows typically call with a rough, croaking “caw caw”. This call can be heard far away and also helps them communicate in a flock.
2867.m: Carrion crows croak a loud “caw caw”.

2868.q: When are striped hyenas usually active?
2868.e: Striped hyenas are nocturnal. During the day they usually rest in caves or hiding places.

2869.q: What is the easiest way to tell a drake from a female mallard?
a: By the male’s brilliant green head
You can never tell them apart
By the size of its feet
2869.e: The shiny green head is the most striking feature of the male. The female, on the other hand, stays a plain brown.
2869.m: The green head shows it’s the male.

2870.q: How does a great tit behave when it discovers a bird table for the first time?
a: It approaches carefully and watches first
It dives straight at it without thinking
It flies far away again at once
It calls all the other animals over loudly
2870.e: Great tits are cautious birds. They first watch a new feeding place from close by before they dare to fly to it.
2870.m: Great tits approach new food carefully.

2871.q: What shape are the cells in a honeycomb?
2871.e: The six-sided cells fit together perfectly and save space and wax. This makes bees especially clever builders.

2872.q: What do wasp larvae in the nest get to eat?
2872.e: The workers catch insects and chew them into a mash. They feed this mash to the larvae.

2873.q: What does the term “resident bird” mean, compared with a migratory bird?
a: It stays in its area all year round
It travels far away every year
2873.e: Resident birds such as the blackbird or the sparrow stay in their home area all year and do not fly south. They have to cope with cold and lack of food in winter too.

2874.q: What do male bumblebees (drones) mainly do?
a: They collect most of the nectar
They guard the nest with their sting
2874.e: Male bumblebees, also called drones, do not help with collecting or building. Their job is to mate with young queens.

2875.q: What happens when the grass snake gets too cold?
2875.e: Its body processes slow down a lot in the cold. It then hardly moves at all.

2876.q: Can woodlice sting or bite people?
a: No, they are harmless to people
Yes, they spread dangerous diseases by biting
2876.e: Woodlice have neither a sting nor poison. They are harmless to people.

2877.q: What is the most striking feature of a male lion?
2877.e: The male lion has a thick mane around his head and neck. It makes him look bigger and more impressive.
2877.m: The mane belongs to the male lion.

2878.q: What does the adult lake trout mainly feed on?
2878.e: Large lake trout hunt other fish, for example whitefish or perch. That is why they are called predatory fish.
2878.m: Adult lake trout mainly eat fish.

2879.q: How many parts is a butterfly’s body made of?
2879.e: Like all insects, the butterfly has a body with three sections. The legs and wings are attached to the thorax.

2880.q: Where are a large part of the octopus’s nerve cells?
2880.e: In the octopus very many nerve cells are right in the arms. This lets the arms feel and grip almost on their own.
2880.m: Octopus arms almost think for themselves.

2881.q: Which fungal disease is a serious threat to fire salamander populations in Europe?
2881.e: The skin fungus Batrachochytrium salamandrivorans, Bsal for short, destroys the animals’ skin and can wipe out whole populations. It was probably brought in from Asia.
2881.m: Bsal is a serious danger to fire salamanders.

2882.q: What can a butterfly use to taste whether a flower is sweet?
2882.e: The butterfly has tiny taste cells on its feet. As soon as it lands, it can tell whether there is nectar.

2883.q: Does the blue whale have a dorsal fin?
a: Yes, but a rather small one
Yes, a huge one like a sail
2883.e: Compared with its huge body, the blue whale’s dorsal fin is rather small. You often see it when the whale dives briefly.
2883.m: Its dorsal fin is rather small.

2884.q: What do Alpine newts often do during the day when they live on land?
a: They hide under stones or wood
They swim in the open sea
2884.e: During the day the Alpine newt likes to retreat to damp, sheltered places such as under stones or dead wood. It usually only becomes active at dusk.
2884.m: The Alpine newt likes to hide during the day.

2885.q: Which animal is one of the hedgehog’s natural enemies?
2885.e: Foxes, badgers and large owls can be dangerous to a hedgehog. But adult hedgehogs are well protected by their spines.
2885.m: Foxes and badgers sometimes hunt hedgehogs.

2886.q: What sounds does a least weasel make?
2886.e: Least weasels communicate with short, high sounds, especially when they feel threatened or are quarrelling. These sounds are usually quiet and easy to miss.

2887.q: What is a baby donkey called?
2887.e: A young donkey is called a foal, just like a baby horse. It stays with its mother for a long time.
2887.m: A baby donkey is called a foal.

2888.q: What does the abbreviation “EU” stand for?
2888.e: The EU is a group of countries in Europe. They work together on issues such as trade, the environment and travel.

2889.q: Why is the European pond turtle called that?
a: It lives in marshes, ponds and calm waters
It lives only in the sea off Europe
It was discovered in a swamp in America
2889.e: The pond turtle lives in calm waters with a muddy bottom, such as ponds and marshes. It is the only native turtle in Switzerland.
2889.m: Pond turtles live in calm waters.

2890.q: Which part of the kangaroo’s body is especially big?
2890.e: Kangaroos have very big back feet. That is why scientists call their family the macropods, which means “big feet”.

2891.q: What does the law of the lever say, put simply?
a: Effort times effort arm equals load times load arm
The shorter the lever, the less force you need
2891.e: With a lever: the longer the effort arm compared with the load arm, the less force you need to use. That is why long seesaws are easier to work than short ones.
2891.m: A long lever arm saves force.

2892.q: How do many songbirds react when a kestrel flies nearby?
a: They warn each other with alarm calls or hide
They fly straight at the kestrel to greet it
They build a nest together with it
They stay completely calm, as the kestrel is no danger to them
2892.e: Even though the kestrel mainly hunts mice, it sometimes catches small birds. That is why many songbirds give alarm calls or look for cover when a kestrel appears.
2892.m: Songbirds warn each other about the kestrel.

2893.q: Is the tawny owl a migratory bird, or does it usually stay in its territory all year?
a: It is a resident bird and stays in its territory
It flies to Africa every winter
It moves to the mountains only in summer
2893.e: The tawny owl does not normally fly to warm countries but stays in its territory all year round. Only in very harsh weather may it move short distances.
2893.m: The tawny owl stays in its territory as a resident bird.

2894.q: Who usually looks after a young koala on their own?
2894.e: With koalas, almost always only the mother looks after the young. She carries it in her pouch and later piggyback on her back.
2894.m: The koala mother raises the young alone.

2895.q: What happens to the forest when wild boar root through it?
2895.e: When wild boar dig through the ground, the soil is loosened. This can even be good for new plants.

2896.q: What is the opposite of a dictatorship?
2896.e: In a democracy the people have a say in who governs. That is the opposite of a dictatorship, where one person decides alone.
2896.m: Democracy is the opposite of dictatorship.

2897.q: How are groups of male alpacas often kept?
a: In a separate group from the females
Always together with all the females
2897.e: Males are usually kept separately from the females. This means less fighting and no unwanted breeding.
2897.m: Males often live in their own group.

2898.q: What does the common buzzard use to grab and kill its prey?
2898.e: Common buzzards grab their prey with strong, sharp claws called talons. These powerful feet are an important weapon when hunting.

2899.q: What do studies show about how dogs react to people’s facial expressions?
a: Dogs can recognise human facial expressions and react to them
Dogs only react to loud noises
2899.e: Research shows that dogs can tell human emotions apart from facial expressions. This is thought to be the result of humans and dogs developing together over a long time.

2900.q: What is an election ballot paper?
a: A paper on which you tick names for an election
2900.e: The election ballot paper lists the names of people or parties. You tick who you want to elect.
2900.m: On the election ballot paper you choose people.

a: A very cold continent at the South Pole
A warm continent at the equator
An ocean near the North Pole
2901.e: Antarctica lies at the Earth’s South Pole and is mostly covered with thick ice. It is almost always very cold there.
2901.m: Antarctica is at the South Pole and is freezing cold.

2902.q: About how old can a white stork get?
2902.e: White storks can live up to twenty years in the wild. That is quite old for a bird.

2903.q: What does the term ‘Dirty War’ refer to in Argentina?
a: The persecution and murder of supposed opponents of the government by the military dictatorship
The Falklands War against Great Britain
A civil war between Peronists and Radicals
2903.e: During the Argentine military dictatorship from 1976 to 1983, thousands of people were arrested, tortured and killed in the ‘Dirty War’. Many of the victims, the ‘disappeared’, were never found.
2903.m: The Dirty War claimed thousands of victims.

2905.q: How old can pond turtles get?
2905.e: Pond turtles live slowly and can get very old. That is why protecting adult animals is especially important.
2905.m: Pond turtles live for many decades.

2906.q: Why does the koala have rather little energy and often move slowly?
a: Because eucalyptus leaves provide few nutrients
Because it is too heavy to walk
2906.e: Eucalyptus leaves are hard to digest and provide only a little energy. That is why the koala saves strength by sleeping a lot and keeping still.

2907.q: About how many toes does an elephant have on each foot?
a: Five, but not all of them can be seen
2907.e: Elephants have five toes on each foot, but they are hidden inside the thick foot. From the outside you usually see only large, round nails.

2908.q: What is it called when people carry common toads safely across the road in buckets?
a: Toad patrol during the toad migration
2908.e: In spring volunteers put buckets along toad fences. This way they help the animals cross roads safely.
2908.m: Volunteers carry toads across the road.

2909.q: In which habitats are otters typically found?
2909.e: Otters need clean water with enough fish and hiding places on the bank. That is why they live by rivers, lakes or even on coasts.
2909.m: Otters live by rivers, lakes and coasts.

2910.q: What is special about cats’ hearing compared with humans’?
a: Cats hear much higher frequencies than humans
2910.e: Cats can hear sounds at much higher frequencies than humans, for example the faint squeaks of mice. This makes them very good hunters.
2910.m: Cats hear much higher frequencies than we do.

2912.q: What else is the squirrel’s tail used for when it sleeps?
a: As a pillow for other animals
2912.e: When a squirrel sleeps, it often wraps its bushy tail around itself. This keeps it nice and warm.
2912.m: The tail is also used as a blanket.

2913.q: What do you call a song you can’t get out of your head?
2913.e: A catchy piece of music that you keep humming is called an “earworm” in everyday speech. The word comes from German, where “Ohrwurm” is also the name of the earwig.
2913.m: Catchy songs are also called earworms.

2914.q: On which river does the old Landhaus in the town of Solothurn stand?
2914.e: The Landhaus is an old building right on the bank of the Aare. In the past, goods from the boats were stored there; today it hosts parties and concerts.
2914.m: The Landhaus in Solothurn stands on the Aare.

2915.q: What does the Roman snail do before it mates?
a: It performs a special courtship ritual
It builds a nest of twigs
2915.e: Before mating, two Roman snails touch each other with their feelers for a long time. This ritual can last several hours.
2915.m: There is a ritual before mating.

2916.q: How many piglets does a mother pig (sow) usually have at once?
2916.e: A sow often has eight to twelve piglets in a litter. That is why she has many teats, so that all the piglets can drink.
2916.m: A sow has lots of piglets at once.

2917.q: Does the puma normally live in a pack?
a: Yes, in large packs of over 20 animals
2917.e: Pumas are loners. Only mothers with young, and pairs during the mating season, are together.

2918.q: What does a llama often do when its load is too heavy?
2918.e: Llamas refuse to work when they are overloaded. They simply lie down and won’t get up again.

2920.q: About how long do most jellyfish live?
a: A few months to about a year
2920.e: Most jellyfish live only a few months to about a year. Then they die and new jellyfish grow up.
2920.m: Jellyfish usually live only a few months.

2921.q: Apart from fish, what does the otter sometimes eat?
2921.e: As well as fish, the otter sometimes catches frogs, crayfish or small water birds. This way it can eat whatever is available.
2921.m: Otters also eat frogs and crayfish.

2923.q: Which animal is closely related to the African buffalo?
2923.e: Buffalo and domestic cattle belong to the same family, the bovids. But they are different species.

2924.q: Which birds like eating aphids in the garden?
2924.e: Tits search twigs for small insects, and aphids are among them. They are especially important when raising their young.
2924.m: Tits help fight aphids in the garden.

2925.q: How many legs does a pond skater have?
2925.e: Like all insects, the pond skater has six legs. Spiders, on the other hand, have eight.

2926.q: Why are millipedes usually active at night?
a: At night it is damper and cooler, so they dry out less
During the day they sleep in water
They are afraid of loud noises
2926.e: In the dark the air is damper. They are also safer from many enemies at night.
2926.m: At night it is damper and safer.

2927.q: What sound does a cockerel make in the morning?
2927.e: The cockerel crows especially early in the morning to show its territory. You often hear this loud call even before sunrise.

2928.q: About how long do young jaguars stay with their mother?
2928.e: The young learn to hunt from their mother. At about one to two years old they go off on their own.
