2928.m: Jaguar cubs learn from their mother for years.

2929.q: How does a mother least weasel communicate with her young?
a: Through sounds and direct body contact
Only through scent marks from far away
2929.e: The mother stays close to her litter and feeds the young regularly. Sounds and touch help them keep in contact.
2929.m: Closeness and sounds connect mother and young.

2930.q: About how big is a kestrel compared with a town pigeon?
a: About the same size or a little smaller
As big as an adult eagle
2930.e: A kestrel is about the size of a town pigeon, often even a little smaller and slimmer. With a body length of around 30 to 35 centimetres it is a medium-sized falcon.
2930.m: The kestrel is about the size of a pigeon.

2931.q: What do magpie parents especially often catch to feed their young in the nest?
2931.e: While raising their young, magpie parents collect lots of protein-rich insects and larvae to feed their fast-growing chicks. This food provides important energy.
2931.m: Magpie chicks get lots of insects.

2932.q: What effect does the Gulf Stream have on the climate in Western Europe?
a: It makes summers hotter than in the tropics
It brings more snow to the lowlands
2932.e: Ocean currents such as the Gulf Stream carry warm water from tropical regions to more northerly areas. As a result, winters in Western Europe, for example, are milder than they would be without this current.

2933.q: Which prey can a strong eagle owl sometimes even overpower?
a: Young foxes or other birds of prey
Large sharks in the open sea
2933.e: Thanks to its strength, an eagle owl can sometimes even catch young foxes or other birds of prey and owls. This puts it at the top of the food chain in many habitats.
2933.m: The eagle owl sometimes even overpowers foxes.

2934.q: What colour is the shell of a typical Roman snail usually?
2934.e: The Roman snail’s shell is usually brown to yellowish with fine spiral stripes. This camouflages it well among the leaves.
2934.m: The shell is yellowish brown and striped.

2935.q: What are the fine hairs on the garden spider’s legs for?
2935.e: With the fine hairs the spider senses the tiniest movements in the air and in its web. This way it notices when something is coming even without ears.

2936.q: In which area of Africa does the western lowland gorilla mainly live?
a: In the Congo Basin in central Africa
In the Sahara in the north
On the Nile in east Africa
At the Cape in South Africa
2936.e: The western lowland gorilla lives in the dense forests of the Congo Basin, for example in Cameroon and Gabon.
2936.m: Lowland gorillas live in the Congo Basin.

2937.q: How many legs does a ladybird have?
2937.e: Ladybirds are insects and, like all insects, have six legs. With them they climb skilfully about on leaves.

a: A friendship between two municipalities in different countries
A football club with players from many countries
2938.e: Two municipalities in different countries can form a partnership to visit each other and exchange ideas. In this way people from different cultures get to know each other.
2938.m: Town twinning links municipalities across borders.

2940.q: How can you often tell a young magpie from an adult?
2940.e: Young magpies at first have a shorter tail than adults, which only grows to full length over time. This is how you can tell young birds from adults.
2940.m: Young magpies have a short tail.

2941.q: About how long does an adult sand lizard grow, including its tail?
2941.e: A large part of this length is the long tail. The body itself is much shorter.
2941.m: With its tail it grows to about 20 centimetres.

2942.q: What do you call animals like the panda that are threatened with extinction and specially protected?
2942.e: The panda is considered an endangered species because there are only a few left in the wild. That is why it is specially protected.
2942.m: The panda is an endangered species.

2943.q: Which kind of tapir is the smallest?
2943.e: The mountain tapir is the smallest of the four species. It usually weighs around 150 to 250 kilograms.
2943.m: The mountain tapir is the smallest species.

2944.q: What role do orcas play in the sea?
a: They are top hunters and keep populations in balance
2944.e: Because orcas hunt many different animals, they make sure that there are not too many animals of one kind in the sea. This keeps everything in balance.
2944.m: Orcas keep the sea in balance.

2945.q: About how many facets can a butterfly’s eyes have?
2945.e: A compound eye is made of many thousands of tiny single eyes. Together they help the butterfly spot movements well.
2945.m: Compound eyes have thousands of parts.

2946.q: On which continent do baboons such as the Guinea baboon live in the wild?
2946.e: Baboons are monkeys that live in Africa. The Guinea baboon is found in western Africa.

2947.q: What do you call a person who looks after a herd of goats as a job or in everyday life?
2947.e: A goatherd leads the herd to the pasture and keeps watch over the animals there. In the story Heidi, Peter is a goatherd like this.
2947.m: A goatherd looks after the goats.

2948.q: What should you do if you see a young tawny owl sitting on a branch or on the ground in spring?
a: Leave it alone, its parents keep feeding it
Throw it back into the air
2948.e: Young tawny owls leave the nest hole before they can fly properly. They have not been abandoned: the parents are nearby and keep feeding them at night.
2948.m: Don’t take young tawny owls, their parents look after them.

2949.q: What is a young okapi called?
2949.e: As with giraffes and cattle, the young is called a calf. It weighs about 15 to 30 kilograms at birth.
2949.m: A young okapi is called a calf.

2950.q: About how fast can a peregrine falcon get in a dive?
2950.e: When diving at its prey, the peregrine falcon reaches top speeds of over 300 km/h. This makes it the fastest animal in the world.
2950.m: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal in the world.

2951.q: How big is the puma’s range compared with other land mammals in the Americas?
2951.e: The puma lives from Canada all the way to Patagonia. This gives it one of the biggest ranges of all.

2952.q: How does an Alpine marmot often behave towards its family members?
a: It grooms their fur and snuggles up to them
It constantly attacks its brothers and sisters
It avoids all contact with its family
It always stays far away from its parents
2952.e: Marmots show a lot of social behaviour within their family, such as grooming each other’s fur. This strengthens the bonds in the colony.
2952.m: Grooming each other strengthens the bonds.

2953.q: The scientific name of the African wild dog means roughly “painted wolf”. Why does that fit?
2953.e: The wild dog's coat has patches of black, yellow, brown and white. It looks as if someone has painted the animal.

2954.q: What does the hamster use its cheek pouches for?
2954.e: A hamster can collect lots of food in its cheek pouches and carry it to its hiding place. They get really fat when full.
2954.m: Cheek pouches are a hamster’s food bags.

2955.q: Where does the word “puma” come from?
a: From the Quechua language in South America
2955.e: The name comes from Quechua, an indigenous language of the Andes. The animal was called this even before the Europeans arrived.

2956.q: Which danger especially threatens the okapi?
2956.e: Its forest habitat is getting smaller, and okapis are hunted. Armed conflicts also get in the way of protecting them.

2957.q: When is the Alpine marmots’ mating season usually?
2957.e: In spring, right after the animals wake from hibernation, the marmots mate. This way the young are born in time for summer.
2957.m: After waking up comes the mating season.

2958.q: Can a sea turtle pull its head back into its shell?
a: Only the young can do that
2958.e: Unlike many tortoises, sea turtles cannot pull their head and legs into their shell. Their shell is not built for it.
2958.m: They can’t pull their head in.

2959.q: The African buffalo is one of Africa’s “Big Five”. Which other animal is also one of them?
2959.e: The “Big Five” are the elephant, rhino, lion, leopard and buffalo. The name comes from big-game hunters of the past.
2959.m: The buffalo is one of the “Big Five”.

2960.q: What sound do llamas often make to communicate?
2960.e: Llamas hum in many situations, for example out of curiosity or worry. Mothers also hum to their young.

2961.q: What does the scientific name Hippocampus mean?
a: Something like horse and sea monster
2961.e: The word comes from Greek and is made up of the words for horse and sea monster. That is how this special fish got its name.

2962.q: About how old can common wall lizards get in the wild?
2962.e: In the wild common wall lizards usually reach an age of a few years. Many fall victim to enemies or the harsh winter before then.
2962.m: Wall lizards live for several years in the wild.

2963.q: Which animals are among the robin’s enemies?
a: Cats, birds of prey and martens
2963.e: Cats, birds of prey and martens like to hunt small birds such as the robin. That is why it likes to hide in thick bushes.
2963.m: Cats and birds of prey are enemies.

2964.q: What are the coins worth less than one franc called?
2964.e: In Switzerland the small coins are called rappen (centimes in French). 100 rappen make one franc.

2965.q: What is striking about a bonobo’s face?
a: It is dark and has red lips
It is pink with white spots
It is completely covered in white fur
2965.e: Bonobos have a dark face with strikingly red lips. This is a feature that makes them easy to recognise.

2966.q: What have genetic studies of African “golden jackals” shown?
a: They belong to a separate species, the African golden wolf
2966.e: The animals in Africa used to be thought of as golden jackals. But their DNA showed that they form a different species.
2966.m: Africa’s golden jackal is a golden wolf.

2967.q: Why are rabbits important prey animals in nature?
a: Many predators such as foxes eat them
They are too big for enemies
2967.e: Rabbits are food for many predators, for example foxes and birds of prey. That makes them an important part of the food chain.
2967.m: Rabbits are prey for many predators.

2968.q: How does the snow leopard usually hunt?
a: It creeps up and pounces on its prey
2968.e: The snow leopard usually lives alone. It stalks its prey across the terrain and overpowers it with a leap.
2968.m: It is a lone hunter that stalks its prey.

2969.q: Is the orca a predator at the top of the food chain?
a: Yes, it is considered a top hunter in the sea
No, it is hunted by small fish
No, it is a prey animal
2969.e: Normally nothing hunts the orca. That is why it is right at the top of the sea’s food chain.
2969.m: The orca is the strongest hunter in the sea.

2970.q: How long does a pair of peregrine falcons sit on their eggs?
2970.e: Incubation lasts about 29 to 33 days. Then the small young falcons hatch, helpless at first.
2970.m: About a month until the chicks hatch.

2971.q: What special ability do orcas use to find their way in murky water?
a: A sense of smell like a dog’s
2971.e: With clicking sounds and their echoes, orcas can find prey well even in murky water. This is called echolocation.
2971.m: Orcas locate things with echoes in the water.

2972.q: Which habitat does the badger most like to live in in Switzerland?
2972.e: The badger likes woods with lots of hedges and bushes. There it finds enough cover and food.

2973.q: What do okapis use to mark their territory?
a: Scents from glands on their feet
2973.e: Okapis have scent glands on their feet and use them to mark their paths. Urine is also used.

2974.q: What does a newborn elephant calf feed on first?
2974.e: Elephants are mammals and feed their young with milk. Only later do the calves also eat plants.
2974.m: Elephant calves drink their mother’s milk.

2975.q: What colour is the top of a male sparrow’s head usually?
2975.e: The top of a male house sparrow’s head is usually grey. It also has brown stripes on the sides of its head.
2975.m: The male sparrow has a grey head.

2976.q: What does an earthworm do when it suddenly senses light?
a: It quickly pulls back into the soil
2976.e: Earthworms cannot see, but their skin can sense light. When there is light they quickly hide again so that they do not dry out.

a: A thinker who had new ideas about a fair society
2977.e: Karl Marx was a German thinker in the 19th century. His ideas became the basis of communism.
2977.m: Karl Marx thought about a fairer world.

2978.q: In which cities does the European Parliament mainly meet?
2978.e: The European Parliament has its main seat in Strasbourg but often also meets in Brussels. There elected members represent the citizens of the EU countries.
2978.m: The EU Parliament meets in Strasbourg and Brussels.

2979.q: Which Indigenous peoples of North America traditionally hunted bison?
a: The Plains peoples, for example the Lakota
2979.e: The peoples of the Great Plains depended heavily on the bison. They used its meat, hides and bones.
2979.m: Bison were vital for the peoples of the prairie.

2981.q: How do bonobos usually move around on the ground?
a: Only hopping on their back legs
Sliding on their belly like snakes
2981.e: On the ground, bonobos lean on the knuckles of their hands. Sometimes, though, they walk upright for short distances.

2982.q: Roughly how long do ravens incubate their eggs?
2982.e: After the eggs are laid, it takes about three weeks for young ravens to hatch. During this time the male mainly brings food.

2983.q: How big is a bumblebee colony compared with a honeybee colony?
a: Much smaller, often only a few hundred insects
Much bigger, with many thousands of insects
There is only one bumblebee per nest
2983.e: A bumblebee colony usually has only a few hundred insects. A honeybee colony is often much bigger, with many thousands of bees.
2983.m: Bumblebee colonies are small, honeybee colonies are big.

2984.q: What can zoos do for gibbons?
a: Run breeding programmes and teach people about the threats
They make gibbons live on the ground
2984.e: Many zoos take part in breeding programmes for endangered species. They also tell visitors how gibbons can be protected.

2985.q: Why does the bearded vulture often have rusty red feathers on its belly?
a: It mixes paint with its saliva
2985.e: Bearded vultures deliberately rub themselves in reddish soil or mud containing iron oxide. This gives their white feathers a rusty red colour.
2985.m: The rusty red comes from a mud bath.

2986.q: How long is a jaguar's tail compared with other big cats?
a: It has no tail at all
2986.e: Compared with its body, the jaguar's tail is rather short. It usually measures about 45 to 75 centimetres.
2986.m: Jaguars have a fairly short tail.

2987.q: What do we call the insects and spiders drifting high in the air that swifts eat?
2987.e: Aerial plankton is made up of tiny insects and spiders carried upwards by the wind. Swifts catch this food while flying.
2987.m: Aerial plankton is the swift's food.

2988.q: What does it mean that baboons are omnivores?
a: They eat both plant and animal food
2988.e: Omnivores use many sources of food. This helps baboons survive in different habitats.

2989.q: Where does a female carp usually lay her eggs?
a: In a hollow in the gravel
2989.e: The female carp sticks her eggs to water plants. There they are well hidden and protected.
2989.m: Carp eggs stick to water plants.

2990.q: How does the hooded crow look different from the carrion crow?
a: It has a grey body with a black head and wings
It is much bigger than an eagle
2990.e: The hooded crow is closely related to the carrion crow, but it has a grey body while its head, wings and tail stay black. In some places the two species form mixed pairs.
2990.m: Hooded crows have a grey body.

2991.q: What colour is a koala's fur usually?
2991.e: A koala's fur is usually grey or greyish brown. This gives it good camouflage in the trees.
2991.m: Koala fur is usually grey to brown.

2992.q: How many eggs does a mallard usually lay?
2992.e: A clutch usually has between eight and twelve eggs. The female then incubates them herself.

2993.q: Apart from its lungs, what else can the common frog breathe with?
2993.e: The common frog's skin is thin and moist. It can take in extra oxygen through it, especially in winter in the water.
2993.m: Common frogs also breathe through their skin.

2994.q: What do you call the movable connection between two bones?
2994.e: Joints connect bones and make movement possible. Cartilage, ligaments and fluid make sure they work well.
2994.m: Joints connect bones so they can move.

2995.q: What is the small device on a bike called that makes electricity for the light from the movement of the wheel?
2995.e: A dynamo makes electricity from the turning of the wheel. This lets the bike light shine without a battery.
2995.m: The dynamo turns movement into electricity.

2996.q: What does the female sea turtle mainly use her back flippers for on land?
a: Digging the nest for her eggs
2996.e: On land the female uses her back flippers like little spades to dig a hole for the eggs. Afterwards she carefully covers the nest with sand again.
2996.m: Back flippers dig the egg nest in the sand.

2997.q: How do adult bearded vultures usually react to people near their nest?
a: They are very sensitive to disturbance
They come closer out of curiosity
They show no reaction at all
2997.e: Bearded vultures react badly to disturbance near their nest and may even abandon their eggs or chicks. That is why it is important not to disturb nesting areas.
2997.m: Disturbance at the nest is dangerous.

2998.q: How does a grasshopper behave when it gets cold?
a: It becomes even faster than usual
It grows new wings at once
2998.e: Grasshoppers need warmth to be active. When it is cold they move only very slowly.
2998.m: Cold makes them tired and slow.

2999.q: What hatches from an ant egg?
2999.e: First a larva hatches from the egg. Later it becomes a pupa and then a fully grown ant.

3000.q: Why are bees important for plants and people?
a: They pollinate many flowers so that fruit can grow
They make noise to scare off pests
3000.e: When bees fly from flower to flower, they carry pollen along. This lets plants produce seeds, and lots of fruit and vegetables can grow.

3001.e: In electoral fraud votes are manipulated or miscounted so that the desired candidate wins. In dictatorships this is a common way of staying in power.
3001.m: False votes fake a real election.

3002.q: At what age are golden eagles usually able to breed?
3002.e: Golden eagles only get their full adult plumage at about 4 to 5 years old, and then they can breed. Before that they go through several juvenile plumages.
3002.m: They can breed at about 4 years old.

3003.q: What do great crested grebe chicks' feathers usually look like?
a: Black and white stripes like a little watermelon
3003.e: The young chicks have a typical black and white striped pattern that is often compared to a little watermelon. This pattern helps camouflage them.
3003.m: Chicks are striped black and white like a melon.

3004.q: Roughly how big is an ant?
3004.e: Most ants are tiny. They often measure only a few millimetres.

3005.q: How does a stone marten typically move?
3005.e: The stone marten's typical way of moving is a smooth, arched bounding run. This lets it dash quickly and nimbly across the ground.

3006.q: What do we call the large, flat antlers of a bull elk (moose)?
3006.e: The elk's antlers are broad and widen out like a shovel or an open hand. That is why they are called palmate antlers.

3007.q: Why was the bear JJ3 shot in the Grisons in 2008?
a: It kept coming too close to villages and lost its fear
It had escaped from a zoo
It had eaten all the fish in the lake
3007.e: JJ3 kept looking for food in villages and lost its fear of people. The authorities classed it as a risk bear and had it shot. This caused a lot of debate.
3007.m: JJ3 was shot as a risk bear in 2008.

3008.q: Roughly how old are the oldest known ancestors of dragonflies?
3008.e: Dragonfly-like insects already existed in the Carboniferous period. They are among the oldest flying insects.

3009.q: What does a hamster do with leftover food?
a: It hides it as a store
3009.e: Hamsters love collecting food and hiding it in small stores. That way they always have something to eat later.

3010.q: Off which continent does the island of Madagascar, home of the ring-tailed lemur, lie?
3010.e: Madagascar lies in the Indian Ocean off the east coast of Africa. It is one of the biggest islands in the world.
3010.m: Madagascar lies off Africa's east coast.

3011.q: Does a pike sometimes eat frogs or small ducks too?
a: No, pike eat nothing at all
3011.e: The pike is not fussy and also eats frogs or sometimes small ducklings that end up in the water. It is a very versatile hunter.
3011.m: Pike also eat frogs and chicks.

3012.q: Roughly how big is an adult mosquito?
3012.e: An adult mosquito is usually only a few millimetres long and very light. That is why it can land on your skin almost silently.
3012.m: Mosquitoes are only a few millimetres long.

3014.q: What is the smaller, often brownish relative of the peregrine falcon that often hovers over meadows to hunt?
3014.e: The kestrel is a close relative of the peregrine falcon, but smaller and browner. It often hunts by hovering in the air over open meadows.
3014.m: The kestrel is a small relative.

3015.q: Which group of amphibians does the alpine newt belong to?
3015.e: Unlike frogs, tailed amphibians keep their tail as adults. The alpine newt belongs to this group.
3015.m: Alpine newts keep their tail all their lives.

3016.q: Some ants look for food, others stay in the nest. Why?
3016.e: An ant colony has different jobs. Some ants look for food, others look after the larvae.

3017.q: Which farm animal is the Alpine ibex closely related to?
3017.e: The ibex and the domestic goat belong to the same genus, Capra. That is why the two animals are alike in many ways.
3017.m: Ibex and goat are close relatives.

3018.q: Where does a brown bear usually make its winter den?
a: In a cave it digs itself or a natural one on a hillside
Always in an abandoned bird's nest
Always in the middle of an open field
3018.e: Brown bears often dig a den into a slope themselves or use natural rock crevices and tree roots as shelter. They often line the floor with grass and leaves.
3018.m: Bear dens are usually on hillsides.

3019.q: What do ladybirds do in autumn before winter arrives?
a: They look for a sheltered hiding place
They build a nest of twigs
They eat until they grow thick fur
They migrate to Africa like birds
3019.e: When it gets cooler, ladybirds look for hiding places under bark, in leaves or in cracks. There they wait, protected, for the next spring.
3019.m: Autumn means finding a hiding place.

3020.q: On which continent is the giraffe's home?
3020.e: Giraffes originally come only from Africa. There they live in savannahs south of the Sahara.

3021.q: What does the great tit have down the middle of its yellow belly?
3021.e: A black stripe runs down the middle of its yellow belly. In males it is usually wider than in females.
3021.m: The black belly stripe is typical.

3022.q: What does it mean that gibbons often live in pairs?
a: Males and females often stay together for a long time
They live together only in winter
3022.e: Many gibbon species form steady pairs that raise young together for a long time. This is called living in pairs.
3022.m: Gibbon pairs often stay together for a long time.

3023.q: What happens with a wage garnishment?
a: Part of the wage is withheld directly to pay off debts, but the subsistence minimum stays protected
The whole wage is taken immediately
The employer must dismiss the person
The person automatically gets a higher wage
3023.e: With a wage garnishment, part of the income is withheld to pay off outstanding debts. But the person keeps the subsistence minimum needed to live.
3023.m: Garnishment, but the subsistence minimum stays.

3024.q: What does the great spotted cuckoo do with its eggs?
a: It lays them in other birds' nests, often magpies'
It buries them in the sand
It carries them around in its beak
It lays them in the water
3024.e: The great spotted cuckoo is a relative of our common cuckoo. It often lays its eggs in magpies' nests, and the magpies then raise the strange chick.
3024.m: The great spotted cuckoo lets magpies raise its chicks.

3025.q: What do some dictators like to build to look powerful?
a: Huge statues and pictures of themselves.
3025.e: Big monuments and pictures are meant to show how strong and important the ruler supposedly is. This is called a personality cult.

3026.q: Which wild animal is today's domestic chicken originally descended from?
3026.e: The red junglefowl lives in the wild in Asia and is the ancestor of all domestic chickens. It already looks very much like a farm chicken.
3026.m: The red junglefowl is the ancestor.

3027.q: Does a mother shark look after her young after they are born?
a: Mostly not, the young are independent at once
She carries them around in her mouth
3027.e: Most baby sharks have to look after themselves from birth. They can swim and hunt straight away.
3027.m: Young sharks are on their own from the start.

3028.q: When does the grey heron's breeding season usually start in Switzerland?
a: As early as February or March
3028.e: Grey herons start building nests and breeding early in the year, often before winter is over. That gives the young enough time to grow up.

3029.q: How many suckers can a single octopus arm have?
3029.e: Each arm of an octopus often has several hundred suckers. With them it can grip things very firmly.
3029.m: Each arm has lots of suckers.

3030.q: What happens to reindeer antlers every year?
a: They are shed and grow back
They stay the same for life
3030.e: Reindeer shed their antlers every year. Then a new, often bigger set grows back.

3031.q: What colour is a pike usually?
3031.e: The pike is green to brown with yellow spots. This lets it hide well among water plants.
3031.m: Green and yellow colours help with camouflage.

3032.q: What is special about the head hair of many bonobos?
a: It is parted in the middle
It forms a mane like a lion's
3032.e: The hair on bonobos' heads often lies so that it looks like a centre parting. This makes the hairstyle look almost human.
3032.m: Bonobos often have a centre parting.

3033.q: What do buzzards show in the sky during courtship?
3033.e: During courtship, buzzards perform spectacular flying displays with dives and loops. In this way the partners court each other and strengthen their bond.
3033.m: Courtship flights show impressive flying skills.

3034.q: What do giant panda mothers do shortly after their baby is born?
a: They take great care of the tiny cub
They leave it alone in the forest at once
They give it to another animal
They take it straight to the river
3034.e: Panda mothers are very caring in the first weeks. They hold their tiny cub in their arms almost all the time.
3034.m: Panda mothers take loving care of their cub.

3035.q: What does a roe deer do when it gets a fright?
a: It gives a barking call and runs away
It just lies down and sleeps
3035.e: When a roe deer senses danger, it can give a barking warning call. Then it runs away quickly.
3035.m: Frightened roe deer bark and flee.

3036.q: What happens once a tawny owl has grabbed its prey with its talons?
a: It usually kills it at once with a precise bite
It lets it go again straight away
It carries it alive to the nest and never kills it
It waits several hours until it dies by itself
3036.e: As soon as the tawny owl has grabbed prey with its talons, it usually kills it quickly with a precise bite. This way it loses as little time and energy as possible.
3036.m: Tawny owls kill prey quickly with a bite.

3037.q: What does the wood mouse do when it finds food it does not need straight away?
a: It just leaves it lying there
3037.e: The wood mouse hides leftover food in small hiding places so it can eat it later.

3038.q: What most clearly sets the great tit apart from the blue tit?
a: It is bigger and has a black head
It is smaller and has a blue head
It has a much longer beak
3038.e: The great tit is clearly bigger than the blue tit and has a black head instead of a blue one. Both have a yellow belly.
3038.m: The great tit is bigger with a black head.

3039.q: When is the puma usually most active?
3039.e: Pumas are mostly active at dusk and at night. That is when they hunt most often.
3039.m: Pumas hunt mainly at night and in the evening.

3040.q: What is separation anxiety in dogs?
a: Strong stress behaviour when the dog is left alone
3040.e: Some dogs show separation anxiety by barking, destroying things or being restless when they have to stay home alone. It often comes from too little training or upsetting experiences.
3040.m: Separation anxiety shows when the dog is alone.

3041.q: What is special about the skinny pig, a particular guinea pig breed?
a: It is as small as a mouse
3041.e: The skinny pig is a breed that has almost no hair. These animals need extra protection so they do not get cold or sunburnt.
3041.m: Skinny pigs have almost no fur.

3042.q: How many young does a female meerkat usually have in one litter?
3042.e: A litter usually has two to four young. They are born in the burrow.
3042.m: A litter usually has two to four young.

3043.q: Is the edible dormouse a protected species in Switzerland?
a: No, it counts as a pest with no protection
3043.e: The edible dormouse is protected in Switzerland because it is one of the native wild animals. So it must not simply be caught or killed.
3043.m: The edible dormouse is protected in Switzerland.

3044.q: Roughly how old can horses get?
3044.e: With good care, horses can live quite long, often 25 to 30 years. That is much longer than a hamster's life.

3045.q: Why is the magpie partly seen as useful for farming?
a: Because it eats many harmful insects
3045.e: Magpies eat a large number of insects and other pests that could harm plants. In this way they help farmers, even if they are sometimes seen as a nuisance.

3046.q: Which sex of the European eel usually grows bigger?
3046.e: Female eels grow faster and get bigger. The male usually reaches only about half the length.

3047.q: Why do young penguin chicks often stay together in a group while their parents hunt?
a: It protects them better from enemies and cold
Because they think it is funny
3047.e: These groups of chicks are called a nursery or crèche. Together the young are warmer and better protected from enemies, while a few adult penguins keep watch.
3047.m: Penguin chicks form groups for protection.

3048.q: How heavy can an adult mute swan get?
3048.e: An adult mute swan can weigh up to 15 kilograms. This makes it one of the heaviest birds that can still fly.
3048.m: Swans can weigh up to 15 kilos.

3049.q: Which legs does a newt larva grow first?
a: All four at the same time
3049.e: Newt larvae grow their front legs first. With frog tadpoles it is the other way round: the back legs come first.
3049.m: Newt larvae get their front legs first.

3050.q: What do some young carrion crows do before they breed themselves?
a: They help their parents raise more young
They move to the desert alone
They build their own nest at once
They leave their family for ever
3050.e: Some young carrion crows stay with their parents for a while and help them raise the next brood. This is called cooperative breeding.
3050.m: Young crows sometimes help their parents.

3051.q: Why do meerkats often sunbathe outside their burrow in the morning?
a: To warm up after the cool night
3051.e: Nights in their homeland are often cool. In the morning they warm their bodies in the sun.
3051.m: In the morning they warm up in the sun.

3052.q: What does an adult wasp especially like to eat?
a: Sweet things like fruit or lemonade
3052.e: Adult wasps love sweet things. That is why they often come to cakes or drinks.

3053.q: Roughly how big does an adult European tree frog get?
3053.e: The tree frog is a very small frog, usually only a few centimetres long. Even so, it is a skilful jumper and climber.
3053.m: The tree frog is small but a real climbing expert.

3054.q: Which of these animals belongs to the bear family, like the brown bear?
3054.e: The giant panda is a true bear, even though it eats almost only bamboo. Koalas and raccoons are sometimes called bears, but they belong to other animal groups.
3054.m: The giant panda is a bear too.

3055.q: How does a peregrine falcon behave towards other peregrines in its breeding territory?
a: It happily shares the territory with strange falcons
3055.e: Peregrine falcons are territorial and defend their breeding area against intruders with loud calls and targeted attacks in flight. This keeps their hunting ground safe for the family.

3056.q: How do goats help when they eat thorny bushes?
a: They keep pastures free of scrub
3056.e: Goats are happy to eat thorny scrub that other animals leave alone. In this way they help keep overgrown pastures open.

a: A part of Switzerland with its own government
3057.e: Switzerland is made up of many cantons. Each canton has its own laws and its own government.
3057.m: A canton is a part of Switzerland.

3058.q: What does a common toad mainly take in through its skin?
3058.e: Common toads can take in water through their skin, especially on their belly. That is why they do not have to drink with their mouths like we do.
3058.m: Toads take in water through their skin.

3059.q: How do male giraffes often fight over rank?
a: They swing their necks against each other
3059.e: In this fight, called necking, the males swing their long necks against each other. The stronger one often wins the higher rank in the group.
3059.m: Male giraffes fight with their necks.

3060.q: What colour is the fur of a typical leopard?
3060.e: A typical leopard has yellowish to golden brown fur with dark rosettes. The belly is lighter.
3060.m: Leopard fur is golden brown with rosettes.

3061.q: What colour is a barn owl's back usually?
3061.e: The barn owl's back shimmers golden yellow to brownish. This colour camouflages it well at dusk.

3062.q: How can you often tell that a European pond turtle is a male?
a: By its reddish eyes and longer tail
By a crest on its head
3062.e: Males often have reddish eyes and a longer, thicker tail. Females tend to have yellowish eyes.
3062.m: Eye colour and tail give away the male.

3063.q: What does a dolphin breathe with?
3063.e: Dolphins have lungs and must come to the surface to breathe. There they open the blowhole on top of their head.
3063.m: Dolphins breathe with lungs, not gills.

3064.q: When is the hippopotamus usually active?
3064.e: Hippos are nocturnal. They leave the water when it gets dark and cooler to eat grass.

3066.q: Why is the seahorse called that?
a: Because its head looks like a horse's head
Because it runs like a horse
Because it lives in a stable
3066.e: With its curved snout, the seahorse's head looks like a little horse's head. That is why people gave it this name.
3066.m: Its head looks like a horse.

3067.q: How do golden eagle pairs usually behave towards each other?
a: They often stay together for life
They split up after every brood
Females never hunt with their partner
3067.e: Golden eagles are usually monogamous and often stay with the same partner for many years or even their whole life. They defend their territory together.
3067.m: Golden eagle pairs usually stay together for life.

3068.q: Where in Switzerland can you often see large groups of resting wild geese?
a: On large lakes such as Lake Constance
In the middle of the desert
3068.e: Large lakes are important resting places for migrating birds. Wild geese take a break there on their long journey and find enough food.
3068.m: Wild geese like to rest on large lakes.

3069.q: What happens to an edible dormouse's body weight shortly before hibernation?
a: It goes up a lot because of fat reserves
3069.e: Before hibernating, the edible dormouse eats a lot and builds up plenty of fat. This fat serves as an energy store during its long sleep.
3069.m: Before hibernation it builds up fat.

3070.q: Where can you often find ants' nests in Switzerland?
a: Only high in the mountains above the snow
Only in the middle of a lake
Only in the cellar of a house
3070.e: Ants live in many places. Their nests are found especially often in woods, meadows or gardens.
3070.m: Ants live in woods and gardens.

3071.q: What does the mother ibex do right after her kid is born?
a: She first hides it in a safe spot in the rocks
She takes it straight into a big herd
She leaves it all alone and no longer cares for it
She carries it in her mouth for several weeks
3071.e: Right after the birth, the mother often hides her kid in a sheltered spot in the rocks. After a few days the kid already follows its mother everywhere.
3071.m: First hidden, then the kid follows.

3072.q: How does an orangutan react when it senses danger?
a: It usually retreats into the trees
It rolls up into a ball
It always stays motionless on the ground
3072.e: When in danger, it climbs higher up. There it is safer from many enemies.

a: Alone or in pairs, not in big shoals
Always in huge groups of thousands
3073.e: Seahorses do not swim in big shoals like many other fish. Usually you see them alone or in twos.
3073.m: Seahorses usually live alone or in pairs.

3074.q: Where does the fire salamander have particularly large poison glands?
a: At the tip of its tail
3074.e: Behind the eyes there are two large glands, the parotoid glands. A poisonous fluid can come out of them.
3074.m: Poison glands sit behind the eyes.

3075.q: What does the organisation Amnesty International work for?
a: Respect for human rights around the world
Peace between the EU and NATO
3075.e: Amnesty International is an independent organisation that works for human rights and makes abuses public. For example, it collects signatures for people in prison.
3075.m: Amnesty International fights for human rights.

3076.q: How do researchers often recognise individual lynx?
a: By their individual pattern of spots
By the colour of their eyes
By their smell from a distance
3076.e: Every lynx has a unique pattern of spots, rather like a fingerprint. With camera traps, researchers can tell individual animals apart.

3077.q: What is an adult male pig called?
3077.e: The male pig is called a boar. It is usually bigger and more strongly built than the sow.
3077.m: An adult male is called a boar.

3078.q: Besides being a bird of ill omen, what reputation did the raven have in many old stories?
a: It was also a symbol of wisdom
It was a symbol of stupidity
It was a symbol of laziness
It was a symbol of fearfulness
3078.e: Despite its gloomy reputation as a bringer of bad luck, in other cultures the raven was also seen as wise and clever. This double meaning appears in many myths and fairy tales.
3078.m: In myths it is also a symbol of wisdom.

3079.q: What does the pH value of a liquid measure?
a: How acidic or alkaline it is
3079.e: The pH value shows whether a liquid is acidic, neutral or alkaline. It usually ranges from 0 (strongly acidic) to 14 (strongly alkaline).
3079.m: The pH value measures acidic or alkaline.

3080.q: What is the joint sitting of the National Council and the Council of States called, for example to elect the Federal Council?
3080.e: On certain occasions such as the election of the Federal Council, the National Council and the Council of States meet together as the United Federal Assembly.
3080.m: When both chambers sit together, it is called the United Federal Assembly.

3081.e: Because of its strong back legs and big tail, a kangaroo cannot hop backwards. It always moves forwards.

3082.q: Which order of birds does the buzzard belong to?
3082.e: The buzzard belongs to the birds of prey. These birds have strong feet with talons and a hooked beak for hunting.
3082.m: The buzzard is a bird of prey.

3083.q: Where do wild asses still live today?
a: In dry regions of Africa and Asia
3083.e: Wild asses still live in some dry regions of Africa and Asia. Sadly, they have become very rare there.
3083.m: Wild asses live in Africa and Asia.

3084.q: How do female chamois usually live with their young?
3084.e: Female chamois form small herds with their kids and other females. This way they can warn each other of danger.
3084.m: Female chamois live in groups with their kids.

3085.q: Why do orcas usually live in groups?
a: Because they hunt together and look after the young
Because they are afraid of fish
3085.e: In a group, orcas help each other hunt and keep an eye on the young. This is called social behaviour.

3086.q: How many young does a female baboon usually have at once?
3086.e: Usually a single baby is born. Twins are rare.

3087.q: On which day of the week do Christians usually meet for a church service?
3087.e: Many Christians see Sunday as a special day. They often go to church and rest.
3087.m: Sunday is the Christian holy day of the week.

3088.q: In which nests does a female cuckoo usually lay her eggs?
a: Always those of the same bird species
Those of any bird species she finds
Only those of large birds of prey
3088.e: Each female cuckoo usually lays her eggs with just one bird species, for example always with the reed warbler. That way her egg looks like the other eggs in the nest.
3088.m: Each female has her own host bird.

3089.q: Which predator is one of the natural enemies of bison in North America?
3089.e: Wolves hunt in packs, mainly young, sick or weak bison. Healthy adults defend themselves well.
3089.m: Wolves hunt bison, especially weak ones.

3090.q: How is the llama often seen in stories and everyday life in South America?
3090.e: Llamas have been important domestic animals for a long time. They provide wool and carry loads.
3090.m: The llama is an ancient domestic animal.

3091.q: In which habitat is the polecat found especially often?
a: Only in the middle of big cities
Only in very dry desert areas
Only high up in the mountains
3091.e: The polecat likes to stay near ponds, streams and damp meadows. There it finds frogs and other prey it likes to eat.

3092.q: Is the garden spider an insect?
3092.e: Spiders belong to the arachnids and not to the insects. They have eight legs and no antennae.

3093.q: Which senses does the mole mainly use to find its prey?
3093.e: Because the mole can see almost nothing, it relies on its sensitive nose and touch-sensitive hairs. This lets it sense worms in the dark soil.
3093.m: Nose and whiskers replace the eyes.

3094.q: Who makes sure that horses have healthy hooves?
3094.e: The farrier checks the hooves regularly and sometimes fits them with horseshoes. This keeps the horse's feet healthy.
3094.m: The farrier looks after the hooves.

3095.q: What do fire salamander larvae eat in the water?
a: Small water insects and the larvae of other animals
3095.e: In the stream, the larvae hunt small water insects, small crustaceans and sometimes other amphibian larvae too. Even as larvae they are predators.
3095.m: Larvae already hunt in the stream.

3096.q: What does the mole like to eat most of all?
3096.e: Earthworms are the mole's favourite food. It finds them in the soil with its sensitive nose.

3097.q: How soon can a newborn goat kid usually stand?
a: After a short time, often within minutes or hours
Never, it always has to be carried
3097.e: Goat kids are precocial, which means they are well developed at birth. They can stand on their wobbly legs shortly after they are born.

3098.q: How does an elk (moose) usually run away from danger?
3098.e: Elk are fast and can run very quickly over short distances. They reach about 50 to 60 km/h.

3099.q: What is remarkable about the size of the least weasel's prey?
a: It can sometimes kill prey bigger than itself
It never hunts anything bigger than itself
It hunts big animals only in groups
3099.e: Despite its small size, the least weasel sometimes even overpowers young rabbits that are much heavier than itself. Its bold, fast attack helps it do this.
3099.m: Least weasels also hunt bigger prey.

a: A locust that travels in huge swarms
A locust that walks instead of jumping
A locust that lives only in the mountains
3100.e: Migratory locusts sometimes form huge swarms. These swarms can strip whole fields bare.
3100.m: Swarms can strip whole fields bare.

3101.q: How do adult tapirs usually live?
3101.e: Adult tapirs usually live alone. Only mothers with young, or pairs during mating, stay together.

3102.q: How does a kingfisher typically hunt?
a: It dives head first into the water from a perch
It walks along the bank and snaps
It flies high in the air and catches insects
It waits hidden in the water for prey
3102.e: From a branch or stone above the water, the kingfisher watches the fish. When it spots one, it dives in head first in a flash.
3102.m: A head-first dive from a perch into the water.

3103.q: What colour is a roe deer's coat in winter usually?
3103.e: In winter the roe deer changes its coat. It then becomes greyish brown and thicker so the deer does not get cold.
3103.m: In winter the coat is greyish brown.

3104.q: Which scientist became famous because goslings followed him as if he were their mother?
3104.e: Konrad Lorenz studied the behaviour of goslings closely. In doing so he discovered the phenomenon of imprinting.
3104.m: Konrad Lorenz studied imprinting in geese.

3105.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker's plumage mainly look like?
a: Black and white with red patches
3105.e: The great spotted woodpecker has a striking pattern of black, white and red. This makes it easy to recognise in the woods.
3105.m: The great spotted woodpecker wears black, white and red.

3106.q: What is the most likely difference between male and female tree frogs?
a: Males have a vocal sac on their throat
3106.e: Only the males have a stretchy vocal sac that they use to call. Females do not have this visible structure.
3106.m: Only males have the vocal sac.

3107.q: How do donkeys show how they feel?
a: With the position of their ears
3107.e: A donkey's ears tell you a lot about its mood. When they stand upright, the donkey is alert and interested.

3108.q: What is a female orca called?
3108.e: Female orcas are called cows. This word is often used for whales.
3108.m: A female orca is called a cow.

3109.q: Why do fishermen on Lake Constance catch fewer whitefish today than in the past?
a: The lake has fewer nutrients and less plankton grows
The lake has become much warmer
The lake has too much salt
There are no nets any more
3109.e: Because the water quality is better, less phosphorus gets into the lake. As a result, less plankton grows and there is less food for whitefish.

3110.q: Which big cats in Africa and Asia are the jaguar's relatives?
3110.e: The genus Panthera includes the lion, tiger, leopard and jaguar. They can roar.
3110.m: Jaguar, lion, tiger and leopard are Panthera.

3111.q: Who mainly incubates the eggs in tawny owls?
3111.e: In tawny owls, only the female incubates the eggs and keeps the young warm. During this time the male's job is to bring food.
3111.m: Female tawny owl incubates, male hunts.

3113.q: What is a climate feedback, such as the ice-albedo feedback?
a: An effect that strengthens or weakens an original climate change
3113.e: When ice melts, less sunlight is reflected and the Earth warms further, which makes even more ice melt. Such reinforcing cycles are called feedbacks.

3114.q: What does a very young carp eat first?
3114.e: Tiny young carp cannot eat big chunks yet. First they eat very small creatures in the water, called plankton.
3114.m: Young carp first eat tiny plankton.

3115.q: Where does the white stork spend the winter?
3115.e: Many white storks fly to Africa in autumn because it is warm there and there is enough food. In spring they come back.
3115.m: Storks spend the winter in Africa.

3116.q: Which animal group do slow worms and their relatives belong to?
3116.e: Slow worms and their relatives are lizards, even though many have no legs or only tiny ones. Like many lizards, the slow worm can shed its tail, for example.
3116.m: Slow worms are lizards, not snakes.

3117.q: In which habitats are wolves found around the world?
3117.e: Wolves are very adaptable and live in very different habitats, from dense forests and open steppes to high mountains. This makes them one of the most widespread predators.
3117.m: Wolves live in many different habitats.

3118.q: Which animal group does the woodlouse belong to?
3118.e: Woodlice are crustaceans, even though they live on land. They are related to crabs and prawns.

3119.q: How well can a stone marten climb?
a: Very well, it even climbs walls and trees
It only moves on flat ground
Only with help from other animals
3119.e: Stone martens are skilful climbers and use this to get into lofts or over walls. This makes them successful at finding food in towns and villages.
3119.m: Stone martens are skilful, agile climbers.

3120.q: What most clearly sets spiders apart from insects?
a: Spiders have eight legs, insects six
Spiders have wings, insects do not
3120.e: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs and two body parts. Insects have six legs and three body parts.
3120.m: Eight legs for spiders, six for insects.

3122.q: What does an earthworm absolutely need so that it does not dry out?
3122.e: An earthworm's skin must always stay moist, otherwise it cannot breathe. That is why it stays in damp soil.

3123.q: What does it mean that ring-tailed lemurs are ‘endemic’ to Madagascar?
3123.e: Endemic means that a species naturally lives only in one particular area. For ring-tailed lemurs, that is Madagascar.
3123.m: Endemic means a species is native only to that place.

3124.q: What do praying mantises have on their heads to sense smells and touch?
3124.e: Antennae are sense organs. They are important for many insects, but for the praying mantis, sight plays the bigger role.

3126.q: When do young least weasels become independent?
a: After just a few weeks they start hunting themselves
They stay with their mother for life
3126.e: Least weasels develop very quickly and soon leave their mother to hunt for themselves. This fits their short lifespan overall.

3127.q: Why do many dictators have a very large army?
a: To protect their power and intimidate critics.
3127.e: A large army helps the dictator stay in power. It can stop protests and spread fear.
3127.m: Large armies keep dictators in power.

3128.q: What teeth do alpacas have at the front of their upper jaw?
a: No upper incisors, just a dental pad
3128.e: At the front of their upper jaw, alpacas have a hard pad instead of incisors. They use it to pluck grass.
3128.m: Alpacas have a dental pad on top.

3129.q: What job do woodlice do in the soil?
a: They break down dead material and make humus
They loosen the soil with horns
3129.e: As decomposers, woodlice break up dead plant material. This is then broken down further by fungi and bacteria.
3129.m: Woodlice are important decomposers in the soil.

3130.q: What do scientists now know about how reindeer see in the UV range?
a: They see only in black and white
3130.e: Unlike humans, reindeer can see UV light. This helps them spot food and enemies in the snow.

3131.q: What sets a hornet apart from an ordinary wasp?
3131.e: The hornet is also a wasp, but it is much bigger. However, it is not more aggressive than other wasps.

3132.q: Is the carp popular with anglers too?
a: Yes, because it can grow very big and strong
No, it can never be caught
3132.e: Because carp can grow big and strong, many anglers love the challenge of catching one. They are often put back into the water afterwards.
3132.m: Carp are very popular with anglers.

3133.q: What is it called when bees carry pollen from one flower to another?
3133.e: When bees collect nectar, pollen sticks to them, and they carry it to the next flower. This allows plants to produce seeds.

3134.q: How well can a buzzard spot prey from high up?
a: Very well, its eyes are extremely sharp
Very badly, it is almost blind
Only if the prey does not move
3134.e: The buzzard has excellent eyes and can spot even small prey from a great distance. This sharp eyesight is vital for hunting from the air.

3135.q: What makes the European Economic Area (EEA) different from the EU?
a: The EEA allows access to the single market without being an EU member
The EEA has its own army
The EEA is bigger than the EU
The EEA consists only of Switzerland
3135.e: Countries such as Norway are in the EEA without being EU members. Switzerland belongs neither to the EU nor to the EEA, but has its own agreements with the EU.
3135.m: The EEA allows market access without joining the EU.

3136.q: Where does an edible frog often sit to warm up in the sun?
a: On water lily leaves or at the water's edge
Deep down at the bottom of a lake
In the middle of a road
3136.e: Edible frogs like to sunbathe on floating leaves such as water lilies or right on the bank. This lets them raise their body temperature.
3136.m: Edible frogs sunbathe on leaves near the bank.

3137.q: How can you best recognise fire salamander larvae in the water?
a: By yellowish spots where the legs join the body and their outer gills
3137.e: The larvae have bushy outer gills and often yellowish spots where the legs join the body. This makes them easy to tell apart from other amphibian larvae.
3137.m: Gills and spots give the larva away.

3138.q: What does it usually mean when a guinea pig squeaks loudly?
a: It is looking forward to food
It is hungry only at night
3138.e: Many guinea pigs squeak excitedly when they hear the fridge or a bag of vegetables. They then expect something tasty to eat soon.
3138.m: Squeaking often means food is coming.

3139.q: What happens to an edible dormouse's heartbeat during hibernation?
3139.e: During hibernation, the edible dormouse's heart beats only very slowly. This saves energy that it needs for the long sleep.
3139.m: The heartbeat becomes very slow during hibernation.

3140.q: What do young people do in a youth parliament?
a: They talk about politics and bring in ideas
They train for a sports competition
3140.e: In a youth parliament, young people can have their say, even before they are allowed to vote. This way they practise democracy.
3140.m: In a youth parliament, young people practise politics.

3141.q: How many legs does a mosquito have?
3141.e: Like all insects, the mosquito has six thin legs. It uses them to hold on to plants or skin.

3142.q: Which big cat is especially closely related to the jaguar?
3142.e: The jaguar, leopard, lion and tiger belong to the same genus of big cats, Panthera. The puma, cheetah and lynx do not.
3142.m: The jaguar is closely related to the leopard, lion and tiger.

3143.q: Why is the robin considered a good singer?
a: It always sings the same note
It sings only once a year
3143.e: The robin switches between many different notes when it sings. That is why its songs sound so varied.

3144.q: Do male sea turtles ever come back onto land after they have hatched?
a: No, they usually stay in the sea all their lives
3144.e: Once a young male turtle has crawled into the sea, it normally never leaves the water again. Only the females later go ashore to lay eggs.
3144.m: Males usually stay in the sea for ever.

3145.q: What do sharks use to sense very weak electrical signals from other animals?
a: Small sense organs on their snout
3145.e: These special pores on the snout are called ampullae of Lorenzini. With them the shark can even sense animals hiding in the sand.
3145.m: Sharks sense electrical signals with their snout.

3146.q: What does the pond skater use its short front legs for?
3146.e: The front legs grab and hold prey. Then the pond skater stabs it with its mouthparts.

3147.q: Which animals are among the predators of woodlice?
3147.e: Many small hunters eat woodlice, such as spiders or ground beetles. Hedgehogs, birds and toads catch them too.
3147.m: Woodlice are eaten by many animals.

3148.q: What is it called when the sheep come back down from the alpine pasture to the valley in autumn?
3148.e: In autumn, herders drive the sheep from the alpine pasture back to the valley. This is called the Alpabzug. It is often a big festival with music and decorations for the animals.
3148.m: In autumn the sheep come down from the alp.

3149.q: What are the giraffe's long legs especially good for?
3149.e: The giraffe's long legs help it run fast and keep a good lookout for enemies. Giraffes never climb trees.

3150.q: Does a starfish have a brain like we humans do?
a: No, it has no real brain
Yes, a brain like a dog's
3150.e: Starfish do not have a real brain, only a nervous system. Even so, they can sense their surroundings.

3151.q: Roughly how old can a pike get?
3151.e: Pike can live a long time, some for over 20 years. They keep growing bigger as they age.
3151.m: Pike can live a long time.

3152.q: Roughly how long does it take for a kestrel egg to hatch?
3152.e: The kestrel's incubation period lasts about 28 days. During this time it is mainly the female that sits on the eggs.
3152.m: Kestrel eggs take about four weeks.

3153.q: In the wild, budgies are green and yellow. What other colours can pet budgies be?
3153.e: People have bred budgies, so today there are many colours, such as blue or white. In the wild, though, they are mostly green and yellow.
3153.m: Pet budgies come in many colours.

3154.q: Which wild animals can be dangerous to young elephant calves?
3154.e: Adult elephants have almost no natural enemies. But young, unprotected calves can be attacked by lions.
3154.m: Lions can be dangerous to elephant calves.

3155.q: Besides plants, what else do mallards like to eat?
3155.e: Mallards are omnivores and also like small animals. Water insects, worms and snails are often on their menu.
3155.m: Ducks also eat small water creatures.

3156.q: What do you call people who examine and research something carefully?
3156.e: Researchers, also called scientists, study the world to find out new things. They ask questions and look for answers.

3157.q: Besides hiding, how else do rabbits protect themselves from enemies?
a: By running fast in a zigzag
3157.e: When a rabbit flees, it often runs in a zigzag. This makes it harder for enemies to catch it.

3158.q: What do you call someone who is locked up because of their opinions?
3158.e: Political prisoners are in prison because they spoke their minds openly. This happens mainly in dictatorships.
3158.m: Political prisoners are jailed for their opinions.

3159.q: What does the ‘double majority’ mean for a change to the Federal Constitution?
a: It needs both a majority of the voters and a majority of the cantons
It needs twice as many votes as usual
Only the Federal Council decides twice
3159.e: For changes to the constitution, a simple majority of the voters is not enough. A majority of the cantons must also agree.
3159.m: Changing the constitution needs a majority of the people and of the cantons.

3160.q: How does a golden eagle pair usually react when a strange eagle enters its territory?
a: It drives the intruder away with flying manoeuvres
It moves away itself at once
It builds a nest for it
3160.e: Golden eagles actively defend their territory against other eagles, often with impressive flying manoeuvres and loud calls. This protects their hunting ground and their nest site.

3161.q: What was a main cause of the Korean War (1950 to 1953)?
a: The communist North attacked the non-communist South to unite Korea
China and the USA were arguing over Taiwan
The UN wanted to colonise Korea
3161.e: North Korea under Kim Il-sung attacked the South in 1950 to unite the divided country under communist rule. The war ended in 1953 without a winner, with the division that still exists today.
3161.m: The Korean War began when the North attacked the South.

3162.q: What have people traditionally used dromedaries for?
3162.e: Dromedaries carry people and luggage through the desert. They also provide milk and wool.

3163.q: What are most of the ants in a colony?
3163.e: Most ants in a nest are workers. They look for food and build the nest.
3163.m: Workers do most of the work.

3164.q: Who in a wolf pack often looks after the pups, even if it is not their parent?
a: Older brothers and sisters from earlier litters
Always a strange wolf from another pack
Nobody, pups are independent from birth
3164.e: In a wolf pack, older siblings from earlier litters often help raise the little pups. In this way the whole pack learns to share responsibility.

3165.q: How does the beaver keep its fur waterproof?
a: It greases it with an oily substance from a gland
It lets it dry in the sun
It changes its fur every day
3165.e: The beaver regularly grooms its thick fur with an oily substance from special glands. This keeps it water-repellent and keeps the beaver warm in cold water.

3166.q: Which colours are especially common on bumblebees?
3166.e: Most bumblebees have a pattern of black, yellow and white. These colours warn enemies that the bumblebee can sting.
3166.m: Black, yellow and white are typical.

a: No, it is not a fish
Yes, it is a perfectly normal fish
3167.e: Although many people think so, a jellyfish is not a fish. It belongs to a completely different animal group, the cnidarians.
3167.m: A jellyfish is not a fish.

3169.q: Which animal group do spiders, studied by arachnologists, belong to?
3169.e: Spiders are not insects but arachnids with eight legs. Researchers who study spiders are called arachnologists.

3170.q: What is striking about the okapi's face?
a: A pale face with big eyes
3170.e: Its face is paler, its eyes are big and its snout is long. This helps it see well in the dim light of the forest.

3171.q: What role do jackals play in their habitat?
a: They keep small animals in check and clear away carrion
3171.e: By hunting mice and eating carrion, they help keep nature in balance. This keeps habitats clean.
3171.m: Jackals tidy up and control small animals.

3172.q: Why does a wasp sting hurt?
a: Because venom gets into the skin
3172.e: The venom irritates the skin and causes pain and swelling. That is why you feel a sting straight away.

3173.q: In which year did Solothurn become a member of the Old Swiss Confederacy?
3173.e: Solothurn joined the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1481, together with the town of Fribourg.
3173.m: In 1481, Solothurn became part of the Confederation.

3174.q: What does a horse breathe through?
3174.e: Unlike humans, horses cannot breathe through their mouths. They take in air only through their big nostrils.
3174.m: Horses breathe only through their nose.

3175.q: What does it mean when dolphins are called very social animals?
a: They live closely together with other dolphins
They do not like contact with others
3175.e: Social means that dolphins like living, playing and helping each other together. This makes them very sociable animals.
3175.m: Dolphins are sociable and live in groups.

3176.q: How long does the female golden eagle incubate the eggs?
3176.e: Golden eagle incubation lasts about 43 to 45 days. During this time it is usually the female that sits on the eggs.

3177.q: Which statement about the leopard compared with the lion and the tiger is true?
a: It is smaller than the lion and the tiger
It is bigger than the tiger
It is the biggest cat in the world
It is the same size as a lynx
3177.e: The leopard is a medium-sized big cat. Lions and tigers are much heavier.
3177.m: The leopard is smaller than the lion and the tiger.

3178.q: How do chimpanzees sometimes move when they are carrying something?
3178.e: When a chimpanzee carries something, it sometimes walks a short way upright on two legs. Normally, though, it moves on all fours.
3178.m: Chimpanzees sometimes walk on two legs.

3179.q: Which South-East Asian country is still ruled by a communist party today?
3179.e: Laos became communist in 1975 and has since been ruled by the Lao People's Revolutionary Party. Like Vietnam and China, it is a one-party state.
3179.m: Laos is still ruled by communists today.

3180.q: What was otter fur often used for in the past?
3180.e: Because of its thick, warm fur, the otter used to be hunted a lot. The fur was made into furs, which greatly reduced the numbers of otters.
3180.m: Hunting for fur hit the otter hard.

3181.q: Roughly how many hours a day does a cow spend eating?
3181.e: Cows spend many hours a day eating and chewing the cud, because grass is not very nutritious. This way they get enough energy.
3181.m: Cows eat for many hours a day.

3183.q: What do slow worms still have in common with their ancestors that had legs?
a: Remains of the shoulder and hip bones are still in their body
They have hidden toes on the outside
They have nothing in common any more
3183.e: Their ancestors had legs, which disappeared over the course of evolution. Remains of bones are still found in the skeleton.
3183.m: Remains of legs survive in the skeleton.

3184.q: How long can an orca stay under water before it has to breathe?
3184.e: Orcas can dive for a few minutes. Then they have to come to the surface to breathe through their blowhole.
3184.m: Orcas dive for a few minutes.

3185.q: What is the wild camel species living in the deserts of Mongolia and China called?
3185.e: The wild Bactrian camel has two humps like the domestic Bactrian camel, but it is a separate species. It now lives only in a few desert areas in Asia.
3185.m: The wild camel lives in Asia's deserts.

3187.q: Which octopus species is known for its strong venom?
3187.e: The blue-ringed octopus is small, but its venom is very dangerous. You can recognise it by the bright blue rings on its skin.

3188.q: What colour is a pupa often, so that it is well camouflaged?
a: Green or brown like its surroundings
3188.e: Many pupae are green or brown. This means they hardly stand out among leaves or on twigs and are protected from enemies.

3189.q: What do we know today about the St Helena giant earwig?
a: It is thought to be extinct
It lives only in caves in the Alps
It was only discovered last year
3189.e: No living one has been found for decades. That is why the species is considered extinct.

3190.q: What happens when buffalo have eaten too much grass in one area?
a: They move on to new pastures
From then on they eat meat
3190.e: Buffalo move on when food gets scarce. This lets the grass recover.
3190.m: Buffalo move on to new pastures.

3191.q: What are the yellow lumps of pollen on a bee's back legs called?
3191.e: These little yellow lumps on a bee's legs are called pollen loads. You can sometimes see them clearly when the bee flies home.

3192.q: What effect does the Alpine salamander's skin poison have on predators?
a: It puts them off, so they often let go
3192.e: The poison in its skin tastes bad and is toxic. That is why many predators quickly let go of the salamander and avoid it afterwards.
3192.m: Its skin poison puts off enemies.

3193.q: Where do sheep in Switzerland often live in summer?
a: On the alpine pasture in the mountains
3193.e: In summer, many Swiss sheep spend their time on the alpine pasture, high up in the mountains. There is lush grass there.
3193.m: Sheep spend the summer on the alp.

3194.q: When catching prey, what job do the spines on a mantis's grasping legs do?
3194.e: The prey is clamped between the lower and upper parts of the leg. The spines stop it from escaping.

3195.q: What does a female cuckoo often do before laying her egg in another bird's nest?
a: She warms the nest up first
3195.e: The female cuckoo often watches another bird's nest for a while before she strikes. That way she knows exactly when the host birds are briefly away.
3195.m: The cuckoo watches the nest first.

3196.q: What does a snail always carry on its back?
3196.e: The snail's shell grows with the snail and protects its soft body. Some kinds of snail have no shell at all.
3196.m: The snail always carries its shell with it.

3197.q: How old do wild kingfishers usually get?
3197.e: Most kingfishers in the wild live only a few years, because many young birds die in their first year. Cold and predators take a heavy toll.
3197.m: Kingfishers usually live only a few years.

3198.q: Which animal group do harbour seals, sea lions and walruses belong to?
3198.e: Harbour seals belong to the pinnipeds, which also include sea lions and walruses. All of them have legs that have turned into flippers.

3199.q: What is the difference between AHV (1st pillar) and the pension fund (2nd pillar)?
a: AHV is basic state insurance for everyone, the pension fund is occupational provision through the employer
Both are exactly the same system
The pension fund is voluntary for everyone without a job
AHV is paid only by the self-employed
3199.e: AHV is the basic state provision that all working people pay into. The pension fund is occupational provision that runs through the employer and gives extra security for your income.
3199.m: AHV is run by the state, the pension fund through work.

3201.q: What kind of animal is the greenshank?
a: A wading bird with long legs
3201.e: The greenshank is a wading bird. With its long, greenish legs it wades through shallow water looking for food.
3201.m: The greenshank is a wading bird.

3202.q: Why can a mole easily turn round in a narrow tunnel?
a: Its fur does not lie in one fixed direction
It is as tiny as an ant
It has a bendy shell on its back
3202.e: A mole's hairs do not point in any fixed direction. So it can dash forwards and backwards through its tunnels without its fur getting in the way.
3202.m: Fur without a set direction helps it turn.

3203.q: How many claws does a tiger have on one front paw?
3203.e: A tiger has five claws on each front paw. They are sharp and help it hold on to prey.
3203.m: A tiger has five claws on each front paw.

3204.q: Since which decade have bearded vultures been reintroduced to the Alps?
3204.e: From 1986, researchers released captive-bred bearded vultures back into the Alps. Since then their numbers have slowly recovered.

3205.q: The scientific name of the stag beetle is Lucanus cervus. What does the Latin word cervus mean?
3205.e: Cervus is Latin for deer. The name fits because the males have jaws like a stag's antlers.

3206.q: Which animal appears alongside a key in the coat of arms of the canton of Geneva?
3206.e: The Geneva coat of arms is divided and shows a black eagle on one side and a golden key on the other. The eagle once stood for the Holy Roman Empire, the key for the Church.
3206.m: Geneva shows an eagle and a key.

3207.q: Roughly how long can an earthworm live?
3207.e: In good conditions, earthworms can live several years. In nature, though, they are often eaten by enemies before they get that old.

3208.q: What does a gander often do to protect his nest and family?
a: He hides quietly in the grass
He flies far away at once
3208.e: The gander guards the nest during the breeding season. If someone comes too close, he often attacks bravely, hissing.
3208.m: The gander bravely defends his nest.

3209.q: What does a goldfish like to eat best?
3209.e: The goldfish is an omnivore and eats plants, small insects and special fish food. Too much food harms it, though.

3211.q: Which family does the okapi belong to?
3211.e: The okapi is the only living close relative of the giraffe. Together they make up the giraffe family.
3211.m: The okapi is the hidden giraffe.

3212.q: Roughly how long is a female African buffalo pregnant?
3212.e: The cow carries her calf for almost a year. Usually only one calf is born.
3212.m: Buffalo cows are pregnant for almost a year.

3213.q: What do drones do in a bee colony?
3213.e: Drones neither help with collecting nor with building. Their only job is to mate with a young queen.

3214.q: What does a tapir's tail look like?
a: With a tuft like a lion's
Long and bare like a rat's
3214.e: Tapirs have only a short, stubby tail. It hardly matters to them.

3215.q: What usually makes a wild boar look clearly different from a pink domestic pig?
a: The wild boar's dark, bristly coat
3215.e: While many domestic pigs look pale and almost hairless, wild boar have a thick, dark coat of bristles. This protects them from cold and thorns in the forest.
3215.m: Wild boar have a thick, dark coat.

3216.q: Which hyena species is fairly rare and lives in southern Africa?
3216.e: The brown hyena lives in southern Africa, especially in dry areas. It has long, shaggy fur.
3216.m: Brown hyenas live in southern Africa.

3217.q: Why do storks usually avoid flying over the open sea?
a: Because there is no warm rising air there
Because they do not like water
Because it is too noisy there
3217.e: Over the sea there are no warm thermals to carry the storks upwards. That is why they prefer to fly over land.
3217.m: There are no thermals over the sea.

3218.q: How many eggs does the female great spotted woodpecker usually lay?
3218.e: The female lays several white eggs in the tree hole. Both parents then share the incubation.
3218.m: She usually lays four to seven eggs.

3219.q: What is special about a dog's nose print?
a: Like a fingerprint, it is unique to each dog
All dogs have the same nose print
Only certain breeds have a nose print
The nose print changes every day
3219.e: The fine pattern on the surface of the nose is different for every dog, much like a human fingerprint. In some countries it is even used for identification.
3219.m: A nose print is as unique as a fingerprint.

3220.q: What do young lions like doing to practise hunting?
a: Playing and play-fighting with each other
3220.e: Play-fighting and practising hunting help young lions become successful hunters later. They learn important skills from their mothers and siblings.

3221.q: In which country does a particularly large part of the world's red kites live?
3221.e: Germany is home to a very large share of the world's red kite population. Protecting this species there is therefore especially important.
3221.m: Germany has a great many red kites.

3222.q: How many cubs does a female leopard usually have per litter?
3222.e: A female leopard usually has two to three cubs, rarely only one. The cubs are born blind.
3222.m: Leopards usually have two to three cubs.

3223.q: How does a tiger mark its territory?
a: With scent marks and scratch marks
3223.e: Tigers leave scent marks and scratch marks on trees to show other tigers where their area begins. That way other tigers know that someone already lives here.
3223.m: Tigers mark their territory with scent.

3224.q: Why are there different seasons on Earth?
a: Because the Earth’s axis is tilted relative to the sun
Because the Earth is sometimes nearer to and sometimes further from the sun
Because the sun goes round the Earth
Because the moon blocks the sunlight
3224.e: The Earth’s axis is slightly tilted. As a result, the sun shines more or less strongly on the northern and southern hemispheres depending on the time of year.
3224.m: The tilt of the Earth’s axis causes the seasons.

3225.q: Which animal group does the Bactrian camel belong to?
3225.e: The Bactrian camel gives birth to live young and feeds them milk. That is why it counts as a mammal.
3225.m: Bactrian camels feed their young milk.

3226.q: Should you bath guinea pigs regularly?
a: No, it is usually not necessary
Yes, in hot water three times a day
3226.e: Guinea pigs groom their own fur and normally do not need bathing. Bathing too often can even harm them and cause stress.
3226.m: Guinea pigs rarely need a bath.

3227.q: Who mainly incubates the eggs in eagle owls?
a: Nobody, the eggs keep themselves warm in the nest
3227.e: In eagle owls, almost only the female incubates. During this time the male brings her food.
3227.m: Female eagle owl incubates, male hunts.

3228.q: Which predator is one of the main enemies of young African buffalo?
3228.e: Lions hunt mainly young, sick or old buffalo. Healthy adults often defend themselves together in the herd.
3228.m: Lions are the buffalo's main enemies.

3229.q: How is the lake trout related to the brown trout?
a: It is the same species but lives in lakes
It is not related at all
It is a cross between brown trout and pike
3229.e: Lake trout and brown trout belong to the same species, Salmo trutta. The lake trout is a form that spends most of its life in a lake.
3229.m: Lake trout and brown trout are closely related.

3230.q: What is one thing hyenas mark their territory with?
3230.e: Hyenas smear a substance from their anal glands onto grass stems. For other hyenas this scent is like a calling card.

3231.q: What does the efficiency of a machine describe?
a: The ratio of useful energy to energy put in
The maximum speed of a machine
3231.e: Efficiency shows how much of the energy put in is actually used for the intended purpose. Some is usually lost as heat or through friction.
3231.m: Efficiency shows the share of energy that is used.

3232.q: Which animals are among the predators of large perch?
3232.e: Perch are hunted by predatory fish such as the pike, by birds such as the cormorant and by the otter. Young perch also fall prey to smaller predators.

3233.q: Where does the folk belief about Seven Sleepers' Day on 27 June come from?
a: From a Christian legend about seven sleeping brothers
From seven weather forecasts a year
From seven farmers who fell asleep
3233.e: Seven Sleepers' Day goes back to an old Christian legend about seven sleeping brothers and has nothing to do with the animal. In German the edible dormouse has the same name, but that is just a coincidence.
3233.m: Seven Sleepers' Day comes from a legend, not the animal.

3234.q: Where do African wild dogs raise their pups?
a: In a burrow, often an old one dug by other animals
In a nest in the trees
In rock crevices high in the mountains
3234.e: Wild dogs often use abandoned burrows of animals such as aardvarks. There the pups are protected.
3234.m: Pups grow up in a burrow.

3235.q: How widespread is the edible frog in Switzerland?
a: It is one of the commonest amphibians
It lives at only one single lake
It was only discovered last year
It lives only in the high Alps above 3,000 metres
3235.e: The edible frog is one of the commonest amphibians in Switzerland and lives in many ponds in the lowlands. It is also often found in garden ponds.
3235.m: The edible frog is a common Swiss amphibian.

3236.q: What does it mean when a species is described as endemic?
a: It occurs naturally only in a particular, limited area
It is found all over the world
3236.e: Endemic species have usually developed on islands or in isolated regions and occur naturally nowhere else. They are often especially vulnerable to environmental change.
3236.m: Endemic species live in only one place.

3237.q: Roughly how heavy is a housefly?
a: Only a few milligrams, so very light
About as heavy as an apple
About as heavy as a cat
3237.e: A housefly weighs only a few milligrams. That is so light you would hardly feel it.
3237.m: Houseflies are as light as a feather.

3238.q: How does an adult brown bear normally live?
a: Mostly alone, roaming a large area
Always in pairs with a partner
In fixed family groups all its life
3238.e: Apart from mothers with cubs, brown bears mostly live alone. Each one roams a large area looking for food.

3239.q: What may adult goldfish do with their newly hatched young?
a: They carry them around in their mouths
3239.e: Goldfish do not look after their young and sometimes even eat the tiny babies. That is why young fish are often kept separately.
3239.m: Goldfish do not care for their young.

3240.q: Why is a bumblebee's fur important for pollination?
a: It only protects it from rain
