3240.e: The bumblebee's fine fur means that lots of pollen sticks to it. In this way it is carried from flower to flower.
3240.m: Fur catches pollen when visiting flowers.

3241.q: Which animal family does the stone marten belong to?
3241.e: Stone martens belong to the mustelid family, together with the badger, otter and stoat. This family has a great many species.

3242.q: What do wood ants especially like to eat?
3242.e: Wood ants hunt small insects. They also like the sweet honeydew made by aphids.
3242.m: Wood ants eat insects and honeydew.

3243.q: Which group of birds does the budgie belong to?
3243.e: The budgie belongs to the large parrot family. It is a small kind of parrot.

3245.q: How can you often recognise a grass snake by its head?
a: By two pale half-moon patches behind the head
By a red cross on its head
By a zigzag band on its back
3245.e: Behind its head, the grass snake usually has two yellowish to whitish patches that look like half-moons. They are often framed by black patches.
3245.m: Pale half-moon patches behind the head.

3246.q: What does it show when lots of earthworms live in a garden?
a: The soil is healthy and fertile
3246.e: Earthworms only like good, loose soil with enough food. So lots of worms are a sign of a healthy garden.
3246.m: Lots of worms show healthy soil.

3247.q: Which sense especially helps the grass snake track down prey?
a: The sense of touch in its wings
3247.e: With its tongue and smelling organ it finds the scent trails of its prey. This helps it at dusk too.
3247.m: Its sense of smell leads it to prey.

3248.q: Which animals are natural enemies of the tawny owl?
3248.e: Bigger birds of prey and owls such as the eagle owl or the goshawk can be dangerous to the tawny owl. Martens sometimes threaten eggs and young too.
3248.m: Eagle owls and goshawks are tawny owl enemies.

3249.q: How long is a wood mouse's tail compared with its body?
a: Almost as long as its body
Much longer than its whole body
It has no tail at all
3249.e: The wood mouse's tail is almost exactly as long as its body. It helps with climbing and keeping its balance.
3249.m: The tail is almost as long as the body.

3250.q: Which animal miaows and is one of the most popular pets in Switzerland?
3250.e: The cat is the most common pet in Switzerland. Many cats go outdoors and hunt little mice.
3250.m: The cat is a popular Swiss pet.

3251.q: Apart from their lungs, how else do adult fire salamanders breathe?
a: Through an air hole in their back
3251.e: The thin, moist skin takes in extra oxygen. That is why the skin must always stay moist.

3252.q: How long do young mute swans usually stay with their parents?
3252.e: The young often stay with their parents until the autumn. After that they become independent and find their own areas.
3252.m: The young stay with their parents for months.

3253.q: What are a hamster's babies called?
3253.e: Baby hamsters are called pups, as with many other small animals. They are born naked and blind.

3254.q: Which ape is the biggest in the world?
3254.e: Of all the apes and monkeys alive today, the gorilla is the biggest and heaviest. The males in particular grow huge.
3254.m: The gorilla is the biggest ape.

3255.q: What is a young elk (moose) called?
3255.e: Young elk are called calves. Fawn is used for young deer such as roe deer.

3256.q: Where does the edible dormouse prefer to build its nest?
a: In tree holes or nest boxes
3256.e: Edible dormice like to use natural tree holes or nest boxes put up by people as their nest. There they are well protected.

3257.q: What does a pecking order mean in a group of dogs?
a: A social order of who gives way to whom
The order in which they eat people
3257.e: Groups of dogs have social structures that used to be strongly compared with the pack behaviour of wolves. Newer research shows that these relationships are more complex and flexible than once thought.
3257.m: A pecking order shapes how dogs live together.

3258.q: On which continent do particularly large locust swarms often occur?
3258.e: Large locust swarms form especially often in hot, dry parts of Africa. There they can cause farmers many problems.

3259.q: Which animal group does the red squirrel belong to?
3259.e: The red squirrel is a rodent. Rodents typically have front teeth that keep growing all the time.

3260.q: Which animal has a very long neck so it can eat the highest leaves?
3260.e: The giraffe is the tallest land animal in the world and has a neck up to two metres long. This lets it reach leaves high up in the treetops.
3260.m: The giraffe has the longest neck.

3261.q: How does the Roman snail pull in its tentacles when it gets a fright?
a: It turns them inside out, like the finger of a glove
3261.e: The tentacles can be pulled inwards like the finger of a glove turned inside out. This protects the snail's sensitive eyes.
3261.m: Tentacles turn inside out in danger.

3262.q: Roughly how long does it take for a tadpole to become a fully formed frog?
a: A few weeks to a few months
3262.e: Depending on the water temperature, the change from tadpole to little frog takes several weeks to a few months. After that the young frogs leave the water.
3262.m: The change takes weeks to months.

3263.q: How does the tawny owl usually spend the day?
a: It rests hidden and well camouflaged against a tree trunk
It bathes in water for hours
It flies long distances through the town
3263.e: During the day the tawny owl usually sits motionless close to a tree trunk, where its feathers camouflage it perfectly. It only becomes active at dusk.
3263.m: The tawny owl rests camouflaged on a trunk by day.

3264.q: What is an adult female sheep called?
3264.e: An adult female sheep is called a ewe. She takes loving care of her lambs.
3264.m: A female sheep is called a ewe.

a: A popular uprising against the communist government was crushed by Soviet troops
3265.e: In autumn 1956 many people in Hungary rose up against communist rule. The Soviet Union sent tanks to end the uprising.
3265.m: In 1956 the Soviets crushed the Hungarian Uprising.

3267.q: What other name do baboons have because of their snout?
3267.e: Their snout looks like a dog's head. That is why baboons are also known as dog-faced monkeys.
3267.m: Baboons are also called dog-faced monkeys.

3268.q: What does ‘cold-blooded’ mean for the sand lizard?
a: Its body temperature depends strongly on its surroundings
It can change its colour as it likes
It is born warm and cold by turns
It changes its whole skin every year
3268.e: Cold-blooded animals warm up by sunbathing, for example, and cool down again in the shade. This sets them apart from mammals and birds.
3268.m: In the cold-blooded sand lizard, body temperature follows the surroundings.

3269.q: When do male reindeer usually shed their antlers?
a: After the rutting season, in winter
3269.e: The males often lose their antlers in early to midwinter. The females keep theirs longer, usually until after their calves are born.

3270.q: Which animal usually has finer wool than the llama?
3270.e: The alpaca is known for especially fine wool. It is smaller than the llama.
3270.m: Alpacas give finer wool than llamas.

3271.q: Why do bumblebees only very rarely sting people?
a: They are peaceful and only sting when pestered
They have no sting at all
3271.e: Bumblebees are naturally calm creatures. They only sting if you grab them firmly or disturb their nest.

3272.q: Which North American predator was brought to Europe for fur farms and now partly lives in the wild?
3272.e: The American mink was bred on fur farms in Europe because of its fur. Some escaped or were released and now live in the wild. The otter, badger and stoat are native to Europe.
3272.m: The American mink went wild in Europe.

3273.q: What are alpacas mainly kept for?
3273.e: Alpaca wool is soft, warm and fine. It is used to make jumpers, hats and socks, for example.

3274.q: How does a goat kid usually call for its mother?
3274.e: Kids bleat when they are looking for their mother or are hungry. The mother goat recognises the voice of her own kid.
3274.m: Kids call their mother by bleating.

3275.q: What stands up on your skin when you get goose bumps?
3275.e: When it is cold, tiny muscles in the skin tighten. Then the tiny hairs stand up, and the skin looks like that of a plucked goose.
3275.m: With goose bumps, the tiny hairs stand up.

3276.q: Where does a koala mother first carry her baby?
3276.e: Like other marsupials, the koala mother carries her tiny baby in a pouch on her belly. There it drinks milk and grows.
3276.m: Koala babies first grow in the pouch.

3277.q: What does a polar bear usually do when it meets a person?
a: It usually keeps out of their way
It follows them like a dog
It lies down and falls asleep
3277.e: Polar bears normally prefer to avoid people. Only very hungry polar bears can become dangerous.

3278.q: What happens to a mute swan's feathers as it gets older?
3278.e: Young grey swans gradually lose their grey feathers. As adults they are then brilliant white.
3278.m: Over time the grey turns white.

3279.q: Which big cat is the fastest over short distances?
3279.e: The cheetah is the fastest land animal in the world and briefly reaches over 100 km/h. Leopards, lions and tigers are much slower.
3279.m: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

3280.q: How does the sand lizard most likely spot prey such as insects?
a: It sees the movement with its good eyes and snaps in a flash
It waits motionless for days without looking
It hears prey only with huge ears
It smells prey kilometres away with its nose
3280.e: The sand lizard's eyesight is well suited to bright daylight. Moving prey is spotted quickly and hunted.
3280.m: Good eyes help it spot prey.

3281.q: What can butterflies see especially well with their compound eyes?
3281.e: A butterfly's eyes are very sensitive to movement. Many species can even see colours that humans cannot.

3282.q: Are most species of shark dangerous to humans?
a: Yes, every shark is very dangerous
No, there are no dangerous sharks
3282.e: Only very few of the many shark species can be dangerous to humans. Most sharks actually avoid people.
3282.m: Most sharks are harmless to humans.

3283.q: Why does the tawny owl sometimes benefit from nest boxes put up by people?
a: Because natural tree holes have become rare in some forests
Because otherwise it cannot breed anywhere
Because nest boxes protect it from mice
Because it learns to fly with them
3283.e: Tidy forests with few old trees often lack natural holes. Artificial nest boxes then give the tawny owl an important alternative place to breed.
3283.m: Nest boxes help the tawny owl breed.

3284.q: How does a ladybird usually react when you touch it very gently?
a: It pulls in its legs and plays dead
3284.e: Many ladybirds briefly play dead and pull their legs tight against their body. They hope the supposed enemy will lose interest.

3285.q: What is a group of giraffes usually called?
3285.e: Giraffes live together in loose herds. In English a group is sometimes also called a tower, because giraffes are so tall.
3285.m: A group of giraffes is called a herd.

3286.q: Roughly how old can a great crested grebe get in the wild?
3286.e: In the wild, great crested grebes can live surprisingly long, often 15 to 20 years. This depends a lot on food and habitat.
3286.m: Great crested grebes can live up to 20 years.

3287.q: Roughly how fast can a red deer run?
3287.e: Red deer can run very fast, up to 60 km/h. This way they escape danger.
3287.m: Red deer run up to 60 km/h.

3289.q: What colour is an adult wild boar's coat usually?
3289.e: Adult wild boar usually have a dark, brown to black coat. This camouflages them well in the forest.

3290.q: What do the annual rings in a tree trunk show?
a: They show the age of the tree
They show how much rain there will be tomorrow
They show the size of the leaves
3290.e: Each annual ring comes from one year’s growth, wider in spring and narrower in autumn. If you count the rings, you know how old the tree is.
3290.m: Annual rings reveal the age of a tree.

3291.q: How closely is the red panda related to the giant panda?
a: Hardly at all, it belongs to a family of its own
Very closely, it is a dwarf giant panda
It belongs to the cat family
3291.e: Although both are called pandas and eat bamboo, they are not closely related. The red panda belongs to a family of its own, the giant panda to the bears.
3291.m: Red and giant pandas are not closely related.

3292.q: What colour is the white stork's beak?
3292.e: The white stork's long beak is bright red. It uses it to catch its food.

3293.q: What is meant by a monoculture in farming?
a: Growing just one plant species over a large area
Growing many different plant species together
A forest with many animal species
3293.e: In a monoculture only one plant species is grown over large areas, for example only maize. This can exhaust the soil and reduce biodiversity.
3293.m: In a monoculture only one plant species is grown.

3294.q: What danger does lead ammunition pose to red kites?
a: They can be poisoned by lead in shot carrion
They mistake lead for food for their young
They build lead into their nests
Lead stops them from breeding for ever
3294.e: When red kites eat the carcasses of animals shot with lead ammunition, small fragments of lead can end up in their bodies and poison them. That is why lead-free ammunition is recommended.
3294.m: Lead ammunition can poison red kites.

3295.q: What is the typical body shape of the least weasel?
a: Long and slim with short legs
With a long neck like a giraffe
3295.e: Its long, slim body is perfectly suited to hunting in narrow tunnels. Its legs are fairly short.
3295.m: The least weasel is long and slim with short legs.

3296.q: What is the difference between the puma and the lion when it comes to a mane?
a: Only the puma has a mane
3296.e: Male pumas have no mane; only male lions do. This makes the puma and lion easy to tell apart.

3297.q: What happens before a larva becomes a fully grown ant?
a: It stays a larva for ever
3297.e: After the larva comes the pupa stage. Only then does the fully grown ant emerge.
3297.m: After the larva comes the pupa.

3298.q: How old can pet rabbits get?
3298.e: Well cared for pet rabbits often live between eight and twelve years. That is much longer than wild rabbits.

3299.q: Who described the law of gravity, which explains why things fall to the ground?
3299.e: In the 17th century Isaac Newton described how gravity acts between masses. His law of gravitation explains why objects fall to the Earth.

3300.q: What is the general name for fish eggs?
3300.e: The eggs of female fish are called roe. The males' sperm is called milt.

3301.q: Which animals are woodlice closely related to?
3301.e: Woodlice are crustaceans, even though many live on land. Their relatives are crabs, prawns and lobsters.

3302.q: What role do garden ponds play for the alpine newt?
a: They can be important habitats and breeding sites
They are always deadly for it
It lives only in swimming pools
3302.e: Natural garden ponds without fish often give the alpine newt excellent living conditions. Many populations in built-up areas use such man-made ponds for breeding.

3303.q: What does a contented pig sometimes show with its curly tail?
a: It wags it cheerfully to and fro
3303.e: A lively, active tail can be a sign that a pig feels good. A drooping tail, on the other hand, can be a sign that it feels unwell.

3304.q: How do some host birds react when they recognise a strange cuckoo egg?
a: They sometimes throw it out of the nest
They feed it twice as much at once
They build a second nest for it
3304.e: Some host birds recognise a cuckoo egg and throw it out of the nest or abandon the nest completely. That is why the cuckoo egg has to look as much like the host's eggs as possible.
3304.m: Some birds recognise the fake egg.

3305.q: What threatens the polar bear most today?
a: Pack ice melting because of climate change
3305.e: Because global warming means there is less ice, polar bears find it harder to hunt seals. This makes survival more difficult.
3305.m: Melting ice puts polar bears at risk.

3306.q: Roughly how much food does an adult Asian elephant eat each day?
3306.e: Because of its huge body, the elephant needs a lot of food. So it spends a large part of the day eating.
3306.m: Elephants eat over 100 kilograms a day.

3307.q: Where are a dragonfly's wings and legs attached?
3307.e: The thorax carries all six legs and both pairs of wings. It contains the strong flight muscles.
3307.m: Wings and legs are on the thorax.

3308.q: What can you use to see things a little bigger, for example an ant?
3308.e: A magnifying glass has a curved glass that makes small things look bigger. Children often use one to look at insects more closely.
3308.m: A magnifying glass makes small things bigger.

3309.q: How does the golden eagle carry larger prey to its nest?
a: It carries it in its talons while flying
It pushes it up the mountain
It lets the young walk to the prey
It pulls it on a string
3309.e: With its powerful talons, the golden eagle can carry medium-sized prey to its nest in flight. Very heavy prey, though, is often eaten on the spot.
3309.m: Prey is flown to the nest in its talons.

3310.q: Which plants do great crested grebes often use in their courtship dance?
a: Water plants that they show off in their beak
3310.e: During the courtship dance, both partners often dive at the same time and bring water plants to the surface to show each other. This ritual strengthens their bond.
3310.m: Water plants are part of the courtship ritual.

3311.q: How does a fox typically move in snow so that its tracks look almost like a straight line?
a: It puts its back paws exactly in the prints of its front paws
It rolls along like a ball
3311.e: A fox walks in a straight line with its back paws stepping almost exactly into the prints of its front paws. This makes its tracks in the snow look like a narrow, straight line.
3311.m: Fox tracks form a straight line.

3312.q: What often sets a domestic goose apart from a wild goose?
a: Domestic geese hardly fly long distances any more
3312.e: Through breeding, many domestic geese have become heavier and so fly only a little or not at all. Wild geese, on the other hand, fly long distances every year.
3312.m: Domestic geese mostly no longer fly far.

3313.q: Roughly how long is a marmot mother pregnant?
3313.e: After mating in spring, the female carries her young for about five weeks. Then the young are born in the burrow.
3313.m: Baby marmots develop for about five weeks.

3314.q: How do you often first notice a kingfisher flying past?
a: By a flash of blue over the water
By its shadow on the ground
3314.e: Because of its speed and colour, you often see only a blue flash shooting past over the water. Only afterwards do you realise it was a kingfisher.
3314.m: A fast blue flash over the water.

3315.q: Why is the cockchafer called the ‘May bug’?
a: Because it usually appears in May
Because it eats eggs in May
Because it is named after a Mr May
3315.e: The beetles emerge in spring and often fly in May. That is where the name comes from.
3315.m: The name comes from its flying season in May.

3316.q: What does the elephant need its trunk for?
3316.e: The trunk is both nose and hand. The elephant can use it to suck up water, grab branches and smell.
3316.m: The trunk is the elephant's most important tool.

3317.q: What especially threatens the habitat of the European tree frog?
a: The loss of natural ponds and pools
3317.e: Many small bodies of water have been drained or built over. Without suitable ponds, the tree frog can no longer breed.
3317.m: Fewer ponds put the tree frog at risk.

3318.q: What do many mallards in Switzerland do in winter?
a: They often stay here if the water does not freeze
They sleep through the whole winter
3318.e: Many mallards stay in Switzerland all year round. Only when the water freezes do they look for other open water.
3318.m: Some ducks stay here in winter.

3319.q: Roughly how long is an adult magpie, including its tail?
3319.e: An adult magpie measures about 44 to 46 centimetres from head to tail tip. A large part of this length is its long tail.

3320.q: Is the common earwig poisonous to humans?
a: Yes, it has a poisonous sting
3320.e: The earwig has no poison. Its pincers are harmless to humans.
3320.m: Earwigs are not poisonous to humans.

3321.q: How many young does a mother shark usually have at once?
a: Only a few, often fewer than ten
Only one in her whole life
3321.e: Compared with many other fish, sharks have only a few young. In return, the babies are bigger and stronger from the start.
3321.m: Sharks have only a few young.

3322.q: How many toes does a chicken usually have on each foot?
3322.e: A chicken normally has four toes on each foot. Three point forwards, one points backwards.
3322.m: A chicken's foot has four toes.

3323.q: What is the process called by which the kidney regulates the body's water and salt balance?
3323.e: In osmoregulation, the kidney controls how much water and salt stay in the body or are excreted. This keeps the make-up of the blood stable.
3323.m: The kidney regulates water and salt.

3324.q: What does a common wall lizard's habitat absolutely need?
a: Hiding places such as stone piles and cracks in walls
3324.e: Stone piles and cracks in walls give protection from enemies and cold. Without such hiding places the wall lizard cannot survive.

3325.q: Which wild duck is the domestic duck descended from?
3325.e: Almost all the domestic ducks we know are originally descended from the wild mallard. People tamed them long ago.
3325.m: Domestic ducks come from the mallard.

3326.q: What makes the Alpine salamander's way of producing young very different from most frogs?
a: There is no larval stage living in water
It mates only once in its life
It does not have young at all
3326.e: While frogs usually lay spawn in water and go through a tadpole stage, the Alpine salamander gives birth to fully developed young. This means it does not depend on ponds or streams.
3326.m: Unlike frogs, the Alpine salamander has no water larvae.

3328.q: Since which year has Switzerland been a member of the UN?
3328.e: For a long time Switzerland stayed out of the UN because of its neutrality. Only after a referendum did it officially join in 2002.

3329.q: What does it mean that jackals are also scavengers?
3329.e: Carrion means dead animals. Jackals like to eat it, for example the leftovers of large predators' prey.
3329.m: Carrion is dead animals, which jackals also eat.

3331.q: Is the mute swan a protected animal in Switzerland?
3331.e: The mute swan is protected in Switzerland. This means you must not simply catch or disturb it.

3332.q: How long is the deadline for calling an optional referendum against a federal law?
3332.e: After a law is published, its opponents have 100 days to collect signatures.
3332.m: You have 100 days for a referendum.

3333.q: What do you call the direct change from solid to gas without a substance becoming liquid?
3333.e: In sublimation, a solid turns directly into a gas, like dry ice, for example, which simply disappears into the air. There is no liquid stage in between.
3333.m: In sublimation, a solid turns directly into a gas.

3334.q: How do orcas communicate with each other?
3334.e: Orcas make many different sounds to communicate. Each family even has its own calls.

3335.q: Which animal group does the praying mantis belong to?
3335.e: The praying mantis has six legs and a body divided into three parts. These are typical features of insects.
3335.m: Praying mantises are insects with six legs.

3336.q: What is the normal body temperature of a healthy cat?
a: About 42 degrees Celsius in every cat
3336.e: At 38 to 39 degrees, a cat's normal body temperature is a little higher than a human's. This is part of the animal's normal metabolism.
3336.m: Cats are a little warmer than humans.

3337.q: What helps a mute swan swim so well?
3337.e: The mute swan has webbing between its toes, like paddles. This lets it move powerfully through the water.

3338.q: What was the aim of the Kyoto Protocol?
a: To commit countries to reducing greenhouse gases
To redraw the borders between states
To regulate world trade in oil
To secure peace between Japan and the USA
3338.e: The Kyoto Protocol was an international agreement under which industrial states were to cut their greenhouse gas emissions. It was an important forerunner of the later Paris Climate Agreement.
3338.m: Kyoto committed states to protecting the climate.

3339.q: What does a young worker honeybee do first?
3339.e: Young bees first work inside the hive and clean the honeycomb. Only later in life do they fly out to collect nectar.
3339.m: Bees have different jobs depending on their age.

3340.q: Besides insects, what else does a hedgehog like to eat?
3340.e: Hedgehogs are not fussy and also like eating earthworms, beetle larvae and small spiders. This makes them useful insect eaters.
3340.m: Hedgehogs also eat worms and larvae.

3341.q: What do you hear music and voices with?
3341.e: Your ears catch sound waves and pass them on to the brain. There they become sounds and words.

3342.q: Do ants have ears to hear with?
a: Yes, big ears on their head
Yes, but only on their belly
No, they hear with their eyes
3342.e: Ants do not have ears like we humans do. They sense shaking and vibrations through their body.

3343.q: What makes the bearded vulture look different from most other European vultures?
3343.e: Unlike many vultures with a rounded tail, the bearded vulture has a strikingly long, wedge-shaped tail. You can recognise it by this from far away.
3343.m: Its tail is long and wedge-shaped.

3344.q: What is the job of the pale patch on the rump of a fleeing roe deer?
a: It warns other deer of danger
3344.e: When a roe deer flees, its pale rump patch is easy to see. This lets other deer know that danger is near.
3344.m: The rump patch warns other deer.

3345.e: With white storks, the mother and father take turns sitting on the eggs. That way both can also go and find food.

3346.q: What does a red deer stag need its antlers for?
a: To impress other stags and to fight
3346.e: A stag shows its strength with its antlers. In autumn, stags sometimes use them to fight over the females.
3346.m: Antlers show strength in a fight.

3347.q: Roughly how far can a lynx jump?
3347.e: The lynx's powerful back legs allow long jumps. This helps it make surprise attacks on prey.
3347.m: A lynx jumps far and powerfully.

a: At the tip of an arm
3348.e: A starfish's mouth sits right in the middle of its underside. It eats its prey from there.
3348.m: The mouth is underneath, in the middle.

3349.q: How many young does a mother hedgehog usually have at once?
3349.e: A mother hedgehog usually gives birth to four or five hoglets. She looks after her young on her own.
3349.m: Hedgehog mothers usually have four or five young.

3350.q: What sound does a cow make?
3350.e: Cows make a deep sound called mooing. They use it to talk to each other or to their calf.

3351.q: How do reindeer get to their food under the snow in winter?
a: They dig tunnels with their antlers
They wait for the snow to melt
3351.e: Reindeer scrape the snow away with their broad hooves. They can smell the lichens even under the snow.

3352.q: How common is the tawny owl in Switzerland compared with other owls?
a: It is the commonest owl in Switzerland
It does not live in Switzerland at all
3352.e: The tawny owl is considered the commonest and most widespread owl in Switzerland. It lives in many forests, parks and even towns.
3352.m: The tawny owl is the commonest Swiss owl.

3353.q: What do magpies do when they find more food than they can eat at once?
a: They just leave it lying there
They always give it to other animals
3353.e: Magpies often hide extra food in different places so they can come back to it later. This behaviour is called food storing or caching.

3354.q: How many legs does an insect such as a beetle or an ant have?
3354.e: All insects have exactly six legs. That sets them apart from spiders, for example, which have eight. Insects also have a body in three parts.

3355.q: What is special about giraffes' blood pressure?
a: It is much higher than in most other animals
It is much lower than in all animals
Giraffes have no blood pressure at all
It is exactly like a mouse's
3355.e: Because the blood has to be pumped so far up to the head, giraffes have very high blood pressure. Their heart and blood vessels are especially strong because of this.
3355.m: Giraffes have very high blood pressure.

3356.q: What is meant by the greenhouse effect?
a: Gases in the atmosphere keep heat on Earth
The sun comes closer to the Earth every year
It makes the Earth spin faster
3356.e: Certain gases such as CO2 let sunlight through to the Earth but hold back the heat radiation that the Earth gives off again. Without this natural effect, it would be much colder on Earth.
3356.m: Greenhouse gases keep heat in the atmosphere.

3357.q: What is the great spotted woodpecker especially good at?
3357.e: The great spotted woodpecker hacks holes in wood with its hard beak. This is how it finds food and makes its nest hole.

3358.q: What is a good hiding place for an adder?
3358.e: There it finds warmth and shelter. That is why stone piles are important for nature conservation.

3359.q: Which language does the word ‘hippopotamus’ come from?
3359.e: Hippopotamus comes from Greek: hippos means horse and potamos means river. So the word means ‘river horse’.
3359.m: Hippopotamus is Greek for river horse.

3360.q: What does the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), based in Geneva, deal with?
a: Worldwide rules for telecommunications and the internet
3360.e: The ITU coordinates technical standards for telephone, radio and the internet worldwide. It is one of the oldest international organisations and is based in Geneva.
3360.m: The ITU sets the rules for communications technology worldwide.

3361.q: What does the word ‘pest’ mean for greenfly in the garden?
a: They harm crops and weaken them
They are always poisonous to humans
3361.e: Pests are animals that damage plants or harvests. In nature, though, greenfly also play a part as food for other animals.
3361.m: A pest is an animal that harms crops.

3362.q: Which colour of clothes do mosquitoes often especially like?
3362.e: Mosquitoes often spot dark clothes more easily than light ones. That is why people in dark T-shirts sometimes get bitten more often.

3363.q: What does a wild hamster build for itself underground?
3363.e: Wild hamsters dig deep burrows with several tunnels and chambers. There they sleep and store their food.

3364.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
3364.e: In 1969 the American Neil Armstrong became the first person to step onto the Moon. His famous words were: “That’s one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind.”
3364.m: Neil Armstrong was the first to walk on the Moon.

3365.q: What is the group of young males that do not live in the main herd called?
3365.e: Older or young bulls often form their own groups. They join the herd mainly in the mating season.

3366.q: Which sense is especially important for the puma when hunting at night?
a: Good eyesight even in low light
3366.e: Cats can see much better in the dark than humans. This helps the puma hunt at dusk and at night.
3366.m: Pumas see well in the dark.

3367.q: How does its wide head help the hammerhead shark?
a: It helps it see and sense better
It helps it hide in the sand
3367.e: Because the head is so wide, the eyes and sense organs are far apart. This lets the hammerhead notice more of its surroundings.
3367.m: The wide head helps it sense and see.

a: Live or from an egg, depending on the species
Always from eggs in the sand on the beach
3368.e: Depending on the shark species, the young are born live or hatch from eggs. Both happen among sharks.
3368.m: Baby sharks hatch from eggs or are born live.

3370.q: In which canton did women get the cantonal right to vote as early as 1959, well before the rest of Switzerland?
3370.e: In 1959 the canton of Vaud became the first canton in Switzerland to introduce women's suffrage at cantonal level. National women's suffrage only followed in 1971.
3370.m: In 1959 Vaud was the first canton to introduce women's suffrage.

3371.q: How long can a male emperor penguin go without food while keeping the egg warm?
3371.e: While the male keeps the egg warm, he eats nothing and lives off his fat. This can last many weeks until the female comes back.
3371.m: Male emperor penguins go hungry for weeks for the egg.

3372.q: Why are many seahorse species under threat today?
a: They are caught and sold as souvenirs or medicine
They cannot cope with salt water
3372.e: People catch many seahorses to sell, for example as souvenirs or for traditional medicine. This is making some species rarer and rarer.
3372.m: Being caught threatens many seahorse species.

3373.q: In which habitats on land does the common frog feel especially at home?
a: Only in snow high in the mountains
3373.e: The common frog likes damp, shady places such as woods, meadows and gardens with ponds. There it finds enough food and hiding places.
3373.m: Common frogs like damp, green places.

a: The highest law of a state, which sets out rights and limits on power.
3374.e: A constitution sets out how a state is organised and what rights citizens have. In dictatorships the constitution is often ignored or changed.

3375.q: Do goldfish have eyelids that let them close their eyes?
3375.e: Goldfish have no eyelids, so they cannot close their eyes. That is why they sleep with their eyes open.
3375.m: Goldfish sleep with their eyes open.

3376.q: How does the swift usually catch its prey?
a: With its beak wide open, in mid-flight
By pecking for insects on the ground
By diving into the water like a kingfisher
With its talons like a bird of prey
3376.e: While flying, the swift opens its beak wide and scoops up small insects in mid-air. This way of hunting suits its life in the air perfectly.
3376.m: Prey is caught in flight with an open beak.

3377.q: What sound does a dog normally make?
3377.e: Barking is the typical sound dogs use to communicate, for example to give a warning. Some dogs also howl or growl.
3377.m: Dogs bark to make themselves heard.

3378.q: Why are many female ducks' feathers rather brown and plain?
a: For camouflage while sitting on the nest
Because females do not like colourful feathers
3378.e: The brown, speckled feathers help the mother duck hide on the nest. This gives the eggs better protection from enemies.
3378.m: Brown feathers camouflage her while she incubates.

3379.q: How can you best tell the difference between a white and a black rhino?
a: By the shape of the mouth
By the colour of the fur
By the size of the ears
By the length of the tail
3379.e: The white rhino has a broad, flat mouth for eating grass. The black rhino has a pointed lip for eating leaves.
3379.m: The mouth shows which rhino it is.

3380.q: In which habitats can you find the great tit in Switzerland?
3380.e: The great tit lives in woods, parks and gardens. It is even found in the middle of towns if there are trees.
3380.m: Great tits live in woods and gardens.

3381.q: Which animal is the African wild dog more closely related to than to the hyena?
3381.e: Wild dogs belong to the dog family, so they are related to wolves. Hyenas belong to a family of their own.
3381.m: Related to the wolf, not the hyena.

a: They are among the more primitive primates
They have only half as many teeth
They are only half as big as humans
They live only half the year
3383.e: Lemurs show many features of early primates, such as a moist nose. That is why they are grouped apart from monkeys and apes.

3384.q: What is the firm case that some moth caterpillars pupate inside called?
3384.e: Before pupating, some caterpillars spin a cocoon of silk threads around themselves. Inside it they are well protected.

3385.q: Which animals are the hippopotamus's closest living relatives?
3385.e: Strange as it sounds, whales and dolphins are the hippo's closest relatives. They share common ancestors.
3385.m: Whales are related to the hippo.

3386.q: What does a bonobo mainly eat?
3386.e: Fruit makes up most of its diet. It also eats leaves, shoots and other plant parts.

3387.q: Why is the kingfisher seen as a sign of good water quality?
a: Because it only finds enough fish in clean, natural waters
Because it survives only in chemically cleaned water
Because it drinks and tests the water directly
Because anglers use it to check the water
3387.e: Only clean water has enough small fish for the kingfisher. So if it lives there, that shows the water is healthy.
3387.m: Kingfishers show that water is clean.

3388.q: Which animals can be dangerous to swan cygnets?
3388.e: Small cygnets are not yet as big and strong as their parents. Foxes or large fish can be dangerous to them.
3388.m: Foxes are a danger to cygnets.

3389.q: Why is the sand lizard a good example of species protection in Switzerland?
a: Because it shows how important natural, dry habitats are for many species
Because it is the only protected reptile in Switzerland
Because it has died out in Switzerland
Because it lives in every Swiss garden
3389.e: Protecting the sand lizard's habitat often helps many other animals and plants that need similar conditions. That is why it is seen as an important species in nature conservation.
3389.m: Protecting it helps other species too.

3390.q: Why did people once take chamois to faraway countries such as New Zealand?
a: So they could be hunted there
So they could herd sheep there
So they could eat weeds in gardens
3390.e: Chamois were released in New Zealand, for example, so that hunters could hunt them there. Today wild populations live there.

3391.q: What do stork partners do when they meet again at the nest?
a: They clatter their beaks together as a greeting
They fly away again at once
They build a new nest somewhere else at once
3391.e: When a stork partner comes back to the nest, both greet each other by loudly clattering their beaks together. This strengthens their bond.
3391.m: A greeting with shared beak clattering.

3392.q: Why are many garden owners in Switzerland pleased to have edible frogs in their garden pond?
a: Because they are natural pest controllers and bring life to the pond
3392.e: Edible frogs eat lots of insects and so help keep a natural balance in the garden. Their calls and behaviour also bring a garden pond to life.
3392.m: Edible frogs liven up garden ponds naturally.

3393.q: What is a pond turtle's shell made of?
a: Bony plates covered with horny scutes
Only hard scales that can be shed
3393.e: The shell is firmly joined to the skeleton, for example to the ribs. That is why a turtle can never climb out of its shell.
3393.m: The shell is part of the skeleton.

3395.q: Roughly how long is a female wolf pregnant before her pups are born?
3395.e: A she-wolf's pregnancy lasts about 63 days, so about nine weeks. Then usually several pups are born at the same time.
3395.m: She-wolves carry their pups for about nine weeks.

3396.q: What does a grasshopper use to jump so far?
3396.e: The back legs are much stronger than the other legs. They work like springs.
3396.m: Strong back legs make the jump.

3397.q: Which African country is known as the place where Jane Goodall studied chimpanzees?
3397.e: Jane Goodall studied chimpanzees in Gombe National Park in Tanzania. She watched the animals there for many years.
3397.m: Tanzania is known for Jane Goodall's research.

3398.q: How does a housefly manage to land on the ceiling?
a: It turns over in the air just before landing
It sticks spit on its feet first
3398.e: Just before a housefly reaches the ceiling, it flips over in the air in a flash. This lets it land feet first.

3399.q: How does the bearded vulture's feeding differ from the golden eagle's hunting?
a: The bearded vulture hardly hunts at all but eats dead animals
The bearded vulture hunts only live fish
The bearded vulture hunts only at night
The bearded vulture eats only plants
3399.e: Golden eagles often catch live animals themselves, while the bearded vulture mainly uses carrion and bones. So it is more of a scavenger than a hunter.
3399.m: The bearded vulture scavenges instead of hunting.

3400.q: Which animal group do whitefish belong to?
3400.e: Whitefish have a skeleton made of bone and breathe with gills. That is why they belong to the bony fish.

3402.q: Why do squirrels have to gnaw all the time?
a: Because otherwise their teeth fall out
3402.e: A squirrel's front teeth keep growing throughout its life. Gnawing keeps them at the right length.

3403.q: What is the famous children's story whose main character was originally a roe deer?
3403.e: The story of Bambi was written by Felix Salten and is really about a roe deer. In the famous Disney film, though, Bambi looks a bit different.
3403.m: Bambi was originally a roe deer.

3404.q: Roughly how old can a sheep get?
3404.e: A sheep lives about 10 to 12 years. With good care some sheep can live even longer.

3405.q: How does a great crested grebe usually react when an enemy surprises it?
a: It dives instead of flying away
It attacks the enemy at once
It freezes motionless in the water
3405.e: Because diving is quicker than taking off, the great crested grebe usually escapes under water. There it is also hard to see.
3405.m: In danger it prefers to dive.

3406.q: How fast can a pet cat run?
3406.e: Over short distances, a pet cat can run at up to 48 km/h. That is usually enough to catch a mouse.
3406.m: Cats can sprint very fast for a short time.

3407.q: How do young meerkats learn to eat dangerous prey such as scorpions?
a: Adults first bring them made-safe prey and practise with them
They read about it in books
They learn it alone, by chance
They are never allowed to eat scorpions
3407.e: Older meerkats first bring the young dead prey or prey with the sting removed. Later the young practise with live prey.
3407.m: Adults teach the young to hunt.

3408.q: What is the force between two electrically charged particles called?
3408.e: The Coulomb force describes the attraction or repulsion between electric charges. Like charges repel, opposite charges attract.
3408.m: Charges attract or repel each other.

3409.q: Since when have golden hamsters been kept as pets?
3409.e: People only started breeding golden hamsters as pets in the 1930s. Before that they were known only from the wild in Syria.
3409.m: Hamsters have only been pets since about 1930.

3410.q: What colour is the great tit's back?
3410.e: The great tit's back shimmers greenish to olive. This lets it hide well among leaves.

3412.q: What happens to a male octopus after mating?
a: It becomes a father and helps out
It looks for a new den
3412.e: Many male octopuses die only a short time after mating. This is part of their short life cycle.

3413.q: Where does the red kite often look for food when farmers mow their fields?
3413.e: Mowing disturbs or injures small animals such as mice or insects. The red kite takes advantage of this and circles over the fields.
3413.m: Red kites like to hunt over mown meadows.

3414.q: In which waters does the edible frog like to live best?
3414.e: Edible frogs prefer ponds, pools and lakes with calm water. There they find enough plants and food.
3414.m: The edible frog likes calm, still water.

3415.q: Are guinea pigs closely related to rabbits?
a: No, they belong to different animal groups
Yes, they are practically the same species
Yes, rabbits are their direct parents
Yes, they can have babies together
3415.e: Even though guinea pigs and rabbits are often kept in a similar way, they are not closely related biologically. Rabbits even belong to a completely different group, the lagomorphs.
3415.m: Guinea pigs are not related to rabbits.

3416.q: How many legs does an ant have?
3416.e: Ants are insects. All insects have exactly six legs.

3417.q: Which creature is closely related to the stag beetle?
3417.e: The lesser stag beetle is a smaller relative in the stag beetle family. It also lives in dead wood.
3417.m: Lesser stag beetles are relatives of the stag beetle.

3418.q: Why does the cuckoo chick sometimes hatch faster than the host bird's eggs?
a: So it can be first to throw the other eggs out
Because it is incubated at a colder temperature
3418.e: Hatching early gives the cuckoo chick an advantage, because it can then throw the other unhatched eggs out of the nest first. This way it gets all the food for itself.
3418.m: Hatching early gives the cuckoo an advantage.

3420.q: Do sparrows prefer to live alone or with others?
3420.e: Sparrows are sociable birds and like living in larger groups. Together they are better protected from enemies.

3421.q: How many wings does a bumblebee have?
3421.e: A bumblebee has two pairs of wings, so four wings in all. With them it can even carry heavy loads such as pollen.

3422.q: How did the rule of the Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu end?
a: In 1989 he was overthrown in a revolution and executed
He resigned voluntarily and went into exile
He ruled until he died of old age
The EU made him an honorary citizen
3422.e: At the end of 1989 there was a violent uprising against Ceaușescu in Romania. He and his wife were shot after a short trial.

3423.q: What is the typical leap a fox uses to catch a mouse under the snow called?
3423.e: In the mousing pounce, the fox jumps high into the air and then dives nose first into the snow. This lets it surprise the mouse from above.
3423.m: The catching leap is called the mousing pounce.

3424.q: What affectionate name is the white stork sometimes given in old German stories?
3424.e: In old tales the stork is sometimes called Adebar. This name comes from earlier forms of the German language.
3424.m: Adebar is an old name for the stork.

3425.q: Why do dromedaries live in Australia today?
a: They were brought in as pack animals in the 19th century
They were released as zoo animals
3425.e: They were brought to Australia to carry goods through the desert. Later many were set free and went wild.
3425.m: They came to Australia as pack animals.

3426.q: In which year did East and West Germany become one country again?
3426.e: One year after the fall of the Wall, the GDR and the Federal Republic of Germany were reunited. That was on 3 October 1990.

3427.q: Does the stone marten truly hibernate in winter?
a: No, it stays active all year
Yes, it sleeps right through from October to April
Yes, but only for two weeks
No, it migrates to Africa instead
3427.e: Unlike some small mammals, the stone marten does not truly hibernate. It stays active all year round and looks for food in winter too.
3427.m: The stone marten does not hibernate.

3428.q: Where does the bright blue colour of the kingfisher's feathers really come from?
a: From light being scattered by the structure of the feathers
3428.e: The blue does not come from a pigment but from the fine structure of the feathers, which scatters the light. This is called structural colour.
3428.m: The blue comes from light, not pigment.

3429.q: Why do wild boar often churn up the forest floor?
3429.e: Wild boar dig in the soil with their snouts because tasty roots and worms are hidden there. This is also called rooting.
3429.m: Rooting is how they look for food.

3430.q: What must young aphids do in order to grow?
3430.e: Aphids have a firm skin that does not grow with them. So they shed it several times, usually four times before becoming adults.

3431.q: Why do newborn piglets drink their mother's milk straight after birth?
a: The first milk protects them from illness
Otherwise they must find food themselves at once
3431.e: The mother's first milk is very special. It protects the little piglets from illness in their first days.
3431.m: The first milk protects young piglets.

3432.q: Are there different species of mole in the world?
a: No, there is only one species
No, moles live only in Switzerland
No, moles live only in Africa
3432.e: There are several different species of mole around the world. Here in Switzerland we have the European mole.
3432.m: There are several mole species worldwide.

3433.q: Roughly how big does an adult ladybird get?
a: About the size of a small pea
As big as a hen's egg
3433.e: Most ladybirds are only a few millimetres long, about the size of a small pea. Even so, they eat an amazing amount.
3433.m: Ladybirds are as small as peas.

3434.q: What job does a meerkat standing upright on a mound have while the others are feeding?
a: It keeps watch and warns the group
It calls the young to play
3434.e: Meerkats take turns as sentries. If the sentry spots an enemy, it warns the group with a loud call.

3435.q: Why do many robins die in their first year?
a: Because of cold, enemies and lack of experience
3435.e: Young robins do not know dangers as well as adult birds. Cold and enemies are especially hard on them.

3436.q: What do young marmots often do before starting a family of their own?
a: They help their parents raise younger brothers and sisters
They leave the colony right after birth
They build their own burrow far away at once
They never live with the family again
3436.e: Young marmots often stay with their family for one or two years. During this time they help raise their younger siblings.

3437.q: What kind of feet does a roe deer have?
a: Cloven hooves, so two toes per foot
Hooves like a horse with one toe
3437.e: Roe deer are even-toed hoofed animals. Their feet have two toes that together form a hoof.

3438.q: Which woodlouse species is common in gardens in Switzerland?
3438.e: The common rough woodlouse is common in Central Europe. You often find it on walls, under stones and in gardens.
3438.m: The common rough woodlouse is common in gardens.

3439.q: Where does the golden eagle get its English name from?
a: From the golden feathers on the back of its neck
3439.e: Adult golden eagles have feathers on the back of the head and neck that shimmer golden brown. That is where the name golden eagle comes from.
3439.m: Golden neck feathers give it its name.

3440.q: How does a stone marten usually behave towards people?
a: It avoids direct contact and is rather shy
It actively seeks people out for cuddles
It regularly attacks people on purpose
It happily lets people stroke it
3440.e: Although the stone marten often lives near people, it usually stays shy and careful. As a rule it avoids direct contact with humans.

3441.q: Which animal family do the jackal, wolf and domestic dog belong to?
3441.e: The jackal, wolf and domestic dog belong to the dog family. Their scientific genus is called Canis.
3441.m: Jackal, wolf and dog belong to the dog family.

3442.q: How many arms does a sunstar, a large kind of starfish, have?
3442.e: The sunstar is a large starfish with many arms, usually between 8 and 14. This makes it look like a sun with rays.

3443.q: In which season can you see many common frogs crossing roads?
3443.e: As soon as temperatures rise in spring, common frogs start their journey to the ponds. On the way they often have to cross roads.
3443.m: Many common frogs migrate in spring.

3444.q: What does a goose swallow to help grind up plants in its stomach?
3444.e: Geese have no teeth. So they swallow small stones that help grind up the tough plant parts in their stomach.

3445.q: How does a new bee develop?
a: From an egg, via larva and pupa
3445.e: The queen lays an egg in a cell of the honeycomb. A larva hatches from it, later turns into a pupa and finally becomes a fully grown bee.
3445.m: Bees develop from egg to bee.

3446.q: What is a squirrel's nest called?
3446.e: A squirrel's nest is called a drey and is made of twigs, moss and leaves. It is usually high up in a tree.
3446.m: A squirrel's nest is called a drey.

3447.q: When is the wood mouse most active?
a: Only at midday in the sun
Only in the depths of winter
3447.e: The wood mouse is nocturnal and looks for food mainly in the dark.

3448.q: What does a goose's beak look like?
a: Broad, with fine ridges for plucking plants
Pointed and hooked like an eagle's
Geese have no beak at all
3448.e: The broad beak has small ridges along the edge, called lamellae. With them the goose can tear off grass easily and sieve food from the water.
3448.m: A goose's beak has fine ridges.

3449.q: What colour is the red kite's tail compared with the rest of its feathers?
3449.e: The red kite's tail is reddish with fine dark bars across it. Together with its forked shape, this is an important way to recognise it.

3450.q: Which organ produces the hormone insulin?
3450.e: The pancreas makes insulin, which lowers the blood sugar level. It also produces digestive enzymes.

3451.q: What is it called when goat herds come back down from the alpine pasture to the valley in autumn?
3451.e: In autumn it gets too cold on the mountain pastures and the goats move back down to the valley. This is called the Alpabzug.
3451.m: In autumn the goats come down to the valley.

3452.q: How many young does a puma usually have in one litter?
3452.e: Female pumas usually have two or three young, sometimes up to four. They raise them alone.
3452.m: Pumas usually have two or three young.

3453.q: What special adaptation does the Alpine salamander show compared with amphibians from warmer regions?
a: It is adapted to cool temperatures and short summers
It needs very high temperatures to survive
It can live only in deserts
It needs salt water to survive
3453.e: In the mountains, summers are short and temperatures are lower than in the lowlands. Over time the Alpine salamander has adapted to these special conditions.
3453.m: It is adapted to cool mountain conditions.

3454.q: Roughly how old can chamois get in the wild?
3454.e: In the wild, chamois can reach a ripe old age of 15 to 22 years. This also depends on food and enemies, though.

3455.q: Many hundreds of years ago, who often bred carp in ponds?
3455.e: In the past, monks liked to breed carp in ponds near their monasteries. That way they could eat fish on fasting days too.
3455.m: Monks used to breed carp in ponds.

3456.q: How does a male great spotted woodpecker attract a female?
a: With a present made of grass
3456.e: Drumming is like a call to possible partners. The one who drums loudest often has a good chance.

3457.q: Roughly how old can alpine newts get when kept by people?
3457.e: When kept by people, for example in a garden pond without predators, alpine newts can get quite old. In the wild they usually live shorter lives.
3457.m: Alpine newts can live 15 to 20 years.

3458.q: Roughly how many teeth does an orca have?
3458.e: Orcas have lots of pointed teeth in their mouth. They use them to grip their prey tightly.

3459.q: Which group of birds does the bearded vulture belong to?
3459.e: The bearded vulture is a bird of prey, like eagles and falcons. But it hardly hunts itself and mainly eats bones.
3459.m: The bearded vulture is a bird of prey.

3460.q: What does the cheetah often do before eating its prey?
3460.e: Because the cheetah is weak after its sprint, it looks around carefully. This way it notices in time if other predators want to steal its prey.
3460.m: The cheetah stays careful after the hunt.

3461.q: What clearly sets a butterfly apart from a bee?
3461.e: Unlike bees, butterflies cannot defend themselves with a sting. Instead, they are often protected by camouflage or warning colours.

3463.q: Roughly how long are native dung beetles?
3463.e: Most native species are between 1 and 2.5 centimetres long. That makes them much bigger than ants.
3463.m: Dung beetles are about 1 to 2 cm long.

3464.q: How many young does a least weasel usually have per litter?
3464.e: A typical litter has several small, helpless young. The mother looks after them on her own.
3464.m: A least weasel usually has four to six young per litter.

3465.q: What does it mean when an animal species is extinct?
a: Not a single animal of that species is alive any more
The animals are hibernating at the moment
The animals live only in zoos now
The animals have moved to another country
3465.e: If a species is extinct, there is not a single animal of that species left in the world. When habitats disappear, species are at risk. Nature conservation aims to prevent this.
3465.m: When a species dies out, it is gone for ever.

3466.q: What does a wasp build its nest from?
3466.e: The wasp chews wood fibres with saliva into a pulp. This turns into grey paper for the nest.
3466.m: Wasps build nests from wood paper.

3467.q: Which plant parts can the white rhino eat especially well thanks to its wide mouth?
3467.e: The white rhino's broad, flat mouth is perfectly shaped for plucking short grass right at ground level. That is why it is also called the grazing rhino.
3467.m: The wide mouth is made for grass on the ground.

3468.q: How big can a wolf pack's territory be?
a: Only a few hundred square metres
As big as a football pitch
3468.e: A wolf pack claims a large territory, which can cover several hundred square kilometres depending on how much prey there is. The pack defends this area against other packs.

3469.q: How fast can a brown bear run over short distances?
3469.e: Despite its size, a brown bear can be amazingly fast over short distances, up to about 50 kilometres an hour. So running away is not a good idea for people.
3469.m: Brown bears are very fast over short distances.

3470.q: Which animal hops on strong back legs and carries its young in a pouch?
3470.e: The kangaroo lives in Australia and can jump very far with its strong legs. The young grow up in their mother's pouch.
3470.m: The kangaroo carries its babies in a pouch.

3471.q: What kind of landscape do red kangaroos like to live in best?
3471.e: Red kangaroos like dry, open areas such as the grasslands and semi-deserts of Australia. There they find enough grass to eat.
3471.m: Red kangaroos live in dry areas.

a: Meat, for example capybaras, caimans and tapirs
3472.e: The jaguar is a meat eater and catches many different animals. These include capybaras, peccaries, tapirs and caimans.
3472.m: The jaguar is a meat eater.

3473.q: How does a wild sow behave towards her piglets?
a: She does not look after them
She leaves them alone in the forest
3473.e: A wild sow keeps a very close eye on her little piglets. She stays near them and warns them of danger.

3474.q: What is a female red fox called?
3474.e: A female fox is called a vixen. The male, on the other hand, is called a dog fox.
3474.m: The female fox is called a vixen.

3475.q: Which large animal group does the tree frog belong to?
3475.e: Like all frogs, the tree frog is an amphibian. These animals typically live both in water and on land.
3475.m: Amphibians live in water and on land.

3476.q: What is a male duck called?
3476.e: The male duck is called a drake. He often has more colourful feathers than the female.
3476.m: The male duck is called a drake.

3477.q: What is a baby hippo called?
3477.e: Young hippos are called calves, just like young cows or elephants. They stay with their mother for a long time.
3477.m: A baby hippo is called a calf.

3478.q: What is true of the elk's (moose's) coat?
a: It is thick, with hollow hairs that keep it warm
3478.e: Some of the hairs are hollow and insulate well against the cold. This is how elk survive harsh winters.

3479.q: What is a horse with a reddish-brown coat called?
3479.e: A horse with a reddish-brown coat is called a chestnut. In German it is called a ‘Fuchs’ (fox), because foxes have reddish-brown fur too.
3479.m: A chestnut horse is reddish brown.

3480.q: How fast does a blue whale calf grow in its first months?
a: Very fast, it puts on lots of weight
It does not grow at all
It grows very slowly, like a tree
3480.e: Thanks to its mother's rich, fatty milk, a blue whale calf puts on an enormous amount of weight every day. This makes it one of the fastest-growing animals.

3481.q: Why can penguins swim in the icy sea without getting cold?
a: Because of a layer of fat and thick feathers
Because they have warm blood like fish
Because they never stay in the water long
3481.e: A thick layer of fat and tight-fitting, oiled feathers keep penguins warm in cold water. This lets them dive and hunt for hours.
3481.m: Fat and feathers keep penguins warm in the water.

a: A group of the 20 most important economies in the world
A UN department for environmental issues
3482.e: In the G20 the governments of the biggest economies meet to talk about the economy, the climate and other global issues. Switzerland is not one of the permanent members.
3482.m: The G20 are the 20 biggest economic powers.

3483.q: Roughly how heavy is a great spotted woodpecker?
a: About as heavy as a bar of chocolate
3483.e: A great spotted woodpecker weighs only about 70 to 90 grams. That is really very light.
3483.m: It is very light, about 80 grams.

3484.q: Why do you sometimes see dead common toads on roads in spring?
a: Because cars run them over while they migrate
3484.e: On the way to their breeding ponds, common toads often have to cross roads. Without toad fences or help, sadly many are run over.
3484.m: Roads are dangerous during the migration.

3485.q: What colour is a newborn bison calf's coat usually?
3485.e: Bison calves are reddish to orange brown. Later they get darker and turn brown.
3485.m: Calves are reddish, adults dark brown.

3486.q: Which baboon species is named after an Egyptian god?
3486.e: The Anubis baboon, also called the olive baboon, is named after the ancient Egyptian god Anubis. It lives in a wide belt right across Africa.
3486.m: The Anubis baboon recalls a god.

3487.q: What shape are the pupils in a fox's eyes?
3487.e: Foxes have upright, slit-shaped pupils, similar to cats. This helps them see well at dusk too.

3488.q: Roughly how long can a swift stay in the air without landing?
a: Up to ten months in a row
3488.e: Outside the breeding season, swifts almost never land. They eat, sleep and even mate in flight.
3488.m: Swifts live almost all the time in the air.

3489.q: How does the tree frog spend the winter?
a: On land, buried in the soil or under leaves
3489.e: In winter the tree frog digs itself in on land or hides under leaves and moss. There it rests until spring.
3489.m: A winter rest, well hidden on land.

3490.q: Which country calls itself the “Land of the Thunder Dragon” and still shows the dragon on its flag today?
3490.e: Bhutan is also called the “Land of the Thunder Dragon”. The yellow and orange halves of the flag stand for worldly and spiritual power.
3490.m: Bhutan's flag shows a thunder dragon.

3491.q: What should you do if you find a stag beetle on a path?
a: Leave it alone or gently move it to the side of the path
Pick it up and take it home
3491.e: It is protected and must not be caught. On a path, though, it is in danger of being run over.

3492.q: What do cows absolutely need to drink every day?
3492.e: Cows drink a lot of fresh water every day because they are big and give a lot of milk. Without enough water they would be unwell.
3492.m: Cows need lots of fresh water.

3493.q: Is the chimpanzee threatened with extinction?
a: No, there are far too many
No, it is not threatened at all
It lives only in zoos now
3493.e: Wild chimpanzees are endangered because their habitat keeps getting smaller. That is why they are on the Red List.

3494.q: Which animal group does the bonobo belong to?
3494.e: The bonobo is a great ape, just like gorillas, orangutans and chimpanzees. These animals are especially intelligent.

3495.q: How do buffalo protect themselves from flies?
a: They flick their tail and ears
They wear covers made of leaves
3495.e: They wave annoying insects away with their tail and ears. Mud baths help too.
3495.m: Tail and ears keep flies away.

3496.q: Roughly how long do young ravens stay in the nest before they can fly?
3496.e: The young birds grow up in the nest and are ready to fly after about five to six weeks. After that they start exploring their surroundings on their own.
3496.m: Nest time lasts about five to six weeks.

3497.q: When can you hear edible dormice especially loudly?
a: In late summer during the mating season
Only in the depths of winter
3497.e: In late summer especially, edible dormice make loud whistling and squeaking sounds. These calls are often for finding a partner or defending their territory.
3497.m: They are especially loud in late summer.

3498.q: Where in Switzerland can you find lots of ducks?
a: On lakes, rivers and ponds in parks
Only high up in the mountains
3498.e: Ducks need water to live. So in Switzerland you often find them on lakes, rivers and ponds, even in the middle of towns.

3499.q: What are the tunnels that an earthworm digs in the soil good for?
a: Air and water can get into the soil more easily
3499.e: Earthworm tunnels are like little pipes in the soil. They let air and rainwater reach plant roots more easily.
3499.m: Worm tunnels let air and water through.

3500.q: What is the third, see-through eyelid that dogs have called?
3500.e: The nictitating membrane protects and moistens the eye, in addition to the upper and lower lids. It is usually hidden in the inner corner of the eye.
3500.m: The nictitating membrane is the third eyelid.

3502.q: Why do harbour seals like to rest in groups?
a: Together they are safer from enemies
Because that is the only way they can fall asleep
3502.e: When resting on sandbanks, harbour seals are safer in a group, because many eyes spot danger sooner. When fishing, though, each seal hunts on its own.
3502.m: They rest together and hunt alone.

3503.q: When does a slow worm shed its tail?
a: Every time it sheds its skin
3503.e: The shed tail keeps moving and distracts the enemy. This lets the slow worm escape.

3504.q: How do farmers in Switzerland often protect their sheep from wolves?
a: With specially trained livestock guardian dogs
By letting the sheep roam free at night
3504.e: Livestock guardian dogs live with the flock day and night and defend the sheep against wolves. Fences and night pens also help against attacks.
3504.m: Guardian dogs protect sheep from wolves.

3505.q: Does an eel eat while migrating to the sea?
3505.e: On its long journey, the eel lives off its fat reserves. Its gut largely shrinks away.

3506.q: What does the common frog do when it is very cold outside?
a: It migrates to a warm country
It stays active the whole time
3506.e: When it gets cold in winter, common frogs hide away and hardly move. This rest helps them get through the cold season.
3506.m: In winter the common frog takes a winter rest.

3507.q: How well can penguins see under water?
a: Very well, better than most humans
Not at all, they are blind
3507.e: Penguins' eyes are perfectly suited to seeing under water. This lets them spot and hunt fish there easily.
3507.m: Penguins see very well under water.

3508.q: Which predator often catches salmon in rivers in Alaska?
3508.e: Brown bears stand in rivers and catch the salmon swimming upstream. The fat helps them get through the winter.
3508.m: Brown bears eat salmon in the river.

3509.q: Where does the peregrine falcon prefer to breed?
a: On rock ledges and tall buildings
In nests it builds in trees
3509.e: Peregrine falcons nest on steep cliffs, but they also use church towers or tower blocks as substitute cliffs. There their young are safe from many enemies.
3509.m: Cliffs and tall buildings serve as nest sites.

3510.q: Which animals does the lynx hunt most often in Switzerland?
3510.e: Roe deer are the lynx's most important prey in Switzerland. It adapts to where they live in the forests.
3510.m: Roe deer are top of the menu.

a: Antigens are recognised, antibodies bind to them
Antibodies are recognised, antigens bind to them
The body makes antigens, viruses make antibodies
Antigens and antibodies are two names for the same thing
3511.e: Antigens are structures, for example on viruses, that the immune system recognises as foreign. Antibodies are defence proteins that bind specifically to these antigens.

3512.q: What does an earthworm's skin feel like when you touch it gently?
3512.e: An earthworm's skin is always covered with a little slime. This makes it smooth and protects the worm from drying out.
3512.m: Worm skin is smooth and moist.

3513.q: How does the altitude of its habitat affect how long the Alpine salamander takes to produce young?
a: The higher the habitat, the longer the young take to develop
Altitude has no effect at all
The higher it is, the faster it goes
It only has young at low altitudes
3513.e: In colder, higher areas the body works more slowly, so the young take longer to develop inside their mother. In warmer, lower areas it goes faster.

3514.q: What happens to many grey herons in Switzerland in winter?
a: Many stay, because the water often stays free of ice
Most of them die in winter
3514.e: Because many Swiss lakes and rivers rarely freeze over completely, lots of grey herons spend the winter here too. Only in hard frosts do some move further south.
3514.m: Many grey herons stay here in winter too.

3515.q: What helps the common wall lizard climb walls so skilfully?
3515.e: With small, sharp claws on each toe, the wall lizard finds a grip everywhere. This lets it climb vertical walls with ease.

3516.q: Does the barn owl fly to Africa in winter?
a: No, it usually stays here all year
No, it flies to the North Pole
3516.e: Unlike some birds, the barn owl is not a migrant. It stays in its area all year round.
3516.m: It does not migrate to warm countries.

3517.q: Does a brown bear eat or drink during its winter rest?
a: No, it lives off its fat reserves
Yes, it carries on eating normally every day
3517.e: During its winter rest, a brown bear takes in neither food nor water. Instead it lives off the fat reserves it built up by eating in autumn.
3517.m: In winter the bear eats nothing at all.

3518.q: What are baby edible dormice like when they are born?
a: Naked and with their eyes closed
With teeth for eating straight away
3518.e: Baby edible dormice are naked and blind at birth, like other baby rodents. Their mother looks after them in the nest.
3518.m: The young are born naked and blind.

3519.q: What is the flap of skin hanging from an elk's (moose's) throat called?
3519.e: Elk have a hairy flap of skin under the chin. It is called the bell or dewlap and is very noticeable in bulls.
3519.m: The bell hangs from the elk's throat.

3520.q: In which season are most bison calves born?
a: In the middle of high summer
3520.e: In spring there is fresh grass and mild weather. That is good for mother and calf.
3520.m: Bison calves mostly arrive in spring.

3521.q: What is the fur on a wood mouse's belly like?
a: The same reddish brown as on top
3521.e: The fur on the wood mouse's belly is pale, almost white, while on its back it is reddish brown.
3521.m: The wood mouse has a pale belly and a reddish brown back.

3523.q: Which feathers of a cockerel are often especially long and curved?
3523.e: Many cockerels have long, arching tail feathers that shine brightly. This makes them look very different from the hens with their shorter feathers.
3523.m: A cockerel's tail feathers are often long.

3524.q: Roughly how fast can a wild rabbit run?
3524.e: Wild rabbits can run amazingly fast to escape enemies. Up to 50 km/h is possible.

3525.q: What special quality is the carp often said to have?
a: It is thought to be especially tough and adaptable
It is thought to be the fastest fish in the world
It is thought to be poisonous
It is thought to be a flying fish
3525.e: The carp copes well with different conditions, such as warmer water or less oxygen. That is why it is seen as a very tough fish.
3525.m: The carp is a tough, adaptable fish.

3526.q: Why should a hamster's cage not stand in full sun?
3526.e: Hamsters cope badly with heat and can overheat in too much sun. A cool, shady spot is much better for them.
3526.m: Hamsters do not like full sun.

3527.q: How do gorillas normally behave within their own group?
3527.e: Within a group, gorillas are usually calm and get on well. They groom each other and play together.

3528.q: What was the Reichstag fire in 1933?
a: A fire in the German parliament building that the Nazis used for their own ends.
A festival planned by the Nazis.
A natural event with no consequences.
3528.e: After the Reichstag fire the National Socialists blamed their opponents and severely restricted basic rights. This helped them expand their power.
3528.m: The fire served as an excuse to seize power.

3529.q: What do bees build their honeycomb from?
3529.e: Bees make wax in their bodies and shape the honeycomb from it. They store honey and pollen in the honeycomb.

3530.q: What mistaken belief once led to ibex being hunted heavily?
a: People believed their horns and blood had healing powers
People wanted to keep them as pets in stables
Their fur was needed for carpets in palaces
People thought they were dangerous predators
3530.e: In the past, many people believed that the ibex's horns, blood or other body parts could cure diseases. This superstition led to heavy hunting.

3531.q: What do researchers use an orca's saddle patch for?
a: To count them by the moon
3531.e: Because each patch looks a little different, researchers can recognise individual orcas. It is like a fingerprint.
3531.m: The saddle patch makes each orca unique.

3532.q: What does an octopus use to crack hard mussel shells?
3532.e: The octopus's hard beak is strong enough to open mussel shells. This lets it get at the flesh inside.

3533.q: Roughly how old can a brown trout get in the wild?
3533.e: Brown trout can live several years in clean waters. In the wild, some even reach almost 10 years.

3534.q: How can you recognise young salmon that still live in the river?
a: By dark marks on their sides
3534.e: Young salmon in the river have dark marks across their sides. These camouflage the young fish on the gravel bed.
3534.m: Young river salmon have dark marks.

3535.q: Where does a housefly often hide in winter?
a: In the middle of a lake
3535.e: In winter the housefly looks for sheltered, warm cracks in houses or barns. That is where it best survives the cold.

3536.q: How do adult raven pairs usually behave towards each other?
a: They often stay together for life
3536.e: Ravens are seen as monogamous birds that often keep the same partner for many years. This close bond helps them raise their young and defend their territory.
3536.m: Raven pairs often stay together for life.

3537.q: What is World Refugee Day for?
a: To remember people who have had to flee from war or danger
To celebrate new countries on the map
To remember the founding of the EU
3537.e: On World Refugee Day, people all over the world think of those who have had to leave their homes. It is meant to show that refugees need help and protection.

3538.q: Why must people not disturb harbour seals in their habitat?
a: Because they are protected wild animals
Because otherwise they lose their fur
3538.e: Harbour seals are protected in many countries because they used to be hunted heavily. Disturbing them while they rest can harm their health.

3539.q: Does the badger usually look for food alone or in a group?
a: Mostly alone, even if it lives with others
Always in a big pack like wolves
Always in a pair with a fox
3539.e: Although several badgers can live in the same sett, each one usually goes off to look for food on its own. That way they do not get in each other's way.
3539.m: Badgers mostly look for food alone.

3540.q: In which surroundings are seahorses also often found?
3540.e: Coral reefs offer lots of colourful hiding places and food. Seahorses can also camouflage themselves well there.
3540.m: Coral reefs are a good habitat.

3541.q: How heavy can an adult domestic pig get?
3541.e: Depending on the breed and how they are kept, domestic pigs can get quite heavy. Some breeds even weigh well over 200 kilograms.
3541.m: Domestic pigs can get very heavy.

3542.q: What rank does the buzzard have among Switzerland's birds of prey?
a: It is the commonest bird of prey
It is the rarest bird of prey
It is only found in winter
3542.e: The buzzard is the commonest bird of prey in Switzerland. You often see it on fence posts or circling in the air.
3542.m: The buzzard is Switzerland's commonest bird of prey.

3543.q: What happens when a dolphin is injured or ill?
a: The group leaves it alone at once
It is sent out of the sea
3543.e: Dolphins are very social animals and help each other. Sometimes healthy dolphins hold an injured one up to the surface so it can breathe.
3543.m: Dolphins help sick members of their group.

3544.q: How is the edible frog protected by law in Switzerland?
a: It is protected and must not simply be caught
It may be kept as a pet anywhere
It has no protection at all
3544.e: In Switzerland, all native amphibians, including the edible frog, are protected by law. You must not simply catch them or destroy their habitat.
3544.m: The edible frog is protected in Switzerland.

3545.q: How long is the common wall lizard's tail compared with the rest of its body?
a: Exactly as long as a leg
3545.e: The wall lizard's tail is about twice as long as its head and body together. It helps it balance and climb.
3545.m: The tail is about twice as long as the body.

3546.q: What sound does a mosquito make when it flies?
3546.e: The whining comes from the mosquito moving its wings up and down very fast. The faster they beat, the higher the sound.

3547.q: What job do dung beetles do in nature's cycle?
a: They are decomposers and return nutrients to the soil
3547.e: Dung beetles break up and bury dung. This makes the nutrients available to plants again.

3548.q: Do some sharks have a special skin that protects their eyes when they attack?
a: No, sharks never close their eyes
No, sharks have no eyelids at all
3548.e: Some sharks can pull a see-through nictitating membrane over their eyes. This protects the eyes when they bite.
3548.m: The nictitating membrane protects some sharks' eyes.

3549.q: Why is the starfish called a starfish?
a: Because it looks like a star and lives in the sea
Because it glows like a star at night
Because it only comes out at night
Because it likes lying in the sun
3549.e: The starfish gets its name from its shape. But it is neither a real star nor a fish; it is an animal that lives on the seabed.
3549.m: The name only fits its shape.

3550.q: What colour are wild budgies usually?
3550.e: In the wild, budgies are mostly green with a yellow head. This lets them hide well in the grass.
3550.m: Wild budgies are green and yellow.

3551.q: How does a sand lizard usually react when it feels threatened and cannot escape?
a: It tries to bite or stays motionless
It puffs itself up like a balloon
3551.e: As a last defence, the sand lizard can bite, although this rarely happens. It often tries to stay unnoticed first.
3551.m: As a last resort it bites.

3552.q: How far can a hedgehog wander in one night looking for food?
a: It does not move at all
3552.e: Looking for food, a hedgehog often wanders several kilometres in one night through gardens and meadows. That is why it needs connected, hedgehog-friendly gardens.
3552.m: Hedgehogs wander long distances at night.

3553.q: What is one feature of a reindeer's coat?
a: It is very thick and keeps it warm
3553.e: The coat is made of thick hair that traps lots of air. This keeps the animal warm even in great cold.
3553.m: Thick fur protects against the cold.

3554.q: What is typical of the horns of an adult African buffalo bull?
