4169.q: What is the easiest way to tell male and female kestrels apart by their looks?
a: The male's head and tail are blue-grey, the female's are more brown
The male is clearly bigger than the female
Only the female has feathers on her legs
The male has no black spots in its feathers
4169.e: Male kestrels have a striking grey-blue head and tail. Females are browner overall and a little bigger than the males.
4169.m: The male has a blue-grey head and tail.

4170.q: What was the name of the only party allowed in the Soviet Union?
a: Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU)
4170.e: In the Soviet Union, the CPSU was the only party allowed. It controlled the state, the economy and society almost completely.
4170.m: The CPSU was the only party in the USSR.

4171.q: What happened to the wolf in Switzerland in the 19th century?
a: It was wiped out by hunting
It was put under strict protection
It moved to Africa of its own accord
4171.e: In the 19th century the wolf was hunted heavily in Switzerland because it was seen as a danger to farm animals. The last wolf of that time was shot in 1871; after that the species disappeared for over a hundred years.
4171.m: The wolf was wiped out in the 19th century.

4172.e: Cockchafers are prey for bats, birds such as crows and starlings, and hedgehogs. Their grubs are eaten, for example, by moles.

4173.q: Which statement about the Alpine salamander and people is true?
a: It is not dangerous to people with normal contact
Its bite is deadly to people
It is poisonous to people if they just look at it
4173.e: The Alpine salamander's skin poison is mainly aimed at smaller predators. For people, normal, careful contact is usually harmless, but you should wash your hands afterwards.
4173.m: Harmless to people if you are careful.

4174.q: Which strong bovine animal often used to pull the plough across the field?
4174.e: Oxen are large, strong cattle. In the past they pulled ploughs and carts, before there were tractors.
4174.m: Oxen used to be strong working animals.

4175.q: What is the area a pack regularly roams through called?
4175.e: The area in which a pack moves around and hunts is called its home range or territory. For wild dogs it is especially large.
4175.m: The home range is their hunting ground.

4176.q: How do bison herds often defend their calves against wolves?
a: They stand around the calves to protect them
4176.e: Adults form a protective ring and keep attackers at a distance. This keeps the calves safer.

a: Herons, cormorants and large predatory fish
4178.e: Larger birds and predatory fish catch eels. But adult eels have only a few natural enemies.

4179.q: What does the tawny owl stand for in many old folk tales and myths?
a: It was often seen as a spooky bird of bad luck because of its night call
It was a symbol of running fast
It was a symbol of fish and water
It was never mentioned in stories
4179.e: Because the tawny owl calls at night and usually stays out of sight, folk beliefs in the past often saw it as a spooky bird or a bringer of bad luck. Today we know that its call is simply for marking its territory.
4179.m: The tawny owl was once seen as a bird of bad luck.

4180.q: What did the eagle owl often stand for in folk beliefs in the past?
a: In many places it was seen as a bringer of bad luck or a spooky bird
Everywhere it was a symbol of winning the lottery
It was kept as a pet like a dog
It was a symbol of plants growing fast
4180.e: Because of its night call and its spooky appearance, the eagle owl was a bird of bad luck in many old stories. Today we know that such ideas are not based on scientific facts.
4180.m: The eagle owl was often seen as a bird of bad luck.

4181.q: Which organisation uses a light blue flag with a map of the world surrounded by a white olive wreath?
4181.e: The UN flag shows a map of the world framed by two olive branches as a symbol of peace. The UN was founded in 1945 and the flag introduced in 1947.
4181.m: The UN flag stands for peace worldwide.

4182.q: What is a “stink fight” among ring-tailed lemurs?
a: Males spread scent on their tails and wave them at their rival
Two males throw fruit at each other
The animals splash each other with water
The females chase males with loud screams
4182.e: The males rub their tails on scent glands on their arms. Then they waft the smell towards their rival without hurting each other.
4182.m: In a stink fight, smell decides.

4183.q: Why are housefly maggots useful for nature?
a: They help break down rubbish and dead plants
4183.e: Housefly maggots break down rotting matter and rubbish. This way they help to make nature clean again.

4184.q: Can a polar bear smell seals from a long way away?
a: No, it can hardly smell anything
No, it cannot smell at all
4184.e: The polar bear's nose is very sensitive. It can smell a seal even several kilometres away.
4184.m: Polar bears smell seals from kilometres away.

4185.q: How do swan parents sometimes protect their little cygnets?
a: They let them ride on their back
They carry them in their beak
4185.e: Little cygnets can ride on their parents' backs. There they are protected and can rest.
4185.m: Cygnets can ride on their parents' backs.

4186.q: What is the basic principle of a heat pump?
a: It takes heat from the surroundings and releases it in the house
It produces heat directly from electricity by burning
It pumps hot water from the sea into the house
It stores sunlight in a battery
4186.e: A heat pump takes in heat from the air, the ground or the groundwater, even when they are cool. With a little electricity, this heat is then raised to a higher temperature and fed into the house.
4186.m: Heat pumps get heat from the surroundings.

4187.q: Why do swifts find it hard to take off from the ground?
a: Their legs are very short and weak
4187.e: The swift's short legs are hardly any good for walking or pushing off from the ground. That is why they almost only land on vertical surfaces.
4187.m: Short legs make taking off from the ground hard.

4188.q: Why do alpacas often use a shared dung pile?
a: It helps reduce parasites on the pasture
They use it to mark roads
They eat the dung as their main food
4188.e: Alpacas like to do their droppings in the same places. This makes cleaning up easier and reduces germs on the pasture.

4189.q: Which animals are among the natural enemies of the elk?
4189.e: Wolves and bears mainly catch calves and weakened animals. Adult elk defend themselves by kicking.

4190.q: What do guinea pigs eat most?
4190.e: Hay is the most important food for guinea pigs and should always be available. It also helps wear down their teeth.
4190.m: Hay is the number one food.

4191.q: Which two classes did Marx set against each other in capitalism?
4191.e: Marx saw history as shaped by the class struggle between the property-owning bourgeoisie and the propertyless proletariat. According to Marx, the working class would one day rise up against the owners.
4191.m: Marx set the proletariat against the bourgeoisie.

4192.q: How do dolphins show that they are friends?
4192.e: Dolphins are very social animals. Dolphins that are friends rub or touch each other with their flippers.
4192.m: Friends rub gently against each other.

4193.q: What do a slow worm's teeth look like?
4193.e: With its small teeth it can hold on to slippery prey. They are harmless to people.

4194.q: What is the fine, soft wool of the cashmere goat used for?
4194.e: Soft cashmere wool is obtained from the fine undercoat of certain goats. It is made into cosy jumpers.

a: No, they are afraid of water
4195.e: Pigs are amazingly good swimmers and like going into the water when it is hot. This also helps them cool down.

4196.q: Which statement about the snow leopard and hibernation is true?
a: It sleeps for five months in a cave
4196.e: The snow leopard stays active in winter too and keeps hunting. Its thick fur protects it from the cold.

4197.q: What else is a fox's bushy tail called?
4197.e: The fox's bushy tail is also called its brush. It helps the fox balance and acts as a signal to other foxes.
4197.m: A fox's tail is also called its brush.

4198.q: How well does a tiger see in the dark?
a: Very well, much better than a person
Exactly as well as a person
It cannot see anything in the dark
4198.e: Tigers see much better than people at night. This helps them hunt in the dark.
4198.m: Tigers see very well at night.

4199.q: Which waters does the hippo like to live in best?
4199.e: Hippos live in warm rivers and lakes in Africa. There they have enough room to dive and cool down.

4200.q: What is the brown, mottled pattern in the eagle owl's feathers for?
a: It camouflages it well from enemies and prey
It is only for courtship and has no other purpose
It is meant to scare other eagle owls
It shows how old the bird is
4200.e: The eagle owl's brown speckled feathers help it hide well on rocks and in trees during the day. This means other animals hardly ever spot it.
4200.m: Eagle owl feathers camouflage it well.

4201.q: How long can dolphins hold their breath before they have to come up again?
4201.e: Dolphins can stay under water for a few minutes before they have to come up to breathe. Then they quickly take in fresh air.
4201.m: Dolphins dive for minutes before they breathe.

4202.q: Is the carp a predatory fish or a peaceful fish?
a: A peaceful fish, it does not hunt large fish
A predatory fish that hunts other fish
A fish that only eats meat
A fish that eats nothing at all
4202.e: The carp is one of the peaceful fish. It mainly eats small creatures and plants and does not hunt large fish.
4202.m: The carp is a peaceful fish.

4203.q: Which other animals are sometimes prey for the red kite?
4203.e: The red kite sometimes catches smaller birds too, especially weakened or young ones. Larger mammals such as roe deer are not its prey.
4203.m: Small birds are on the menu too.

4204.q: When is the wels catfish mainly active?
4204.e: The wels catfish mainly hunts at dusk and at night. During the day it often hides in hollows or under roots.
4204.m: The wels catfish hunts at night.

4206.q: What is special about pill millipedes among millipedes?
a: They can roll up into a ball
4206.e: Pill millipedes look like pill woodlice and roll up into a ball when in danger. But they are millipedes, not crustaceans.
4206.m: Pill millipedes roll up into a ball.

4207.q: How many feelers does a Roman snail have on its head?
4207.e: The Roman snail has four feelers. The two long ones have eyes, the two short ones are for smelling.
4207.m: Four feelers on the snail's head.

4208.q: What happens if a starfish loses an arm?
a: It never gets an arm again
4208.e: Starfish can grow back lost arms. But it takes many months.

4209.q: How do the weasel and the stoat differ in size?
a: Both are exactly the same size
4209.e: The stoat is the weasel's bigger relative. But both belong to the same genus of the marten family.
4209.m: The weasel is the smaller relative.

4210.q: What does the blue whale do before it dives for a long time?
a: It takes a deep breath at the surface
It eats plants one last time
4210.e: So that the blue whale can stay under water for a long time, it breathes in deeply once more first. After that it can dive for a while.
4210.m: First a deep breath, then dive.

4211.q: What kind of animal is a cow?
4211.e: The cow is a mammal because it feeds its calves with milk and has fur. It is also an even-toed hoofed animal.

4212.q: When do the larvae of many whitefish hatch from their eggs?
4212.e: In cold water the eggs develop slowly. That is why the larvae often only hatch after several weeks or months.
4212.m: In cold water development takes longer.

4213.q: What is special about a camel's red blood cells?
4213.e: Camels have oval red blood cells. Even when the camel drinks a lot of water, they can take in water well without bursting.

4214.q: What is typical of an eagle owl's face compared with many other birds?
a: A clearly marked facial disc that helps with hearing
A completely smooth face with no special feathers
A beak hidden completely in the feathers
A face that looks like a fish's
4214.e: The facial disc of fine feathers guides sound better to the eagle owl's ears. This lets it pinpoint sounds even more precisely.
4214.m: The facial disc helps the eagle owl hear.

4215.q: What shows us that the blackbird is well adapted to living near people?
a: It also nests in gardens and on balconies
It avoids all contact with people
It only lives far away in untouched wilderness
It can only survive in zoos
4215.e: Blackbirds even build their nests in hedges on balconies or in gardens right in the middle of built-up areas. This shows how well they have adapted to living alongside people.
4215.m: Blackbirds even nest in towns and gardens.

4216.q: What is special about the puma's back legs compared with its front legs?
4216.e: The long back legs give the puma enormous jumping power. With them it is very good at getting over obstacles and distances.
4216.m: Strong back legs make for long leaps.

4217.q: How does the magpie usually behave towards people?
a: Careful, but curious and quick to learn
4217.e: Magpies watch people closely and quickly learn where there is food. Even so, they usually stay careful and keep their distance.

4218.q: What colour is the golden jackal's coat usually?
4218.e: The golden jackal's coat shimmers golden yellow to greyish. Depending on the season and area, it can be a little darker or lighter.
4218.m: Golden jackals have golden yellow to greyish brown fur.

4219.q: Which dog breed is considered one of the fastest in the world?
4219.e: Sighthounds such as the greyhound can briefly reach speeds of over 60 km/h. They were originally bred for coursing.

4220.q: Which animal results when a horse and a donkey mate?
4220.e: If you cross a horse with a donkey, you get a mule or a hinny, depending on which parent was male or female. These animals are often especially tough and sure-footed.
4220.m: Horse and donkey make a mule.

4221.q: What makes the mute swan a special bird?
a: It is one of the heaviest birds that can fly
It is the smallest water bird
4221.e: Despite its great weight, the mute swan can still fly. That is rare for such heavy birds.
4221.m: The mute swan is heavy but can still fly.

4222.q: Why do meerkats spend almost the whole day looking for food?
a: Their prey is small, so they need a lot of it
They only eat once a year
4222.e: Insects, larvae and spiders are small. To get full, meerkats have to dig in the sand for hours.
4222.m: Small prey means a long search for food.

4223.q: What are the hard patches of skin on the dromedary's chest and knees?
a: Calluses that protect it when it lies down
4223.e: When the animal lies down on hot ground, the calluses protect its skin. They are thicker than the rest of the skin.
4223.m: Calluses protect it when lying down.

4224.q: What does the praying mantis eat?
a: It hunts other insects and eats them
It only drinks nectar from flowers
4224.e: The praying mantis is a predator. It catches flies, grasshoppers and other insects.

4225.q: What does the octopus especially use its ink for?
4225.e: The cloud of ink confuses the attacker and hides the octopus for a moment. This lets the octopus swim away quickly.

4226.q: What is the best way to tell that a slow worm is not a snake?
a: It has eyelids and can blink
It has legs under its belly
4226.e: Snakes have no movable eyelids, but slow worms do. The slow worm has no venom fangs.

4227.q: Is the fish sold in German-speaking countries as “Seelachs” (literally “sea salmon”) a true salmon?
a: No, it belongs to the cod family
Yes, it is the same fish
Yes, it is a freshwater salmon
4227.e: The “Seelachs”, known in English as coley or saithe, is related to the cod. It is not closely related to the salmon.

4228.q: Where does the conger eel live?
a: In the sea on rocky coasts and near wrecks
4228.e: Conger eels are large sea fish with a snake-like body. During the day they hide in cracks in the rock and in wrecks.
4228.m: Conger eels are large sea eels.

4229.q: Why can a warmer lake become a problem for whitefish?
4229.e: Whitefish like cool water. If the lake gets warmer, the oxygen content drops and the fish get stressed.

4230.q: When are most red deer calves born?
a: In late spring or early summer
In high summer in great heat
4230.e: Most calves are born in May or June. Then there is enough fresh food for the mother.
4230.m: Calves are born in early summer.

4231.q: What is the protective layer around nerve fibres that speeds up signals called?
4231.e: The myelin sheath wraps around many nerve fibres like insulation. It makes electrical signals travel much faster.

4232.q: What colour is a weasel's coat typically?
a: Brown on top, white on the belly
4232.e: The brown back camouflages it in the grass, and from below the white belly does not stand out against the bright sky. This two-colour coat is common in many martens.

4233.q: How many wings does a grasshopper usually have?
4233.e: Most grasshoppers have two pairs of wings. That makes four wings altogether.
4233.m: Grasshoppers have two pairs of wings, so four wings.

4234.q: Why do you wash your hands before eating?
a: So that no germs get into your mouth
So that your hands get cold
4234.e: There are often invisible germs on your hands. Washing removes them before you eat.
4234.m: Before eating, you wash your hands clean.

4235.q: What do stag beetle larvae live on?
4235.e: The larvae live in the ground on rotting roots and tree stumps. They eat the decomposed wood.
4235.m: Larvae eat rotten wood in the ground.

4236.q: What are young fish called just after hatching, when they still have a yolk sac?
4236.e: Newly hatched fish first live off their yolk sac. They are called larvae or fry.
4236.m: Fish larvae live off their yolk sac.

4237.q: About how tall is a Bactrian camel at the shoulder?
4237.e: The humps stick up even higher. That is why the animal looks very big overall.
4237.m: A shoulder height of a good two metres.

4238.q: What do researchers often use today to watch secretive lynx?
a: Lynx collars on every animal from birth
4238.e: Camera traps in the forest automatically photograph animals passing by. This lets researchers recognise individual lynx by their pattern of spots.
4238.m: Camera traps reveal the secretive lynx.

4239.q: In which part of the USA was the puma wiped out almost everywhere?
4239.e: In the east of the USA the puma was hunted heavily and wiped out almost everywhere. A small remaining population survived in Florida.
4239.m: It was wiped out in the eastern USA.

4240.q: Can Swiss citizens living abroad take part in federal votes?
a: Yes, if they are entered on the electoral register of a Swiss municipality
No, they automatically lose the right to vote
Only in elections, not in votes
Only if they live in Europe
4240.e: Swiss citizens living abroad can register on the electoral register of a voting municipality, for example their home municipality or their former municipality of residence. In this way they keep the right to vote in federal votes.
4240.m: Swiss citizens abroad can still have their say.

a: Support for poorer countries from richer countries and organisations
4241.e: Development cooperation includes financial, technical and staff support so that poorer countries can develop economically and socially. Switzerland does this, among other ways, through the SDC.

4242.q: What is a typical feature of fish, the group the wels catfish belongs to?
4242.e: The body temperature of fish depends on their surroundings. That is why the wels catfish is sluggish in winter.

4243.q: How do meerkats often find their food?
a: They dig for it in the ground
They pick it from tall trees
4243.e: They scratch in the sand with their claws and find insects and larvae there. Their good sense of smell also helps them.

a: A machine that turns wind into electricity
4244.e: The wind turns the large blades of the turbine. This turning is then converted into electricity.
4244.m: Wind turns the blades, and the blades make electricity.

4245.q: How is the carrion crow often shown in many old stories and myths?
a: Sometimes as a bird of bad luck with a bad reputation
Always as a symbol of good luck
As a sacred animal with no negative meaning at all
4245.e: In many old stories and folk beliefs, the carrion crow was long seen as a bird of bad luck because of its black colour and harsh call. Today we know that it is a very clever and useful bird.
4245.m: Crows were often seen as birds of bad luck in the past.

4246.q: What are the Bactrian camel's long eyelashes for?
a: They protect the eyes from sand and dust
They camouflage it in the snow
4246.e: Long eyelashes and nostrils that can close protect it from sandstorms. This keeps the desert dust out.
4246.m: Eyelashes protect against sand and dust.

4247.q: Which bird especially likes eating earthworms?
4247.e: Blackbirds often look for earthworms in the grass and skilfully pull them out of the ground. Worms are an important food for them.

4248.q: What is usually true of common buzzards in Switzerland?
a: They usually stay here all year
They fly to Africa every winter
They never move but stay on the same branch
They leave Switzerland for ever after breeding
4248.e: Many common buzzards in Switzerland are resident birds and stay here in winter too. Populations further north in other countries, on the other hand, often move further south.

4249.q: Which statement about the protection status of the Alpine marmot in Switzerland is true?
a: Hunting is regulated by law and limited in time
It may be hunted all year without limits
It is not protected by law at all
It has died out completely in Switzerland
4249.e: In Switzerland the Alpine marmot is a species that may be hunted, but hunting is regulated by law and limited in time. This is meant to stop the numbers falling too much.
4249.m: Laws regulate the hunting of marmots.

4250.q: Where does the eastern grey kangaroo live?
4250.e: The eastern grey kangaroo lives in Australia. It likes forests and meadows with lots of juicy grass.

a: Messenger substances that send signals to organs through the blood
Cells that are only found in the brain
4251.e: Hormones are made by glands and released into the blood. They control, for example, growth and metabolism.
4251.m: Hormones are messengers in the blood.

4252.q: How many fingers or toes does the slow worm have?
4252.e: It no longer has any limbs. That is why it moves by slithering.

4253.q: What happens to kingfishers in harsh, long winters when the water freezes over?
a: Many starve because they can no longer fish
They move out to the sea
They go to sleep like marmots
4253.e: When the water is frozen, the kingfisher can no longer dive and cannot catch fish. That is why many kingfishers die of hunger in harsh winters.
4253.m: Frozen water is a big threat to the kingfisher.

4254.q: How many young does a bonobo mother usually have at once?
4254.e: Usually only one baby is born. Twins are very rare.
4254.m: Usually only one baby is born.

4255.q: How does a mute swan usually hold its neck when swimming?
4255.e: The mute swan's long neck is typically curved elegantly in an S shape. You often see this in pictures of swans.
4255.m: The neck is held in an S shape.

4257.q: What is an important difference between a mosquito and a crane fly?
a: The crane fly does not bite people
The crane fly only lives in the sea
The crane fly only eats wood
4257.e: Crane flies look a bit like big mosquitoes, but they do not bite people. Even so, many people mix up the two insects.
4257.m: Crane flies do not bite people.

4258.q: Where does the common earwig originally come from?
4258.e: The common earwig originally lives in Europe and parts of Asia. People later brought it to North America and other areas too.

4259.q: What actually is a sea turtle?
a: A reptile that lives in the sea
4259.e: Sea turtles are reptiles, not fish. They breathe air, even though they live in the sea.
4259.m: Sea turtles are reptiles in the sea.

4260.q: Why do a swan's feathers stay dry even though it swims in the water?
a: It only swims for a very short time
Its feathers are made of wax
4260.e: Swans have a small spot on their back where they get oil from. They rub it into their feathers, so the water rolls off.

4261.q: Which dragonfly in Switzerland has a broad, flat abdomen that is blue in the male?
4261.e: The broad-bodied chaser has a broad, flattened abdomen. In the male it has a powdery blue coating.
4261.m: The broad-bodied chaser has a blue abdomen.

4262.q: Which special ability helps the kestrel find mice from high up?
a: It can see UV light and so spot the mice's urine trails
It can see in the dark like an owl
It smells the mice from the air
It hears the mice rustling quietly in the grass
4262.e: Mice mark their runs with urine, which reflects UV light. The kestrel's eyes can see this UV light and so spot the trails in the grass.

4263.q: Why do some edible dormice have no young at all in some years?
a: Because there is too little food such as beechnuts
Because it is too cold for them
4263.e: If there are not enough beechnuts and nuts in a year, female edible dormice often do not have young at all. This saves energy for their own survival.
4263.m: Little food often means no young.

4264.q: Where does the female praying mantis often stick her egg case?
a: On plant stems, twigs or stones
4264.e: The egg case is called an ootheca. The female sticks it to firm things among the plants, so it stays in place over the winter.
4264.m: Egg cases stick to stems and stones.

4265.q: What is a possible danger for herds of alpacas on pastures in Switzerland?
a: Dogs or predators such as the wolf
4265.e: Wild or free-roaming dogs and wolves can attack alpacas. That is why secure fences are important.

4266.q: In golden jackals, what is often true about the size of males and females?
a: The males are usually a little bigger
The females are twice as big
4266.e: Males are usually a little bigger and heavier. But the difference is not very big.
4266.m: Males are usually a little bigger.

4268.q: What does a robin like to eat best?
4268.e: Robins look on the ground for insects, spiders and worms. That is their favourite food.

4269.q: How many young does a female stoat usually have per litter?
4269.e: A litter usually has 4 to 9 young. The exact number also depends on how much food there is.
4269.m: A litter usually has 4 to 9 young.

4270.q: What do you put on a horse's back so that you can ride it?
4270.e: The saddle is put on the horse's back so that the rider can sit comfortably and safely. It is fastened with a girth.

4271.q: Which planet is the biggest in our solar system?
4271.e: Jupiter is so big that many Earths would fit inside it. It is made mainly of gas.

4272.q: What is the group of related animals that includes the llama, alpaca, guanaco and vicuña called?
4272.e: These four animals are called New World camels, or llamas in the wider sense. They live in South America.
4272.m: Llamas and alpacas are New World camels.

4273.q: What happens to the back legs when a tadpole turns into a frog?
a: They grow first, before the front legs appear
4273.e: During metamorphosis the tadpole's back legs grow first, and the front legs follow later. The tail shrinks away step by step.
4273.m: The tadpole gets back legs first, then front legs.

4274.q: What is the largest dragonfly in central Europe called?
4274.e: The emperor dragonfly grows up to about 8 centimetres long. It often hunts over ponds.
4274.m: The emperor dragonfly is very large.

4275.q: What does the lake trout mainly need its tail fin for?
a: For pushing itself along when swimming
For holding on to the bank
4275.e: With strong strokes of its tail fin the fish pushes itself forward. It also helps it jump over small obstacles.
4275.m: The tail fin drives the fish forward.

4276.q: What does the stoat's winter coat typically look like?
a: White, with a black tip to the tail
4276.e: In colder regions the stoat changes to an almost white coat in winter. Only the tip of its tail stays black all year round.
4276.m: The stoat turns almost white in winter.

a: A research centre where countries study physics together
A football stadium for world cups
4277.e: At CERN researchers from many countries work together to learn more about how the world is made. It lies partly in Switzerland and partly in France.
4277.m: At CERN many countries do research together.

4278.q: What colour are the tail feathers of many cockerels often?
4278.e: Cockerels often have especially colourful and shiny tail feathers, while hens are usually plainer. The striking feathers help the cockerel impress the hens.

4279.q: In which waters do seahorses usually live?
a: In rivers high up in the Alps
4279.e: Seahorses like warm, shallow water near the coast. There they find enough plants and food.
4279.m: Warm coastal waters are their home.

4280.q: Why is the grass snake protected in Switzerland?
a: Its habitats are being lost and it is endangered
Because it bites too many people
4280.e: Wetlands are disappearing, so its habitat is becoming scarce. It is protected in Switzerland.

4281.q: How many insects do great tit parents catch in a day for their young?
4281.e: Great tit parents hunt insects and caterpillars all day for their hungry young. In one day that can be several hundred small creatures.
4281.m: Great tits catch lots of insects for their young.

4282.q: Why do people all over the world keep chickens?
a: So that they guard the house
4282.e: People have kept chickens for a very long time, mainly for their nutritious eggs and their meat. That is why there are chickens almost everywhere in the world.
4282.m: Chickens give us eggs and meat.

4283.q: Why are swallows useful for farms?
a: They eat lots of annoying flying insects
They chase all the mice off the farm
4283.e: Swallows eat large numbers of flying insects such as flies and mosquitoes. That is why they have always been seen as useful and welcome guests on farms.
4283.m: They eat lots of annoying insects.

4284.q: What does the otter use its whiskers, also called vibrissae, for?
a: To track down prey in murky water
To keep its balance when climbing
4284.e: With its sensitive whiskers the otter feels the tiniest movements in the water. This helps it catch fish even when it cannot see well.
4284.m: Vibrissae help it hunt in murky water.

4285.q: What do lower-ranking wolves often do when the lead wolf comes back?
4285.e: Licking the lead wolf's mouth is a greeting ritual and shows respect and belonging. This behaviour goes back to puppyhood, when pups beg for food this way.
4285.m: Mouth-licking shows respect in the pack.

4286.q: How does the pike usually swallow its prey?
a: It chews it for a long time like we chew bread
It splits it into tiny pieces
It just lets the prey go again
4286.e: The pike holds its prey with its sharp teeth and then usually swallows it whole. It cannot chew like we do.
4286.m: The pike swallows its prey whole.

4287.q: How old do meerkats usually get in the wild?
4287.e: In the wild they often live to about five to ten. In zoos they can live a little longer.

4288.q: Roughly how many different kinds of jellyfish are there?
4288.e: Researchers know of over 2,000 different kinds of jellyfish. They live in all the world's oceans and come in very different sizes.
4288.m: There are over 2,000 kinds of jellyfish.

4289.q: What are a beetle's hard wing cases for?
a: They protect the delicate flying wings
4289.e: Under the wing cases are the thin wings the beetle flies with. The wing cases are opened up when it flies.
4289.m: Wing cases protect the flying wings underneath.

4290.q: Apart from mice, which prey is especially often on the eagle owl's menu?
a: Birds such as crows or other owls, and also hedgehogs and hares
Only bits of plants and berries
4290.e: The eagle owl is a very versatile hunter and, as well as mice, catches birds, other owls, hedgehogs or hares. Sometimes it even overpowers young foxes.
4290.m: Eagle owls eat many different kinds of prey.

4291.q: What colour are a mallard's eggs usually?
4291.e: Mallard eggs are usually a plain greenish brown. This camouflages them well in the nest.

4292.q: How does the earthworm help rainwater soak into the ground better?
a: Its tunnels work like little pipes
It drinks all the water itself
It builds dams out of soil
4292.e: The fine tunnels in the soil carry the water further down. This way rainwater soaks in faster and puddles do not form.
4292.m: Worm tunnels carry water into the ground.

4293.q: Does a tiger prefer to live alone or in a group?
a: In families with lots of relatives
4293.e: Tigers are loners and usually live alone. Only mothers live together with their young.

4294.q: In German, a baby seal lying alone on the beach and calling for its mother has a special name. What is it?
4294.e: A little seal that calls loudly for its mother is called a “Heuler” in German. Usually the mother soon finds her baby again.
4294.m: In German, calling seal pups are called “Heuler”.

4295.q: What do the perch's vertical stripes mainly help it with?
4295.e: The stripes break up the outline of its body, especially among water plants. This makes it harder for both prey and enemies to see it.

4296.q: What does the well-known call often said to belong to the tawny owl sound like?
4296.e: The female often calls a sharp “kewick”, while the male calls the well-known wavering “hoo-hoo-hooo”. Together this makes the classic owl call.
4296.m: The tawny owl calls kewick and hoo-hoo-hooo.

4297.q: What is a male elk called?
4297.e: Male elk are called bulls. Females are called cows.

a: A leopard or jaguar with black fur
4298.e: Black panthers are usually leopards or jaguars whose bodies make especially large amounts of dark pigment. In slanting light you can often still see the spots.
4298.m: A black panther is usually a black leopard or jaguar.

4299.q: About how fast can a roe deer run?
a: Up to about 60 kilometres per hour
4299.e: Roe deer can flee very fast with big leaps. They reach up to about 60 kilometres per hour.
4299.m: Roe deer can flee very fast.

4300.q: How do most damselflies hold their wings at rest?
4300.e: Most damselflies fold their wings together over their abdomen when resting. This sets them apart from dragonflies.

a: Money borrowed from a bank to buy something like furniture or a car, which must be paid back with interest
A loan you only get for food
Money the state gives to all young people
4301.e: With a consumer loan you borrow money for purchases and later have to pay it back with interest. This can quickly lead to debt if you are not careful.
4301.m: A consumer loan must be paid back with interest.

4302.q: In which part of a lake do whitefish usually swim?
a: In the reeds by the shore
4302.e: Many whitefish are open-water fish. They often travel in shoals through the lake, far from the shore.
4302.m: Whitefish usually live in open water.

4303.q: What sometimes happens with large perch?
a: They eat smaller perch of their own kind
They only drink water and eat nothing
4303.e: When there is little other food, large perch also eat smaller members of their own species. This behaviour is called cannibalism.
4303.m: Large perch also eat small perch.

4304.q: What is the name of the well-known mountain pass in the Jura that belongs to the canton of Solothurn?
4304.e: The Passwang lies in the Jura mountains in the canton of Solothurn and is popular with hikers and cyclists. From there you have a great view of the mountains.
4304.m: The Passwang is a pass in the Jura near Solothurn.

4305.q: What does a dolphin's skin feel like?
4305.e: Dolphins have no scales. Their skin is smooth and feels a bit like rubber.
4305.m: Dolphin skin is smooth, without scales.

4306.q: Which electoral system is mostly used to elect the Council of States?
4306.e: In a majority vote, whoever gets the most votes wins. This is how the Council of States is elected in most cantons.
4306.m: For the Council of States, whoever has the most votes usually wins.

4307.q: Who built the first successful powered aeroplane in 1903?
4307.e: In 1903 Orville and Wilbur Wright from the USA made the first controlled powered flight. Their aeroplane was called the Flyer.
4307.m: The Wright brothers invented the powered aeroplane.

4308.q: In German the guinea pig is called “Meerschweinchen” (literally “little sea pig”), even though it does not live in the sea. Where does the name probably come from?
a: The animals came to Europe across the sea and squeak a bit like little pigs
Because they can swim in the sea
4308.e: People think the name comes from the fact that the animals were brought to Europe across the sea. Also, their squeaking sounds remind some people of little pigs.
4308.m: The name recalls the sea and a pig.

4309.q: What is a swift's nest mainly made of?
a: Feathers, stalks and other material caught in the air
Stones it picks up from the ground
Mud it shapes like a swallow
4309.e: Because swifts hardly ever land, they collect their nesting material straight out of the air while flying. They glue the light pieces together with saliva to make a firm nest cup.
4309.m: Nesting material is collected in flight.

4310.q: Which part of a chimpanzee's body often has hardly any hair?
4310.e: A chimpanzee's face is usually almost hairless. This makes its facial expressions easy to see.
4310.m: The chimpanzee's face has hardly any hair.

4311.q: What is considered the biggest threat to the weasel today?
a: Loss of habitat through intensive farming
There is no threat at all
4311.e: Where hedges and meadows disappear, the weasel loses important hunting grounds and hiding places. Near-natural landscapes are therefore important for protecting it.

4312.q: What does the cockchafer grub do in winter?
a: It digs deeper into the ground
It spins a cocoon on a tree
4312.e: When there is frost, the grub moves down into deeper layers of soil that do not freeze. In spring it comes back up.

4313.q: How does the common wall lizard spend the winter?
a: In a winter stiffness in sheltered hiding places
It stays active like in summer
4313.e: When it is cold, the wall lizard looks for cracks and holes and becomes almost motionless. This winter stiffness lasts until temperatures rise again.

4314.q: What way of life does the otter usually have?
a: It lives in colonies like penguins
4314.e: Otters normally live alone and defend their own territory. They only get together in the mating season or with their own young.

4315.q: Which animal in North America is a relative of the African buffalo?
4315.e: Bison also belong to the cattle family. But they are a different species and live in North America.

4316.q: Which places does the cellar woodlouse especially like?
4316.e: The cellar woodlouse needs moisture, otherwise it dries out. That is why it likes living in cellars, under stones or in the compost heap.
4316.m: Cellar woodlice like it damp and dark.

4317.q: What happens when a garden spider moults?
a: It sheds its old skin, which has got too tight
4317.e: A new, softer skin grows under the old one. Then the spider climbs out of its old covering.
4317.m: It leaves its old skin behind.

4318.q: What are the young of the African wild dog called?
4318.e: As with other dogs, the young are called pups. They are born blind.
4318.m: Young wild dogs are called pups.

4319.q: How does a silverback often show its strength without really fighting?
a: By beating its chest loudly and showing off
4319.e: Instead of fighting straight away, the silverback prefers to show its strength by loud drumming and big gestures. This often lets it avoid a fight.

4320.q: How does a goldfish normally move through the water?
a: It moves its body and tail fin from side to side
It flies briefly over the water
4320.e: The goldfish swims by moving its body, and especially its tail fin, from side to side. The other fins help it steer.
4320.m: Goldfish swim with their body and tail fin.

4321.q: Which predators especially threaten the Alpine newt in ponds?
4321.e: In ponds and pools, it is mainly fish and predatory dragonfly larvae that lie in wait for newts and their larvae. That is why Alpine newts often avoid waters with lots of fish.
4321.m: Fish and dragonfly larvae endanger Alpine newts.

4322.e: The cubs are blind at birth and depend on their mother. Their eyes only open after a few days.

4323.q: How can you tell an adult rook from a carrion crow?
a: By the pale, bare skin at the base of its beak
4323.e: Adult rooks have a pale, featherless patch at the base of their beak. In the carrion crow the base of the beak is covered with small black bristly feathers.
4323.m: Rooks have a pale, bare beak base.

4324.q: What do young chimpanzees like doing, just like human children?
4324.e: Young chimpanzees like playing together, climbing and romping about. This way they learn important skills for growing up.
4324.m: Young chimpanzees like to play, just like children.

4325.q: What are the clumps of eggs the common frog lays in the water called?
4325.e: The common frog lays its eggs in large lumpy heaps called spawn clumps. These float on the surface of the water.
4325.m: Common frog eggs form a spawn clump.

a: Yes, especially the males often fly
4326.e: They fly clumsily with their body held upright. Males in particular fly about looking for females.

4327.q: What did the scarab stand for in ancient Egypt, among other things?
4327.e: New beetles hatch from the ball of dung. The Egyptians saw this as a sign of new life.

4328.q: How many seasons are there in Switzerland?
4328.e: In Switzerland there are spring, summer, autumn and winter. Each season lasts about three months.
4328.m: There are four seasons a year.

4329.q: Which position does a marmot often take up when it is keeping watch?
a: It stands upright on its back legs
It lies flat on the ground the whole time
It hangs upside down from a branch
It rolls up like a hedgehog
4329.e: When a marmot stands on its back legs, it can see further over the grass. This lets it spot approaching dangers earlier.

4330.q: How is the bonobo classified by the conservation organisation IUCN?
4330.e: The bonobo is considered endangered. Only a small part of the number of animals that used to live remains.

4331.q: What is often special about how the spots of fire salamanders are arranged?
a: It can range from a few large spots to lots of small dots
There are always exactly two spots
The spots are identical on every animal
The spots disappear after a year
4331.e: The pattern varies a lot from animal to animal: some have large spots, others fine stripes or lots of small dots. This variety makes every animal unique.
4331.m: Patterns range from spots to stripes.

4332.q: What relationship do female elephants usually have with their herd?
a: They stay together all their lives
They fight each other all the time
4332.e: Female elephants usually stay together with their daughters and sisters all their lives. This close family bond is very important to them.

4333.q: Where do domestic pigs normally live on a farm?
4333.e: The pigsty gives the animals shelter from the weather and a quiet place to sleep. Often they also have an outdoor area.

4334.q: What does the wolf mainly feed on?
a: Hoofed animals such as roe deer and red deer
4334.e: Wolves are meat-eaters and mainly hunt larger prey such as roe deer, red deer or wild boar. But smaller animals are also on their menu.

4335.q: Why does a housefly clean itself with its legs so often?
a: So that its feet can smell and taste well
4335.e: Because the housefly tastes and smells with its feet, they have to be clean. That is why it cleans its legs especially often.

4336.q: What is the difference in size between gibbons and orangutans?
a: Gibbons are much smaller and lighter
4336.e: Orangutans are great apes and are heavy. Gibbons are the lesser apes.

4337.q: About how heavy can a fully grown male otter get?
4337.e: Male otters usually weigh between six and ten kilograms. Females are usually a little lighter.
4337.m: An otter weighs up to about ten kilograms.

a: On the sides of the head, for a wide field of view
Only facing forwards like an owl's
On the top of the head
4338.e: Eyes on the sides give animals that flee from danger a very wide all-round view. This way alpacas spot danger early.
4338.m: Eyes on the sides give an all-round view.

4339.q: In which landscape does the African wild dog live most often?
a: In the high mountains of the Alps
4339.e: It needs open country where it can hunt its prey well. It usually avoids dense rainforests and deserts.
4339.m: Wild dogs need open country for hunting.

4341.q: How are tawny owl numbers in Switzerland doing at the moment?
a: It is not considered threatened and is widespread
It has already died out in Switzerland
It is now only found in zoos
4341.e: The tawny owl is a widespread and not threatened owl species in Switzerland. It benefits from being able to adapt well to different habitats.
4341.m: The tawny owl is not threatened in Switzerland.

a: The varroa mite and too few flowering meadows
4342.e: The varroa mite is a small parasite that can weaken bees and make them ill. A lack of flower meadows also makes it hard for bees to find enough food.
4342.m: Varroa mites are a serious danger to bee colonies.

4343.q: What does the cow give us that we like to drink?
4343.e: Cows give milk, which is used to make cheese, yoghurt and butter, for example. That is why there are cows on many Swiss farms.

4344.q: What is the golden eagle's large nest called?
4344.e: The nest of birds of prey such as the golden eagle is called an eyrie. A drey is a squirrel's nest, and a den is the home of a fox or a badger.
4344.m: An eagle's nest is called an eyrie.

4345.q: About how big is an adult bumblebee?
a: About as big as the top joint of your thumb
As small as a grain of sand
4345.e: Depending on the species, a bumblebee is about one to three centimetres long. That is roughly the size of the top part of a thumb.

4346.q: Which habitat does the red kite especially prefer?
a: Open farmland with fields and scattered trees
Thick, dark primeval forest without clearings
High mountain peaks above the tree line
4346.e: The red kite needs open areas for hunting and trees for nesting. A varied landscape with fields, meadows and forest edges suits it best.
4346.m: The red kite loves open farmland.

4347.q: What happens to the pollen the bumblebee collects?
a: It is taken to the nest as food for the larvae
It turns into honey for people
It is eaten and immediately forgotten
4347.e: The bumblebee carries the pollen it has collected back to the nest in its pollen basket. There it is important food for the larvae.
4347.m: Pollen becomes food for the larvae in the nest.

4348.q: How does a horse like to eat throughout the day?
a: Not at all, horses never eat
4348.e: A horse's stomach is quite small, so it prefers to eat lots of small portions spread over the day. This keeps its digestion healthy.

4349.q: What shape is an eagle owl's beak?
a: Thin and long like a hummingbird's
Broad and flat like a duck's
4349.e: The eagle owl's beak is strong and curved like a hook. With it, it can tear meat off its prey.
4349.m: The eagle owl has a strong hooked beak.

4350.q: What does a trout often do during the day when it is very bright?
a: It hides in the shade under stones
It swims up to the sunny surface
It digs itself deep into the sand
4350.e: In strong light trout often look for a shady hiding place under stones or plants. There they feel safer from enemies.

4351.q: Why is the sparrow's short, strong beak so handy?
4351.e: With its short, cone-shaped beak the sparrow can crack open hard seeds and grains well. This way it gets to the nutritious kernels inside.

4352.q: What is the adult female wild boar called?
4352.e: The female wild boar is called a sow. She looks after the piglets.
4352.m: A female wild boar is called a sow.

4353.q: Why is the golden jackal called an opportunist?
a: It adapts its diet to what is available
It only eats one single plant
It only lives in one single tree
4353.e: Opportunist means someone who makes use of opportunities. The golden jackal eats whatever it can find most easily around it.

4354.q: What can you see especially clearly on the toes of the tree frog compared with other native frogs?
a: Large, round sticky pads on the tips of the toes
4354.e: The striking sticky pads on the tips of the toes are typical of the tree frog. They let it climb, which many other frog species cannot do.

4355.q: Which group of animals does the earwig belong to?
4355.e: The earwig is not a worm but an insect. It has six legs and a body with a head, thorax and abdomen.

4356.q: How does a blackbird usually move on the ground?
4356.e: Blackbirds move forward on the ground by hopping or running fast. In between they often stop briefly.
4356.m: Blackbirds hop and run on the ground.

4357.q: Where does a housefly most like to lay its eggs?
4357.e: Houseflies like to lay their eggs on manure, rubbish or rotting matter. There the maggot that hatches finds enough food.
4357.m: Eggs are laid on rubbish or manure.

4358.q: What is unusual about young female stoats?
a: They can already become pregnant before they are weaned
They never have young of their own
They stay blind all their lives
4358.e: Amazingly, young female stoats can already become pregnant before they are even fully weaned. This helps the species increase quickly.

4359.q: In which city does the Swiss government, the Federal Council, meet?
4359.e: Bern is Switzerland’s federal city, and the Federal Council works there. The whole country is governed from there.

4360.q: About how big can a giraffe's heart be?
a: About as small as a pea
4360.e: The giraffe's heart has to pump blood a very long way up to the head. That is why it is especially big and strong.
4360.m: Giraffe hearts are very big and strong.

4361.q: How does the edible dormouse behave during the day?
a: It sleeps hidden in a hole
It climbs the tallest trees to enjoy the sun
4361.e: During the day the edible dormouse goes into a hole or hiding place and sleeps. Only at night does it become active again.
4361.m: During the day it sleeps in hiding.

4362.q: Where does the eel like to hide during the day?
a: In hollows, under stones or in the mud
On open sandbanks in the sun
4362.e: The eel loves hiding places on the bottom of the water. There it is protected from enemies.

4363.q: How is the lake trout rated in Switzerland?
a: It is the most common fish species
It is a species brought in from elsewhere
4363.e: Built-up streams and barriers to migration make life hard for the lake trout. That is why it is on the Red List in Switzerland.

4364.q: How does a cockchafer often react when you touch it?
a: It plays dead or lets itself drop
4364.e: Many beetles pull in their legs and stay completely still. This protects them from predators.

4365.q: Which group of animals does the dragonfly belong to?
4365.e: Dragonflies have six legs and a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen. These are typical features of insects.

4366.e: Forests are cleared, and leopards are hunted for their fur. There are also conflicts with people when livestock is killed.
4366.m: Habitat loss and poaching threaten leopards.

4367.q: Is it allowed to hunt beech martens in Switzerland?
a: Yes, but not during the closed season
Yes, all year with no rules
4367.e: In Switzerland the beech marten is one of the animals that may be hunted. But in spring and summer it has a closed season so that the young can grow up in peace. The cantons regulate the hunting in more detail.
4367.m: There is a closed season for beech martens.

4368.q: Where in Europe is the Alpine newt widespread?
a: In central Europe and the Balkans
4368.e: The Alpine newt lives in large parts of central Europe and reaches as far as Greece in the Balkans. In many countries it is a common kind of newt.
4368.m: The Alpine newt lives in large parts of Europe.

4369.q: How many eggs can a female carp lay at once?
4369.e: Female carp lay a huge number of eggs at once, often several hundred thousand. But not all the eggs become big fish.
4369.m: Carp lay a huge number of eggs.

4370.q: In which country do giant pandas live in the wild?
4370.e: Giant pandas only live in the wild in the mountain forests of China. There they are specially protected.
4370.m: China is the home of giant pandas.

4371.q: Who usually has the pups in a pack?
a: All the females at the same time
4371.e: Usually only the highest-ranking pair breeds. The other animals help raise the young.
4371.m: Usually only the leading pair has pups.

4372.q: How does the wood mouse move when climbing?
a: It climbs skilfully up plants and bushes
It needs wings to do it
4372.e: The wood mouse is a skilful climber and likes climbing up bushes and plants to get to food.

4373.q: Where does the common toad travel to in spring?
a: To a pond or lake to spawn
4373.e: In spring common toads travel to ponds and lakes to lay their eggs there. This journey is also called the toad migration.
4373.m: In spring toads travel to the pond.

4374.q: What is the best way to recognise a male sparrow?
a: By the black patch on its throat
4374.e: Male sparrows have a black patch under their beak, called a bib. Females do not have this patch.
4374.m: Males have a black patch on their throat.

4375.q: What sound does a sheep make?
4375.e: Sheep make the sound baa, which is also called bleating. This is how they talk to each other and call their lambs.

4376.q: What happens to an elephant's back teeth during its life?
a: They are replaced by new ones several times
They all fall out at once
4376.e: Elephants get several sets of new back teeth during their lives. When the last teeth are worn down, it becomes harder for them to eat.
4376.m: Back teeth grow back several times.

4377.q: How do baboons defend themselves against enemies?
a: Together as a group, especially the males
They hide one by one in the ground
4377.e: Adult males have large canine teeth and stand up to enemies. The group warns each other with loud calls.

4378.q: What does the return of the otter to Switzerland show?
a: That the rivers and lakes are recovering
That the rivers have got warmer
That more roads have been built
4378.e: After decades without otters, individual animals have been seen again in recent years. This shows that the waters are slowly recovering.
4378.m: The otter is slowly returning to Switzerland.

4379.q: In the picture a trout is jumping. What does it often do this for?
a: To get over small obstacles and steps
To hunt birds in the air
4379.e: Brown trout can jump over small waterfalls and weirs. Sometimes they also leap for insects.

4380.q: What does the dromedary feed on?
a: Plants, including thorny and salty ones
4380.e: Dromedaries are plant-eaters. In the desert they eat grasses, leaves and even thorn bushes.

4381.q: What happens when a strange pike swims into another pike's territory?
a: They become best friends at once
4381.e: Pike defend their own area in the water. They do not like other pike coming near them.

4382.q: What are fish like the lake trout, which hunt and eat other fish, called?
4382.e: The lake trout hunts live prey, mainly smaller fish. So it is a predatory fish. Fish that feed on plants and small creatures are called peaceful fish.
4382.m: The lake trout is a predatory fish.

4383.q: What does the European pond turtle mainly eat?
a: Small animals such as insects, tadpoles and small fish
4383.e: The pond turtle is mainly a meat-eater. It also hunts worms and snails.
4383.m: The pond turtle mainly eats small animals.

4384.q: Which animals eat earwigs, among others?
4384.e: For many small predators, earwigs are a meal. Shrews and spiders are among them too.
4384.m: Birds, toads and hedgehogs hunt earwigs.

4385.q: How are the toes on a cuckoo's foot arranged?
4385.e: The cuckoo has two toes pointing forwards and two backwards. This lets it hold on to branches well.
4385.m: The cuckoo has a handy climbing foot.

4386.q: What happens to a young cuckoo as soon as it can fly?
a: It flies south on its own
It stays with its foster parents for life
It immediately looks for its real mother
It builds a nest for its foster parents
4386.e: As soon as the young cuckoo can fly, it leaves its foster parents and sets off all alone on the long journey to Africa. It never meets its real parents along the way.
4386.m: A young cuckoo migrates all on its own.

4387.q: What kind of teeth do adult donkeys have, because they chew a lot of tough grass?
4387.e: Donkeys have strong molars that grind tough grass and straw well. Their teeth keep growing a little throughout their whole life.

4388.q: Which animal with big round ears and a colourful coat of yellow, black and white patches can you see in the picture?
4388.e: The African wild dog has an irregular, patchy coat. Each animal has its own pattern, a bit like a fingerprint.
4388.m: Every wild dog has a unique coat pattern.

4389.q: Why do wild geese often fly in a V formation in the sky?
a: Because it helps them save energy
Because it helps them hide better
Because it helps them swim faster
4389.e: Flying in the slipstream of the bird in front, the other geese need less effort. This lets them save energy on long journeys.
4389.m: The V shape saves energy when flying.

4390.q: Roughly how big does an adult tawny owl get?
4390.e: The tawny owl is a medium-sized owl with a body length of around 37 to 43 centimetres. Females are usually a little bigger than males.
4390.m: A tawny owl is about 40 centimetres long.

4391.q: In which mountain range did llamas originally live?
4391.e: Llamas come from the Andes. They are adapted to heights of several thousand metres.
4391.m: Llamas are animals of the Andes.

a: No, it is not a fish
Yes, it is a small fish
4392.e: Even though it lives in the sea, the starfish is not a fish. It belongs to a completely different group of animals.
4392.m: The starfish is not a fish.

4393.q: How can you recognise the redshank?
4393.e: The redshank's legs are bright orange-red. That is where its name comes from.

4394.q: How common is the magpie in Switzerland?
a: Widespread in the Central Plateau and in villages
4394.e: In Switzerland the magpie is common, above all in the Central Plateau and in towns, villages and fields. It is one of the best-known native birds.

4395.q: Which country does the budgerigar originally come from?
4395.e: Budgies come from Australia, where they live in the wild. Only later did they become popular pets.

4396.q: What is it called when salmon return from the sea to rivers to spawn?
4396.e: Salmon often swim far upstream to their spawning grounds. This journey is called the spawning migration.

4398.q: In which waters do most species of dolphin live?
a: In seas all around the world
Only in very cold polar seas
4398.e: Dolphins live in seas almost all over the world, from warm to cooler waters. Some species like it warmer, others cooler.

4399.q: How long can a kingfisher's nesting tunnel be?
4399.e: The tunnel it digs itself can lead up to one metre into the bank. At the end there is a round nesting chamber.
4399.m: The nesting tunnel goes up to one metre deep.

4400.q: What covers the body of the grass snake?
4400.e: Its body is covered in horny scales. They protect it from drying out.

4401.q: In which well-known fairy tale does a rooster appear together with a donkey, a dog and a cat?
4401.e: In this fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm, an old donkey, a dog, a cat and a rooster set off together for Bremen. In the end, together they chase robbers out of a house.
4401.m: The rooster is one of the Town Musicians of Bremen.

4402.q: What is the first thing a baby kangaroo has to do by itself after it is born?
4402.e: Straight after birth, the tiny baby has to crawl all on its own along the long way to its mother's pouch. Nobody helps it.
4402.m: The baby crawls to the pouch by itself.

4403.q: In which region does the Malayan tapir live?
4403.e: The Malayan tapir lives in Southeast Asia, for example on Sumatra and in Malaysia. It is the only species of tapir outside the Americas.
4403.m: The Malayan tapir lives in Southeast Asia.

4404.q: How does a baby gibbon spend its first weeks?
a: It clings to its mother's belly
It lies alone in a nest on the ground
Its father bathes it in water
4404.e: Newborn gibbons cling to the fur on their mother's belly. That way they stay safely with her even when she swings through the trees.
4404.m: Baby gibbons cling to their mother.

4405.q: What does a young cuckoo eat while it sits in another bird's nest?
a: Insects brought by its foster parents
Nothing at all, it goes hungry
4405.e: While the young cuckoo sits in the nest, its foster parents constantly bring it insects and caterpillars to eat. It begs for food especially loudly and persistently.
4405.m: Foster parents bring the cuckoo insects.

4406.q: What makes the common wall lizard especially different from mammals?
a: It is cold-blooded rather than warm-blooded
It feeds its young on milk
4406.e: Mammals keep their body temperature steady by themselves, but wall lizards do not. That is why they depend on warmth from outside.

4407.q: Which group of insects does the cockchafer belong to?
4407.e: The cockchafer is a beetle, and beetles are one of the groups with the most species of all. It belongs to the scarab beetle family.
4407.m: Cockchafers are beetles, more precisely scarab beetles.

4408.q: What does opposition mean in politics?
a: People or parties who disagree with the government.
4408.e: An opposition criticises the government and proposes other solutions. In dictatorships the opposition is often banned or persecuted.
4408.m: The opposition thinks differently from the government.

4409.q: How do wolves usually manage to hunt large prey?
4409.e: Because a single wolf can hardly overpower a large animal such as a deer, wolves usually hunt together in a pack. This way they can bring down much bigger animals.
4409.m: Hunting works better in a pack.

4410.q: What do chickens like to do to keep themselves clean?
4410.e: Chickens roll around in sand or soil. The dust bath gets rid of parasites in their feathers.
4410.m: Chickens like to bathe in dust.

4411.q: Why do you often find slow worms on forest paths after rain?
a: They hunt snails and worms there
4411.e: After rain, lots of snails and worms come out. The slow worm uses this chance to hunt.
4411.m: After rain there is more prey.

4412.q: What food does a common buzzard eat in addition to mice?
4412.e: As well as mice, the common buzzard also eats earthworms, beetles, amphibians and sometimes carrion. This makes it very adaptable.
4412.m: The buzzard eats many different things.

4413.q: How is a brown bear's winter rest different from true hibernation as in some small mammals?
a: In the brown bear, body temperature drops only slightly and it can still be woken
In the brown bear, body temperature drops much more than in small animals
Brown bears never wake up at all during the whole time
Brown bears keep eating regularly during this time
4413.e: In true hibernators such as marmots, body temperature drops very sharply. In the brown bear it is lowered only slightly, which is why it can be woken during its rest.
4413.m: A bear's winter rest is milder than true hibernation.

4414.q: What sometimes happens when a dead whale lies on the shore?
a: Several polar bears feed on it together
All the polar bears run away
The polar bears bury it in the snow
The polar bears ignore it completely
4414.e: Polar bears normally live alone. But at a large dead whale, several polar bears may for once gather to feed.
4414.m: With big prey, several feed together.

4415.q: How many teeth does an adult wolf have?
4415.e: Wolves have 42 strong teeth for gripping prey and breaking up meat and bones. Their long canine teeth are especially striking.

4416.q: What does the fur of young lynxes look like compared with adults?
a: Similarly spotted, but often softer and paler
4416.e: Young lynxes already have the typical spotted pattern, but their fur is softer. As they get older, the pattern becomes stronger and clearer.

4417.q: How many eyes does a bumblebee have?
a: Five, two large and three small
4417.e: Bumblebees have two large compound eyes for seeing and three small simple eyes on top of the head. These help them sense light.

4418.q: How are a donkey's ears different from a horse's?
a: Donkeys have no ears at all
4418.e: Compared with horses, donkeys have strikingly long ears. These help them hear especially well and cool down.

4419.q: What does the robin eat in winter as well as insects?
4419.e: When there are few insects in winter, the robin also eats berries and seeds. That way it still finds enough food.
4419.m: In winter it also eats berries.

4420.q: Roughly how long does a lioness carry her cubs in her belly before they are born?
a: About three and a half months
4420.e: A lioness is pregnant for about three and a half months before the cubs are born. This is called the gestation period.
4420.m: Lion cubs grow for about three and a half months before birth.

4421.q: Which animal from South America is a relative of the dromedary?
4421.e: Like the dromedary, the llama, alpaca and vicuña belong to the camel family. But they have no hump.
4421.m: The llama is a relative of the dromedary.

4422.q: What is the booklet called that explains the issues before a vote?
4422.e: Before every vote, all voters receive a booklet explaining the issues. This way they can find out more.
4422.m: The voting booklet explains the issues.

4423.q: What does a magpie like to eat most?
a: Almost anything, it is an omnivore
4423.e: Magpies eat insects, carrion, eggs, fruit, seeds and even rubbish. This varied diet helps them survive almost anywhere.
4423.m: Magpies eat almost anything they find.

4424.q: What does a solar cell do?
a: It turns sunlight directly into electricity
It stores heat for the night
4424.e: In a solar cell, particles of light hit a special material and free electrons in it. This movement of electrons produces the electric current.
4424.m: Solar cells turn light into electricity.

4425.q: Which sense helps you feel whether something is hot or cold?
a: The sense of touch in your skin
4425.e: In your skin there are tiny sensors that feel warmth, cold and pressure. That is the sense of touch.
4425.m: Your skin feels hot and cold.

4426.q: Why does the wall lizard shed its tail?
a: To be able to swim faster
4426.e: The twitching, detached tail distracts a predator for a moment. During that time the lizard can escape.
4426.m: A distraction saves it from enemies.

4427.q: Which animals is the slow worm more closely related to than to snakes?
4427.e: The slow worm is a lizard without legs. That is why it is more closely related to lizards than to snakes.
4427.m: The slow worm is a relative of lizards.

4428.q: What does a wild hamster do at night?
a: It runs a long way to look for food
It sleeps deep in its burrow
4428.e: In the wild, hamsters are awake at night and run long distances to look for food. That is why a pet hamster needs a wheel in its cage.
4428.m: Wild hamsters run far at night.

4429.q: Apart from light, what else does the sun give the Earth?
4429.e: The sun's rays warm up the Earth. Without this heat, it would be far too cold on Earth for life.
4429.m: The sun brings light and heat.

4430.q: What does a dog do when it is tired and relaxed?
4430.e: A tired dog looks for a cosy spot and lies down to sleep. On average, dogs sleep many hours a day.

4431.q: On which continent does the jaguar live in the wild?
4431.e: The jaguar is found in Central and South America. In the past its range also reached further into what is now the southern USA.

4432.q: How wide can a white stork's outspread wings be?
4432.e: A white stork's wingspan is around two metres. That makes it one of the largest birds in our region.
4432.m: The white stork has a wingspan of about two metres.

4433.q: What is the Japanese eel especially well known for in Japan?
a: As a popular fish to eat
As a good-luck charm at New Year
4433.e: Grilled eel is called unagi in Japan and is very popular. Because so many are caught, the Japanese eel is now endangered.
4433.m: The Japanese eel is a popular food fish.

4434.q: Roughly how old can African elephants live to be in the wild?
4434.e: Elephants can live to a great age. In the wild some even reach an age similar to humans.
4434.m: Elephants can live a very long time.

4435.q: How good is a hyena's sense of smell?
4435.e: Hyenas can smell carrion and prey from a great distance. This helps them find food.
4435.m: Hyenas smell food over long distances.

4436.q: Why is the name “pygmy chimpanzee” a bit misleading?
a: Bonobos are only slightly smaller than chimpanzees
Bonobos are not apes at all
4436.e: Bonobos are more slender, but not really tiny. That is why the name bonobo caught on.
4436.m: Bonobos are only a little smaller than chimpanzees.

4437.q: How many spots does the best-known ladybird in Switzerland have?
4437.e: The seven-spot ladybird is the most common species here. You can recognise it by its seven black spots on a red back.

4438.q: What special ability do the grey heron's eyes have when hunting?
a: They face forwards for good depth perception
They only see in black and white
They do not let light through
They only look to the side
4438.e: Forward-facing eyes allow the grey heron to judge distances very accurately. This is important for a precise stab at its prey.

4439.q: Is the blue whale threatened with extinction today?
a: No, there are huge numbers of them
It was wiped out a long time ago
4439.e: In the past a great many blue whales were hunted, so today there are not so many left. That is why it is protected.
4439.m: Blue whales need to be protected.

4440.q: When is the eagle owl mainly active?
a: Only in the depths of winter
4440.e: The eagle owl is active mainly at dusk and at night. During the day it usually rests hidden in a sheltered spot.
4440.m: The eagle owl hunts at dusk and at night.

4441.q: Which large group of animals does the jellyfish belong to?
4441.e: Jellyfish belong to the cnidarians because they have stinging cells. They are neither fish nor mammals.

4443.q: What does it mean that the red kite is an opportunistic feeder?
a: it eats almost anything it can find easily
it eats only a single kind of animal
it never hunts itself, but begs
4443.e: An opportunistic feeder adapts its feeding flexibly to what is available. So the red kite both hunts and eats carrion, depending on what is around.
4443.m: The red kite eats whatever is available.

4444.q: Why do butterflies sometimes drink at puddles?
a: To take in water and salt
4444.e: In damp sand and puddles, butterflies find water and salts their bodies need. That is why you often see them sitting there.
4444.m: At puddles they get salt and water.

4445.q: How long does a moose calf stay with its mother?
4445.e: The calf follows its mother until the next spring. By then she usually has a new young one.

4446.q: Where does the lake trout lay its eggs?
a: In hollows in the gravel of a stream bed
On water plants in the reeds
In the mud at the bottom of the lake
In a nest on the shore
4446.e: The eggs are laid in a hollow in the gravel and then lightly covered with gravel. This protects them from the current and from enemies.
4446.m: The eggs lie in the gravel.

4447.q: Roughly how many flowers do bees have to visit to collect nectar for some honey?
4447.e: For one jar of honey, bees together have to visit thousands of flowers. That is why many bees always work together.
4447.m: Honey needs lots of flower visits.

4448.q: What do an African buffalo's hooves look like?
a: Round and undivided like a horse's
4448.e: It walks on two toes that are covered with hooves. That makes it an even-toed ungulate.

4449.q: What colour are the patches on a king penguin's head?
4449.e: The king penguin has striking orange patches on its head and neck. After the emperor penguin, it is the second largest species of penguin.
4449.m: The king penguin has orange head patches.

4450.q: What is the goat breed called that is known for its especially fine wool?
4450.e: The cashmere goat has a very fine, soft undercoat. It is made into luxury fabrics.
4450.m: The cashmere goat gives the finest wool.

4451.q: What do you use a curry comb for when looking after a horse?
a: To brush the coat and remove dirt
4451.e: With a curry comb you brush dirt and loose hair out of the horse's coat. Many horses also find it pleasant.
4451.m: The curry comb cleans a horse's coat.

4452.q: How well can trout see with their eyes?
a: Quite well, even well enough to spot insects
They can only see at night
They see everything only in black and white
4452.e: Trout have fairly good eyes and can easily spot insects and other prey in the water. Good eyesight helps them hunt.

4453.q: How often is an alpaca usually shorn?
4453.e: The wool grows back slowly. So one shearing a year is usually enough.

4454.q: What do some ants do when they find a large source of food?
a: They call lots of helpers with scent trails
They eat it all up themselves
They hide it from their own colony
4454.e: When an ant finds lots of food, it lays a scent trail to the nest. That way many other ants quickly come to help.

4455.q: Roughly how many grams does an adult wood mouse weigh?
4455.e: An adult wood mouse weighs only about 15 to 25 grams, so it is very light.

4456.q: What are the ring-shaped spots in a leopard's fur called?
4456.e: The leopard's spots are arranged in rings and look like little roses. That is why they are called rosettes.
4456.m: Leopards have rosettes in their fur.

4457.q: What shape does a typical anthill often have?
a: Round like a ball in the air
4457.e: Many wood ants build their nest as a dome-shaped mound. The shape helps the rain run off.

4458.q: Roughly how big is a finished barn swallow's nest compared with a coffee cup?
a: About the size of half a coffee cup
As big as a whole barrel
Only as big as a pinhead
4458.e: A barn swallow's nest is roughly the size of half a coffee cup, so quite compact. Even so, several chicks fit inside.
4458.m: A swallow's nest is about as big as half a cup.

4459.q: How many toes does a guinea pig have on its back feet?
4459.e: Guinea pigs have only three toes on their back feet but four on their front feet. You can easily see these small differences if you look closely.
4459.m: Guinea pigs have three toes at the back.

4460.q: How do alpacas chew the cud?
a: They bring food back up and chew it again
They store it in cheek pouches
They digest it in their beak
4460.e: Alpacas are ruminants and chew their food several times. For this they have a stomach with several chambers.
4460.m: Alpacas chew their food several times.

4461.q: What does an alpine newt do when it spots prey?
a: It lies in wait and snaps quickly
4461.e: Alpine newts hunt by waiting motionless for prey to come past. As soon as an insect or worm is within reach, they snap at lightning speed.
4461.m: Alpine newts wait patiently for prey.

4462.q: What fins does the eel have?
a: One continuous fin made of the dorsal, tail and anal fins
4462.e: In the eel, the dorsal, tail and anal fins merge into one another. It also has small pectoral fins.
4462.m: The eel has one continuous fin.

4463.q: How can children earn a little money themselves?
a: With small jobs, for example watering the neighbours' flowers
By simply getting it from a cash machine
By asking the municipality for it
4463.e: By helping a little at home or in the neighbourhood, children can earn some extra money. But ask your parents first.
4463.m: Small jobs earn you your own money.

4464.q: How does a millipede usually move along?
4464.e: The legs move one after another in waves. That way the animal moves forward slowly but powerfully.
4464.m: Waves of legs push it forward.

4465.q: Which fin does the seahorse not have?
4465.e: Unlike many fish, the seahorse has no tail fin, because it uses its tail for holding on. But it does have a small dorsal fin and pectoral fins.
4465.m: It has no tail fin at all.

4466.q: What happens to a hippo's nostrils when it dives?
4466.e: When it dives, the hippo simply shuts its nostrils. That way no water gets in.

4467.q: In red kites, which sex is usually a little bigger and heavier?
4467.e: As in many birds of prey, female red kites are bigger and heavier than the males. This is called reversed size difference.

4468.q: What is the perch, called “Egli” in German-speaking Switzerland, called in French-speaking Switzerland?
4468.e: In French the perch is called perche. Brochet is the pike, truite the trout and carpe the carp.
4468.m: In French-speaking Switzerland the perch is called “perche”.

4469.q: What grows on a goat's head and is never shed?
4469.e: Unlike a deer with its antlers, a goat never loses its horns. They keep growing throughout its whole life.

4470.q: What do seahorses have instead of teeth?
a: A tube-shaped mouth for sucking in food
4470.e: Instead of teeth, seahorses have a thin tube-shaped mouth. With it they suck in small prey as if through a straw.

4471.q: Which senses especially help meerkats find prey in the sand?
4471.e: With their noses and ears they find insects under the ground. They do not have echolocation or a heat sense.
4471.m: Nose and ears help them search.

a: The carrier of genetic information in cells
4472.e: DNA is a molecule that contains the building plans for living things. It is found in the nucleus of almost all cells.

4473.q: Why are praying mantises protected in some countries?
a: Because their numbers can fall due to loss of habitat
Because there are too many of them
4473.e: Dry grasslands and warm slopes are becoming rarer. This means praying mantises are losing their habitats too.

4474.q: Which animal lives in the Swiss Alps, is a good climber and is often confused with the chamois?
4474.e: The ibex and the chamois look alike, but the ibex is much bigger and has much thicker, ridged horns. Both species live above the tree line.
4474.m: The ibex and the chamois are often confused.

4475.q: Where does the grey heron usually build its nest?
a: High in trees, often in colonies
In holes in the ground on riverbanks
Right on the ground in the reeds
In rock crevices high in the mountains
4475.e: Grey herons usually breed in large nests high up in trees. Several pairs often nest close to each other.
4475.m: Grey herons nest high in trees.

4476.q: Which fin is especially long in the wels catfish?
4476.e: In the wels catfish, the anal fin reaches almost to the tail fin. The dorsal fin, on the other hand, is very small.
4476.m: Long anal fin, small dorsal fin.

4477.q: How does a carrion crow usually fly?
a: straight ahead with strong, steady wingbeats
4477.e: Carrion crows typically fly in a straight line with strong, steady wingbeats. This makes them different from some birds of prey, which often glide.

4478.q: Which sea creature has eight arms and can change its colour?
4478.e: The octopus has eight arms and lives in the sea. It can change its colour in a flash to hide.

4479.q: Why do some ants carry a heavy piece of food together?
a: Because they are not allowed to carry it alone
Because the food does not taste good
4479.e: Several ants together can carry heavier things than one alone. They work together as a team.

4480.q: How are wild leopards doing in the world today?
a: There are many more every year
4480.e: Leopards are considered threatened worldwide. They are losing habitat and are poached. Some subspecies are already very rare.

4482.q: What do you call animals that hunt and eat other animals?
