4482.e: The puma is a predator. In its habitat it is often at the top of the food chain.

4483.q: What does a mother cow do when her calf is in danger?
4483.e: A mother cow protects her calf when it is in danger and stays close to it. The bond between cow and calf is very strong.

4484.q: What do many ants do in winter?
a: They rest through the winter in their nest
4484.e: In winter it gets too cold for the ants. They hide deep in the nest and hardly move at all.
4484.m: In winter ants rest in the nest.

4485.q: Roughly how long are alpacas pregnant?
4485.e: Female alpacas are pregnant for around eleven months. That is much longer than many other domestic animals.
4485.m: Alpacas are pregnant for about eleven months.

4486.q: How can you tell a harbour seal from a sea lion?
a: It has no visible ear flaps
4486.e: Sea lions have small visible ears and can prop themselves up on their flippers. Harbour seals have only ear holes and shuffle along on their bellies.
4486.m: Harbour seals have no visible ears.

4487.q: What colour is the Saanen goat usually?
4487.e: The Saanen goat is white and originally comes from the Saanenland in the canton of Bern. It gives a lot of milk.
4487.m: The Saanen goat is white and Swiss.

4488.q: What does a grasshopper chew its food with?
a: With strong jaws in its mouth
4488.e: The grasshopper has strong mouthparts for chewing. With them it breaks up grasses and leaves well.

4489.q: You see a picture of a leopard with jet-black fur. What is it often called?
4489.e: A leopard with black fur is often called a black panther. In good light you can still faintly see its rosettes.
4489.m: The black panther is a leopard.

4490.q: Roughly how old can alpine marmots live to be in the wild?
a: Only up to about two years
4490.e: In the wild, alpine marmots can reach a fairly great age of around fifteen years. That is a lot for a small mammal.
4490.m: Marmots can live a long time.

4491.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
4491.e: An octopus has three hearts that pump its blue blood around its body. Two of the hearts are just for the gills.

4492.q: Where do sea turtles mainly live?
a: In warm and temperate seas worldwide
4492.e: Sea turtles are found in warm and temperate oceans all around the world. They do not live in cold lakes or rivers in Switzerland.
4492.m: They live in warm seas worldwide.

4493.q: How do young bonobos learn what they can eat?
a: They copy a lot from their mother
They read instructions in the forest
4493.e: Young bonobos watch their mother and other members of the group. That is how they learn which fruits and plants are edible.

4494.q: What do you call animals that are active only at night?
4494.e: Nocturnal animals such as owls or hedgehogs sleep during the day and only wake up at dusk or at night. That way they can avoid enemies better.
4494.m: Nocturnal animals sleep during the day.

4495.q: When are most harbour seal pups born in the Wadden Sea?
4495.e: In the Wadden Sea, most harbour seal pups are born in June or July. Then it is warm and there are plenty of fish.
4495.m: Harbour seal pups are born in early summer.

4496.q: How do the cheetah's teeth compare with those of other big cats?
4496.e: The cheetah has smaller teeth than a lion, for example. This leaves room in its head for large nasal passages, which it needs for breathing.

4497.q: How does the great spotted woodpecker find insects under the bark?
a: it pecks small holes and pulls them out
it smells them from far away
it waits until they come out
4497.e: With its strong beak it knocks the bark open. That is how it gets to the larvae and beetles living underneath.
4497.m: It pecks holes to find beetles.

4498.q: What is the young of a buffalo called?
4498.e: As with cattle, the young is called a calf. It is fed on its mother's milk.

4499.q: What special shape do the swift's wings have?
a: narrow and curved like a sickle
round and short like a sparrow's
broad and straight like an eagle's
4499.e: The narrow, sickle-shaped wings make the swift especially fast and agile. This outline in flight helps you tell it apart from swallows.
4499.m: Sickle wings make the swift fast.

4500.q: What does it mean that leopards are mostly solitary?
a: They mostly live and hunt alone
They only live alone in zoos
4500.e: Adult leopards usually live alone and defend a territory. Only mothers with young go around together.

4501.q: How does a pond skater move along?
a: It glides with powerful rowing strokes
It pulls itself along with sticky threads
4501.e: It pushes off with its middle legs and glides quickly across the water. Its legs stay on the surface while it does so.
4501.m: Rowing strokes let it glide over the water.

4502.q: What are the spawn ribbons of the perch often attached to?
4502.e: The sticky spawn ribbons are wrapped around plants, branches or roots. That way they stay in place in shallow water.
4502.m: Spawn ribbons hang on plants and branches.

4503.q: Does the panda mainly eat plants, even though it is a bear?
4503.e: Although pandas belong to the bears, they eat almost nothing but bamboo. Only very rarely do they eat other plants or small animals.

4504.q: Which group of animals do gibbons belong to?
4504.e: Gibbons are primates and belong to the lesser apes. So they are closely related to orangutans, gorillas and chimpanzees.

4505.q: How many horns does the Indian rhinoceros have?
4505.e: The Indian rhinoceros has just a single horn on its nose. This makes it different from the African rhinos.
4505.m: The Indian rhino has only one horn.

4506.q: What happens to a horse's skin when it works very hard?
a: It sweats, much like a human
4506.e: Like humans, horses can sweat to cool down. This is quite rare among animals.

4507.q: What do newly hatched praying mantises look like?
4507.e: The praying mantis does not go through a pupa stage. The young look like the adults and grow by moulting.
4507.m: The young look like small adults.

4508.q: Roughly how long does it take a cockchafer to develop from egg to beetle in Central Europe?
4508.e: The grubs need several years before they turn into pupae. In Central Europe it usually takes three to four years.

4509.q: Why are lynxes sometimes moved from one area to another?
a: To improve the genetic variety of small populations
Because otherwise they would die out immediately
Because they have become too tame
So that they can live in zoos
4509.e: Small, separated lynx populations suffer from too little genetic variety. Moving animals helps to connect different groups.

4510.q: What happens if an earthworm is cut in two?
a: Usually one part dies; only sometimes does a bit grow back
Nothing, it does not even notice
4510.e: Contrary to what many people believe, a worm cut in two usually does not become a whole new worm. Only sometimes can the front part survive and grow back a small piece.
4510.m: A worm cut in two does not become two worms.

4511.q: How soon can newborn hippo calves swim?
4511.e: Hippo calves can swim or walk in the water shortly after birth. This is important because they are often born in the water.
4511.m: Hippo calves swim almost straight away.

4513.q: How does a least weasel mark its territory?
a: It does not mark its territory at all
4513.e: Like many members of the weasel family, the least weasel has scent glands that it uses to mark the borders of its territory. This warns other weasels not to come in.

4514.q: Which animal has long, curved horns and climbs steep rocks in the Alps?
4514.e: The ibex lives high in the mountains and can climb steep rock faces thanks to its special hooves. The chamois climbs too, but has only short little horns. The ibex is the heraldic animal of the canton of the Grisons.
4514.m: The ibex climbs in the mountains.

4515.q: How many stomach chambers do cattle have compared with llamas?
4515.e: Cattle have four stomach chambers. Llamas manage with three.
4515.m: Cattle have four chambers, llamas three.

4516.q: Which bear is especially closely related to the brown bear?
4516.e: Polar bears and brown bears are very close relatives and can even have young together. Despite their German names, which include the word “bear”, the koala, raccoon and anteater are not true bears at all.
4516.m: The polar bear is a close relative of the brown bear.

4517.q: What does the grey heron do with larger prey before swallowing it?
a: It turns it so that it slides down head first
It shares it with other herons
4517.e: So that the prey slides down more easily, the grey heron usually turns it so the head goes into its beak first. It often swallows large fish whole.

4519.q: What does a dragonfly larva eat?
a: Small water animals such as water fleas and mosquito larvae
4519.e: The larvae are predators. Large larvae even catch tadpoles or small fish.

4520.q: What are baboons' cheek pouches for?
a: For storing food for a short time
4520.e: Baboons can gather food in their cheek pouches and chew it later in peace. This lets them take in food quickly and then move away.
4520.m: Cheek pouches store food for a short time.

4521.q: What do plants do with sunlight?
a: They use it to make food to grow
They use it to glow at night
They use it to warm the soil
They store it in their roots
4521.e: Plants use sunlight to make food from water and a gas from the air. This is called photosynthesis.

4522.q: How does a housefly usually protect itself from danger?
a: It flies away in a flash
It makes itself look very big
4522.e: A housefly has no weapons to fight with. Instead it simply flees in a flash as soon as danger threatens.

a: Current is proportional to voltage and inversely proportional to resistance
Voltage and current are independent of each other
Resistance always decreases with more voltage
4523.e: Georg Simon Ohm found that I = U / R. So if you increase the voltage with the same resistance, the current rises in proportion.
4523.m: Current is voltage divided by resistance.

4524.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker do when it senses danger?
a: it hides behind the tree trunk
it calls for help loudly like a human
4524.e: The great spotted woodpecker is very cautious and quickly slips round to the other side of the trunk. Then its enemies can no longer see it.

4525.q: What helps the Roman snail glide along?
4525.e: The snail gives off slime so that it can glide more easily over the ground. The slime also protects it from sharp edges.

4526.q: On which continents is the brown bear found naturally today?
a: In Europe, Asia and North America
4526.e: The brown bear lives in parts of Europe, Asia and North America. There are no wild brown bears in Africa, South America or Australia.
4526.m: Brown bears live on three continents.

4527.q: What does a housefly often do with its front legs?
a: It rubs them together to clean itself
It digs a hole with them
It raises the alarm with them
4527.e: You often see houseflies rubbing their front legs together. This is how they clean themselves and remove dust from their bodies.
4527.m: Flies clean themselves with their legs.

4528.q: What is special about a moose's hoof?
a: It is broad and can spread
It is round and tightly closed
4528.e: The broad hooves spread the animal's weight. That way the moose sinks less deeply into snow and bog.
4528.m: Broad hooves carry it over snow.

4529.q: What colour is the beak of a male blackbird?
4529.e: The male's beak is bright yellow-orange and stands out clearly. The female has a darker beak.
4529.m: The blackbird's beak is bright yellow-orange.

4530.q: What makes the common frog different from the green water frog?
a: The common frog mostly lives on land
The common frog always lives in water
The common frog is bright green
The common frog has no webbed feet
4530.e: While the water frog almost always stays in or by the water, the common frog spends most of its time on land in woods or meadows. It only goes into the water to spawn.
4530.m: The common frog mostly lives on land, not in water.

4531.q: Roughly how big can the territory of a pair of golden eagles be?
4531.e: A pair of golden eagles claims and defends a large territory that can cover several dozen square kilometres. The exact size depends on how much food there is.

4532.q: You would like something expensive. What is a sensible thing to do?
a: Put some money aside every week until you have enough
Borrow money from friends straight away
Empty a brother's or sister's piggy bank
Lie to your parents so they buy it
4532.e: If you regularly put a little money aside, over time you will have enough for what you want. This is called saving.
4532.m: Save step by step for what you want.

4533.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker especially like to drum on?
4533.e: Dead wood sounds much louder than living branches. That way it can be heard over a long distance.

4534.q: What does the logo of the sports brand Puma show?
4534.e: The company Puma is named after the animal and uses a leaping big cat as its logo. The animal stands for speed and strength.
4534.m: The Puma logo shows a big cat.

4535.q: What do donkeys like to do to protect themselves from flies and insects?
a: They roll in dust or sand
4535.e: Donkeys like to roll in the dust because it keeps annoying flies away and protects their coat. Afterwards they give themselves a good shake.
4535.m: Donkeys like to roll in the dust.

4536.q: Which behaviour shows that ravens are playful animals?
a: they slide down snowy slopes for fun
they build little dams for fun
they jump into the water like dolphins
they climb trees playfully like monkeys
4536.e: Observations show that ravens slide on snow or ice for fun. This playful behaviour is seen as a sign of their great intelligence.
4536.m: Ravens slide in the snow for fun.

4537.q: What do chickens do to warn each other of predators?
4537.e: Chickens have different calls for different dangers, for example for enemies on the ground or in the air. This way they warn the whole group.
4537.m: Alarm calls protect the whole flock.

4538.q: Which enemies does the adult fire salamander have despite its poison?
a: Some birds, grass snakes and raccoons
None, because nothing can attack it
Only large fish in the sea
4538.e: Despite its poison, the fire salamander is sometimes eaten by grass snakes, certain birds or raccoons that have spread into the area. Not all animals are equally sensitive to its poison.

4539.q: What are gibbon calls mainly important for?
a: For marking territory and for the pair bond
For warning about people in the village
4539.e: Gibbons sing loud songs that carry far through the forest. This shows other groups where their territory is and strengthens the bond between the pair.
4539.m: Gibbon song shows territory and togetherness.

4540.q: Does the badger sometimes share its sett with another wild animal?
4540.e: Sometimes a fox lives in one part of a large badger sett. The two usually keep out of each other's way.
4540.m: Sometimes a fox and a badger share a sett.

4541.q: Which huge sandy desert do many of our migrating birds fly across on their way to Africa?
4541.e: On their way to warmer areas, many migrating birds cross the huge, dry Sahara. This part of the journey is especially tiring for the birds.
4541.m: The Sahara is a big obstacle for migrating birds.

4542.q: What does the body mainly need vitamin C for?
a: For a strong immune system and healthy connective tissue
4542.e: Vitamin C supports the body's defences and is important for the skin and for healing wounds. The body cannot make it itself.
4542.m: Vitamin C strengthens your immune system.

4543.q: What does the mute swan use its long neck for?
4543.e: The long neck is like a tool for feeding. With it the swan reaches plants that grow deeper in the water.
4543.m: The long neck helps with feeding.

4544.q: Why should you not scatter bird food straight on the ground?
a: It quickly gets dirty and wet
Birds do not like the ground
4544.e: Food on the ground quickly gets wet or dirty and diseases can spread more easily. That is why it is better to use a bird table.
4544.m: Bird tables are cleaner than the ground.

4545.q: Does the blue whale have teeth in its mouth?
a: Yes, lots of small sharp teeth
4545.e: Instead of teeth, the blue whale has long, comb-like baleen plates in its mouth. It uses them to filter krill from the water.
4545.m: Baleen instead of teeth in a whale's mouth.

4546.q: What do you call storks that stay here all year round?
4546.e: Some storks no longer fly to Africa nowadays but stay here all year. Birds like this are called resident birds.

4547.q: Why do researchers like to observe chimpanzees so much?
a: Because they are very similar to us humans
Because they are the biggest apes
4547.e: Chimpanzees are our closest relatives in the animal kingdom. That is why researchers also learn a lot about us humans by studying them.
4547.m: Chimpanzees are very similar to humans.

4548.q: What is the home called that a beaver builds from branches and mud?
4548.e: A beaver lodge is a dome-shaped structure made of branches and mud, usually standing by the water. The entrance is underwater so that enemies cannot get in.

4549.q: Where does the alpine newt often spend the winter if it stays on land?
a: Under leaves, stones or in compost heaps
In the middle of a frozen lake
In a bird's nest high in a tree
4549.e: For the cold season, the alpine newt looks for a frost-free hiding place, for example under leaves, stones or in a compost heap. It stays there until spring.
4549.m: Compost heaps make good winter quarters.

4550.q: Roughly how many teeth does an adult lion have?
4550.e: An adult lion has about 30 sharp teeth. The long canine teeth in particular help it hold on to its prey.

4551.q: What is typical of the red panda's tail?
a: It has no tail at all
It is short like a hare's
4551.e: The red panda has a long, bushy tail with rings. It helps it balance in the trees.
4551.m: The red panda has a ringed tail.

4552.q: How many legs does a stag beetle have?
4552.e: Like all insects, it has six legs. They are attached to the middle part of the body, the thorax.

4554.q: How many arms does a starfish usually have?
4554.e: Most starfish have five arms growing around the middle. But some species have more arms.

4555.q: What is an important reason why the great crested grebe is protected in Switzerland today?
a: Its numbers fell in the past due to hunting and loss of habitat
Because it is considered dangerous to people
Because it is very rarely eaten
4555.e: Hunting and loss of habitat once caused numbers to fall sharply. Today protection measures have allowed the species to recover.

4556.q: What is special about the eel's skin?
a: It is slimy and has very small scales
It is covered with large hard plates
It is covered all over in spines
4556.e: The eel's scales are tiny and embedded in its skin. A layer of slime protects it and makes it smooth.
4556.m: Eels are slippery and hardly have scales.

a: Through very little precipitation over a long time
4558.e: Deserts are often in areas with particular wind patterns where hardly any rain clouds reach. That is why hardly any precipitation falls there for years.

4559.q: How does an earthworm lay its eggs?
a: In a nest made of twigs
In a cave made of stone
In an egg like a bird
4559.e: The earthworm forms a small cocoon with the thick band around its body. Inside it, the young worms develop safely.
4559.m: Baby worms grow in a cocoon.

4560.q: When do you normally hear the cuckoo calling in Switzerland?
a: In spring, when it comes back
Only in the depths of winter
4560.e: The cuckoo returns from its winter quarters in spring and starts calling straight away. For many people its call is a sign that spring has arrived.

4561.q: Why do moose like to eat water plants?
a: They contain important minerals such as sodium
They are poisonous and protect them
4561.e: Water plants provide salt and minerals that are often missing on land. That is why moose visit lakes in summer.

4562.q: What do the young eel larvae look like that drift across the Atlantic to Europe?
a: Flat and see-through like a leaf
Like tadpoles with tufts of gills
4562.e: The larvae are flat, see-through and leaf-shaped. This lets them drift towards Europe with the Gulf Stream.
4562.m: Eel larvae are flat like a leaf.

4563.q: Which sense is especially important for the stoat when hunting?
a: The sense of touch in its ears
4563.e: With its keen sense of smell, the stoat tracks down mice even in their hidden tunnels. This makes it a successful hunter.
4563.m: The sense of smell helps it hunt.

4564.q: What happens to the male mute swan's knob during the breeding season?
4564.e: In males, the knob grows a little during the breeding season. Afterwards it gets a bit smaller again.
4564.m: The knob grows in the breeding season.

4566.q: What does a mute swan do when it feels threatened?
4566.e: When a swan feels threatened, it hisses loudly like a snake. This is how it warns other animals or people.

a: Velvet, a skin full of blood vessels
4568.e: The velvet supplies the growing antlers with blood. Once the antlers are finished, the velvet is rubbed off.

4569.q: Which animal is one of the most important natural enemies of young ibex kids?
4569.e: Golden eagles can catch small kids that are still clumsy, especially when they wander away from their mother. The bearded vulture mainly eats bones from dead animals. Adult ibex have hardly any natural enemies.
4569.m: The golden eagle hunts young kids.

4570.q: What is the thin membrane called that surrounds the lung and lets it glide in the chest?
4570.e: The pleura consists of two smooth layers with fluid between them. This lets the lung glide smoothly when you breathe.
4570.m: The pleura lets the lung glide.

4571.q: How does a female alpine salamander normally bring her young into the world?
a: As live young, not as eggs
4571.e: Unlike many other amphibians, the female does not lay eggs but gives birth to fully developed young. This is called giving birth to live young.
4571.m: Alpine salamanders give birth to live young.

4572.q: What does it mean when people say penguins are monogamous?
a: Many often stay with the same partner
4572.e: Many penguin species find a partner and stay together for several years, sometimes for life. This is called monogamous.
4572.m: Many penguins stay loyal to one partner.

4573.q: Which prey animals does the African wild dog often hunt?
4573.e: It hunts antelopes such as impalas and sometimes young wildebeest too. The prey depends on the area.
4573.m: Impalas and wildebeest are on the menu.

4574.q: What does an adult tree frog mainly eat?
4574.e: Tree frogs are pure meat eaters and hunt small insects and spiders. They do not eat plants.

4575.q: How well can a pine marten climb?
a: It climbs very skilfully and can even jump from branch to branch
It climbs only very slowly and clumsily
It only climbs on very flat stones
4575.e: The pine marten is an excellent climber and moves through the treetops with great ease. It can even make daring leaps between branches.

4576.q: What do African buffalo do when they notice danger?
a: They raise their heads and watch
4576.e: Alert animals warn each other, often through their posture or sounds. Then the herd can flee or gather together.
4576.m: Buffalo keep a watchful eye on their surroundings.

4577.q: What do a cat's ears often reveal about its mood?
a: ears turned back often show fear or anger
the position of the ears only shows the weather
cats cannot move their ears at all
4577.e: Cats can turn their ears independently of each other and use them to show their mood. Ears laid back usually point to fear, anger or readiness to defend themselves.
4577.m: The position of the ears shows a cat's mood.

4578.q: Roughly how heavy is an adult grey heron?
4578.e: Despite its impressive size, the grey heron weighs relatively little, usually around one and a half kilograms. Its feathers and hollow bones make it light for flying.
4578.m: It is lighter than you might think.

4579.q: Which animal family does the least weasel belong to?
4579.e: The least weasel belongs to the family Mustelidae, the weasel family. This also includes the stoat and the badger.
4579.m: The least weasel is a small mustelid.

4581.q: What colour is a wood mouse's fur usually?
a: Reddish-brown on top and white on the belly
4581.e: The wood mouse's fur is reddish-brown on top but pale, almost white, on the belly. This helps it hide well among leaves.
4581.m: Reddish-brown on top, white on the belly.

4582.q: Which season is the main breeding season of the blackbird?
a: Only in the middle of winter
4582.e: Spring and summer are the main time when the blackbird builds nests and raises its young. That is also when there is the most food in nature.
4582.m: Blackbirds breed mainly in spring and summer.

4583.q: Which river was especially important for salmon migrating into Switzerland in the past?
4583.e: The Rhine flows into the North Sea. In the past, salmon swam up it as far as Switzerland.
4583.m: Salmon came to Switzerland via the Rhine.

4584.q: Apart from howling, how else do wolves communicate with each other?
a: Through body posture, facial expression and the position of their ears
Only through changes in the colour of their fur
4584.e: As well as sounds such as barking and growling, wolves also use their posture, their ears and their facial expressions to show their mood. This way pack members understand each other even without loud noises.
4584.m: Wolves also communicate through body language.

4585.q: What sound does a goose typically make?
4585.e: Geese make loud honking calls. They use them to communicate with each other and to warn of danger.

4586.q: What do ducklings usually sound like?
4586.e: Little ducklings make fine, soft peeping sounds. This helps them keep in contact with their mother.

4587.q: What do ibex do when they feel threatened?
a: They flee in a flash to rocky ground that is hard to reach
They dig themselves in at lightning speed
4587.e: When in danger, ibex flee to steep, inaccessible rocky ground where most enemies cannot follow them. Their climbing skills are their best protection.
4587.m: Fleeing to steep ground protects the ibex.

4588.q: Who does a rooster usually live with on a Swiss farm?
a: With the ducks in the pond
With the dog in its kennel
4588.e: In Switzerland, roosters are usually kept together with a group of hens, often with space to roam outside. There they can scratch and peck.
4588.m: Roosters usually live with several hens.

4589.q: What is it called when an animal looks like another object or living thing so that it is not noticed?
4589.e: Some praying mantises look like leaves, twigs or flowers. This makes them hard to spot.

4591.q: What does a mute swan do to keep its feathers clean?
a: it preens them every day with its beak
it lets other birds clean them
4591.e: With its beak, the swan pulls and smooths each feather one by one. This keeps its plumage clean and waterproof.
4591.m: The beak is also a cleaning tool.

4592.q: What is the spout of water called that a blue whale blows into the air when it breathes out?
4592.e: When the blue whale breathes out, a tall fountain of water and air appears. Researchers call this spout the blow.

4593.q: Roughly how long does a hen sit on an egg before a chick hatches?
4593.e: A hen's egg takes about 21 days to hatch. Only then does the little chick break out of the shell.
4593.m: A hen's egg takes about three weeks to hatch.

4594.q: What does the reindeer especially like to eat in winter?
4594.e: In winter, reindeer scrape away the snow and eat lichens. This so-called reindeer lichen grows on the ground of the tundra.

4595.q: What does the barn owl like to eat most?
4595.e: The barn owl feeds mainly on small mice. It catches them at night in the fields.

4596.q: Where does the name “dromedary” originally come from?
4596.e: The name goes back to the ancient Greek “dromas”, which means runner. It refers to the animal's speed.

4597.q: Which statement about the tail of orangutans is true?
a: They have a long gripping tail
They have a short furry stump of a tail
4597.e: Like all great apes, orangutans have no tail. This makes them different from many other monkeys.

4598.q: Why should you wash your hands after touching a tree frog?
a: The slime on its skin can irritate your eyes
It is deadly poisonous to humans
Its skin turns your hands green
4598.e: The slime on a tree frog's skin can cause a burning feeling if it gets into your eyes. That is why it is wise to wash your hands after touching one.
4598.m: Wash your hands after touching one.

4599.q: What often happened to farms in communist countries?
a: They were merged into large state farms
They were sold to rich families
4599.e: In many communist countries, farmers had to give up their farms. The state then farmed the land collectively.
4599.m: Farms often belonged to the state.

4600.q: What is the central statement of Einstein’s special theory of relativity?
a: The speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all observers, time and space are relative
Time passes at exactly the same rate for everyone in the universe
Gravity does not exist in the theory of relativity
Mass and energy have nothing to do with each other
4600.e: Einstein showed that the speed of light in a vacuum is always the same, no matter how fast observers are moving. It follows that time and space are perceived differently depending on the state of motion.
4600.m: The speed of light is constant, time is relative.

4601.q: Which big railway town belongs to the canton of Solothurn?
4601.e: Olten is also in the canton of Solothurn and is known as an important railway junction. From there, trains go in many directions across Switzerland.
4601.m: Olten is an important railway town in the canton of Solothurn.

4602.q: Which animals are relatives of the snow leopard?
a: The deer and the roe deer
4602.e: They all belong to the genus Panthera. Genetically, the tiger is its closest relative.
4602.m: The tiger and the lion are relatives.

4603.q: Why do cows often stand together in a group in the pasture?
a: They like living in a herd
They do not like other cows
4603.e: Cows are sociable animals and like to live together in a herd. In a group they feel safer.
4603.m: Cows like living in a herd.

4604.q: Roughly how many years does a beaver live in the wild?
4604.e: In the wild, beavers usually live to about 7 to 10 years. In human care they can live a little longer because dangers such as predators are missing.

4605.q: What do sheep sometimes eat in winter as well as grass, when little fresh green grows?
4605.e: In winter, when little fresh grass grows outside, sheep are often given dried hay to eat. It is like summer grass packed up for the winter.

4606.q: Which animal is one of the natural enemies of young kangaroos?
4606.e: The dingo is a wild dog in Australia and sometimes hunts young kangaroos. But adult, large kangaroos can defend themselves well.

4607.q: What is the name of a well-known species of wasp often found in Switzerland?
4607.e: The German wasp is one of the most common wasp species here. You can recognise it by its yellow and black stripes.
4607.m: The German wasp is very common.

4608.q: Which family does the African wild dog belong to?
4608.e: It belongs to the dog family (Canidae). Despite its looks, it is not closely related to hyenas.
4608.m: Wild dogs belong to the dog family.

4609.q: Where do chimpanzees mainly live in the wild?
4609.e: Chimpanzees live in the forests and savannahs of Africa. There they find enough fruit and leaves to eat.
4609.m: Wild chimpanzees live only in Africa.

4610.q: What makes llama wool a popular material in cold regions?
a: It insulates well against the cold
4610.e: The thick coat keeps them warm. That is why llamas are suited to the climate of the Andes.

4611.q: Which element do mosquitoes absolutely need for their larvae to develop?
4611.e: Mosquito larvae live only in water and cannot develop without it. That is why mosquitoes always lay their eggs near water.
4611.m: Mosquito larvae need water to live.

4612.q: Which birds of prey are among the enemies of the adder?
a: The short-toed snake eagle and the common buzzard
4612.e: Birds of prey sometimes catch snakes. Foxes, wild boar and hedgehogs are also among its enemies.

4613.q: What is the difference between a mandatory and an optional referendum?
a: With a mandatory one, a proposal goes to the people automatically; with an optional one, only with enough signatures
With an optional one, only Parliament decides
The mandatory one only exists in municipalities
4613.e: Certain proposals such as constitutional amendments must go to the people. Federal acts only go to the people if there are enough signatures.
4613.m: Mandatory is automatic, optional needs signatures.

4614.q: Roughly how high is the record speed measured for a peregrine falcon in a dive?
4614.e: The fastest measured dive of a peregrine falcon was almost 390 km/h. That makes it the fastest animal in the world.
4614.m: Almost 390 km/h in a record dive.

4615.q: How are hyenas useful for the ecosystem?
a: They clear away carrion and keep things clean
4615.e: By eating dead animals, hyenas stop diseases from spreading. They even make use of bones.

4616.q: What is the panda a symbol of around the world today?
4616.e: The panda is a popular symbol for protecting endangered animals and nature. Many organisations use its image.
4616.m: The panda stands for nature conservation.

a: a large group of sparrows flying together
4617.e: When many sparrows fly through the air together, it is called a flock. In a group they are better protected from enemies.
4617.m: Many sparrows together are called a flock.

4618.q: What important job do tapirs do in the forest?
a: They spread seeds in their droppings
4618.e: Tapirs eat fruit and later pass the seeds out again. This helps new trees to grow.
4618.m: Tapirs spread seeds in the forest.

4619.q: What is the body of the garden spider mainly made up of?
a: Two parts, the front body and the abdomen
4619.e: Unlike insects, spiders have only two body parts. At the front, head and chest are joined together, and behind that comes the round abdomen.
4619.m: A spider's body has two parts.

4620.q: Which is bigger and heavier in golden eagles?
a: Both are exactly the same size
4620.e: In golden eagles, the females are clearly bigger and heavier than the males. This size difference is called reversed sexual dimorphism.

4621.q: What, among other things, does the earwig use its pincers for?
a: For defence and for holding on
4621.e: With its pincers the earwig can defend itself against enemies and grab others of its kind. They also help when males fight with each other.
4621.m: The pincers are for defence and holding on.

4622.q: Which legs does the pond skater mainly use for rowing?
4622.e: It pushes itself forward over the water with its middle pair of legs. They work like a pair of oars.
4622.m: Middle legs row, back legs steer.

4623.q: How do pairs of ravens usually behave towards their territory?
a: they often defend it all year round
they give it up straight after the breeding season
they willingly share it with other pairs
4623.e: Paired ravens usually claim and defend their territory against other ravens all year round. This gives them enough food and a good breeding site in the long term.

4624.q: How many legs does an adult fire salamander have?
4624.e: Like all amphibians, the fire salamander has four legs. It uses them to waddle slowly along.
4624.m: Four legs carry the fire salamander.

4625.q: Which bird is one of the most dangerous natural enemies of the alpine marmot?
4625.e: The golden eagle is one of the largest birds of prey in the Alps and also hunts marmots. The bearded vulture, on the other hand, mainly eats bones from dead animals. Marmots warn each other with whistles as soon as an eagle appears.
4625.m: The golden eagle hunts marmots from the air.

4626.q: Which dog was once specially bred to hunt badgers in their setts?
4626.e: The dachshund has short legs and a narrow body so that it fits into narrow badger setts. That is also where its name comes from: “Dachs” is German for badger.
4626.m: The dachshund is named after the badger.

4627.q: What happens to the wood mouse in winter?
a: It stays active and looks for hidden food stores
It hibernates deeply like a hedgehog
4627.e: Unlike a hedgehog, the wood mouse does not hibernate. It stays active and lives on food stores it has collected.

4628.q: How many legs does an insect such as an ant have?
4628.e: Insects such as ants, beetles or bees have exactly six legs. This makes them different from spiders, for example, which have eight legs.

4630.q: What is an international treaty referendum?
a: Under certain conditions the people can vote on international treaties
A referendum only for EU countries
A treaty that only the Federal Council signs
4630.e: Certain important international treaties are subject to a mandatory or optional referendum. This lets the people have a say on foreign policy matters too.
4630.m: International treaties can also be put to the people.

4631.q: Roughly how high can a puma jump from a standing position?
a: Not at all, it cannot jump
4631.e: Pumas have powerful back legs and can jump several metres high. They are also very good at long jumps.

4632.q: What kind of ears does a hamster have?
a: Very pointed ears like a fox
4632.e: Hamsters have small, round ears on their heads. They hear very well with them, even quiet sounds.

4634.q: What do baby dolphins drink at the start of their lives?
4634.e: Dolphin mothers feed their young with very fatty milk. This helps the baby grow strong quickly.
4634.m: Baby dolphins drink their mother's milk.

4635.q: How does the brimstone butterfly usually spend the winter?
a: As an adult butterfly hidden in bushes
As an egg deep in the ground
4635.e: In winter, the brimstone hides among leaves or in shrubs. That is why you can see it on the very first warm days of spring.
4635.m: The brimstone spends the winter hidden away.

4636.q: Why does a male blackbird sing so loudly?
4636.e: With its song, the male blackbird shows other males that this area is already taken. At the same time it attracts a female.

4637.q: What colour is a horse that is called a “grey”?
4637.e: A grey horse has a white or light grey coat. Many greys even get lighter as they get older.
4637.m: A grey horse is usually white.

4638.q: What do young earwig nymphs look like?
4638.e: The nymphs already look very like the adults, but they are smaller and have no wings yet. They keep growing with each moult.
4638.m: Nymphs already look like the adults.

4639.q: Why is the garden spider's web sticky?
a: So that insects get stuck on it
4639.e: The sticky threads make flying insects stick to the web. That way the spider can catch them easily.

4640.q: Which larvae with pincer-like jaws hunt aphids and are also called “aphid lions”?
4640.e: Lacewing larvae grab aphids with their sucking jaws and suck them dry. That is why they are called aphid lions.
4640.m: Lacewing larvae are called aphid lions.

4641.q: What is the mating season of bison called?
4641.e: In hoofed animals, the mating season is called the rut. In bison it takes place in summer.
4641.m: The mating season of hoofed animals is called the rut.

4642.q: What happens if more people say Yes than No in a vote?
a: The proposal is forgotten at once
4642.e: If there are more Yes votes than No votes when they are counted on voting Sunday, the proposal is accepted.
4642.m: If there are more Yes votes, the proposal is accepted.

a: Dead wood that is left in the forest
4643.e: Deadwood is important for many animals, including stag beetles. Larvae, fungi and many other species live in it.
4643.m: Deadwood is a habitat for many animals.

4644.q: Roughly how long is a newborn blue whale calf?
4644.e: Even at birth, a blue whale calf is as long as a small lorry. After that it keeps growing very quickly.
4644.m: Baby blue whales are already huge.

4645.q: How do baby hamsters come into the world?
a: They hatch from an egg like chicks
They hatch from a pupa like butterflies
4645.e: Hamsters are mammals and have live young. At first the young drink their mother's milk.
4645.m: Hamsters give birth to live young.

4646.q: How does the wels catfish behave when the water is warm in summer?
a: It is active and eats a lot
4646.e: Warm water makes the wels catfish active and hungry. In the cold winter, on the other hand, it is rather sluggish.
4646.m: Warmth makes the wels catfish active.

4647.q: Which two fins are set far back on the pike, near the tail fin?
4647.e: In the pike, the dorsal fin and anal fin are set very far back, almost at the tail fin. This gives it extra power when it shoots forward.
4647.m: Dorsal and anal fins are set far back.

4648.q: What do you call the area that a puma claims for itself and defends against other pumas?
4648.e: Pumas mark their territory with scent marks and scratches. This tells other pumas that it is taken.

4649.q: When is the main breeding season of the magpie?
a: In spring, usually between March and May
4649.e: Magpies breed mainly in spring, when there is enough food for raising the young. The female sits on the eggs for about three weeks.

4650.q: What is the main task of the UNHCR?
a: To protect and support refugees around the world
4650.e: The UNHCR is the refugee agency of the United Nations. It works to make sure that people who have fled get protection, shelter and rights.
4650.m: The UNHCR protects refugees around the world.

4651.q: How does a carrion crow behave towards its territory during the breeding season?
a: it defends it fiercely against intruders
it willingly shares it with all other crows
it leaves it for the whole summer
4651.e: During the breeding season, pairs of carrion crows fiercely defend their territory against other crows and possible enemies. This protects their nest and young.

4652.q: Roughly how many eggs does a female grass snake lay?
4652.e: The size of the clutch can vary depending on the age and size of the female. Usually it is about 10 to 30 eggs.
4652.m: A clutch usually has 10 to 30 eggs.

4653.q: What happens when a shark loses a tooth?
a: A new tooth grows in its place
The shark can no longer eat
It has a gap in its teeth for ever
4653.e: Sharks have many rows of teeth in their mouths. If a tooth falls out, a new one simply moves up.

4654.q: Which genus does the snow leopard belong to, just like the lion and the tiger?
4654.e: Like the lion, tiger, leopard and jaguar, the snow leopard belongs to the genus Panthera. Its scientific name is Panthera uncia.
4654.m: The snow leopard belongs to the genus Panthera.

4655.q: Why do reptiles such as lizards often bask on warm stones?
a: To raise their body temperature, as they are cold-blooded
4655.e: Because reptiles cannot control their body temperature themselves, they use the warmth of the sun to become active and able to move. When it gets too hot, they look for shade again.
4655.m: Reptiles use the sun to warm up.

4656.q: Why does a stone marten often bite cables in a car's engine compartment?
a: It is defending its territory against the scent of other martens
Because it likes the colour of the cables
Because it needs the rubber as food
Because it plays with them like a ball
4656.e: Martens mark their territory with scents. If it smells another marten in the engine compartment, the stone marten often attacks the cables aggressively.

4657.q: What does the black-backed jackal sometimes catch?
4657.e: It hunts small animals and sometimes also young antelopes. Jackals often hunt together.
4657.m: Young antelopes are on the menu too.

4658.q: Which of these snakes in Switzerland is venomous?
4658.e: There are two venomous snakes in Switzerland: the asp viper and the adder. The other three snakes are harmless to humans.

4659.q: Which large group of insects does the mosquito belong to?
4659.e: Mosquitoes belong to the true flies because they have only one pair of real wings for flying. Houseflies belong to the same group, by the way.
4659.m: Mosquitoes are true flies, like houseflies.

4660.q: Why do woodlice avoid dry, sunny places?
a: They quickly lose water there and dry out
They are blind in the light
4660.e: Their shell does not protect them well against losing water. That is why they stay in damp places.

4661.q: Roughly how long can an adult eagle owl get?
4661.e: An adult eagle owl reaches a body length of up to about 75 centimetres. That makes it much bigger than most other European owl species.
4661.m: Eagle owls grow up to 75 cm long.

4662.q: What does the wood mouse often collect for the winter?
a: Seeds and nuts as a store
4662.e: The wood mouse hides seeds and nuts in its burrow so that it has enough to eat in winter.
4662.m: It collects seeds for the winter.

4663.q: What is the hollow called in which a trout lays its eggs?
4663.e: This hollow in the gravel bed of a stream is called a redd. The trout digs it especially for its eggs.
4663.m: The redd is the trout's nursery.

4664.q: What is typical of the stripe along the side of a male alpine newt in breeding colours?
a: It is bluish with black dots
4664.e: In breeding colours, the male shows a typical bluish band along the sides of its body, marked with black dots. This feature helps to identify it.
4664.m: The side stripe is bluish with dots.

4665.q: What place does the moose have in the wildlife of Scandinavia?
a: It is seen as a national symbol there
It is kept as a pet
4665.e: In Sweden and Norway the moose is very well known. It is one of the typical animals of the north.
4665.m: The moose is a symbol of Scandinavia.

4666.q: Which close relative is the stone marten often confused with?
4666.e: Stone martens and pine martens look very alike. You can tell them apart mainly by the patch on the throat and the colour of the nose.
4666.m: Stone and pine martens look very alike.

4667.q: What is the trout's dark back and pale belly for?
a: For camouflage against enemies from above and below
So that it glows in the dark
4667.e: From above, the dark colour is hard to see against the dark river bed. From below, the pale belly is hard to see against the bright sky. This camouflages the trout well.
4667.m: The colours camouflage the trout from enemies.

4668.q: Where does the well-known breed of miniature donkey originally come from?
4668.e: The miniature donkey originally comes from the Italian island of Sardinia. Today it also lives in many other countries as a popular pet.

4670.q: What kind of beak does the great spotted woodpecker have?
a: a hooked beak like a bird of prey
4670.e: The firm, pointed beak is shaped like a small chisel. With it the woodpecker can work on hard wood.
4670.m: Its beak is as hard as a chisel.

4671.q: How is the kestrel's hunting technique different from the peregrine falcon's?
a: The kestrel often hovers in the air, the peregrine usually hunts in a fast dive
The kestrel only hunts underwater, the peregrine never does
Both hunt only fish in the same way
The kestrel never hunts in the air, only on the ground
4671.e: While the kestrel looks for mice mainly by hovering above the ground, the peregrine falcon usually hunts other birds in a breathtaking dive. Both species are falcons, but they have different hunting styles.
4671.m: The kestrel hovers, the peregrine dives.

4672.q: How do jackals mark their territory?
4672.e: The scent marks show other jackals that the area is taken. Howling backs up this message.

4674.q: What do you call animals that, like the wild dog, hunt and eat other animals?
4674.e: Predators feed on other animals that they hunt. The wild dog is one of them.

4675.q: What is a direct counter-proposal by Parliament to a popular initiative?
a: An alternative proposal that is voted on together with the initiative
A second initiative by the people
A law without a popular vote
4675.e: Parliament can set its own counter-proposal against a popular initiative. Voters then decide between the initiative, the counter-proposal and the status quo.
4675.m: Parliament can make its own counter-proposal.

4677.q: What do orangutans use their hands for when eating?
a: They peel fruit and crack nuts
They catch fish in the river
They beat their chests like gorillas
4677.e: Their skilful hands help them open hard shells. Thanks to their opposable thumbs, they can grip very precisely.

4678.q: What eyes does an eel have compared with its body?
4678.e: The eyes are small because the eel hunts mainly by smell. In the silver eel stage they get bigger.

4679.q: What bedding does a hamster need in its cage?
4679.e: Hamsters need soft bedding in which they can dig and build a nest. This is like their burrow in the wild.

4680.q: How big can a large starfish get?
4680.e: Some large species of starfish grow over 50 centimetres across. But most starfish are much smaller.

4681.q: What colours does a wasp usually have?
4681.e: The yellow and black stripes warn other animals. That way they know the wasp can sting.
4681.m: Yellow and black means take care.

4682.q: Where does the wood mouse often build its nest?
a: In a burrow under the ground
In the middle of the river
4682.e: The wood mouse digs a burrow with tunnels under the ground. There it is protected from enemies and bad weather.
4682.m: Its nest is under the ground.

4683.q: How many points do the antlers of an adult roe buck usually have?
a: Six points, so three on each side
4683.e: An adult roe buck usually has antlers with six points. It is then also called a six-pointer.

4684.q: How many young does a mother mole usually have at once?
4684.e: A mother mole usually gives birth to three to four young. They are born blind and naked.
4684.m: A mole usually has three to four young.

4685.q: In which season does the wood mouse have especially many young?
a: Only in the depths of winter
Only in autumn when it snows
4685.e: In spring and summer there is plenty of food, which is why the wood mouse has especially many young then.
4685.m: Spring and summer are the time for young.

4686.q: What do you call people who are allowed to hunt red deer?
4686.e: Hunters look after the game in the forest and may hunt under strict rules. This keeps the number of red deer under control.

4687.q: How do African buffalo often behave during the hottest part of the day?
a: They rest in the shade or wallow in mud
4687.e: At midday it is very hot, so the animals rest. They often feed in the morning, evening and at night.
4687.m: At midday buffalo rest in the shade.

4688.q: What kind of teeth does the stone marten have, as a typical carnivore?
a: Only flat grinding teeth like a plant eater
Only soft milk teeth for its whole life
4688.e: Like other carnivores, the stone marten has sharp carnassial teeth that it uses to grab and cut up prey. Its teeth suit its varied, meat-rich diet.
4688.m: The stone marten has sharp carnassial teeth.

4689.q: How many puppies does a female dog usually have at once?
4689.e: Depending on the breed and size of the dog, different numbers of puppies are born, often between four and eight. Large breeds usually have more young than small ones.
4689.m: A female dog often has several puppies.

4690.q: What grows on the lower jaw of some male trout in autumn?
4690.e: In autumn, trout lay their eggs. Then some males get a lower jaw that curves upwards and looks like a hook.
4690.m: Male trout get a hook on their jaw in autumn.

4691.q: In pike, which usually grow bigger, females or males?
a: Both are always exactly the same size
It depends only on the weather
4691.e: Female pike usually grow bigger and heavier than the males. The biggest pike ever caught are almost always females.

4692.q: Which animals are among the natural enemies of ring-tailed lemurs?
a: The fossa and birds of prey
4692.e: On Madagascar, the fossa, a cat-like predator, is one of the animals that hunt ring-tailed lemurs. Birds of prey can also be dangerous.
4692.m: Fossas and birds of prey hunt lemurs.

4693.q: What is a popular sport with dromedaries in Arab countries?
4693.e: Camel races are held in countries such as the United Arab Emirates. Dromedaries are specially bred for them there.
4693.m: Camel racing is popular in Arabia.

4694.q: Why are fish ladders built in Swiss streams for the lake trout?
a: So that it can migrate to its spawning grounds
So that anglers can catch it more easily
So that it is warmer in winter
4694.e: The lake trout migrates from the lake into streams to spawn. Weirs and power stations often block its way, and fish ladders help it get past them.
4694.m: Fish ladders help the lake trout migrate.

4696.q: In common toads, which is usually bigger, the male or the female?
a: both are always the same size
it depends only on the weather
4696.e: Female common toads are bigger and heavier than the males. You can see this especially well in the mating season in spring.

4697.q: Where does the lynx mainly live in Switzerland?
a: In the Jura and the Alps
In towns on the Central Plateau
4697.e: The lynx lives in heavily wooded areas of the Jura and the Alps. There it finds enough cover and prey.
4697.m: The Jura and the Alps are lynx country.

4698.q: Why do millipedes need a damp environment?
a: They only drink rainwater from puddles
They can only breathe in water
4698.e: Their body covering gives little protection against losing water. That is why they avoid dry, sunny places.

4699.q: What is it called when the cows come back down from the alpine pasture to the valley in autumn?
a: Alpabzug, the descent from the alp
Alpaufzug, the ascent to the alp
4699.e: In autumn the cows walk from the alpine pasture back to the valley; this is called the Alpabzug. The cows are often beautifully decorated for it.
4699.m: In autumn the cows come back from the mountains.

4700.q: Roughly how long does the larvae's journey from the Sargasso Sea to Europe take?
a: Several months to over a year
4700.e: The larvae drift towards Europe with the Gulf Stream. The exact length of time is disputed, but it lies between months and about two years.
4700.m: The larvae's journey takes a very long time.

4701.q: Which animal can be dangerous to a jackal?
4701.e: Larger predators such as leopards can catch jackals. Pups are especially at risk.

4702.q: What are gibbons also called, because they are smaller than gorillas and orangutans?
4702.e: Gibbons form a family of their own and are called lesser apes. Gorillas, orangutans and chimpanzees are the great apes.

4703.q: Which gland in the neck controls the body's metabolism with hormones?
4703.e: The thyroid sits in the neck and produces hormones that control how the body uses energy. For this it needs iodine from food.

4704.q: What is the spectacular dance of the great crested grebe for, in which two birds face each other holding plants in their beaks?
a: For finding a partner and strengthening the pair bond
For marking their territory against fish
4704.e: The courtship dance helps the birds find a partner and strengthen their relationship. They often present each other with water plants.
4704.m: Dancing bonds great crested grebe pairs.

4705.q: What colour are the robin's eggs?
4705.e: The robin's eggs are cream-coloured with reddish speckles. This camouflages them well in the nest.
4705.m: The eggs are cream with speckles.

4706.q: Which order of mammals does the African buffalo belong to?
4706.e: It has two main toes that bear hooves. This is typical of even-toed ungulates.

4707.q: How many wings does a dragonfly have?
4707.e: Dragonflies have two pairs of wings, so four wings. They can move them independently of each other.
4707.m: Two pairs of wings, four wings.

4709.q: What makes a veiltail different from an ordinary goldfish?
4709.e: The veiltail was bred to have especially long, soft fins. Because of this it swims more slowly than an ordinary goldfish.

4710.q: What is the pale patch on a roe deer's bottom called?
4710.e: Roe deer have a pale patch on their hindquarters. It is called the rump patch and is easy to see when the deer runs away.
4710.m: The pale patch on the bottom is the rump patch.

4711.q: What is the female cat called?
4711.e: The female is called a queen, although people often just say cat. She gives birth to the kittens.
4711.m: The queen is the female cat.

4712.q: What do wild boar have on their heads that helps them smell well and dig?
4712.e: The wild boar's snout is very flexible and sensitive. With it the boar smells and digs at the same time.
4712.m: The snout is both nose and digging tool.

4713.q: What does the adder mainly eat?
4713.e: It mainly eats mice, lizards and frogs. Young adders tend to catch smaller prey such as lizards or young frogs.

4714.q: Roughly how big is a robin?
a: About as big as a sparrow
4714.e: The robin is a small bird, about as big as a sparrow. It weighs only a few grams.
4714.m: The robin is as small as a sparrow.

4715.q: What does a male alpine newt do during courtship in the water?
a: It performs a courtship dance in front of the female
It builds a nest of stones
4715.e: The male shows the female eye-catching courtship behaviour with tail movements and scents. This is how it woos a partner.

4716.q: How many species of tortoise or turtle are originally native to Switzerland?
4716.e: The European pond turtle is the only species of turtle that occurs here naturally. All other turtles and tortoises in Switzerland come from people keeping them.
4716.m: Only one turtle species is native here.

4718.q: What does the European pond turtle use to break up its food?
a: A rasping tongue like a snail
4718.e: Turtles have no teeth. Their jaws are covered with sharp horny edges that they use to bite off pieces of prey.
4718.m: Turtles have a horny beak instead of teeth.

4721.q: What ability do alpine newts have if they lose a leg or their tail?
a: They can grow the limb back
4721.e: Tailed amphibians such as the alpine newt have an amazing ability to regenerate. Lost legs or parts of the tail can grow back over time.

4722.q: Which animal is shown on the flag of Wales?
4722.e: The red dragon has been the symbol of Wales for centuries. It can be seen on the flag on a green and white background.

4723.q: How can you usually recognise a tree felled by a beaver?
a: By the cone-shaped gnaw marks on the trunk
4723.e: Beavers gnaw trees from all sides until a pointed, cone-shaped stump is left. These typical marks are a sure sign that beavers are around.
4723.m: Gnaw marks give the beaver away.

4724.q: When can young barn owls fly?
4724.e: Young barn owls need about two months before they can fly. After that they practise flying and hunting.

4725.q: Roughly how long can a barn swallow's migration route be?
4725.e: On their migration between Europe and Africa, barn swallows often travel several thousand kilometres, up to about 10,000 kilometres. That is an enormous achievement for such a small bird.

4726.q: What are young barn owls called while they are still in the nest?
4726.e: Young barn owls are called nestlings as long as they stay in the nest. Their parents feed them.

4727.q: Which group of animals does the dromedary belong to?
4727.e: Dromedaries give birth to live young and feed them with milk. This is typical of mammals.

4728.q: Which fish are seahorses closely related to?
4728.e: Pipefish are long, thin fish that belong to the same family as the seahorse. Both have a similar body structure.

4729.q: How does the female alpine newt usually differ in colour from the male?
a: The female is plainer and brownish
The female has stripes like a zebra
4729.e: While the males wear eye-catching, colourful breeding colours in the water, the female usually stays an inconspicuous brownish grey. This protects her better from enemies.
4729.m: Females are less colourful than males.

a: A dense, evergreen forest with lots of rain
A forest in the middle of the desert
4730.e: In tropical rainforests it rains a lot all year round. That is why especially many different plants and animals live there.
4730.m: In the rainforest it rains a lot all year.

4731.q: What sounds do otters make to communicate?
4731.e: Otters communicate with high, whistling sounds. These help them keep in contact with others of their kind or with their young.

4732.q: What do mute swans usually do when they are not eating or swimming?
4732.e: Swans spend a lot of time cleaning their feathers with their beaks. This keeps them clean and waterproof.

4733.q: How well do bison see compared with their senses of smell and hearing?
a: Their sense of smell is very good, their eyesight rather average
4733.e: Bison rely heavily on smell and hearing. That way they notice enemies in time.
4733.m: Bison smell and hear very well.

4734.q: What happened with the fall of Saigon in 1975?
a: The Vietnam War ended with victory for the North Vietnamese communists
Vietnam was divided into four states
The USA won the Vietnam War
4734.e: On 30 April 1975 North Vietnamese troops captured the South Vietnamese capital Saigon. The Vietnam War thus ended with a communist victory and the unification of the country.
4734.m: In 1975 Saigon fell and Vietnam was united.

4735.q: Which nimble animal with very long legs often hunts insects in houses?
4735.e: The house centipede is a centipede with very long, thin legs. It hunts insects and spiders in buildings and is harmless to humans.
4735.m: House centipedes have extremely long legs.

4736.q: How does a blackbird find earthworms in the ground?
a: It tilts its head and looks closely
It smells them from the air
It only listens to other birds
4736.e: The blackbird tilts its head to one side and looks and listens very carefully for movement in the grass. That way it spots worms before it grabs them.
4736.m: The blackbird looks for worms with its head tilted.

4737.q: What is the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) known for?
a: Scientific reports on the state of climate change
4737.e: The IPCC regularly summarises the current state of climate research from thousands of studies. Politicians around the world use these reports as a scientific basis.
4737.m: The IPCC summarises the state of climate research.

4738.q: What do you call a group of African buffalo that live together?
4738.e: African buffalo live in herds that, depending on the area, can be made up of a few animals up to several hundred. This protects them better from predators.

4739.q: The brown trout is cold-blooded. What does that mean?
a: Its body temperature adjusts to the water
Its body temperature is always 37 degrees
4739.e: Cold-blooded animals produce hardly any heat of their own. When the water is cold, their body works more slowly.
4739.m: In the cold-blooded brown trout, body temperature adjusts to the water.

4740.q: What is a baby horse called?
4740.e: A young horse is called a foal. It can stand and walk soon after it is born.
4740.m: A baby horse is called a foal.

4741.q: What is the female lion called?
4741.e: The female is called a lioness. Unlike the males, lionesses have no mane.
4741.m: The female is called a lioness.

4742.q: What is the second largest fish in the world, which is also a shark?
4742.e: The basking shark can grow several metres long. Like the whale shark, it eats only tiny creatures from the water.
4742.m: The basking shark is the second largest fish.

4743.q: How do harbour seals usually eat their fish?
a: They chew them for a long time
They cut them up with their flippers
4743.e: Harbour seals have pointed teeth that they use to hold fish, but they hardly chew. Smaller fish are usually swallowed whole.
4743.m: Harbour seals often swallow fish whole.

4744.q: How is the black kite's tail different from the red kite's?
4744.e: The black kite's tail is only slightly notched, while the red kite's tail is deeply forked. This lets you tell the two species apart in flight.
4744.m: The black kite has a shallower tail fork.

4745.q: How well does an elephant see compared with its sense of smell?
4745.e: Compared with their powerful sense of smell, elephants see rather poorly. That is why they rely much more on their noses and their hearing.

4746.q: How does a stone marten typically hunt its prey?
a: By creeping up quietly and skilfully
By drumming loudly from far away
Only in a group with other martens
By waiting for prey without moving
4746.e: The stone marten creeps up quietly on its prey and surprises it with a quick leap. This hunting technique makes it a successful night-time hunter.
4746.m: Creeping up quietly is its hunting technique.

4747.q: What does the praying mantis catch its prey with?
a: With poisonous spines on its abdomen
4747.e: Its front legs are shaped into grasping legs with spines. They shoot forward in a flash and hold the prey tight.
4747.m: Spiny grasping legs seize the prey.

4748.q: How varied are the coat colours of different goat breeds?
a: Very varied, from white to brown to black and patched
4748.e: Depending on the breed, there are goats in many colours: white, brown, black or with colourful patterns. Each Swiss breed often has its own typical colour.

4749.q: Can the mosquito pupa move in the water?
a: No, it only hangs on plants
4749.e: Unlike many other insect pupae, the mosquito pupa can move in the water and even swim away when there is danger. But it does not stay in this stage for long.
4749.m: Mosquito pupae can swim in water.

4750.q: What happens in a chemical reaction?
4750.e: In a chemical reaction substances combine in new ways and other substances with new properties are formed. For example, burning wood produces ash and smoke.

4751.q: What does the call of a male koala sound most like?
4751.e: The call of a male koala is surprisingly deep and loud and sounds almost like grunting or snoring. At night you can often hear it far across the forest.
4751.m: Koala calls sound deep like a grunt.

4752.q: How does the magpie usually react to new, unfamiliar objects?
a: It eats them at once without checking
It immediately flies away in a panic
4752.e: Magpies are known as curious birds that examine unfamiliar objects carefully before dealing with them. This curiosity is part of their intelligent behaviour.
4752.m: Magpies are curious and careful at the same time.

4753.q: Was the blackbird originally mainly a woodland bird or a town bird?
a: Originally a mountain bird above the tree line
4753.e: The blackbird was originally mainly a shy woodland bird. Only later did it get used to living in towns and gardens too.
4753.m: The blackbird first lived in woodland.

4754.q: Which feature most clearly tells male and female sand lizards apart?
a: Males are green in the mating season
Females are bright red in the mating season
Only males can shed their tails
Females have blue spots on their heads
4754.e: In spring, males turn green along their sides, while females stay more brown. Outside the mating season the difference is less striking.
4754.m: Green colour often gives away the male.

4755.q: In years with little food, what is the longest the edible dormouse's hibernation can last?
4755.e: In years with little food, the edible dormouse's hibernation can last an unusually long time, sometimes up to eleven months. This saves energy when there is hardly any food to be found outside.
4755.m: Hibernation can last up to eleven months.

4756.q: Who teaches young otters to swim and hunt?
4756.e: The mother looks after the young on her own and shows them how to swim and catch fish. Males do not usually help raise the young.
4756.m: The mother teaches the young everything.

4757.q: What is the treeless cold plain called where reindeer live?
4757.e: In the tundra the ground is frozen almost all year round. Only mosses, lichens, grasses and small shrubs grow there.
4757.m: The tundra is a treeless cold region.

4758.q: What does the swift mainly eat?
a: flying insects and spiders in the air
4758.e: Swifts catch their prey in flight with their beaks wide open. These insects and spiders are also called aerial plankton.
4758.m: Swifts hunt insects high in the air.

4759.q: What nickname does the robin have because it likes to look for worms near gardeners?
4759.e: Because it so often turns up near gardeners and waits for worms, it is fondly called “the gardener's friend”. It is very tame when doing so.
4759.m: The robin is called “the gardener's friend”.

4760.q: What is special about gibbons' hands?
a: They have a very flexible wrist that helps with swinging
They have webbing between their fingers
They have hooves instead of fingers
4760.e: A ball-and-socket joint in the wrist lets gibbons turn smoothly while swinging. This protects their joints at high speed.

4761.q: How far can some sea turtles swim on their migrations?
a: Never further than the next beach
4761.e: Some sea turtles travel thousands of kilometres through the oceans on their migrations. That is a truly amazing achievement.

4762.q: What does the tip of the great spotted woodpecker's tongue have?
4762.e: The barbs help it hold on to insects when it pulls them out of the wood. That way they cannot escape.
4762.m: Barbs on the tongue hold on tight.

4763.q: Why do ants often walk one behind the other in long lines?
a: They follow another ant's scent trail
They sing a song while walking
4763.e: Ants leave scents on the ground. Other ants smell this trail and follow it.

4764.q: Does the mole usually live alone or in a large group?
4764.e: Apart from the mating season in spring, the mole usually lives alone in its own tunnel system. It defends its area against other moles.

4765.q: What does a gorilla like to eat most?
4765.e: Gorillas eat almost nothing but plants. All day long they look for leaves, fruit and tender parts of plants.

4766.q: Which family of carnivores does the jaguar belong to?
4766.e: The jaguar belongs to the cat family and, within it, to the big cats. So it is more closely related to the lion and the tiger than to wolves.
4766.m: The jaguar is a big cat.

a: Well, they remember how to get to food
Not at all, they forget everything at once
Only when they are in the barn
4767.e: Goats are considered quite clever animals. They can remember how to get at food and even recognise people they know.
4767.m: Goats are clever animals that can learn.

4768.q: What is a feature of a bison's horns?
a: They are short and curve upwards
They are spiral-shaped and very long
They are straight and point backwards
4768.e: The horns are short, black and curve upwards. Branched shapes are found in antlers.
4768.m: Bison horns are short and curve upwards.

4769.q: What is the duck called that is kept on farms?
4769.e: Domestic ducks live on farms. They come from the wild mallard but were bred by humans.
4769.m: Farm ducks are called domestic ducks.

4770.q: Where does the barn owl hide during the day?
a: In the middle of a meadow
4770.e: During the day the barn owl withdraws to dark hiding places, for example a loft. There it sleeps undisturbed.
4770.m: During the day it rests in the dark.

4771.q: What colour are the great spotted woodpecker's wings mainly?
4771.e: The wings are black with striking white patches. You can see this pattern especially well in flight.

4772.q: Why do aphids often appear in especially large numbers in spring and early summer?
a: Because young shoots have lots of sap and it gets warm
Because they only live in snow
Because they only hatch at night
4772.e: In spring, plants sprout and offer juicy tissue. As temperatures rise, the aphids multiply faster.
4772.m: Warm weather and young shoots help aphids.

4773.q: Which heraldic animal appears on the state coat of arms of Russia?
4773.e: The double-headed eagle goes back to the Byzantine Empire and became Russia's official state coat of arms again in 1993. The two heads look east and west.
4773.m: Russia's coat of arms shows a double-headed eagle.

4774.q: What do you call an area that an animal marks and defends against others of its kind?
4774.e: Snow leopards mark their territory with scent marks and scratches. This tells other animals that the area is taken.
4774.m: A territory is marked and defended.

4775.q: How many antennae does an earwig have on its head?
4775.e: As in most insects, there is one pair of antennae on the head. They are thread-like and can move.
4775.m: One pair of antennae sits on the head.

4776.q: Does a squirrel usually live alone or in large groups?
a: Usually alone, except in the mating season
Always in pairs together for life
Always with a hundred others in the same nest
4776.e: Squirrels mostly live alone. Only in the mating season or when it is cold do they meet up with other squirrels.

4777.q: What is the warm, dry wind called that blows down the mountainsides in the Swiss Alps?
4777.e: The föhn forms when moist air rises up a mountain range, drops its rain and sinks down dry on the other side. As it sinks, the air warms up a lot.
4777.m: The föhn is a warm wind from the mountains.

4778.q: What do whitefish filter out of the water with fine spines on their gills?
4778.e: On the gill arches of whitefish there are fine spines called gill rakers. They hold back plankton when water flows through the gills.
4778.m: Whitefish filter plankton from the water.

4779.q: Apart from eating, what else is plenty of hay in a guinea pig enclosure important for?
a: For hiding and as a soft bed
As a substitute for drinking water
4779.e: Hay is not only food for guinea pigs but also a cosy hiding place and a soft bed. This makes them feel safe and secure.
4779.m: Hay is food and a hiding place at the same time.

4780.q: Roughly how long do baboons live in the wild?
4780.e: Baboons often live 20 to 30 years in the wild. In human care they can live longer.

4781.q: What does a male tree frog do to attract females?
a: It puffs up its vocal sac and calls loudly
4781.e: Male tree frogs have a vocal sac under the chin that they can blow up. With it they make loud calls to attract females.

4782.q: What does a pike feel like when you touch it?
4782.e: Fish have a thin layer of slime on their skin. It protects them from diseases and helps them swim.

4783.q: What does it mean when a dog playing puts its front end flat on the ground and sticks its back end up?
a: It is inviting others to play
4783.e: This posture, also called a play bow, signals to other dogs or people that what follows is just meant as play. It helps avoid misunderstandings.
4783.m: The play bow is an invitation to play.

4784.q: How does a simple electromagnet work?
a: Electricity flows through a coil of wire and creates a magnetic field
A stone is heated until it becomes magnetic
Two mirrors are placed facing each other
Water is poured around a wire
4784.e: When electricity flows through a coiled wire, a magnetic field forms around it. If you switch the electricity off, the magnetic force disappears again.
4784.m: Electricity in a coil makes a magnet.

4786.q: What does a bee show with the round dance?
a: A source of food very close by
A source of food very far away
4786.e: The round dance is simpler than the waggle dance and is used when flowers are found near the hive. The bee turns in circles while dancing.
4786.m: The round dance shows food nearby.

4787.q: How does the lynx behave towards farm animals such as sheep?
a: It can occasionally kill sheep, especially unguarded ones
It only eats grass near sheep
It lives peacefully with flocks of sheep
4787.e: Unguarded sheep can occasionally fall victim to a lynx. Measures to protect flocks help reduce such cases.

4788.q: What kind of coat do rabbits have?
4788.e: Rabbits are covered in soft, thick fur. It keeps them warm and protects their skin.

4789.q: Why do some orca families remember very particular hunting tricks?
a: Because they pass these tricks on over generations
Because they do not like fish
Because they change them at random every day
4789.e: Young orcas learn special hunting techniques from their mothers and grandmothers. That way this knowledge stays in the family.
4789.m: Hunting tricks are passed on in the family.

4790.q: Where does an eagle owl normally make its nest?
a: It does not build a proper nest but uses rock ledges or hollows in the ground
It builds an elaborate nest high up in trees
It builds a nest of mud on riverbanks
It digs its own cave in the ground
4790.e: The eagle owl hardly builds a nest itself but breeds in rock ledges, quarries or abandoned nests of other large birds. Shallow hollows in the ground are also used.
4790.m: The eagle owl uses rock ledges instead of a real nest.

4791.q: Roughly how long is a stoat's tail?
a: Almost as long as its body
4791.e: The stoat's tail is about 6 to 12 centimetres long. At its tip it has the typical black tuft.
4791.m: The tail measures about 6 to 12 cm.

4792.q: What do you call a large group of migrating reindeer?
4792.e: Reindeer live in herds. Some herds are made up of many thousands of animals.

4794.q: How can you often recognise a young budgie that has not yet moulted?
a: The wavy pattern reaches down to the forehead
It has a completely yellow head without waves
It has a long red tail
4794.e: In young budgies, the wavy pattern reaches over the forehead. After the first moult, the forehead becomes smooth and one colour.
4794.m: Young budgies have waves down to the forehead.

4795.q: What does the wave-particle duality of light mean?
a: Light behaves both like a wave and like a particle
Light consists only of solid particles
Light has no physical properties at all
4795.e: Depending on the experiment, light shows the properties of a wave, for example in interference, or of a particle, as in the photoelectric effect. Both descriptions are needed together to understand light fully.
4795.m: Light is both a wave and a particle.

4796.q: What does the pulse you can feel at your wrist show?
a: How many times the heart beats per minute
4796.e: With every heartbeat a wave of blood flows through the arteries. You can feel and count this as your pulse.

4797.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen?
4797.e: The coat of arms of Schaffhausen shows a black ram rearing up on a gold background. The town's name, though, actually comes from “Schiffshausen”, meaning boat houses.

4799.q: What is a striking physical feature of the bison?
4799.e: Above their shoulders, bison have a powerful hump of muscle. It carries the heavy head.

4800.q: What does the body of the alpine salamander show compared with lizards?
a: It has moist, smooth skin instead of dry scales
It has fins instead of legs
4800.e: Although alpine salamanders and lizards look similar at first sight, their skin is very different. Lizards are reptiles with dry scales, while the alpine salamander is an amphibian with moist skin.
4800.m: Moist skin instead of dry scales.

4801.q: How can you often tell who is in charge in a herd of goats?
a: By the colour of the coat
4801.e: Goats often sort out their ranking by gentle or hard head-butting. That way everyone knows who the boss of the herd is.
4801.m: Goats sort out rank by head-butting.

4802.q: Can ducks fly while they are moulting?
a: No, for a short time they cannot fly
4802.e: While moulting, ducks lose many flight feathers at the same time. During this time they cannot fly and prefer to stay hidden.

4803.q: Roughly how big does an adult housefly get?
a: About as big as a small fingernail
4803.e: A housefly is only about six to eight millimetres long. That is roughly the size of a small fingernail.

4804.q: When does the garden spider usually rebuild its web?
a: Often every day, usually in the morning or evening
Only once in its whole life
Only in the depths of winter
4804.e: The web wears out and loses its stickiness. That is why the garden spider often builds a completely new web.

4805.q: Where does the female cockchafer lay its eggs?
