4805.e: The female digs into loose soil and lays her eggs there. She often chooses the edges of woods or meadows.
4805.m: The eggs are laid in the ground.

4806.q: What do roosters sometimes do to sort out their ranking in the group?
a: They test their strength in a fight
4806.e: When several roosters live together, they sometimes sort out their ranking with small fights. The stronger rooster then usually gets first choice of food and hens.
4806.m: Roosters sort out rank by fighting.

4807.q: What does a badger's face typically look like?
4807.e: The badger has a striking face with black stripes over its eyes. This makes it instantly recognisable.

4808.q: What is the hole on an orca's head called that it breathes through?
4808.e: On top of its head the orca has a blowhole. It takes a breath through it every time it comes to the surface.
4808.m: The orca breathes through its blowhole.

a: Sitting on branches, often in forks of branches
Hanging upside down from cave ceilings
4809.e: Gibbons do not build proper nests like orangutans. They sit on thick branches to sleep and rest there.
4809.m: Gibbons sleep sitting in the branches.

4810.q: How long do pairs of mute swans usually stay together?
4810.e: Mute swans usually look for a partner for life. They often stay together for many years.
4810.m: Mute swans usually stay together for life.

4811.q: Roughly what percentage of their genes do humans share with orangutans?
4811.e: The human genome is about 97 percent similar to that of orangutans. This shows how closely related the great apes are.
4811.m: Their genome is very similar to ours.

4812.q: In what posture does the grey heron often stand for hours by the water?
a: Motionless, often standing on one leg
4812.e: So as not to scare off prey, the grey heron often stays completely still for a long time. Sometimes it stands on just one leg.
4812.m: It waits patiently and without moving.

4813.q: How does a harbour seal move on land?
a: It shuffles and wriggles like a caterpillar
4813.e: Harbour seals have flippers, not legs for walking. That is why on land they move rather clumsily by shuffling along.
4813.m: On land the harbour seal shuffles.

4814.q: What is special about the least weasel among carnivores?
a: It is the smallest carnivore in the world
It is the largest carnivore in Europe
It is the fastest land carnivore
It is the heaviest kind of weasel
4814.e: The least weasel often weighs only a few dozen grams. That makes it the smallest carnivore of all in the world.
4814.m: The least weasel: small but brave.

4815.q: What shape are the mole's front paws?
a: Broad like little shovels with strong claws
4815.e: The mole's front paws are turned outwards and very broad. With their strong claws it shovels soil aside with ease.
4815.m: Shovel paws make it a master digger.

4816.q: Why does the stork clatter its beak so often?
a: because it has no voice for singing
4816.e: Storks have no real song. That is why they clatter their beaks to communicate.
4816.m: Clattering is the language of storks.

4817.q: What does a lizard's regrown tail usually look like?
a: Shorter and a different colour than before
4817.e: The regrown tail is often shorter and a different colour. Instead of vertebrae it only contains a rod of cartilage.
4817.m: The new tail is only a replacement.

4818.q: Apart from prey it has killed itself, what else does the wolverine like to eat?
a: Carrion, meaning animals that are already dead
4818.e: The wolverine is not fussy and also eats carrion, the bodies of animals that are already dead. This helps it find enough food even in barren, cold regions.

4819.q: What does the wall lizard do to warm itself up?
a: It digs deep into the ground
It moves fast in the shade
4819.e: Stones store the sun's warmth especially well. That is why the wall lizard often lies motionless in the sun on a wall.
4819.m: Sunbathing warms up the wall lizard.

4820.q: What are the broad, toothed front legs of a dung beetle for?
4820.e: The powerful digging legs push soil aside. This is how the beetles make tunnels under the dung.

4821.q: How do adult wild dogs often bring food to the pups?
a: They bring up meat for them
They put fruit in the nest
4821.e: The adults bring up half-digested meat. This way the pups and the guards at the den are fed too.
4821.m: The pack shares food with the young.

a: A breed of pig specially bred to be small
A piglet that never grows up
A toy shaped like a pig
4822.e: Mini pigs were deliberately bred to stay much smaller than normal domestic pigs. Some people even keep them as pets.
4822.m: Mini pigs stay small through breeding.

4823.q: How do blue whales communicate over long distances?
4823.e: Blue whales send out deep sounds that travel far through the water. This lets them stay in contact over great distances.
4823.m: Deep sounds travel far in the sea.

4824.q: How fast does a blue whale normally swim?
a: Always very fast like a racing car
It does not swim at all
4824.e: The blue whale usually swims leisurely through the water. But when in danger it can briefly go faster.

4825.q: In the photo you can see a spawning pit. How is it made?
a: The female beats a hollow in the gravel with her tail
Beavers dig it for the fish
The male builds it from twigs
It forms when rain churns up the stream
4825.e: The female beats a pit into the gravel bed with her tail. There she lays her eggs and then covers them up again.
4825.m: The female beats pits into the gravel.

4826.q: What does the perch have on its gill cover?
4826.e: The gill cover ends in a sharp spine. That is why you should be careful when handling a perch.
4826.m: Gill cover with a spine, so take care.

4827.q: How does a stoat usually behave towards people?
a: It actively looks for people's company
4827.e: Stoats are shy animals by nature and avoid contact with people. That is why you rarely see them in the wild.

4828.q: What does the shape of the starfish show?
a: It is shaped like a star
It is round like a ball
It is long like a snake
It is square like a dice
4828.e: The starfish's body is shaped like a star, usually with five arms. That is how it got its name.
4828.m: Its body looks like a star.

4829.q: How many toes do tapirs have on their back feet?
4829.e: The back feet have three toes with small hooves. The weight rests mainly on the middle toe.
4829.m: Tapirs have three toes at the back.

4830.q: What does a carp use to swim through the water?
4830.e: Fins help the carp move and change direction. The tail fin gives it the most push.

4831.q: What is the aim of the agreement on the free movement of persons between Switzerland and the EU?
a: People can more easily work and live in Switzerland and the EU
4831.e: This agreement allows citizens of Switzerland and the EU to work, study or live more easily in each other’s countries. It is part of the bilateral agreements.
4831.m: Free movement makes it easier to work and live abroad.

4832.q: In a wild dog pack, who often gets to eat first?
4832.e: In wild dogs, the pups are often allowed to eat first. This is a special kind of social behaviour.
4832.m: In wild dogs, the young often eat first.

4833.q: Why is the great spotted woodpecker important for the forest?
a: it creates holes for other animals
it drives away all other birds
4833.e: The holes it pecks are later used by many other animals. That is why it is called an important species in the forest.

4834.q: Roughly how long does a ladybird live?
4834.e: A ladybird usually lives for only about a year. For a small insect that is quite a long time.

4835.e: Mallards like to sleep right on the water. There they are safe from many enemies that might lie in wait on land.
4835.m: Ducks often sleep on the water.

4837.q: Where in Switzerland do you often see mute swans?
4837.e: Mute swans like to live on lakes and rivers. In Switzerland you find them, for example, on Lake Zurich.
4837.m: Swans like living on large lakes.

4838.q: Which kind of domestic animals do pumas sometimes attack?
4838.e: When wild prey is scarce, pumas occasionally take farm animals. This often leads to conflicts with farmers.

4839.q: Does the mole have visible outer ears?
a: No, it has no outer ear flaps
Yes, huge ears like a hare
4839.e: The mole has no visible ear flaps, only small openings under its fur. That way no soil gets stuck in its ears.

4840.q: What does a hamster line its nest in the cage with?
a: With sand from the sand bath
4840.e: Hamsters like to line their nests with scraps of paper or hay. This makes it soft and cosy for sleeping.

4841.q: What distinguishes a totalitarian dictatorship from an authoritarian one?
a: Totalitarian regimes want to control almost all areas of life, authoritarian ones mainly politics
Totalitarian regimes allow free elections, authoritarian ones do not
Authoritarian regimes always have a state ideology, totalitarian ones do not
Totalitarian regimes are led by kings, authoritarian ones by generals
4841.e: In totalitarian systems such as Nazi Germany or the Soviet Union, the regime tries to control thought, culture and private life. Authoritarian systems usually limit themselves to political control but leave more private freedom.
4841.m: Totalitarian controls everything, authoritarian only politics.

4842.q: How can you often tell a female kingfisher from a male?
a: By the orange lower half of the beak
By the length of its tail
4842.e: Females usually have an orange lower part of the beak, while the male's beak is completely black. This makes it easy to tell the sexes apart.
4842.m: An orange-red lower beak shows the female.

4843.q: Roughly how big is the territory of a single stone marten?
a: It can cover several square kilometres
It is always only a few square metres
Stone martens have no fixed territory at all
It is as big as the whole of Europe
4843.e: Depending on how much food there is, a stone marten's territory can be several square kilometres in size. In towns and villages with plenty of food, territories are often smaller.
4843.m: Territories can be several square kilometres in size.

a: A rule that everyone must follow
4844.e: Laws are rules that apply to everyone in a country. They are decided by parliament or by the people.

4845.q: Which fish belongs, like the carp, to the carp family?
4845.e: The goldfish is a close relative of the carp. Both belong to the carp family.
4845.m: The carp belongs to the carp family.

4846.q: Which parts of plants do aphids especially like to settle on?
a: Young shoots and the undersides of leaves
Only the roots of all species
4846.e: Young shoots have soft tissue and lots of sap. On the undersides of leaves the aphids are also better protected.
4846.m: Aphids often sit on young shoots.

4848.q: What does a chicken use to pick up its food?
4848.e: Chickens peck up their food with their hard beaks. This lets them eat grain, worms and small stones.

4849.q: How does the barn owl hunt its prey?
a: It glides silently over fields and listens
It digs holes in the ground
4849.e: The barn owl flies low and silently over meadows and fields. It hears the mice in the grass before it strikes.

4850.q: What colour is an octopus's blood?
4850.e: Octopus blood is blue because it contains a special substance with copper. In us humans, blood is red because of iron.

4851.q: Which are longer on a chimpanzee: the arms or the legs?
a: The arms are longer than the legs
The legs are longer than the arms
Arms and legs are the same length
4851.e: Chimpanzees have very long arms that are longer than their legs. This helps them climb from branch to branch.
4851.m: Chimpanzee arms are longer than their legs.

4852.q: What is the outer skeleton of woodlice and other arthropods called?
4852.e: An exoskeleton lies on the outside of the body. It protects and supports the animals, but has to be shed for them to grow.
4852.m: The exoskeleton lies on the outside of the body.

4853.q: Does the small remora harm the shark it swims along with?
a: No, the shark is not harmed by it
Yes, it eats the shark up
Yes, it makes the shark ill
4853.e: The remora only takes leftover scraps of the shark's food. This is no problem for the shark itself.
4853.m: The remora does not harm the shark.

4854.q: How many eyes does an earthworm have?
4854.e: Earthworms have no eyes, because they live underground. But they can still sense light with their skin.
4854.m: Earthworms sense light with their skin.

4855.q: How does a mallard move on land?
a: It waddles from side to side
4855.e: On land, mallards walk with short steps and wobble from side to side. This is called waddling.

4856.q: What can a hamster do when it is very frightened and cannot get away?
a: It rolls into a spiky ball
4856.e: A very frightened hamster can defend itself and bite. That is why you should always handle it calmly and carefully.

4857.q: How do dung beetles travel over longer distances?
a: They fly with their membranous wings
They get ants to carry them
4857.e: Under the hard wing cases lie the large membranous wings. With them dung beetles can fly, buzzing loudly.
4857.m: Dung beetles fly with membranous wings.

4858.q: What are the holes on top of the blue whale's head called, through which it takes in air?
4858.e: The blowholes are on top of the head. The blue whale breathes in and out through them when it is at the surface.

4859.q: Where does a hen usually lay her eggs?
4859.e: Hens look for a sheltered place, the nest, to lay their eggs in. It is often lined with straw.

4860.q: What does the young cuckoo do once it is alone in the nest?
a: It lets its foster parents feed it
It builds a new nest itself
It looks for its real parents
4860.e: After the young cuckoo has thrown all the other eggs and chicks out of the nest, it lets its foster parents feed it alone. That way it gets all the food for itself.
4860.m: The young cuckoo gets fed all on its own.

4861.q: What, among other things, does the dor beetle eat?
a: Droppings of wild animals and fungi
4861.e: The dor beetle eats the droppings of roe deer and other wild animals, but also fungi. This helps break down waste in the forest.
4861.m: The dor beetle clears away droppings in the forest.

4862.q: How long can a well cared for goldfish live?
4862.e: With good care, goldfish can live ten years or even much longer. Some live to over twenty.
4862.m: Goldfish can live a very long time.

4863.q: How does a polar bear move through the water?
a: It swims with its big paws
It only drifts on ice floes
It beats its tail like a fish
4863.e: With its big paws, the polar bear can swim as if with paddles. That way it moves along well in the water too.
4863.m: Polar bears swim with their big paws.

4864.q: Which animal is considered the national animal of the Democratic Republic of the Congo?
4864.e: The okapi is considered the national animal of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It appears on stamps and coins.
4864.m: The okapi is Congo's national animal.

4865.q: Which animals are among the natural enemies of the tree frog?
4865.e: Birds such as herons or storks and snakes such as the grass snake hunt tree frogs. Fish also like to eat the tadpoles.
4865.m: Herons and snakes hunt tree frogs.

4866.q: What is especially special about a squirrel's back legs?
a: They are strong and help with long jumps
It has no back legs at all
They are longer than its whole body
4866.e: The strong back legs let the squirrel make long, safe leaps between trees.
4866.m: Strong back legs allow long jumps.

4867.q: How many antennae does a wasp have?
4867.e: The wasp has two antennae on its head. It uses them to smell and feel.

4868.q: What is known about the wood sandpiper in Switzerland?
a: It mainly appears while passing through on migration
It breeds all over the Alps
It spends the winter on glaciers
4868.e: Many wading birds rest by Swiss lakes and rivers on their journey. The wood sandpiper breeds further north.
4868.m: In Switzerland it is mostly a passing migrant.

4869.q: What is the tiger in the Chinese calendar?
a: An animal sign for a whole year
A symbol for a single day
4869.e: In the Chinese calendar the tiger stands for a whole year, called the Year of the Tiger. There are twelve such animal signs.
4869.m: There is a Year of the Tiger.

4870.q: How many species of hyena are there today?
4870.e: The family includes the spotted, striped and brown hyena as well as the aardwolf. Together that makes four species.
4870.m: There are four living species of hyena.

4871.q: Which kind of starfish sometimes destroys coral reefs?
4871.e: The crown-of-thorns starfish eats coral and, in large numbers, can damage whole reefs. It lives mainly in warm seas.

4872.q: What have researchers observed some octopuses doing in aquariums?
4872.e: Some octopuses collect empty shells or pieces of coconut and use them for protection or as a hiding place. This shows how clever octopuses can be.

4873.q: When do baby sea turtles usually crawl out of the sand?
a: Right at sunrise in the morning
4873.e: The little turtles often hatch from their eggs at night. In the dark the danger from enemies is a little smaller.
4873.m: Hatchlings usually set off at night.

4874.q: What is a cow's baby called?
4874.e: A cow's baby is called a calf. A calf can stand and walk shortly after it is born.

4875.q: How does an ibex digest its tough food?
a: It is a ruminant with several stomach chambers
It has no stomach at all
It digests nothing itself, bacteria do everything outside
It swallows stones that grind up the food
4875.e: Like other members of the goat family, the ibex is a ruminant. Its stomach has several chambers in which the food is broken down and digested several times.

4876.q: Where in Switzerland are you most likely to find pond skaters?
4876.e: Many species live on still or slow-flowing water. There they find calm water and prey.

4877.q: What does the earwig use the antennae on its head for?
4877.e: With its antennae it explores its surroundings in the dark. They sense touch and smells.
4877.m: Antennae are for feeling and smelling.

4879.q: What is a woodlouse's body armour made of?
4879.e: The armour is an exoskeleton made of chitin. In crustaceans it is often hardened with lime.
4879.m: The woodlouse's exoskeleton is made of chitin.

4880.q: How do bonobo calls sound compared with chimpanzee calls?
4880.e: Bonobos often have higher voices than chimpanzees. They call, squeak and screech to communicate.

4881.q: What shape is a tapir's body?
4881.e: The tapir has a compact body with a rounded back. This helps it get through dense undergrowth.

4882.q: Roughly how big is a mute swan's wingspan?
4882.e: A mute swan's wings together can be over two metres wide. This helps it fly powerfully.

4883.q: What role does the oldest female orca often play in a group?
a: She leads the group and knows good hunting spots
4883.e: The oldest female has a lot of experience and shows the family where to find food. She is also called the leader of the group.
4883.m: The oldest female orca leads the family.

4884.q: Which danger threatens brown bears most in many parts of the world?
a: Loss and breaking up of their habitat by humans
Natural predators such as large birds
Winters that are too cold everywhere
4884.e: Roads, towns and farming shrink the brown bear's habitat and cut it into pieces. As a result, many bear populations find fewer and fewer connected areas.
4884.m: Habitat loss threatens many brown bears.

4886.q: What is it called when a dog brings back a ball or stick?
4886.e: When retrieving, the dog brings a thrown object back to its owner. Many dogs love this game and learn it quickly.
4886.m: Bringing things back is called retrieving.

4887.q: What is the biggest threat to orangutans?
a: Too little water in the sea
4887.e: Rainforests are cleared for palm oil plantations, timber and settlements. As a result the animals lose their food and their habitat.
4887.m: Deforestation takes away the orangutans' habitat.

4888.q: What does the newly hatched cuckoo chick do in the nest?
a: It throws the other eggs and chicks out of the nest
It immediately builds its own nest
4888.e: The little cuckoo chick pushes the host bird's eggs or chicks out of the nest with its back. That way it is the only chick and gets all the food.
4888.m: The young cuckoo throws out the other chicks.

4889.q: What are a deer's antlers made of?
4889.e: Antlers are made of real bone. While they are growing, they are covered with a soft skin.

4890.q: Roughly how heavy is a striped hyena?
4890.e: Striped hyenas weigh about as much as a large dog. Spotted hyenas get much heavier.
4890.m: Striped hyenas weigh about as much as a large dog.

4891.q: What do swifts do when bad weather with few insects suddenly sets in over a region?
a: they fly long distances away to find better weather
they stay sitting where they are, hungry
they dig themselves into the ground
4891.e: This behaviour is called weather escape. Swifts can cover hundreds of kilometres in a short time to follow areas with more flying insects.
4891.m: In bad weather swifts move far away.

4892.q: What does an elephant do with the water it has sucked into its trunk?
a: It squirts it into its mouth or over its body
It stores it in its trunk for weeks
It uses it to breathe underwater like a fish
4892.e: Elephants do not drink directly through their trunks. They bring the water to their mouths or give themselves a shower with it.
4892.m: Elephants shower themselves with their trunks.

4893.q: Where does an earthworm like to live best?
4893.e: Earthworms dig tunnels in damp soil. There they find food and shelter.

4894.q: What is the large breed of duck from South America called that does not quack but rather hisses?
4894.e: The Muscovy duck originally comes from South America. Unlike other ducks, it tends to make hissing sounds instead of quacking.
4894.m: Muscovy ducks hiss instead of quacking.

4895.q: How many different Swiss mountain dog breeds are there?
4895.e: There are four Swiss mountain dog breeds: the Bernese, the Appenzeller, the Entlebucher and the Greater Swiss Mountain Dog. In the past they were often used as farm dogs.
4895.m: Switzerland has four mountain dog breeds.

4896.q: What happens to the prey after the garden spider has wrapped it up?
a: It injects digestive juice and sucks it out
It just leaves the prey lying there
It gives it away to other spiders
4896.e: The spider bites its prey and injects digestive juice into it. Then it sucks out the dissolved insides, as if through a straw.

4897.q: Roughly how old can fire salamanders live to be in the wild?
4897.e: Fire salamanders can live to an amazing age; some reach over 20 years in the wild. In human care some live even longer.
4897.m: Fire salamanders can live a very long time.

4898.q: What do young wild boar do when they sense danger?
a: They stay with their mother and run away with her
4898.e: Piglets stay close to their mother. When there is danger, they follow her to safety at once.

4899.q: Where does a roe deer fawn hide in its first days of life?
a: Lying very still in tall grass
In a cave under the ground
4899.e: At first a roe deer fawn lies still in the tall grass and hardly moves. That way enemies do not notice it.
4899.m: Fawns lie still and hidden in the grass.

4900.q: Roughly how many muscles does an elephant's trunk have?
4900.e: The trunk is extremely flexible because it is made of countless small muscles. With it the elephant can make very fine movements.
4900.m: The trunk has many thousands of muscles.

4901.q: Which group of animals does the slow worm belong to?
4901.e: The slow worm looks like a snake but is a legless lizard. It belongs to the family of slow worms and glass lizards.

4902.q: On how many legs does a kangaroo hop?
4902.e: The kangaroo hops only on its two strong back legs. It does not need its short front legs for this.

4903.q: What do Christians celebrate at Easter?
a: The end of fasting in Islam
4903.e: At Easter Christians believe that Jesus came back to life after his death. It is one of the most important Christian festivals.
4903.m: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus.

4904.q: What is the most striking feature that lets you recognise a red kite in flight straight away?
a: its tail spread out like a fan
4904.e: The red kite has a clearly notched, forked tail. This makes it easy to tell apart from other birds of prey.
4904.m: A forked tail shows it is a red kite.

4905.q: What is the conservation status of the tree frog in Switzerland?
a: It is considered endangered and is on the Red List
It is not endangered at all
It is only found in zoos
4905.e: In Switzerland the number of tree frogs has fallen sharply. That is why it is considered an endangered species and is specially protected.
4905.m: The tree frog is endangered and protected.

4906.q: Roughly how long are tapirs pregnant?
4906.e: Tapirs carry their young for around 13 months. This is typical for animals of this size.
4906.m: Tapirs are pregnant for over a year.

4908.q: Which animals are among the sparrow's enemies?
4908.e: Cats and small birds of prey such as the sparrowhawk like to hunt sparrows. That is why sparrows are always careful and fly away quickly when there is danger.

4909.q: What does a blackbird often eat in winter?
4909.e: In winter there are fewer worms, so the blackbird then mainly eats berries and fruit. That way it still finds enough energy.
4909.m: In winter the blackbird eats berries.

4910.q: What is the house sparrow usually called in everyday language?
4910.e: The house sparrow is usually just called a sparrow. It likes living near people, in villages and towns.
4910.m: The house sparrow is the sparrow.

4911.q: What do you call people who help govern the municipality, the canton or the country?
4911.e: Politicians work in governments and parliaments. They make important decisions for everyone.
4911.m: Politicians make decisions for the community.

4912.q: What is special about the barn owl's ears?
a: They are not quite at the same height
4912.e: The barn owl's ear openings are slightly offset from each other. This lets it hear very precisely which direction a sound comes from.
4912.m: Offset ears help it tell where sounds come from.

4913.q: What is the pill woodlouse often confused with, because it also rolls up?
a: The pill millipede, a kind of millipede
4913.e: Pill millipedes, which belong to the millipedes, also roll up into a ball. They look like pill woodlice but are not closely related. Pill woodlice are crustaceans.
4913.m: Other animals can roll up too.

4914.q: What is special about the dromedary's red blood cells?
a: They are oval and can cope with swelling a lot
4914.e: The oval shape helps when the animal drinks a lot of water at once. The cells can swell up a great deal without bursting.
4914.m: Oval blood cells cope with lots of water.

4915.q: Who studied chimpanzees in Africa for many years and is famous for it?
4915.e: Jane Goodall lived with chimpanzees in Tanzania for a long time and discovered a lot about their behaviour. This made her world famous.

4916.q: On which continent do most cheetahs live?
4916.e: Cheetahs live mainly in the savannahs of Africa. There is plenty of room to run there.

4917.q: Roughly how long do adult praying mantises live?
4917.e: They hatch from their eggs in spring or early summer. In autumn, when it gets cold, the adults die.

4918.q: Roughly how old can a pet budgie live to be?
4918.e: Well cared for budgies can live for many years, often between 8 and 15. That is amazingly long for such a small bird.

4919.q: How big is a stoat compared with a pet cat?
4919.e: A stoat is much smaller than a pet cat and also weighs much less. Even so, it is a brave and skilful hunter.
4919.m: The stoat is much smaller than cats.

4920.q: In which habitats can you find the cuckoo in Switzerland?
a: In woods, hedges and reed beds
4920.e: The cuckoo lives in a variety of habitats such as woods, hedges, bogs and reed beds. There it finds enough host birds and insects to eat.
4920.m: The cuckoo lives in woods and reeds.

4921.q: What happens when the sand in a sea turtle's nest is especially warm?
4921.e: When the sand is warm, the eggs mostly develop into females. When it is cooler, they tend to become males.
4921.m: Warm sand usually means more females.

4922.q: Where does the European pond turtle often bask in the sun?
a: On tree trunks or stones by the water
In the middle of a road
4922.e: It likes climbing onto branches that stick out of the water. When there is danger, it slides quickly back into the water.
4922.m: Its sunbathing spots are trunks and stones by the water.

4923.q: Because of an old false belief, what is the bearded vulture sometimes called?
4923.e: People used to believe, wrongly, that the bearded vulture carried off live lambs. That is why it was called lammergeier, German for “lamb vulture”, even though this is not true.
4923.m: A wrong name because of a wrong belief.

a: Small animals such as insects and spiders
4924.e: Centipedes are predators and hunt small animals on the ground. They kill their prey with their venomous claws.

4925.q: Which habitat is typical of the African buffalo?
a: High mountains above the tree line
4925.e: It likes grasslands with water and some cover. It can also use forests and swamps.

4926.q: What can a slow worm shed when in danger?
4926.e: Like many lizards, it can shed its tail to distract enemies. The tail only grows back partly.
4926.m: The tail can drop off when in danger.

4927.q: Where does a Roman snail retreat to most quickly when in danger?
a: Into a hole in a branch
4927.e: When in danger, the snail pulls back into its shell in a flash. There its soft body is well protected.
4927.m: When in danger, the snail pulls back into its shell.

4928.q: What does a starfish do when it is lying on its back?
a: It turns itself back over with its tiny feet
It stays lying like that for ever
It waits until a fish turns it over
4928.e: With its many tiny feet, the starfish can turn itself back over. But it takes a while.

4929.q: What is under the ladybird's hard, colourful wing cases?
4929.e: The hard wing cases are like a protective shield. Underneath lie folded, delicate wings that the beetle uses to fly.
4929.m: Real wings lie under the wing cases.

4931.q: Roughly how long does the stag beetle larva take to develop?
4931.e: The larva usually lives in wood for five to eight years. That is much longer than the life of the adult beetle.
4931.m: The larva lives for years, the beetle only briefly.

4932.q: Does the robin tend to live alone or in large groups?
a: Usually alone, outside the breeding season
Only in herds of a hundred animals
4932.e: Except in the breeding season, the robin mostly lives alone. Each bird defends its own small territory.

4933.q: The “Gangfisch” lives in Lake Constance. Which group of fish does it belong to?
4933.e: The Gangfisch is a small species of whitefish from Lake Constance. Whitefish are important food fish in many Swiss lakes.
4933.m: The Gangfisch is a small whitefish from Lake Constance.

4934.q: What colour are an adult mute swan's feathers?
4934.e: Adult mute swans have beautiful snow-white feathers. This makes them easy to see on the water.

4935.q: What kind of claws does a hamster have on its paws?
4935.e: With its small, sharp claws the hamster can dig well. That is how it makes its burrows in the wild.

4936.e: Some budgies learn to repeat short words or sentences. They simply copy sounds they hear often.

4937.q: How does the edible dormouse like to get around best?
a: climbing skilfully from branch to branch
4937.e: The edible dormouse is an excellent climber and moves mostly in the treetops. It jumps skilfully from branch to branch.
4937.m: The dormouse climbs skilfully in trees.

4939.q: What is typical of a mute swan's beak?
4939.e: The beak is orange and has a black knob at its base. That is where the bird gets its German name, “Höckerschwan”, meaning knob swan.
4939.m: Orange-red beak with a black knob.

4940.q: How does the eel move along?
a: By wriggling with its whole body
4940.e: The eel moves by making wave-like movements with its long body. This lets it move well between stones and plants too.

4941.q: What does the panda have around its eyes?
4941.e: Around each eye the panda has a large black patch. This makes its eyes look much bigger.

4942.q: In the photo, the brown trout can hardly be seen on the gravel bed. What is its colouring for?
4942.e: The colours and spots match the bottom of the stream. So the trout is hard to see and can take prey by surprise.

4943.q: Roughly how long does a female cheetah carry her cubs in her belly before they are born?
4943.e: The gestation period of cheetahs lasts about three months. Then the small, helpless cubs are born.
4943.m: Cheetah cubs grow in the belly for about three months.

4944.q: How many toes does a horse have on each foot?
4944.e: Today's horses have only one single toe, which is enclosed by the hoof. Their ancestors millions of years ago still had several toes.
4944.m: Horses have only one toe per foot.

4945.q: How do migrating birds find their way on their long journeys?
a: Among other things, by the Earth's magnetic field
Only by the smell of the water
4945.e: Migrating birds use several aids: the sun, the stars, landscapes and the Earth's magnetic field. That way they find their way over thousands of kilometres.
4945.m: Migrating birds sense the Earth's magnetic field.

4946.q: How does a bumblebee look different from a honeybee?
a: The bumblebee is rounder, fatter and furrier
4946.e: Bumblebees look rounder and have many more hairs than honeybees. This makes them look fluffier and fatter.

4947.q: What does a hamster need its long whiskers for?
a: To find its way in the dark
4947.e: With its whiskers the hamster feels obstacles, even when it is dark. This helps it find its way around.

4948.q: What makes a cheetah's face especially easy to recognise?
4948.e: The black stripes running from the eyes to the mouth are typical of cheetahs. No other big cat has these markings.
4948.m: Tear stripes are typical of cheetahs.

4949.q: What is a nest box for great tits?
a: A small wooden house for breeding
4949.e: A nest box is a small wooden house with a round hole. Great tits like to build their nests in it if there is no natural hole in a tree.
4949.m: Nest boxes replace missing tree holes.

4950.q: What are a goose's soft feathers (down) often used for today?
a: For filling warm jackets and duvets
4950.e: The fine down feathers keep you very warm. That is why they are often sewn into winter jackets and duvets.

4951.q: Where does the lake trout go to spawn?
a: To the deepest part of the lake
4951.e: The lake trout lives in the lake and moves into streams and rivers to spawn. Fish that change habitat like this are called migratory fish.

4952.q: What is the legal status of the red kite in Switzerland?
a: it is not covered by law
4952.e: The red kite is protected in Switzerland. You may neither hunt it nor disturb its nest.

4953.q: What causes the black coat of some jaguars?
4953.e: In melanism, the body produces a particularly large amount of dark pigment. This is an inherited trait and not an illness.

4954.q: What kind of body surface does the alpine salamander absolutely need in order to breathe well?
4954.e: Amphibians such as the alpine salamander breathe partly through their skin. That is why it must always stay moist, otherwise breathing does not work properly.

a: The queen and the males before the nuptial flight
All ants for their whole lives
4955.e: Only the young queens and the males get wings. With them they fly off on the nuptial flight.

4956.q: What is a young llama called?
4956.e: Young llamas are called crias. The word comes from Spanish.
4956.m: A young llama is called a cria.

4957.q: What is a hen called that sits on her eggs to hatch them?
4957.e: A hen that is sitting on eggs is called a broody hen. She sits patiently on the eggs and keeps them warm.
4957.m: A hen sitting on eggs is a broody hen.

4958.q: What does a hedgehog often do first, before it rolls up?
a: It jumps high into the air
4958.e: First the hedgehog stops and listens to what is happening around it. Only when the danger comes closer does it roll up.
4958.m: First the hedgehog listens, then it rolls up.

4959.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult okapi get?
4959.e: Fully grown okapis usually weigh 200 to 300 kilograms. That is about the weight of a large horse or less.

4960.q: How does a horse show that it is happy or is greeting someone?
4960.e: Horses neigh to “talk” to other horses or people. This is how they show joy, for example, or call other horses.

4961.q: What happens when a strange silverback comes into the area of another group?
a: There may be a fight between the silverbacks
The two groups always join together at once
The strange gorillas are greeted in a friendly way
Nothing, they do not even notice each other
4961.e: Silverbacks defend their family and their area. If a strange silverback meets another group, there may be loud threats or even fights.

4962.q: How do toads usually differ from frogs in their skin?
4962.e: Frogs usually have smooth, moist skin, while toads have drier, warty skin. Both are amphibians.

4963.q: What is an adult male gorilla with silver fur on its back called?
4963.e: As a male gorilla gets older, the fur on its back turns silver-grey. That is why it is called a silverback.

4964.q: What is the lake trout's lateral line organ for?
a: To sense currents and movements in the water
4964.e: The lateral line runs along both sides of the body. It senses changes in pressure and movements in the water, for example from prey.
4964.m: The lateral line senses water movements.

4965.q: What is noticeable about the African buffalo's ears?
a: They often hang to the side and are big
They are tiny and cannot be seen
They are pointed and upright like a cat's
4965.e: The big ears often hang down. They are fringed with hair.

4966.q: What colour is the fur of most species of marten and weasel?
a: Black and white striped like a zebra
4966.e: Most species of the weasel family have brown fur, often with lighter patches on the throat or belly. This colour helps them blend in well in forests and on the ground.

4967.q: Why does your face go red when you run fast?
a: More blood flows to the skin to give off heat
4967.e: When you run, you get warm. To get rid of the heat, more blood flows to the surface of the skin.
4967.m: Blood helps to cool you down.

4968.q: Roughly how old can a cheetah live to be in the wild?
4968.e: Wild cheetahs usually live to between ten and twelve. In zoos they can sometimes live a little longer.
4968.m: Cheetahs usually live about ten years.

4969.q: What role do orangutans play for the rainforest?
4969.e: When eating and through their droppings, they spread seeds around the forest. This helps new trees to grow.

4970.q: How many toes do llamas have on each foot?
4970.e: Llamas walk on padded feet and have two toes on each foot. Underneath are soft soles that are gentle on the ground.
4970.m: Llamas have two toes on each foot.

4971.q: Why is it important for a trout to be camouflaged?
a: So that enemies find it harder to spot
So that it does not get cold in winter
So that it can swim faster
So that other fish play with it
4971.e: Predators such as birds or larger fish look for prey in the water. With its camouflage colours, the trout is harder to spot.
4971.m: Camouflage protects the trout from enemies.

4972.q: What do we get from sheep's wool?
4972.e: Sheep's wool is made into warm jumpers, socks and blankets. Wool keeps you warm even when it is wet.
4972.m: Sheep's wool keeps us warm in winter.

4973.q: Why is the bumblebee so important for flowers?
a: It pollinates the flowers while looking for nectar
4973.e: When the bumblebee flies from flower to flower, pollen sticks to its fur and is carried on. This is how many flowers later turn into fruit and seeds.
4973.m: Bumblebees pollinate flowers while looking for nectar.

4975.q: Roughly how big was the wingspan of the prehistoric giant dragonfly Meganeura?
4975.e: Meganeura lived in the Carboniferous period and was one of the largest flying insects known. Its wingspan was around 65 centimetres.
4975.m: Meganeura had a wingspan of about 65 cm.

4976.q: Roughly how wide can an eagle owl's wingspan get?
4976.e: An eagle owl's wingspan can be up to 170 centimetres. That makes it the largest owl in Europe.
4976.m: Eagle owl wings span up to 170 cm.

4977.q: Which part of the world does the carp originally come from?
4977.e: The carp originally comes from Asia. From there it reached Europe a long time ago.
4977.m: The carp originally comes from Asia.

4978.q: What does the stoat like to eat most?
4978.e: Voles and other small rodents are at the very top of the stoat's menu. It is a skilful hunter.

4979.q: What colour is an alpine marmot's fur usually?
a: Black and white striped like a zebra
4979.e: Marmots' thick fur is usually brown to greyish brown. This colour camouflages them well among rocks and earth.
4979.m: Brownish grey fur camouflages them in the mountains.

4980.q: Which kind of jellyfish is common in European seas and usually harmless to people?
4980.e: The moon jellyfish is very common in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. People can usually only feel its sting very weakly.
4980.m: The moon jellyfish is common and usually harmless.

4981.q: Which animals are among the enemies of pond skaters?
4981.e: Fish can catch pond skaters from below. Birds and other predators eat them too.
4981.m: Fish and birds hunt pond skaters.

4982.q: What do ducks often do when danger threatens and they cannot fly away?
a: They swim away quickly or hide in the reeds
They dig themselves into the ground in a flash
They just stand still and sleep
4982.e: When in danger, ducks usually flee quickly into the water or hide in the thick reeds by the bank. There many enemies find it harder to reach them.
4982.m: Ducks flee into the water or the reeds.

a: A tax charged on most goods and services and included in the selling price
A tax that only companies have to pay
A voluntary donation to the state
4983.e: In Switzerland VAT is charged on most goods and services and is already included in the price shown. It is an important source of income for the federal government.
4983.m: VAT is already in the price.

4984.q: Which special structure in its nose helps the peregrine falcon breathe during a fast dive?
4984.e: Small bony bumps in the nostrils slow down the strong air pressure during the high-speed dive. That way the falcon can keep breathing calmly even at great speed.
4984.m: Nose bumps help it breathe in flight.

4985.q: What happened when Nicolae Ceaușescu was overthrown in 1989?
a: The Romanian dictator was overthrown and executed along with his wife.
He resigned voluntarily and went on living in the palace.
He was elected the new president.
4985.e: After mass protests, Ceaușescu was overthrown at the end of 1989, convicted in a summary trial and shot together with his wife Elena. It was one of the bloodiest ends of a communist regime in Eastern Europe.

4986.q: The middle spotted woodpecker looks similar to the great spotted woodpecker. What does it have on its head?
4986.e: The middle spotted woodpecker has a bright red cap on top of its head. Otherwise it is black and white like the great spotted woodpecker.
4986.m: The middle spotted woodpecker has a red cap.

4987.q: How fast do the praying mantis's grasping legs strike?
a: Not at all, they are slow
4987.e: The grasping strike is extremely fast. We can often hardly see it.

4988.q: Roughly how many eggs does a female cockchafer lay?
4988.e: A female usually lays 60 to 80 eggs, often in several batches. That is few compared with some other insects.
4988.m: A female lays about 60 to 80 eggs.

4989.q: Does a rooster only crow in the morning?
a: No, it can crow at any time of day
Yes, only very early in the morning
4989.e: Roosters especially like to crow in the morning, but they can do it at any time of day. It can be set off by light, noises or other crowing roosters, for example.
4989.m: Roosters can crow at any time.

4990.q: What do you call a larger group of mute swans?
4990.e: Several swans together are called a flock. Especially in winter, swans may gather in groups.

4991.q: How long does a grasshopper usually live?
4991.e: Most adult grasshoppers live only a few months. After that their eggs carry on into the next year.
4991.m: One summer of life is enough for it.

4992.q: How do some zoos help gorillas?
a: They make sure gorilla babies are born
They keep all gorillas on their own
4992.e: Zoos work together so that enough healthy gorilla babies are born. This is to stop the species from dying out.
4992.m: Zoos help gorillas with breeding programmes.

4993.q: Roughly how heavy is a newborn okapi?
4993.e: The calf is already quite big at birth. It often stands up after a short time.
4993.m: Okapi calves are quite heavy at birth.

4994.q: What does an ant bite with?
4994.e: Ants have two strong jaws on their heads. With these mandibles they can bite and carry things.

4995.q: Does the edible dormouse grow a new tail if it has lost the skin of its tail?
a: No, the bare stump dries up and falls off
4995.e: If the skin of the tail comes off when the animal is in danger, a bare stump is left. It dries up and falls off, and no new tail grows back.
4995.m: A lost tail does not grow back.

4996.q: Roughly how many harbour seals live in the whole Wadden Sea?
4996.e: Several tens of thousands of harbour seals live in the Wadden Sea; it is one of the largest populations in Europe. Conservationists count the animals regularly.
4996.m: Many thousands of harbour seals live in the Wadden Sea.

4997.q: How fast does a starfish move?
4997.e: Starfish crawl very slowly over the seabed. Even short distances often take them several minutes.

4998.q: There are no lions or tigers in Sri Lanka. So what is the Sri Lankan leopard on the island?
a: The biggest wild cat on the island
An animal that only lives in zoos now
4998.e: Because there are no lions or tigers in Sri Lanka, the Sri Lankan leopard is the biggest wild cat on the island. It is at the top of the food chain.
4998.m: In Sri Lanka the leopard is the biggest wild cat.

5000.q: What do you measure with a voltmeter?
5000.e: A voltmeter shows how big the voltage is between two points in an electric circuit. The unit volt is named after Alessandro Volta.

5001.q: In which woods does the edible dormouse feel most at home?
a: in conifer forests at the North Pole
5001.e: Edible dormice prefer broadleaved and mixed woods, especially with lots of beech trees. There they find enough food such as beechnuts.

5002.e: Woodlice have more than six legs and are not insects. They are crustaceans.

5003.q: Which technique does the golden eagle often use to catch larger animals?
a: It swoops down on its prey in a fast dive
It digs the prey out of the ground
It lies in wait motionless in the water for days
It catches prey only on foot
5003.e: When hunting, the golden eagle flies high over the land and then swoops down on its prey in a fast dive. It can reach very high speeds doing this.
5003.m: It hunts in a fast dive.

5004.q: What makes a penguin's legs different from those of many other birds?
a: They are set far back on the body
5004.e: A penguin's legs are set far back on its body. This makes it an excellent swimmer but makes it waddle on land.
5004.m: Penguin legs are set far back.

5005.q: How does the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) rate the stoat population?
5005.e: Worldwide the stoat is considered not endangered, because it is still common in many regions. Even so, like all wild animals, it needs intact habitats.
5005.m: The stoat is not considered endangered.

5006.q: What special ability does a young cuckoo have, even though it has never met its real parents?
a: It finds its way to Africa by instinct
It can speak like a human straight away
It can swim like a fish straight away
It recognises its real brothers and sisters straight away
5006.e: Although the young cuckoo travels all alone and has never met its real parents, it finds the right way to its winter quarters in Africa by instinct. It is born with this knowledge.
5006.m: The cuckoo finds its way all on its own.

5007.q: How does the presence of peregrine falcons in towns and cities sometimes affect the pigeon population?
a: It has no effect at all
It makes pigeon numbers grow a lot
5007.e: Because peregrine falcons regularly hunt pigeons, their presence can reduce the number of pigeons in some cities. That is why they are sometimes deliberately encouraged to settle there.

5008.q: What are the sugary droppings of aphids called?
5008.e: Because plant sap contains lots of sugar, aphids get rid of the extra sugar as sticky droplets. These are called honeydew.
5008.m: Honeydew is the sticky droppings of aphids.

5009.q: Besides water and light, what does a plant need to grow?
5009.e: Plants take important nutrients from the soil through their roots. Together with water and light they can then grow well.
5009.m: Plants need nutrients from the soil.

5010.q: What do most land woodlice mainly eat?
a: Dead plant material such as rotting leaves
5010.e: Woodlice mainly eat dead plant material. In this way they help break down leaves and wood.
5010.m: Woodlice mainly eat rotting plant material.

5011.q: Which species of penguin has yellow, bristly feathers above its eyes that look like hair?
5011.e: The rockhopper penguin has long tufts of yellow feathers above its eyes. It hops skilfully over rocks, which is how it got its name.
5011.m: The rockhopper penguin has yellow feather tufts.

5012.q: Which organ produces bile for digesting fat and breaks down poisons?
5012.e: The liver is an important organ for removing poisons. It also produces bile, which helps to digest fat.
5012.m: The liver removes poisons from your body.

5013.q: In good conditions, how far away can a wolf's howl be heard?
a: Not at all outside the forest
5013.e: In calm weather and open country, wolves' howling can carry several kilometres. This keeps the pack in contact even over long distances.
5013.m: A wolf's howl often carries for kilometres.

5014.q: What do bison do after eating to digest grass better?
a: They chew it again, as ruminants
They store it in their cheeks
5014.e: Bison bring food back up from the rumen and chew it again. This breaks down the grass better.

5015.q: Which river links Switzerland with the North Sea, so that eels could migrate along it?
5015.e: The Rhine flows from Switzerland into the North Sea. So eels can swim up it from the sea into Switzerland, if there are no obstacles in the way.
5015.m: The Rhine flows into the North Sea.

a: A brochure explaining the proposals being voted on
5016.e: Before every vote, the Confederation sends all voters a booklet with arguments from supporters and opponents.
5016.m: The booklet explains the pros and cons.

5017.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
5017.e: On 9 November 1989 the border between East and West Berlin opened. People celebrated at the Wall.

5018.q: Which country has a red maple leaf on its flag?
5018.e: The maple leaf is Canada's best-known symbol and has been on the flag since 1965. Maple trees grow there in huge forests.
5018.m: Canada has a red maple leaf.

5019.q: Which group of animals does the housefly belong to?
5019.e: Like all insects, the housefly has six legs and a body divided into three parts. That is why it belongs to this large group of animals.

5020.q: How does a woodlouse grow, since it has a rigid exoskeleton?
a: The shell simply grows with it
5020.e: The shell does not grow with the animal. That is why the woodlouse sheds it from time to time and forms a new one.

5021.q: What job do the males of some millipedes have in reproduction?
a: They pass on sperm packets with specially adapted legs
They build a nest of twigs
They carry the young in their mouths
5021.e: In many species, some pairs of legs are adapted for mating. The males use them to pass sperm to the females.
5021.m: Adapted legs are used for mating.

5022.q: What does it mean that orangutans are “diurnal”?
a: They are active during the day and sleep at night
They are only active at night
They are only active in winter
5022.e: Orangutans look for food during the day and rest in their nests at night. So they are not nocturnal.
5022.m: Orangutans are active during the day.

5024.q: In a shop you are given too much change by mistake. What do you do?
a: I tell the shop assistant and give it back
I keep it and say nothing
I give it to a friend
5024.e: Honesty matters a lot with money. Money you receive by mistake should be given back.
5024.m: Honestly give back money you were given by mistake.

5025.q: Where does the red kite usually build its nest, known as an eyrie?
a: right on the ground in the grass
in reed beds by the lake
5025.e: The red kite usually builds its eyrie in old, tall trees at the edge of a wood. From there it has a good view over the open land around it.
5025.m: The red kite nests high up in large trees.

5026.q: What colour are the cockchafer's wing cases?
5026.e: Cockchafers have reddish-brown wing cases. The head and the plate behind it are usually darker.

5027.q: How does a marmot colony usually react when an alarm whistle sounds?
a: The animals quickly flee into their burrows
They just stand still and calm
They all jump into the water at the same time
5027.e: When marmots hear a warning whistle, they flee in a flash into the nearest burrow. There they are safe from birds of prey and enemies on the ground.
5027.m: At the whistle, all flee at once.

5028.q: What does an adult housefly like to eat most?
5028.e: Adult houseflies really like sweet, but also rotting, leftover food. They are not fussy and eat almost anything liquid.

5029.q: Which two species of bison are there today?
5029.e: The American bison lives in North America and the European bison, or wisent, in Europe. Both belong to the genus Bison.
5029.m: There are two bison species today: the American bison and the European bison.

5030.q: What sound does a donkey make?
5030.e: The donkey makes a loud “hee-haw”, which is called braying. You can often hear it from far away.

5031.q: On which river in Zurich do you often see mallards?
5031.e: The Limmat flows right through Zurich. You often see mallards there, just as on the Aare in Bern.

5032.q: What does a contented rabbit often show when you stroke it?
a: It lies there relaxed and closes its eyes
5032.e: A contented rabbit clearly relaxes, lies down and sometimes closes its eyes. This shows that it feels comfortable.

5033.q: Where does an octopus like to hide during the day?
a: In a cave or rock crevice
5033.e: The octopus likes to choose a cave or rock crevice on the seabed as a hiding place. There it is protected from enemies.

5034.q: What do professional fishermen on Lake Constance often use to catch blue whitefish?
5034.e: Drift nets hang freely in the water at the depth where the shoals swim. The fish get caught in them.
5034.m: Drift nets catch whitefish in open water.

5035.q: What colour is the skin of a typical earthworm?
5035.e: Most earthworms are reddish brown. That is because of the blood showing through their thin skin.

5036.q: What effect can wind turbines have on red kites?
a: they put the birds at risk of collision
they are completely harmless to red kites
they give red kites new places to nest
5036.e: Red kites can collide with the turning rotor blades of wind turbines, which is often fatal. That is why red kite areas are taken into account when choosing sites for wind turbines.
5036.m: Wind turbines are dangerous for red kites.

5037.q: What does a mother blue whale feed her calf with?
5037.e: Like all mammal mothers, the mother blue whale gives her calf milk. The calf drinks huge amounts of it every day.

5038.q: What is the salmon's scaly skin for?
a: It stores water like a camel
5038.e: Scales and slime protect against injuries and diseases. They also reduce resistance in the water.

5039.q: What does a starfish have under its skin?
a: A soft shell like a snail
5039.e: Under the starfish's skin lies a hard chalky skeleton made of many small plates. This makes its body firm.
5039.m: A chalky skeleton supports the body.

5040.q: What is the greatest age wild magpies can reach?
5040.e: In the wild, magpies reach an average age of a few years, but some individuals can live to over 15. Many, however, do not survive their first years.
5040.m: Some magpies live to an amazing age.

a: A freshwater fish of its own, not an eel
5041.e: The burbot is a freshwater fish from the cod family. It is not closely related to the eel, even though its German name, “Aalquappe”, sounds similar.
5041.m: The burbot is not an eel.

5042.q: Which water temperature does the brown trout like best?
a: Water that is frozen in winter
5042.e: The brown trout is a cold-water fish. If the water gets too warm, it gets stressed and there is too little oxygen.
5042.m: The brown trout is a cold-water fish.

5043.q: What is typical of a hamster's body shape?
a: A roundish body with short legs
5043.e: Hamsters have a rather round, compact body with short legs. This makes them especially cute to look at.

5044.q: An earthworm has no teeth. Where is its food ground up?
a: At the end of its tail
5044.e: The earthworm has a powerful gizzard. There the food is ground up together with tiny stones.
5044.m: The worm grinds its food in its gizzard.

5045.q: What is the land called where most emperor penguins live?
5045.e: Antarctica is the southernmost and coldest continent on Earth. Emperor penguins are perfectly adapted to life there.

5046.q: What are a pike's teeth like?
a: There are only two big teeth
It has no teeth at all
5046.e: A pike's mouth is full of very many sharp teeth. With them it can hold on to its prey so that it cannot escape.
5046.m: Sharp teeth hold on to the prey.

5047.q: Roughly how long is a female chamois pregnant?
5047.e: A female chamois is pregnant for around six months, about 170 days. Then usually a single kid is born.
5047.m: The chamois carries her young for about six months.

5048.q: What does the kestrel cough up some time after eating?
a: A pellet of hair and bones
5048.e: The kestrel cannot digest the hair and bones of its prey. It coughs them up as a small package called a pellet.
5048.m: It coughs up indigestible remains as a pellet.

5049.q: What colour is a polar bear's skin under its fur?
5049.e: Under its white fur, the polar bear's skin really is black. This helps it absorb the sun's warmth better.
5049.m: A polar bear's skin is black.

5050.q: Does a jellyfish have a heart?
5050.e: Jellyfish have no heart and no blood as we know it. Oxygen passes straight into their bodies through their thin skin.

5051.q: Why are sheep's pupils so special?
a: They are horizontal and help them see almost all the way round
They are round like a human's
Sheep cannot see in the dark
5051.e: Sheep have horizontal pupils. This lets them see almost all the way round and spot dangers such as wolves from far away.
5051.m: Sheep see almost all the way round.

5052.q: How do chamois typically react when hikers come close?
a: They usually flee quickly into steep terrain
5052.e: Chamois are shy wild animals and when in danger usually flee in a flash into steep, inaccessible terrain. There they are safe from most enemies.
5052.m: Chamois usually flee into steep terrain.

5053.q: Roughly how tall is an adult llama at the shoulder?
5053.e: The height at the shoulder is about 1 to 1.2 metres. With its long neck, its head reaches much higher.
5053.m: Llamas are about one metre tall.

5054.q: What colour is the Malayan tapir's coat?
a: Black with a whitish grey back and rump
5054.e: The front of the body and the legs are black, the back and rump whitish grey. In the forest these markings act as camouflage.

5055.q: Which large sea creature actually also belongs to the dolphin family?
5055.e: Even though the orca is called a killer whale, scientifically it belongs to the dolphin family. It is even the largest dolphin in the world.
5055.m: The orca is the largest dolphin.

5056.q: What job do most bees in a colony have?
a: Workers do all the jobs in the hive and outside
5056.e: The workers do almost everything: cleaning, feeding, building honeycomb and collecting nectar. They make up the largest part of the whole colony.
5056.m: Workers do almost all the jobs.

5057.q: In which countries is the adder found?
a: In large parts of Europe and Asia
5057.e: Its range stretches from Western Europe to East Asia. It is one of the most widespread snakes.

5058.q: Apart from fruit, what else does a bonobo often eat?
5058.e: Bonobos add leaves, shoots and pithy plant parts to their diet. This gives them extra nutrients.
5058.m: As well as fruit, bonobos eat leaves.

5059.q: What do you call energy that is obtained from the power of the wind with large wind turbines?
5059.e: Wind drives the large blades of the wind turbines, which produces electricity. Because the wind never runs out, wind energy is a renewable energy.
5059.m: Wind turns the blades, and that makes electricity.

5060.q: Do wild sharks live in Swiss lakes and rivers?
a: No, there are no wild sharks there
5060.e: Sharks live in the sea, not in fresh water such as Swiss lakes. In Switzerland you only find sharks in zoos or aquariums.
5060.m: No wild sharks live in Swiss lakes.

5061.q: How do bees find the way to their flowers?
5061.e: Bees smell the scent of flowers and remember the position of the sun. That way they find their way back to the hive safely.
5061.m: Bees find their way by scent and the sun.

5062.q: What does a butterfly do with its proboscis when it is not drinking?
a: It rolls it up into a spiral
It lets it hang down long
It hides it in its wing
5062.e: When the proboscis is not needed, the butterfly rolls it up like a little spring. To drink, it unrolls it again.
5062.m: The proboscis is rolled up when resting.

5063.q: Why does a falling cat almost always land on its paws?
a: it twists its body in a flash in the air
it has wings under its belly
its bones are made of rubber
it brakes with its tail like a parachute
5063.e: Cats have a very sensitive balance organ in the ear and a flexible back. This lets them twist round in a flash as they fall and usually land on their paws.
5063.m: Cats twist onto their paws as they fall.

5064.q: What does a minimum size mean in fishing?
a: A minimum length a fish must reach before it may be caught
The lowest allowed weight of the fishing line
5064.e: Smaller fish must be put back gently into the water. That way they can grow and breed later.
5064.m: Fish that are too small stay in the water.

5065.q: In which famous Swiss story does a girl live with her grandfather on an alpine pasture and look after goats?
5065.e: In the story of Heidi, Heidi looks after the goats in the Swiss mountains with Peter the goatherd. The story is set in the Grisons.
5065.m: Heidi looks after goats with Peter.

5067.q: What are nitrogen-fixing bacteria on the roots of legumes such as peas for?
a: They convert nitrogen from the air into a form the plant can use
They protect the roots from frost
They store water for dry periods
They produce oxygen for the roots
5067.e: Bacteria that bind nitrogen from the air live in small root nodules. The plant needs this nitrogen to grow, and it also makes soils more fertile.
5067.m: Bacteria supply legumes with usable nitrogen.

5068.q: Which hyena was also part of the Ice Age wildlife in Europe?
5068.e: The cave hyena lived in Europe during the Ice Age. Today it is usually seen as a subspecies of the spotted hyena.
5068.m: Cave hyenas once lived in Europe.

5069.q: What is special about the grey heron's neck?
a: It can be stretched out very far and strike in a flash
It is always stiff and straight
It is short like a duck's
5069.e: The long, flexible neck can be shot forward like lightning to grab prey. This technique is the key to its hunting success.
5069.m: Its neck shoots forward in a flash.

5070.q: Which animal is especially closely related to humans?
5070.e: The chimpanzee is one of the closest living relatives of humans. Our genes are very similar.
5070.m: Chimpanzees are close relatives of humans.

5071.q: How do bison often move when in danger?
a: They run away fast as a herd
5071.e: When in danger, a whole herd can start running. This is called a stampede.
5071.m: Bison herds flee at a gallop.

5072.q: What do llamas' ears often look like?
5072.e: The ears are long and often curved like a banana. This makes llamas easy to recognise.
5072.m: Llama ears are long and curved.

5073.q: What does a tiger use its whiskers for?
a: To find its way in the dark
5073.e: Its whiskers help the tiger feel obstacles even in the dark. This helps it find its way around.
5073.m: Whiskers help it find its way.

5074.q: What did donkeys often pull on farms in the past?
5074.e: Farmers often used donkeys to pull carts or plough fields. Donkeys are strong and have great stamina for work.

5075.q: Where do red kangaroos and grey kangaroos live in the wild?
5075.e: These large kangaroos live only in Australia. There they hop across wide, open grasslands.

5076.q: What are dragonflies' antennae like compared with those of many other insects?
5076.e: Dragonflies have only short, bristle-like antennae. They rely mainly on their eyes.

5077.q: Where do chamois often move to in winter to find food more easily?
a: To lower areas, into woods or places with less snow
5077.e: When everything higher up is covered in snow, many chamois move a little lower into the valley or into woods. There they find food more easily and shelter from the wind.
5077.m: In winter chamois move further down.

5078.q: What are wolf pups like when they are born?
a: With a complete coat pattern like adults
5078.e: Newborn wolf pups can neither see nor hear and depend completely on their mother's care. Their eyes only open after about two weeks.
5078.m: Pups are blind and deaf at birth.

5079.q: What does the earthworm completely lack, unlike insects?
5079.e: Earthworms have no legs; they move only with their muscles. Insects, on the other hand, usually have six legs.

5080.q: Why do peregrine falcons today often nest on tall buildings in cities too?
a: Because tall buildings work like artificial cliffs
Because they are sheltered from the wind there
Because there are especially many fish there
Because they like the warm light
5080.e: Towers and skyscrapers offer ledges similar to natural cliffs. Cities also often have lots of pigeons as prey.

5081.q: What do pandas do most when they are not eating?
a: They build nests out of stones
5081.e: Between their long meals, pandas like to rest. This saves energy, because bamboo gives them little strength.

5082.q: What is the elk called in North America?
5082.e: In North America the elk is called a moose. The caribou, on the other hand, is the reindeer. Confusingly, in North America the word “elk” is used for the wapiti.
5082.m: The moose is the North American name for the elk.

5083.q: What is the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, or OECD for short?
a: A group of countries that promotes the economy
5083.e: The OECD is made up of many economically strong countries, and Switzerland is also a member. It compares economic data and gives recommendations for better policies.
5083.m: The OECD promotes economic cooperation between states.

5084.q: Which three countries border Lake Constance, where many blue whitefish come from?
a: Germany, Poland and the Czech Republic
5084.e: Lake Constance lies where three countries meet. Fishermen from all three countries catch whitefish there.
5084.m: Lake Constance lies in three countries.

5085.q: Why is a white winter coat an advantage for some least weasels?
a: It camouflages them in the snow
It helps them find a partner
5085.e: A white animal hardly stands out in the snow. That way the least weasel can hide better from enemies and from its prey.
5085.m: White in the snow means invisible.

5086.q: Is an elephant's skin equally thick everywhere?
a: No, thick on the back, thin behind the ears
Yes, it is equally thick everywhere
No, it is thinnest on the back
No, it is only thin on the feet
5086.e: The skin on the back can be several centimetres thick. In sensitive places such as behind the ears it is much thinner.
5086.m: The skin is not equally thick everywhere.

5087.q: Besides building dams, what does a beaver do with the trees it fells?
a: It stores branches underwater as winter food
It just leaves them lying around
5087.e: In autumn, beavers collect branches and push them into the mud on the bottom near their lodge. In winter they can reach this food under the ice.
5087.m: Beavers store branches as winter food.

5088.q: Which material stops electricity flowing through a wire into your hand?
5088.e: Plastic does not conduct electricity, which is why cables are covered with it. This means you can touch them safely.

5089.q: What does a ladybird larva mainly eat?
a: Aphids, just like the adult beetle
Only other larvae from its own family
5089.e: The larva is just as hungry as the adult beetle and mainly hunts aphids. In this way it helps plants from an early age.
5089.m: Larvae eat just as many aphids.

5090.q: Why can the tawny owl fly almost silently?
a: Its feathers have a special comb-like structure that muffles the sound of flight
It has no feathers on its wing tips
5090.e: The edges of the tawny owl's flight feathers have comb-like serrations. These break up the air turbulence and make its flight almost silent, which helps when catching prey.
5090.m: Feather combs let the tawny owl fly silently.

5091.q: What does a cockerel have on its toes?
5091.e: A cockerel walks on scaly legs with claws on its toes. With them it can scratch the ground well to find food.
5091.m: A cockerel's feet have scales and claws.

5092.q: Which of these animals is a fruit eater?
5092.e: Fruit eaters feed mainly on fruit. Fruit bats and many gibbons are among them.

5093.q: What is the easiest way to tell a house martin apart from a barn swallow?
a: By the white rump above its tail
5093.e: The house martin has a striking white rump, which the barn swallow does not have. The barn swallow, on the other hand, can be recognised by its rusty red throat.
5093.m: A white rump shows it is a house martin.

5094.q: How does the common wall lizard catch its prey?
a: With a quick snap of its mouth
It waits in the water for fish
5094.e: The wall lizard creeps up on small insects and then snaps at lightning speed. It has no venom.
5094.m: A snap, not a venomous bite.

5095.q: What was the party led by Lenin that took power in Russia in 1917 called?
5095.e: The Bolsheviks were the radical majority faction of the Russian Social Democrats. Under Lenin they led the October Revolution to success.
5095.m: The Bolsheviks were Lenin's party of revolution.

5096.q: How do young mute swans look different from their parents?
a: they are grey instead of white
they are much smaller and colourful
5096.e: Young swans, also called cygnets, have grey plumage. Only after some time do they turn white.
5096.m: Young swans are grey, not white.

5098.q: How many large eyes does a grasshopper have?
5098.e: The grasshopper has two large compound eyes. These are made up of many tiny individual eyes.
5098.m: Compound eyes see with many parts.

5099.q: What does the breast of a female blackbird usually look like?
5099.e: The female's breast is brownish and often lightly speckled. This helps her stay well camouflaged while sitting on her eggs.
5099.m: The female has a brown, speckled breast.

5100.q: How does a stone marten usually live, except in the mating season?
a: Always in pairs all year round
5100.e: Stone martens live alone and defend their own territory. Only in the mating season in summer do males and females meet briefly.

5101.q: Why were wolves wiped out in Switzerland in the past?
a: Because they were seen as a danger to farm animals and people
Because their habitat became too cold
Because they suffered from a disease
Because they could not find enough food
5101.e: Because wolves sometimes killed farm animals, they were hunted intensively for centuries. As a result, the wolf disappeared from Switzerland completely, until it returned much later.
5101.m: Wolves used to be heavily hunted.

5102.q: What do hunters call an especially large, strong stag with magnificent antlers?
5102.e: An especially powerful, old stag with large antlers is called a royal stag. A pricket is a young stag, and a yearling hind is a young female.
5102.m: A strong stag is called a royal stag.

5103.q: Roughly how old can a sand lizard get in the wild?
5103.e: Many die much younger because they are eaten by predators, but in good conditions a sand lizard can live for several years. Some live even longer in captivity.
5103.m: Sand lizards usually live a few years.

5104.q: In which habitat does the least weasel feel especially at home?
a: Only on mountain peaks above 3000 metres
5104.e: Open countryside with mice nearby gives the least weasel the best hunting opportunities. Hedges and stone walls also serve as hiding places.
5104.m: Meadows and hedges are its home.

5105.q: Roughly how long is a female donkey pregnant before her foal is born?
5105.e: A female donkey is pregnant for about a year, about as long as a horse. At birth the foal is already quite big and strong.
5105.m: Donkey foals grow in the womb for almost a year.

5106.q: Which penguin is the smallest in the world?
5106.e: The little penguin only grows to about 30 centimetres. It lives, for example, on the coasts of Australia and New Zealand.
5106.m: The little penguin is the smallest penguin.

5107.q: How are the groups of most baboon species made up?
a: Several males and many females with young
5107.e: Many baboon species live in large groups with several males and females. Hamadryas baboons have smaller harem groups.

5108.q: What is the job of the fire salamander's shiny, moist skin?
a: It helps with breathing and must stay moist
It makes it waterproof like a fish
5108.e: The animal takes in extra oxygen through its moist skin, so the skin must not dry out. Dry conditions are therefore dangerous for the fire salamander.
5108.m: Moist skin is vital for survival.

5109.q: What do barn swallows often do shortly before they leave in autumn?
a: They gather in large flocks on wires
They dig themselves in for the winter
They hide on their own in caves
They build one giant shared nest
5109.e: Before migrating in autumn, barn swallows often gather in large flocks on power lines or in reed beds. From there they set off together on their long journey.
5109.m: Before migrating they gather in flocks.

5110.q: Who builds a new wasp nest in spring?
5110.e: The queen has survived the winter and starts building the nest on her own. Later the workers help her.
5110.m: The queen starts the nest alone.

5111.q: What is a piece of rock from space that has reached the ground called?
5111.e: In space the body is called a meteoroid. Its glow in the atmosphere is a meteor, and what reaches the ground is a meteorite.
5111.m: Meteoroid, meteor and meteorite describe different stages.

5112.q: What is the difference between a wood mouse and a shrew?
a: The wood mouse is a rodent, the shrew is an insect eater
They are exactly the same animal
The wood mouse only lives in water
5112.e: Although both are small and look like mice, the wood mouse is a rodent, while the shrew is an insect eater.
5112.m: The wood mouse is a rodent, unlike the shrew.

5113.q: What is the best way for young wolves to learn to hunt?
a: By playing and watching the older pack members
By being sent into the forest on their own
By reading tracks in the snow without practice
Not at all, hunting is inborn and does not need to be learnt
5113.e: Wolf pups first practise hunting in play with each other and learn important skills. They also watch closely how the adults in the pack go about it.
5113.m: Pups learn to hunt through play.

5114.q: Roughly how long is its tail compared with its body?
a: Almost as long as the body
Only a tenth of the body length
Twice as long as the body
5114.e: The tail is almost as long as the head and body together. It is also thick and bushy.
5114.m: The tail is almost as long as the body.

a: A millipede with a cylindrical body
5115.e: Snake millipedes have a round, cylinder-shaped body. They are millipedes and roll up into a spiral.

5116.q: What is the name of an area in the canton of Solothurn with many fields, close to the canton of Aargau?
5116.e: The Gäu lies in the canton of Solothurn near the border with the canton of Aargau. There are many fields and small villages there.

5117.q: What do hunters call the pale patch on the back end of a red deer?
5117.e: The pale patch on the back end is called the rump patch. When the deer flees, it is easy for other deer to see.
5117.m: The pale patch on the bottom is the rump patch.

5118.q: What material are an elephant's tusks made of?
5118.e: The tusks are made of ivory. They are greatly lengthened upper incisor teeth.
5118.m: Tusks are lengthened incisors made of ivory.

5119.q: What is the stage between caterpillar and butterfly called?
5119.e: Inside the pupa, the caterpillar slowly turns into a butterfly. How long this takes depends on the species.
5119.m: The pupa is the in-between stage.

5120.q: Who founded the organisation called the Red Cross?
5120.e: The Swiss Henry Dunant founded the Red Cross in 1863 after he had seen wounded soldiers at a battle. He later received the first Nobel Peace Prize for it.
5120.m: Henry Dunant founded the Red Cross.

5121.q: What do wasps often do at a picnic?
a: They help themselves to food and drinks
They lay eggs in the cake
They only drink water from the glass
5121.e: Wasps can smell sweet food from far away. That is why they like to land on cake or drinks at a picnic.
5121.m: Wasps love to snack at picnics.

5122.q: Where in Switzerland did the eel use to be more common than today?
a: In rivers and lakes, for example in the Rhine
5122.e: The eel used to live in many Swiss rivers and lakes. Today its routes are often blocked by power stations, so young eels are also released.
5122.m: Eels lived in rivers and lakes.

5123.q: What do fish ladders do for eels?
a: They help them get past obstacles in rivers
They serve as a feeding place
5123.e: Fish ladders and eel passes make it easier for fish to get past weirs. For eels there are special ramps with a rough surface or brushes.

5124.q: What is the name of the animal group that octopuses, cuttlefish and squid belong to?
5124.e: Cephalopods are sea animals with arms around their head. Besides the octopus, they include cuttlefish and squid.

5125.q: What happens to raindrops on a goose's feathers?
a: They soak straight through to the skin
5125.e: Because the feathers are coated in oil, water cannot get in. The drops simply roll off the feathers.
5125.m: Water rolls off a goose's feathers.

5126.q: What is a dung beetle's exoskeleton mainly made of?
5126.e: Insects wear their skeleton on the outside of the body. It is made of a tough substance called chitin.
5126.m: The exoskeleton is made of chitin.

5127.q: How do elephants usually move around?
a: They walk almost silently on soft soles
5127.e: The soles of elephants' feet are soft and cushion-like. This means they can walk surprisingly quietly despite their weight.

5128.q: Roughly how long do young pumas stay with their mother?
a: They leave their mother on the first day
