5128.e: The young learn from their mother how to hunt. After that they look for a territory of their own.
5128.m: Young pumas learn for one to two years.

5129.q: What skin colour do many domestic pigs have under their thin coat?
5129.e: Many well-known breeds of domestic pig have pale, pink skin with a thin coat. But there are also breeds with dark or spotted skin.
5129.m: Many domestic pigs have pink skin.

5130.q: Roughly how fast does a peregrine falcon fly in normal flight, without diving?
a: At around 90 to 110 kilometres per hour
It does not fly actively, it only dives
5130.e: Even in normal flight the peregrine falcon is fast, at around 90 to 110 km/h. It only reaches its top speed when diving.
5130.m: Even its normal flight is fast.

5131.q: What do the feathers of young mallards usually look like?
a: Similar to the female, brownish and speckled
Just as green as the drake
5131.e: Young mallards look like the female at first, brown and speckled. Only later do the young males get their colourful feathers.

5134.q: Who do young mute swans often swim across the lake with in summer?
a: With their parents and brothers and sisters
5134.e: You often see swan families with several cygnets swimming together. The parents keep a close eye on their young.

5135.q: Why does a wooden boat float on water?
a: Because wood is lighter than water
Because water pushes the wood away
5135.e: A piece of wood is lighter than the same amount of water, so it floats on top. A stone is heavier than the same amount of water and sinks.
5135.m: Light materials float, heavy ones sink.

5136.q: What happens to the eggs of the blue whitefish after spawning in open water?
a: They sink to the lake bed
They are carried in the mouth
5136.e: The eggs are heavier than water. They sink to the bottom and develop there in the cold water.
5136.m: Whitefish eggs develop on the lake bed.

5137.q: When do young garden spiders usually hatch from the cocoon?
a: Straight after the eggs are laid in autumn
5137.e: The eggs spend the winter protected in the cocoon. When it gets warmer in spring, the tiny spiders hatch.
5137.m: The young spiders hatch in spring.

5138.q: Apart from red, what colours can ladybirds be?
5138.e: Not all ladybirds are red. There are also yellow, orange or black species with different numbers of spots.

5139.q: What does it mean that the universe is expanding?
a: On average, galaxies are moving further and further apart
The Sun is moving closer to the Earth
5139.e: Edwin Hubble discovered that distant galaxies are moving away from us. The further away a galaxy is, the faster it is moving away.

5140.e: A barometer measures air pressure, meaning how strongly the air presses down on the Earth. Changes in air pressure help to forecast the weather.

5141.q: Besides swimming, what else can the stoat do well?
a: It can jump very far like a kangaroo
It can glow in the dark
5141.e: With its flexible body, the stoat climbs skilfully up trees and rocks. This extends its hunting ground upwards as well.
5141.m: The stoat is a skilful climber.

5142.q: How often a year can a wood mouse have young?
a: Several times, if there is enough food
Only once in its whole life
5142.e: If there is enough food, a wood mouse can have young several times a year.
5142.m: Several times a year, depending on food.

5143.q: What does the great crested grebe's call often sound like in the breeding season?
a: Like the croak of a raven
5143.e: During the breeding season, great crested grebes make loud, barking or creaking calls. These help the partners communicate and defend their territory.
5143.m: Loud calls go with the breeding season.

5144.q: What do budgies like to do to keep themselves clean?
a: Dig in the sand for worms
5144.e: Budgies like to bathe in shallow water and then preen their feathers. This keeps their plumage clean and healthy.
5144.m: Budgies bathe and preen their feathers.

5146.q: What do you call a protected area where animals such as the wild dog live safely?
5146.e: In national parks, animals and their habitats are protected. Wild dogs can live there undisturbed too.
5146.m: National parks protect animals and habitats.

5148.q: Roughly how long is an otter pregnant?
5148.e: An otter's pregnancy lasts around two months. Then the helpless young are born in the den.
5148.m: Pregnancy lasts just over two months.

5149.q: What is the autoimmune disease called in which the pancreas can no longer produce insulin?
5149.e: In type 1 diabetes, the body's own immune system destroys the cells that make insulin. People affected have to inject insulin for the rest of their lives.

5150.q: What happens when a predator grabs a sand lizard by the tail?
a: It can shed its tail and escape
It bites and kills the predator
It squirts venom from the tip of its tail
5150.e: This trick is called autotomy and often saves the lizard's life. The detached tail keeps twitching and distracts the predator.
5150.m: The tail is shed to escape.

5151.q: What does a wood mouse like to eat most?
5151.e: The wood mouse especially likes seeds, nuts and berries. Sometimes it also eats small insects.
5151.m: Seeds and nuts are its favourite food.

5152.q: How can you roughly tell the age of a whitefish?
a: By the growth rings on its scales
By the colour of its eyes
By the length of its barbels
By the number of its teeth
5152.e: Rings form on the scales, a bit like in trees. If you count them, you can estimate the age.
5152.m: Scale rings give away the age.

5153.q: Roughly what is the wingspan of a kestrel?
5153.e: The wingspan of an adult kestrel is roughly 70 to 80 centimetres. The wings are long and pointed.
5153.m: The wingspan is around 70 to 80 centimetres.

5154.q: What should you do first if you are stung by a jellyfish?
a: Carefully rinse the area with seawater
Rub it hard with fresh water
Jump straight back into the sea
5154.e: If you are stung by a jellyfish, it is best to rinse the area carefully with seawater and get help from an adult. Fresh water can even make the pain worse.

5155.q: What does a ladybird do when it is lying on its back?
a: It pushes itself up with its legs and turns over
It stays stuck there helplessly for ever
It waits until another beetle turns it over
5155.e: With a lot of skill, the beetle pushes off with its legs and turns back onto its tummy. Then it can crawl on.

5156.q: What happens when water gets very cold?
5156.e: When water cools below 0 degrees Celsius, it freezes and becomes solid ice. This is called the freezing point.

5157.q: When were the first lynxes reintroduced to Switzerland?
a: Right after the Second World War
5157.e: From the 1970s, lynxes from the Carpathians were brought to Switzerland. This created a new population that grows slowly.
5157.m: The lynx has been returning since the 1970s.

5158.q: Apart from sounds, how do donkeys show other donkeys how they feel?
a: With their ears, head and posture
By changing the colour of their coat
By tapping their hooves on stones
Not at all, only with sounds
5158.e: Donkeys show their mood not only with sounds but also with the position of their ears, head and body. This way they understand each other well.
5158.m: Donkeys also talk with their bodies.

5159.q: What do a wolf's large paws especially help it with?
a: They spread its weight in the snow like snowshoes
They make it slower when swimming
They are only for digging dens
5159.e: A wolf's large paws spread its weight over a larger area. As a result it sinks less deeply into the snow and can move more easily.
5159.m: Large paws help wolves in the snow.

5160.e: Hens lay eggs, from which chicks can later hatch. Some eggs are also eaten by people.

5161.e: Only the male cuckoo makes the well-known “cuckoo” call. The female makes more of a laughing, trilling sound.

5162.q: Why is the praying mantis called a predator among insects?
a: It catches and eats live animals
5162.e: The praying mantis lies in wait without moving and grabs insects at lightning speed with its catching legs. It lives by catching live prey, which makes it a predator.

5163.q: What is the famous bear enclosure in the city of Bern, where live bears are kept, called?
5163.e: The Bear Pit in Bern is one of the city's best-known sights. Visitors can watch live brown bears there.
5163.m: The Bear Pit in Bern has live bears.

5164.q: Roughly how long is a red deer hind pregnant before her calf is born?
5164.e: The pregnancy lasts around eight months. Then usually a single calf is born.

5165.q: What helps the grass snake find prey in the water?
a: It can dive and hunt underwater
5165.e: It can stay underwater for quite a long time. There it catches frogs, tadpoles and fish.
5165.m: Diving is part of hunting too.

5166.q: Why do elephants like to roll in mud?
a: For protection from the sun and insects
5166.e: The mud forms a layer on the skin that protects against sunburn and annoying insects. Then the mud dries and falls off again.

5167.q: How does a wood mouse find its way in the dark?
a: With its whiskers and its sense of smell
It sees nothing in the dark and stands still
5167.e: With its whiskers and fine sense of smell, the wood mouse finds its way even in complete darkness.

5168.q: Who developed the first vaccine against a disease (smallpox)?
5168.e: In 1796 Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine against the dangerous disease smallpox. His discovery laid the foundation for modern vaccinations.

5170.q: What applies when young people under 18 sign a contract such as a mobile phone contract?
a: They usually need their parents' consent, because minors only have limited legal capacity
The contract is always automatically valid
Minors may not sign any contracts at all
The contract is only valid if it is made verbally
5170.e: In Switzerland minors have only limited legal capacity, so many contracts need their parents' consent. This protects young people from financial traps.

5171.q: What can you often tell from a llama's ears?
a: Whether it is male or female for sure
5171.e: Pricked-up ears show attention, while ears laid back often show annoyance. This is how llamas communicate even without sounds.

5172.q: Why do scientists give animals such as the brown trout a Latin name?
a: So that they have the same name all over the world
Because Latin is shorter than English
So that nobody understands the name
Because the animals come from Italy
5172.e: The brown trout has a different name in every language. But the Latin name Salmo trutta fario is used everywhere, so scientists worldwide know which animal is meant.
5172.m: Latin names are valid all over the world.

5173.q: Can a lynx pull in its claws?
a: Only on the front paws, never at the back
5173.e: Like other cats, the lynx can pull in its claws to keep them sharp. When hunting, it extends them on purpose.

5175.q: What is the process called in which a sand lizard sheds its tail for protection?
5175.e: Autotomy means deliberately shedding a body part to escape. It happens in various species of lizard.
5175.m: Shedding the tail is called autotomy.

5176.q: What shape are the horns of the African buffalo?
a: They curve downwards first and then upwards
They are straight and point forwards
5176.e: The horns sweep outwards and downwards and then curve upwards. In old bulls they grow together on the forehead to form a shield.
5176.m: The horns sweep down and up.

5177.q: Does the peregrine falcon build its own nest?
a: No, it lays its eggs in a simple hollow
Yes, a large nest of twigs
Yes, a nest made of clay
Yes, a nest of grass deep in the ground
5177.e: Peregrine falcons do not build a proper nest, they just scrape a shallow hollow on rock ledges or in nest boxes. They lay their eggs straight into it.
5177.m: A simple hollow is enough for the peregrine.

5178.q: Which physical changes are typical of puberty?
a: A growth spurt and the development of adult body features
5178.e: In puberty, hormones change the body into an adult body. This includes growth and physical changes.

5179.q: How is the least weasel's tail different from the stoat's?
5179.e: The stoat always has a black tip at the end of its tail, the least weasel does not. This is the most important way to tell the two species apart.
5179.m: The least weasel has no black tail tip.

5180.q: Roughly how old does a leopard get in the wild?
5180.e: In the wild, leopards usually live 12 to 17 years. In zoos they can live longer.
5180.m: Wild leopards live to about 15 years.

5181.q: What do young pumas look like in their first months?
a: They have dark spots on their fur
They have stripes like a tiger
They look exactly like their parents
5181.e: Puma cubs have spotted fur and blue eyes. The spots fade as they grow up.

5182.q: Who is usually in charge in a group of ring-tailed lemurs?
5182.e: In ring-tailed lemurs, the females rank above the males. For example, they get to eat first.

5183.q: How are the toes of the great spotted woodpecker arranged?
5183.e: This toe arrangement is called a climbing foot. It helps the bird hold on tightly to tree trunks.
5183.m: The great spotted woodpecker has two toes forwards and two backwards.

5184.q: Where do whitefish mainly live in Switzerland?
a: In cool lakes rich in oxygen
In the sea off the coast
5184.e: Whitefish need cool water that is rich in oxygen. They find this mainly in large, deep lakes.

5185.q: When are African wild dogs usually active?
a: Mainly in the morning and evening
Only in the middle of the night
5185.e: They usually hunt in the cooler morning and evening hours. At midday they often rest in the shade.
5185.m: Wild dogs hunt at dawn and dusk.

5186.q: What are water fleas, which whitefish like to eat?
5186.e: Water fleas are tiny crustaceans and part of the zooplankton. They float in open water and are important food for many fish.
5186.m: Water fleas are crustaceans, not insects.

5187.q: What does a male common frog use to hold on to a female when mating?
5187.e: During the mating season, male common frogs have rough pads on their thumbs. With these they can hold on tightly to the female.
5187.m: Nuptial pads help them hold on.

5188.e: They can close their ears when digging. That way no sand gets in.
5188.m: They close their ears when digging.

5189.q: Which animal is the largest living species of deer in the world?
5189.e: The moose grows much bigger and heavier than the red deer. This makes it the largest species of deer.
5189.m: The moose is the largest deer.

5190.q: What colour is the belly of many donkeys compared with the rest of their coat?
a: Exactly as dark as the back
5190.e: Many donkeys have lighter fur on the belly, the muzzle and around the eyes. The back, on the other hand, is usually darker.
5190.m: A donkey's belly is often lighter.

5191.q: How does a bison protect itself from the cold in winter?
a: With a very dense, thick coat
With a layer of fat and no fur
5191.e: The winter coat is especially dense and very warm. Bison do not hibernate.
5191.m: Dense fur protects bison from the cold.

5192.q: What colour is a housefly's body usually?
5192.e: The housefly is usually grey and has four dark stripes on its back. This gives it good camouflage.
5192.m: The housefly is grey with stripes.

5193.q: What is the spotted hyena known for because of its sounds?
a: Its loud call that sounds like giggling
A deep roar like a lion's
5193.e: Spotted hyenas make sounds that sound like laughter. They use them to communicate, for example when excited or fighting.
5193.m: The spotted hyena sounds as if it is laughing.

5194.q: In which years do edible dormice breed especially often?
a: in years with lots of beechnuts
in years with lots of snow
5194.e: When beech trees produce lots of beechnuts (so-called mast years), edible dormice have enough energy to breed. In years with little food, some females have no young at all.

5195.q: The scientific name of the great crested grebe is Podiceps, which roughly means “foot at the rear”. What does that tell you about it?
a: Its legs are set far back on its body
It has feet on its tail
5195.e: The great crested grebe's legs are set very far back. That is ideal for swimming and diving, but bad for walking.

5196.q: How fast can a polar bear run on land for a short time?
5196.e: Over short distances a polar bear can run surprisingly fast. Over a longer time, however, it would quickly get too hot.
5196.m: Polar bears can run very fast for a short time.

5197.q: What does a goose use to protect its feathers from getting wet?
a: Oil from a gland, which it spreads with its beak
5197.e: Geese have a small gland near the tail that produces oil. They spread this oil through their feathers with their beak, so water simply rolls off.

5198.q: When do mallards usually find their partners?
a: Only after their ducklings have hatched
5198.e: Mallards usually look for a new partner for the next breeding season as early as autumn or winter. In spring they then get on with building the nest.

5200.q: What can often be seen at the back end of a perch's first dorsal fin?
5200.e: Many perch have a dark spot at the end of the front dorsal fin. It is one of their identifying features.
5200.m: A dark spot on the dorsal fin.

5201.q: In which season do you hear the eagle owl's courtship call especially often?
a: In late winter, around December to February
In high summer, around July and August
Only in autumn during bird migration
Never, the eagle owl calls equally often all year
5201.e: The eagle owl calls especially during courtship in late winter, to attract partners and mark its territory. Then its deep call can often be heard over long distances.
5201.m: Eagle owls court especially in late winter.

5202.q: What does a cheetah's body look like?
a: Slim and long with long legs
Short and stocky like a bear
5202.e: The cheetah has a very slim body with long, strong legs. That is what makes it so fast when running.
5202.m: The cheetah is built especially slim.

5203.q: Apart from Europe, on which continents is the golden eagle found?
a: Asia, North Africa and North America
Only on islands in the Pacific
5203.e: The golden eagle is widespread and, besides Europe, lives in parts of Asia, North Africa and North America. This makes it one of the most widespread birds of prey in the world.
5203.m: It lives on several continents in the northern hemisphere.

5204.q: What do cockchafer grubs mainly feed on?
5204.e: The grubs eat the roots of grasses, herbs and trees. This means they can damage meadows and forest plantations.

5205.e: Baboons are active during the day. At night they sleep in safe places.

5206.q: Where does the cuckoo get its name from?
a: From the colour of its feathers
From a mountain in the Alps
5206.e: The male calls a loud “cuck-oo”. The bird was named after this call.
5206.m: The cuckoo is named after its call.

5207.q: Which way does a carp's mouth point?
a: It has no mouth at all
5207.e: The carp's mouth points rather downwards. This lets it search well for food on the bottom.
5207.m: A carp's mouth points to the bottom.

5208.q: Why are peregrine falcons protected in Switzerland today?
a: Because their numbers had fallen sharply in the past
Because they became popular as pets
Because they have no natural enemies
5208.e: Because of poisons such as DDT and persecution, their numbers fell sharply in the past. That is why the peregrine falcon is protected today and must not be disturbed.
5208.m: A past decline led to today's protection.

5209.q: Does a broken rhino horn grow back?
5209.e: The horn is made of keratin and, like our fingernails, can slowly grow back if it breaks off. But this takes several years.

5210.q: How old can tapirs get in captivity?
5210.e: In zoos, tapirs can live to over 30. In the wild their life expectancy is usually lower.
5210.m: Tapirs live to over 30 in zoos.

5211.q: In summer, what does the sparrow especially like to eat as well as grain?
5211.e: In summer there are lots of insects, which the sparrow likes to eat, especially to feed its chicks. In winter it mainly eats seeds and grain.
5211.m: In summer sparrows like to eat insects.

5212.q: When do common frogs usually lay their spawn?
a: Very early in spring, often in March
In the middle of winter in December
5212.e: Common frogs are among the first amphibians of the year. Often as early as February or March, they lay their clumps of spawn in ponds and pools.
5212.m: Common frogs spawn very early in the year.

5213.q: What pattern do wild boar piglets have on their fur?
5213.e: Young wild boar have striped fur. This helps them hide in the forest.
5213.m: Wild boar piglets have striped fur.

5214.q: Roughly how much does an adult magpie weigh?
5214.e: An adult magpie weighs on average about 200 to 250 grams. This makes it much lighter than a crow.
5214.m: Magpies weigh about as much as an apple.

5215.q: What is one difference between the soles of the feet of the stone marten and the pine marten?
a: The pine marten has hairy soles, the stone marten bare soles
The stone marten has webbed feet, the pine marten does not
Only the pine marten has claws at all
The stone marten has four toes, the pine marten five
5215.e: The pine marten has hair on the soles of its feet, which helps it climb on branches. The stone marten, on the other hand, has rather bare, hairless soles.
